full_output.methodology: Structural analysis, site-directed mutagenesis, and drug susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and antimicrobial susceptibility of Plesiomonas shigelloides from great cormorants (Phalacrocorax carbo hanedae) in Gifu and Shiga Prefectures, Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 33 out of 69 Plesiomonas shigelloides isolates from great cormorants in Japan showed resistance to ampicillin, tetracycline, and trimethoprim.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using broth microdilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibitory effects of emodin, baicalin, schizandrin and berberine on hefA gene: treatment of Helicobacter pylori-induced multidrug resistance.

hefA.validation_method: real-time quantitative PCR and MIC determination

full_output.key_findings: Emodin, baicalin, schizandrin, and berberine significantly decreased the MICs of amoxicillin and tetracycline against some H. pylori strains, possibly by mechanisms associated with decreasing hefA mRNA expression.
full_output.methodology: Double dilution method, real-time quantitative PCR, and MIC determination.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of NDM-1-producing multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas putida from a paediatric case of acute gastroenteritis, India.

gyrA.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the isolate exhibited amino acid substitution of T83I in gyrA and shows resistance to fluoroquinolones.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first isolation of NDM-1-producing multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas putida from a pediatric case of acute gastroenteritis in India, highlighting the presence of multiple AMR genes and mutations contributing to resistance against various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes and mutations in the isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanism behind Resistance against the Organophosphate Azamethiphos in Salmon Lice (Lepeophtheirus salmonis).

full_output.paper_title: Development of secondary mutations in wild-type and mutant EZH2 alleles cooperates to confer resistance to EZH2 inhibitors.

EZH2.notes: The Y111L mutation occurs in the context of the EZH2 WT allele and was present in all resistant clones.

full_output.key_findings: The study constructed a recombinant HVT vaccine expressing the N-terminal fragment of PmpD from Chlamydia psittaci (rHVT-pmpD-N) and evaluated its immunogenicity and protective efficacy against C. psittaci and Marek's Disease Virus (MDV).
full_output.methodology: The study involved constructing a recombinant HVT vaccine, evaluating its expression, stability, and immunogenicity through various assays including immunoblot, immunofluorescence, and ELISA.

full_output.paper_title: Expression of the AcrAB Components of the AcrAB-TolC Multidrug Efflux Pump of Yersinia enterocolitica Is Subject to Dual Regulation by OmpR.
full_output.key_findings: OmpR regulates the expression of the AcrAB-TolC multidrug efflux pump in Yersinia enterocolitica through dual mechanisms, activating acrAB and repressing acrR.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, promoter-gfp fusion, β-galactosidase assay, and EMSA.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Outer Membrane and Exoproteins of Carbapenem-Resistant Multilocus Sequence Type 258 Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various outer membrane and exoproteins of carbapenem-resistant ST258 K. pneumoniae, including several uncharacterized surface proteins. It also noted the absence of the resistance porin OmpK35 due to a stop codon in the ompK35 gene in this ST258 isolate.
full_output.methodology: Proteomics approach involving 2D electrophoresis and LC-MS/MS to identify surface-associated and culture supernatant proteins.

full_output.paper_title: MKAN27435 is required for the biosynthesis of higher subclasses of lipooligosaccharides in Mycobacterium kansasii.
full_output.key_findings: MKAN27435 is required for the biosynthesis of higher subclasses of lipooligosaccharides (LOS) in Mycobacterium kansasii. Its disruption leads to the absence of LOS-IV, LOS-V, LOS-VI, and LOS-VII, and the accumulation of shunt products derived from LOS-III.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation using specialized transduction, lipid analysis by TLC and mass spectrometry, and complementation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: The vls locus is essential for persistent infection of a natural reservoir host
full_output.key_findings: The vlsE gene is essential for B. burgdorferi to establish persistent infection in the natural reservoir host, Peromyscus maniculatus. Mutants lacking vlsE or expressing a static form of VlsE were unable to persist in the host, highlighting the importance of VlsE antigenic variation for immune evasion.
full_output.methodology: Infection experiments with wild-type and mutant B. burgdorferi clones in murine hosts, PCR analysis of plasmid profiles, and tick transmission studies.
full_output.sample_size: various mouse models and tick experiments

full_output.paper_title: Emissions of Escherichia coli carrying extended-spectrum β-lactamase resistance from pig farms to the surrounding environment.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibilities of enterococcus species isolated from hospital and domestic wastewater effluents in alice, eastern cape province of South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of vancomycin resistance genes (vanB, vanC1, vanC2/3) and the macrolide resistance gene erm(B) in Enterococcus isolates from hospital wastewater and final effluent of a wastewater treatment plant in South Africa.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanistic Pharmacodynamic Modeling of Slow-Binding Inhibitors of PaLpxC
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the mechanism of action of slow-binding inhibitors targeting P. aeruginosa LpxC, a key enzyme in lipid A biosynthesis, and develops a mechanistic PD model linking their binding kinetics to bacterial growth dynamics.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical assays, MIC determinations, and mechanistic pharmacodynamic modeling were used to evaluate the effects of slow-binding inhibitors on bacterial growth and resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antagonism of miR-328 increases the antimicrobial function of macrophages and neutrophils and rapid clearance of non-typeable Haemophilus influenzae (NTHi) from infected lung.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that antagonizing miR-328 enhances the antimicrobial functions of macrophages and neutrophils, leading to improved clearance of non-typeable Haemophilus influenzae (NTHi) from the lungs.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized miRNA inhibition via antagomirs, phagocytosis assays, and bacterial clearance measurements in both in vitro and in vivo models.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Activity of Rifampicin Combined with Daptomycin or Tigecycline on Staphylococcus haemolyticus Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the biofilm formed by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus haemolyticus strains and evaluates the in vitro activity of rifampicin combined with daptomycin or tigecycline against these biofilms. It shows that the tigecycline/rifampicin combination is more effective than daptomycin/rifampicin against ica-independent biofilms formed by S. haemolyticus.
full_output.methodology: Biofilm production was assessed using microtiter plate assays, biofilm detachment assays, and confocal laser scanning microscopy. Antimicrobial susceptibility was evaluated using a biofilm susceptibility assay.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic streptococcal phage λSA2 and B30 endolysins kill streptococci in cow milk and in a mouse model of mastitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the endolysins of streptococcal phages λSA2 and B30, demonstrating their ability to kill streptococci in cow milk and in a mouse model of mastitis. The λSA2 lysin showed high activity against Streptococcus dysgalactiae, Streptococcus agalactiae, and Streptococcus uberis, while the B30 lysin was less effective. The two endolysins exhibited synergistic effects in vitro but not in the mouse model.
full_output.methodology: The study involved biochemical characterization of the endolysins, turbidity reduction assays, plate lysis assays, and evaluation of lytic activity in milk and a mouse model of mastitis.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical and microbiological profiles of shigellosis in children.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-14, and bla TEM-1 genes in ceftriaxone-resistant Shigella flexneri strains, highlighting the emergence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs) in Shigella.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and resistance patterns in Shigella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The Serine Protease Autotransporter Pic Modulates Citrobacter rodentium Pathogenesis and Its Innate Recognition by the Host.

full_output.methodology: Gene knockout, complementation, in vitro mucinase activity assays, and in vivo infection studies in mice.

full_output.paper_title: A Heterologous Reporter Defines the Role of the Tetanus Toxin Interchain Disulfide in Light-Chain Translocation.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the role of the interchain disulfide bond in the light-chain translocation of tetanus toxin using a β-lactamase reporter system. Mutations in the interchain disulfide (C439S, C467S) prevented β-lactamase translocation, demonstrating the necessity of an intact disulfide bond for successful translocation.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic engineering, protein purification, and cell-based assays to analyze the translocation of a β-lactamase fusion protein derived from tetanus toxin.

full_output.paper_title: An Invertron-Like Linear Plasmid Mediates Intracellular Survival and Virulence in Bovine Isolates of Rhodococcus equi.

vapN.mechanism: mediates intracellular survival and virulence in macrophages
vapN.validation_method: deletion mutant analysis and macrophage infection assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the vapN gene on the pVAPN plasmid as essential for intracellular survival and virulence in bovine isolates of Rhodococcus equi, demonstrating its critical role in macrophage proliferation and pathogenesis.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, deletion mutagenesis, macrophage infection assays, and competitive virulence experiments in mice.

full_output.paper_title: Urinary tract infections and antimicrobial sensitivity among diabetic patients at Khartoum, Sudan.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that E. coli was the most common isolate from diabetic patients with urinary tract infections (UTI), and some isolates showed resistance to ampicillin, co-trimoxazole, nitrofurantoin, and amoxicillin-clavulanic acid. K. pneumoniae was also frequently isolated, and multi-drug resistance was observed in 28.2% of the total isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a cross-sectional analysis of urine cultures and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of bacterial isolates from diabetic patients.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiofilm peptides increase the susceptibility of carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolates to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that antibiofilm peptides DJK-6 and 1018 can enhance the susceptibility of carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (KpC) isolates to β-lactam antibiotics, particularly meropenem, by eradicating preformed biofilms and reducing the required antibiotic concentration.
full_output.methodology: The study used microdilution susceptibility assays, flow cell experiments, and checkerboard titration assays to evaluate the antibiofilm and synergistic effects of peptides DJK-6 and 1018 with β-lactam antibiotics against KpC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Role of Pseudomonas aeruginosa low-molecular-mass penicillin-binding proteins in AmpC expression, β-lactam resistance, and peptidoglycan structure.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the role of Pseudomonas aeruginosa low-molecular-mass penicillin-binding proteins (LMM PBPs) in AmpC expression, β-lactam resistance, and peptidoglycan structure. It identifies dacB, dacC, and pbpG as key players in β-lactam resistance and peptidoglycan composition.
full_output.methodology: Mutant construction, MIC testing, HPLC analysis, and Bocillin FL-binding test.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of pre-antibiotic era Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates with respect to antibiotic/disinfectant susceptibility and virulence in Galleria mellonella.

blaSHV.validation_method: experimental validation through cloning and expression in E. coli

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaSHV genes as the cause of penicillin resistance in pre-antibiotic era Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates. Some isolates with blaSHV genes showed resistance to penicillins, and mutations in these genes could enhance resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution for antibiotic susceptibility testing, PCR for gene detection, and cloning and expression in E. coli for functional validation.

full_output.paper_title: Serratia marcescens Cyclic AMP Receptor Protein Controls Transcription of EepR, a Novel Regulator of Antimicrobial Secondary Metabolites.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies eepR and eepS as novel regulators of antimicrobial secondary metabolites in Serratia marcescens, showing that EepR directly regulates the production of prodigiosin and serratamolide.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screens, chromosomal lacZ fusions, qPCR, EMSA, and HPLC-MS analysis were used to characterize the role of eepR and eepS in secondary metabolite production.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity of Class 1 Integron Gene Cassette Rearrangements Selected under Antibiotic Pressure.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the catB9 gene cassette can be rearranged closer to the Pc promoter under chloramphenicol pressure, enhancing chloramphenicol resistance. This rearrangement occurs through excision of upstream gene cassettes rather than direct relocalization of catB9.
full_output.methodology: Chloramphenicol susceptibility testing, PCR analysis, and construction of synthetic integrons.

full_output.paper_title: The Cyclic AMP-Vfr Signaling Pathway in Pseudomonas aeruginosa Is Inhibited by Cyclic Di-GMP.
full_output.key_findings: High levels of c-di-GMP in P. aeruginosa lead to decreased cAMP levels, resulting in reduced expression of acute virulence factors. This study shows that c-di-GMP inhibits the cAMP-Vfr signaling pathway, affecting virulence factor gene transcription.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, reporter assays, and biochemical analyses were used to investigate the relationship between c-di-GMP and cAMP levels in P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Unraveling the Mechanism for the Viability Deficiency of Shewanella oneidensis oxyR Null Mutant.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that the viability deficiency of the Shewanella oneidensis oxyR null mutant is due to abiotic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) generated in lysogeny broth (LB), which is not mitigated by the mutant's inherent antioxidant defenses. Iron species and catalase can suppress this defect by scavenging H2O2.
full_output.methodology: The study employed genetic mutagenesis, complementation, β-galactosidase assays, H2O2 assays, and viability tests to investigate the role of OxyR in H2O2 resistance and the impact of exogenous iron and catalase on the mutant's viability.

full_output.paper_title: A variable DNA recognition site organization establishes the LiaR-mediated cell envelope stress response of enterococci to daptomycin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the adaptive mutation D191N in LiaR, which confers increased daptomycin resistance in Enterococcus faecalis by causing constitutive activation of the protein and enhancing its DNA binding affinity.
full_output.methodology: Structural biology, biochemical assays, and DNA footprinting were used to analyze the role of LiaR and its mutants in daptomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Drug Resistance of Vibrio cholerae, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
full_output.key_findings: The study found increasing antimicrobial drug resistance in Vibrio cholerae isolates from the Democratic Republic of the Congo between 1997 and 2012, with a notable shift towards resistance to multiple antibiotics, including sulfamethoxazole/trime-thoprim, nalidixic acid, erythromycin, chloramphenicol, tetracycline, and ampicillin. The 2011-2012 epidemic was caused by an El Tor variant with a specific antimicrobial resistance profile, showing resistance to most antibiotics except cyclines and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted antimicrobial drug susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method and analyzed genetic diversity through MLVA and whole-genome sequencing.

full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PFGE analysis, and statistical analysis of resistance trends.

full_output.paper_title: Repurposing salicylanilide anthelmintic drugs to combat drug resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies niclosamide and oxyclozanide as effective against drug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating bacteriostatic and bactericidal effects, respectively, without characterizing any specific AMR genes or mutations.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, time-kill studies, membrane permeabilization assays, and cytotoxicity evaluations were conducted.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified specific microbial taxa associated with severe decline in lung function in cystic fibrosis patients, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Rothia mucilaginosa, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Candida albicans. It also noted the absence of fungi and Staphylococcus aureus in stable patients.
full_output.methodology: The study used culture-based methods, T-RFLP analysis, and statistical analyses to compare the airway microbiota of cystic fibrosis patients with stable and severe lung function.

full_output.paper_title: Competition between VanU(G) repressor and VanR(G) activator leads to rheostatic control of vanG vancomycin resistance operon expression.
full_output.key_findings: VanU_G acts as a repressor of the vanG operon by binding to the PUG and PYG promoters, while VanR_G functions as an activator. The balance between these regulators enables rheostatic control of vancomycin resistance gene expression.
full_output.methodology: DNase I footprinting, RT-qPCR, reporter protein activities, CAT assay, purification and phosphorylation assays

full_output.paper_title: Pan-genome dynamics of Pseudomonas gene complements enriched across hexachlorocyclohexane dumpsite.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, annotation, BLASTN analysis, and metagenomic mapping were used to characterize the integron and its associated genes.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence related sequences; insights provided by comparative genomics of Streptococcus uberis of differing virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study compares the genomes of 13 Streptococcus uberis strains, identifying core and accessory genes, and explores the relationship between genome content and virulence. It finds that while certain virulence genes are present in all strains, their sequence variability suggests roles in host-pathogen interactions rather than straightforward virulence determinants.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, comparative genomics, and experimental infection models were used to analyze the virulence and genetic diversity of S. uberis strains.

full_output.paper_title: The Psp system of Mycobacterium tuberculosis integrates envelope stress-sensing and envelope-preserving functions.

Suppressor mutations in fecE and amiC were identified as necessary for the survival of codY mutants.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that bismuth subsalicylate (BSS) and bismuth oxychloride (BiOCl) exhibit antimicrobial activity against various enteric pathogens, including Clostridium difficile, Salmonella, Shigella, and E. coli, as well as antiviral activity against norovirus. The mechanisms involve binding to bacterial membranes and inhibiting growth or reducing viability.

full_output.paper_title: Pyrrolnitrin and Hydrogen Cyanide Production by Pseudomonas chlororaphis Strain PA23 Exhibits Nematicidal and Repellent Activity against Caenorhabditis elegans.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hcnA and prnA as genes responsible for hydrogen cyanide and pyrrolnitrin production in Pseudomonas chlororaphis strain PA23, which exhibit nematicidal and repellent activities against Caenorhabditis elegans.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the in vitro transport activity of the fully assembled MexAB-OprM efflux pump from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, demonstrating its role in multidrug resistance through active substrate transport.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Mutations Detected in Avirulence Genes Overcoming Tomato Cf Resistance Genes in Isolates of a Japanese Population of Cladosporium fulvum.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel mutations in avirulence genes (Avr2, Avr4, Avr4E, Avr5, and Avr9) of Cladosporium fulvum that enable the fungus to overcome resistance genes (Cf-2, Cf-4, Cf-4E, Cf-5, and Cf-9) in tomato plants. These mutations include frameshifts, point mutations, and gene deletions, which result in the loss of HR-inducing activity, thereby allowing the fungus to evade plant immunity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PVX-mediated expression of avirulence genes in tomato plants to assess HR-inducing activity, along with DNA sequencing and PCR analysis to identify mutations in avirulence genes.

full_output.paper_title: Phosphoethanolamine Transferase LptA in Haemophilus ducreyi Modifies Lipid A and Contributes to Human Defensin Resistance In Vitro.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies lptA, ptdA, and ptdB as phosphoethanolamine transferase genes in Haemophilus ducreyi that contribute to resistance against alpha- and beta-defensins. Deletion of these genes increased susceptibility to defensins, while complementation restored resistance.
full_output.methodology: Mutant construction, complementation, antimicrobial peptide bactericidal assays, cell surface charge analysis, and MALDI-MS analysis of LOS.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility profiling and virulence potential of Campylobacter jejuni isolates from different sources in Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antibiotic resistance patterns and virulence factors in Campylobacter jejuni isolates from different sources in Pakistan. Resistance to cephalothin was the most common, followed by sulfamethoxazole+trimethoprim and ampicillin. Virulence factors cadF and mapA were present in all isolates, while neuAB was found in 36% of poultry isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility was determined using the Kirby Bauer Disc Diffusion assay, and virulence factors were detected via PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Evolutionary dynamics of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus within a healthcare system.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the emergence of ACME-II, a type II arginine catabolic mobile element, in ST239 isolates, along with the presence of ermA and ermC genes conferring erythromycin resistance. These elements contributed to the genetic diversity and adaptability of MRSA populations in Singapore.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were used to investigate the population structure and evolutionary dynamics of MRSA in Singaporean hospitals.

full_output.paper_title: Extensive Within-Host Diversity in Fecally Carried Extended-Spectrum-Beta-Lactamase-Producing Escherichia coli Isolates: Implications for Transmission Analyses.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified extensive within-host diversity among fecally carried extended-spectrum-beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli isolates, highlighting the presence of multiple sequence types (STs) and bla CTX-M variants within individuals. The findings suggest that single-colony subcultures may underestimate transmission events, particularly in high-prevalence settings.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was used to analyze the genetic diversity of E. coli isolates from fecal samples, focusing on resistance and virulence gene content.

full_output.paper_title: Mixed Infections and Rifampin Heteroresistance among Mycobacterium tuberculosis Clinical Isolates.

rpoB.notes: Mutations in rpoB gene were associated with rifampin resistance.

full_output.methodology: Spoligotyping, MIRU-VNTR, and rpoB gene sequencing were used to analyze mixed infections and rifampin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: CYP94-mediated jasmonoyl-isoleucine hormone oxidation shapes jasmonate profiles and attenuates defence responses to Botrytis cinerea infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that CYP94B3 and CYP94C1 enzymes play a critical role in the oxidation of jasmonoyl-isoleucine (JA-Ile), affecting the jasmonate profile and defense responses against Botrytis cinerea. Overexpression of these enzymes leads to impaired defense gene induction and reduced resistance to the pathogen.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized mutant and overexpressing plant lines, metabolite profiling via UPLC-MS/MS, and gene expression analyses to investigate the role of CYP94 enzymes in jasmonate metabolism and defense responses.

full_output.paper_title: Multiple antibiotic susceptibility of polyphosphate kinase mutants (ppk1 and ppk2) from Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 as revealed by global phenotypic analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 mutants lacking polyphosphate kinase (ppk1 and ppk2) exhibit increased susceptibility to multiple antibiotics, including Ciprofloxacin, Chloramphenicol, and Rifampicin, suggesting that polyP synthesis is a potential target for antimicrobial drug design.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized Phenotype Microarrays to analyze the phenotypic changes in P. aeruginosa PAO1 polyP kinase mutants (ppk1 and ppk2), assessing their susceptibility to various antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug resistant and carbapenemase producing Enterobacteriaceae among patients with urinary tract infection at referral Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (MDRE) and carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (CPE) among patients with urinary tract infections. MDRE accounted for 87.4% of isolates, with K. pneumoniae and E. coli being the most common. CPE prevalence was 2.73%, and all CPE strains were 100% ESBL producers.
full_output.methodology: The study used disk diffusion method for antibiotic susceptibility testing and CHROMagar KPC medium for detecting carbapenemase-producing strains.

full_output.paper_title: Nosocomial Outbreak of New Delhi Metallo-β-Lactamase-1-Producing Gram-Negative Bacteria in South Africa: A Case-Control Study.

bla_NDM-1.validation_method: real-time PCR testing for bla NDM-1

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the bla_NDM-1 gene as a major cause of carbapenem resistance in Gram-negative bacteria during an outbreak in South Africa.
full_output.methodology: Case-control study with real-time PCR testing for bla NDM-1 in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid emergence of multidrug resistant, H58-lineage Salmonella typhi in Blantyre, Malawi.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the rapid emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) H58-lineage Salmonella typhi in Blantyre, Malawi, with a significant increase in MDR cases from 2011 onwards. The H58 haplotype was strongly associated with MDR, and the MDR region integrated into the chromosome via a Tn21-like element.
full_output.methodology: Longitudinal surveillance, whole-genome sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the emergence and characteristics of MDR S. Typhi.

full_output.paper_title: High frequency of resistance, lack of clinical benefit, and poor outcomes in capreomycin treated South African patients with extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis.

full_output.methodology: Targeted DNA sequencing and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing were used to identify capreomycin resistance mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem non-susceptible enterobacteriaceae in Quebec, Canada: results of a laboratory surveillance program (2010-2012).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various carbapenemase genes, including blaKPC, blaSME, blaOXA-48, blaNDM, and blaNMC, in carbapenem-non-susceptible Enterobacteriaceae isolates in Quebec, Canada. These genes were associated with resistance to carbapenems and other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR, phenotypic detection, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the carbapenemase genes.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo biosynthesis of terpene nucleosides provides unique chemical markers of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 1-tuberculosinyladenosine (1-TbAd) and its isomer N6-tuberculosinyladenosine (N6-TbAd) as unique chemical markers of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection. These compounds are produced through the biosynthetic pathway involving Rv3377c and Rv3378c, which are essential for 1-TbAd synthesis.
full_output.methodology: The study uses lipidomics, mass spectrometry, and NMR spectroscopy to characterize the biosynthesis and structure of 1-TbAd and N6-TbAd.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a PCR-ELISA method for detecting shiga toxin genes (stx1 and stx2) in clinical samples, demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR-ELISA to detect stx1 and stx2 genes in clinical isolates of Shigella dysenteriae and E. coli O157:H7.

full_output.paper_title: Two Routes to Genetic Suppression of RNA Trimethylguanosine Cap Deficiency via C-Terminal Truncation of U1 snRNP Subunit Snp1 or Overexpression of RNA Polymerase Subunit Rpo26.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified RPO26 and RPO31 as dosage suppressors of tgs1Δ cold sensitivity in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, demonstrating that overexpression of these genes can restore growth at low temperatures.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, plasmid construction, and growth assays were used to identify and validate the suppressor roles of RPO26 and RPO31.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Genotypic and Phenotypic Analysis of Cronobacter Species Cultured from Four Powdered Infant Formula Production Facilities: Indication of Pathoadaptation along the Food Chain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Cronobacter sakazakii as the dominant species in powdered infant formula production environments, highlighting differences in phenotypic traits such as biofilm formation and motility between sequence types ST-1 and ST-4.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular subtyping methods including PFGE, MLST, and DNA microarray analysis to characterize Cronobacter isolates from powdered infant formula production facilities and clinical sources.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution and Characterization of Salmonella enterica Isolates from Irrigation Ponds in the Southeastern United States.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance in Salmonella enterica isolates from irrigation ponds, with 98.9% resistant to streptomycin and 20% being multidrug resistant.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing and rep-PCR genetic diversity analysis were used to characterize Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Recent Emergence of Escherichia coli with Cephalosporin Resistance Conferred by blaCTX-M on Washington State Dairy Farms

blaCTX-M.evidence_note: The paper states that blaCTX-M confers resistance to ceftiofur in E. coli.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of Escherichia coli strains carrying the blaCTX-M gene, which confers resistance to cephalosporins, particularly ceftiofur, in Washington State dairy farms.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and susceptibility testing to detect blaCTX-M genes and assess resistance in E. coli isolates from dairy cattle.

full_output.paper_title: VirR-Mediated Resistance of Listeria monocytogenes against Food Antimicrobials and Cross-Protection Induced by Exposure to Organic Acid Salts.

dltABCD.validation_method: mutant analysis and membrane integrity assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies dltABCD and mprF as key genes involved in VirR-mediated resistance of Listeria monocytogenes against food antimicrobials such as nisin, lauric arginate, and epsilon-polylysine.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, membrane integrity assay, and survival assays were used to evaluate the role of VirR-regulated genes in antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial-resistant Escherichia coli and extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli (ExPEC) in public restrooms, highlighting the potential for human fecal contamination and the risk of transmission.
full_output.methodology: Environmental sampling and culturing of E. coli from public restrooms, followed by virulence genotyping, phylogenetic analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli in water sources and the Yamuna River in Mathura, India, highlighting the presence of resistance against multiple antibiotics including tetracycline, streptomycin, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing via disc diffusion method was conducted on E. coli isolates from water samples.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity of Essential Oils and Their Isolated Constituents against Cariogenic Bacteria: A Systematic Review.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the antibacterial activity of essential oils (EOs) and their isolated constituents against cariogenic bacteria, highlighting their potential for use in dental formulations. Key findings include the strong antibacterial activity of several EOs against Streptococcus mutans, Streptococcus sobrinus, Streptococcus sanguinis, Streptococcus salivarius, and Lactobacillus species.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted a systematic review of in vitro and in vivo studies, analyzing the antibacterial efficacy of EOs and their isolated compounds against cariogenic bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Induced autoprocessing of the cytopathic Makes caterpillars floppy-like effector domain of the Vibrio vulnificus MARTX toxin.
Antimicrobial resistance and management of invasive Salmonella disease.

gyrA.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the rise of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Salmonella isolates, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, highlighting resistance mechanisms such as mutations in gyrA conferring fluoroquinolone resistance and the presence of beta-lactamase genes like blaCTX-M-15 and blaOXA-1 on plasmids. It emphasizes the challenges in treating invasive Salmonella infections due to increasing resistance to antibiotics like ceftriaxone and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews literature on antimicrobial resistance in invasive Salmonella infections, focusing on molecular mechanisms and clinical implications.

full_output.paper_title: Knockout of the adp gene related with colonization in Bacillus nematocida B16 using customized transcription activator-like effectors nucleases.

full_output.methodology: TALEN-mediated gene knockout and complementation experiments, PCR, Sanger sequencing, and bioassays were used to analyze the role of the adp gene in colonization and pathogenicity.

full_output.paper_title: Activation of the silent secondary metabolite production by introducing neomycin-resistance in a marine-derived Penicillium purpurogenum G59.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that introducing neomycin-resistance in Penicillium purpurogenum G59 activates the production of bioactive secondary metabolites, including curvularin, citrinin, penicitrinone A, erythro-23-O-methylneocyclocitrinol, and 22E-7α-methoxy-5α,6α-epoxyergosta-8(14),22-dien-3β-ol.
full_output.methodology: The study used neomycin and DMSO to induce resistance in P. purpurogenum G59, followed by bioassays and chromatographic analyses to identify new secondary metabolites.

full_output.paper_title: Curcumin rescues Caenorhabditis elegans from a Burkholderia pseudomallei infection.

curcumin.mechanism: inhibits lipase, protease and biofilm formation

full_output.key_findings: Curcumin was identified as a potential anti-infective agent that extends the survival of C. elegans infected with B. pseudomallei without reducing bacterial viability.
full_output.methodology: Natural product screening using a C. elegans-B. pseudomallei infection model, disc diffusion, and broth microdilution assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed PLGA microparticles loaded with ceftiofur (PLGA-cef) for sustained release and evaluated its in vivo efficacy against Salmonella Typhimurium in rats.
full_output.methodology: Formulation of PLGA-cef microparticles, in vitro release studies, in vivo pharmacokinetic and efficacy evaluations, and toxicological assessments.

full_output.methodology: The modified PR-PCR method was developed using a ddNTP-blocked primer and a mixture of Taq DNA polymerase and high-fidelity DNA polymerase. The method was validated through PCR amplification, gel electrophoresis, and sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first occurrence of Clostridium difficile NAP1/027 in a Mexican hospital, highlighting the presence of toxin genes tcdA, tcdB, cdtA, and cdtB, along with an 18-bp deletion in the tcdC gene, which is associated with increased toxin production.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-Encoded Pgp5 Is a Significant Contributor to Chlamydia muridarum Induction of Hydrosalpinx.

pgp5.notes: Deficiency in Pgp5 reduces hydrosalpinx induction.

full_output.key_findings: Pgp5 deficiency in Chlamydia muridarum significantly reduces hydrosalpinx induction in mice, indicating Pgp5's role as a plasmid-encoded virulence factor.
full_output.methodology: Mouse infection experiments, plaque assays, and cytokine profiling were used to assess the impact of Pgp5 deficiency on C. muridarum pathogenicity.

full_output.paper_title: Regulation by SoxR of mfsA, Which Encodes a Major Facilitator Protein Involved in Paraquat Resistance in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.

mfsA.validation_method: Gene deletion and complementation experiments showing increased susceptibility to paraquat in the mutant

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mfsA as a major facilitator superfamily efflux pump that contributes to paraquat resistance in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, regulated by the SoxR transcriptional regulator.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, qRT-PCR, and electrophoretic mobility shift assays were used to investigate the role of mfsA in paraquat resistance and its regulation by SoxR.

full_output.paper_title: Proteomic Investigation of the Response of Enterococcus faecalis V583 when Cultivated in Urine.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several secreted proteins in Enterococcus faecalis V583 when cultivated in urine, including EF0577, EF2076, EF0063, EF3106, EF0764, EF3054, and EF1550, which are involved in metal transport, adhesion, and other cellular processes.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic polymorphisms of dihydropyrimidinase in a Japanese patient with capecitabine-induced toxicity.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two DPYS gene mutations, c.1001A>G (p.Gln334Arg) and c.1393C>T (p.Arg465Ter), which are associated with capecitabine-induced toxicity due to decreased dihydropyrimidinase activity.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis of the DPYS gene through sequencing and evaluation of urinary pyrimidine levels.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of the gram-negative bacteria isolated from septicemia in Children's Medical Center, Tehran, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance among gram-negative bacteria isolated from bloodstream infections in children, including Pseudomonas species, Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella spp., Escherichia coli, and Salmonella spp.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation and conformational analysis of fluorinated nucleoside antibiotics targeting siderophore biosynthesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated fluorinated nucleoside antibiotics targeting siderophore biosynthesis, focusing on the conformational analysis and biochemical evaluation of SAL-AMS analogs. The research highlighted the importance of fluorination in enhancing the biological activity and pharmacokinetic properties of these compounds.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and conformational analysis of fluorinated nucleoside derivatives of SAL-AMS, along with biochemical and antibacterial evaluations.

full_output.paper_title: Simultaneous Identification of Potential Pathogenicity Factors of Mycoplasma agalactiae in the Natural Ovine Host by Negative Selection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies seven genes, including hypothetical proteins, involved in the colonization and survival of Mycoplasma agalactiae in the natural ovine host. These genes include MAG1050, MAG2540, MAG3390, uhpT, eutD, adhT, and MAG4460.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a transposon mutant library and negative selection through intramammary infection in sheep to identify genes critical for M. agalactiae pathogenicity.

full_output.paper_title: H-NS Silencing of the Salmonella Pathogenicity Island 6-Encoded Type VI Secretion System Limits Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhimurium Interbacterial Killing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the H-NS protein silences the expression of the Salmonella pathogenicity island 6 (SPI-6)-encoded type VI secretion system (T6SS) in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium. Derepression of the T6SS leads to the assembly of dynamic sheath-like structures and interbacterial intoxication.
full_output.methodology: The study uses chromosomal reporter fusions, electrophoretic mobility shift assays, DNase footprinting, and fluorescence microscopy to investigate the regulation and function of the T6SS.

full_output.paper_title: The Pseudomonas aeruginosa PA14 ABC Transporter NppA1A2BCD Is Required for Uptake of Peptidyl Nucleoside Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the Pseudomonas aeruginosa PA14 ABC transporter NppA1A2BCD as necessary for the uptake of peptidyl nucleoside antibiotics, including microcin C, pacidamycin, blasticidin S, and albomycin.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial strain construction, growth assays, and antimicrobial susceptibility tests to analyze the role of the NppA1A2BCD transporter in antibiotic uptake.

full_output.paper_title: Coculture of Staphylococcus aureus with Pseudomonas aeruginosa Drives S. aureus towards Fermentative Metabolism and Reduced Viability in a Cystic Fibrosis Model.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that P. aeruginosa drives S. aureus towards fermentative metabolism and reduces its viability through the production of HQNO and siderophores, which induce fermentation gene expression in S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro coculture systems, RNA-seq, qRT-PCR, and HPLC to analyze gene expression and metabolic changes in S. aureus during coculture with P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Iron Depletion Enhances Production of Antimicrobials by Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: Iron depletion enhances antimicrobial activity of Pseudomonas aeruginosa against Staphylococcus aureus, and this activity is mediated by the production of 2-alkyl-4(1H)-quinolones (AQs).
full_output.methodology: Coculture assays, transwell growth systems, TLC, and UPLC-MS/MS were used to analyze antimicrobial activity and AQ production.

full_output.paper_title: Susceptibility trends and molecular characterization of Gram-negative bacilli associated with urinary tract and intra-abdominal infections in Jordan and Lebanon: SMART 2011-2013.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high rates of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) production among Gram-negative bacilli, particularly CTX-M-15, SHV-12, OXA-48, NDM-1, and KPC-2, which confer resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics and carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization, susceptibility testing, and analysis of beta-lactamase genes in Gram-negative isolates from urinary tract and intra-abdominal infections.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic analyses of penicillin binding protein determinants in multidrug-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae serogroup 19 CC320/271 clone with high-level resistance to third-generation cephalosporins.

full_output.paper_title: Silver oxynitrate, an unexplored silver compound with antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that silver oxynitrate (Ag7NO11) exhibits potent antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity against various bacterial and fungal strains, including multidrug-resistant pathogens such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Candida species.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity of silver oxynitrate through minimum biofilm eradication concentration (MBEC) assays, live/dead staining, and crystal violet assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic-resistant vibrios in farmed shrimp.

full_output.paper_title: Francisella tularensis Subtype A.II Genomic Plasticity in Comparison with Subtype A.I.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies extensive genomic variations between Francisella tularensis subtype A.II strain W4114 and A.I strains, including numerous nucleotide substitutions, insertions, deletions, and chromosomal rearrangements, suggesting genomic plasticity and potential implications for virulence and environmental adaptation.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, whole genome mapping, and comparative genomic analyses were employed to investigate the genomic differences between F. tularensis A.II and A.I strains.

full_output.paper_title: GAPDHs Influence Plant Immune Responses and Autophagy
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that GAPDHs, particularly GAPA1 and GAPC1, play roles in plant immune responses and autophagy. Knockout lines of these genes showed enhanced disease resistance, increased intracellular ROS, and constitutive autophagy. GAPC1 was found to localize to various subcellular compartments and respond to immune signals.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic knockout lines, enzymatic activity assays, confocal microscopy, and molecular biology techniques to investigate the roles of GAPDHs in plant immunity and autophagy.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular and Phenotypic Characterization of Aerococcus viridans Associated with Subclinical Bovine Mastitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized 60 Aerococcus viridans isolates from subclinical bovine mastitis, highlighting their resistance to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, streptomycin, tetracycline, and clindamycin, with notable resistance patterns observed.
full_output.methodology: The study employed 16S rRNA gene sequencing, PFGE, RAPD, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Structural Variabilities in β-Lactamase (blaA) of Different Biovars of Yersinia enterocolitica: Implications for β-Lactam Antibiotic and β-Lactamase Inhibitor Susceptibilities.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified structural variabilities in the blaA gene of Yersinia enterocolitica biovars, which affect the susceptibility to β-lactam antibiotics and β-lactamase inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Loss of Microbiota-Mediated Colonization Resistance to Clostridium difficile Infection With Oral Vancomycin Compared With Metronidazole.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that oral vancomycin significantly disrupts the intestinal microbiota, leading to prolonged loss of colonization resistance to Clostridium difficile infection and increased susceptibility to other nosocomial pathogens such as vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus, carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli. Metronidazole also disrupts the microbiota but to a lesser extent.
full_output.methodology: The study used mouse models to investigate the effects of metronidazole and vancomycin on intestinal microbiota and colonization resistance to Clostridium difficile and other pathogens.

full_output.methodology: Chemical mutagenesis, whole-genome sequencing, and genetic crosses were used to identify and characterize mutations affecting F-actin assembly and Golgi redistribution in Chlamydia trachomatis.

full_output.paper_title: The Clostridium difficile Protease Cwp84 Modulates both Biofilm Formation and Cell-Surface Properties.

full_output.methodology: The study used genetic manipulation, biofilm assays, proteomic analysis, and microscopy techniques to investigate the role of Cwp84 in biofilm formation and cell-surface properties of C. difficile.

full_output.paper_title: Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans QseBC is activated by catecholamines and iron and regulates genes encoding proteins associated with anaerobic respiration and metabolism.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Staphylococcus aureus Isolated from Non-Native Patients with Skin and Soft Tissue Infections in Shanghai.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified differences in the molecular epidemiology of Staphylococcus aureus isolates from non-native and native patients with skin and soft tissue infections, including variations in the prevalence of specific virulence factors such as lukS/F-PV, seg, and sei.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Enterotoxin-Producing Escherichia coli Collected in 2011-2012, Russia.

full_output.paper_title: Enterobacteriaceae isolates from the oral cavity of workers in a Brazilian oncology hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Enterobacteriaceae isolates from the oral cavity of hospital workers, with a significant proportion showing resistance to β-lactam antibiotics. full_output.key_findings: MG428 is a master regulator of recombination in Mycoplasma genitalium, controlling the expression of genes involved in homologous recombination and affecting genetic diversity.

full_output.paper_title: The effect of imipenem and diffusible signaling factors on the secretion of outer membrane vesicles and associated Ax21 proteins in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two Ax21 homologs (Smlt0387 and Smlt0184) and two beta-lactamases (Smlt2667 and Smlt3722) in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia that are secreted in outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) in response to imipenem and diffusible signaling factors.
