full_output.paper_title: A Computational Approach towards the Understanding of Plasmodium falciparum Multidrug Resistance Protein 1.

pfmdr1.validation_method: molecular docking simulations and analysis of binding affinities

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes PfMDR1 as an ATP-binding cassette transporter involved in multidrug resistance in Plasmodium falciparum, identifying its role in reducing drug susceptibility through substrate transport mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Computational modeling, molecular docking, and structural analysis of PfMDR1 interactions with antimalarial drugs.

full_output.paper_title: Structural Basis for Different Substrate Profiles of Two Closely Related Class D β-Lactamases and Their Inhibition by Halogens.

blaOXA-163.validation_method: enzyme kinetic analysis, x-ray crystallography, inhibition assays

blaOXA-48.validation_method: enzyme kinetic analysis, x-ray crystallography, inhibition assays

blaOXA-10.validation_method: protein expression and purification, enzyme kinetic studies

full_output.key_findings: OXA-163 and OXA-48 are class D β-lactamases with distinct substrate profiles. OXA-163 hydrolyzes ceftazidime, whereas OXA-48 preferentially hydrolyzes carbapenems. Structural differences, including a four-amino acid deletion and an S212D substitution, account for the altered substrate specificity. Iodide inhibits both enzymes by altering active site residues and preventing lysine carboxylation.
full_output.methodology: Enzyme kinetic analysis, x-ray crystallography, molecular docking, and inhibition assays were used to characterize the substrate profiles and mechanisms of action of OXA-163, OXA-48, and OXA-10.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Evaluation of Sloppy Molecular Beacon and Dual-Labeled Probe Melting Temperature Assays to Identify Mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis Resulting in Rifampin, Fluoroquinolone and Aminoglycoside Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study compares the performance of Sloppy Molecular Beacon (SMB) and Dual-labeled probe (DLP) melting temperature assays for detecting mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis that confer resistance to rifampin, fluoroquinolones, and aminoglycosides. The SMB assay showed superior sensitivity and specificity for detecting these mutations compared to the DLP assay.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized melting temperature assays to detect mutations in the rpoB, gyrA, rrs, and eis genes of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Essential Role of the ESX-5 Secretion System in Outer Membrane Permeability of Pathogenic Mycobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The ESX-5 secretion system is essential for the growth of Mycobacterium marinum and Mycobacterium bovis. The essentiality of ESX-5 can be rescued by increasing outer membrane permeability, suggesting that ESX-5 substrates are involved in nutrient uptake.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, and conditional expression experiments were used to determine the essentiality of ESX-5 components.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a novel antimicrobial screening system targeting the pyoverdine-mediated iron acquisition system and xenobiotic efflux pumps.

oprM.encodes: outer membrane subunit of the MexAB-OprM xenobiotic efflux pump
oprM.validation_method: antibiotic susceptibility test under iron depleted and replete conditions

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a screening system targeting the iron acquisition system and the MexAB-OprM efflux pump in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The oprM gene was placed downstream of the fpvA gene, allowing monitoring of iron acquisition system activity through antibiotic susceptibility. A compound, YH001, was identified that inhibits the MexAB-OprM efflux pump, enhancing the efficacy of aztreonam.
full_output.methodology: Construction of a recombinant strain with oprM under control of the iron acquisition system, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and chemical library screening.

full_output.paper_title: Mutational Analysis of the Chlamydia muridarum Plasticity Zone.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that PZ genes in C. muridarum are transcribed but are not essential for infection of the murine genital tract. Nonsense mutations in PZ genes resulted in reduced cytotoxicity and moderate attenuation in some cases, but did not significantly affect IFN-γ resistance or overall virulence.
full_output.methodology: Reverse genetics, TILLING, IFU assays, and animal infection models were used to analyze PZ gene function.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of SlpB, a Cytotoxic Protease from Serratia marcescens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SlpB as a new cytotoxic protease from Serratia marcescens, demonstrating its role in secreted protease activity and cytotoxicity to human corneal epithelial cells.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, protease activity assays, and cytotoxicity tests were conducted to characterize SlpB.

full_output.paper_title: Intraspecies Competition in Serratia marcescens Is Mediated by Type VI-Secreted Rhs Effectors and a Conserved Effector-Associated Accessory Protein.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Rhs1 and Rhs2 as T6SS-delivered antibacterial toxins in Serratia marcescens, with Rhs2-CT exhibiting DNase activity. An accessory protein, EagR1, is essential for Rhs1-mediated antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: Coculture assays, mutational analysis, and expression studies in E. coli were used to validate the antibacterial activity of Rhs1, Rhs2, and EagR1.

full_output.paper_title: A relA-dependent regulatory cascade for auto-induction of microbisporicin production in Microbispora corallina.

relA.notes: deletion mutant shows reduced microbisporicin production

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mibR, mibX, and mibEF as critical components in the regulation and immunity of microbisporicin production in Microbispora corallina, highlighting their roles in transcriptional activation and cellular defense mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized transcriptional fusions, gene cloning, and mutant analysis to investigate the regulatory pathways and immunity mechanisms of microbisporicin production.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of Aminoglycoside Acetyltransferase Resistance Enzymes by Metal Salts
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several aminoglycoside acetyltransferase resistance enzymes (AACs) and evaluates the inhibitory effects of various metal salts on their activity. It shows that copper, zinc, and cadmium salts can inhibit these enzymes, reducing the minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of aminoglycosides against bacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used UV-Vis assays, TLC experiments, and MIC determinations to evaluate the inhibitory effects of metal salts on AACs and their impact on aminoglycoside resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations associated with reduced surotomycin susceptibility in Clostridium difficile and Enterococcus species.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in genes such as cls, fabK, ftsH2, padR, mprF2, drmA, EF0797, and EF1367 associated with reduced surotomycin susceptibility in Clostridium difficile and Enterococcus species.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and Sanger sequencing were used to identify mutations in surotomycin-passaged strains.

full_output.paper_title: Metronidazole- and Carbapenem-Resistant Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron Isolated in Rochester, Minnesota, in 2014.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in a metronidazole- and carbapenem-resistant Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron isolate, including nimD, cat, tetX, tetQ, ermF, and a novel beta-lactamase gene.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and determine resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: A mutation of RNA polymerase β′ subunit (RpoC) converts heterogeneously vancomycin-intermediate Staphylococcus aureus (hVISA) into "slow VISA".

rpoC.notes: Mutations in the rpoC gene were associated with the sVISA phenotype.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified that a mutation in the rpoC gene (P440L) contributes to the development of the slow VISA (sVISA) phenotype in Staphylococcus aureus, which is characterized by increased vancomycin resistance and prolonged doubling time. Additional mutations in rpoC, such as F652L, D645E, R646L, and F652I, were found in revertant strains and were considered compensatory or complementary to the P440L mutation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized whole-genome sequencing, complementation experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to analyze the effects of rpoC mutations on vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Structural basis of RND-type multidrug exporters.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the structural basis of RND-type multidrug exporters, focusing on AcrAB-TolC and MexAB-OprM, highlighting their role in multidrug resistance through efflux mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis and functional studies of RND-type multidrug exporters.

full_output.paper_title: Group Selection and Contribution of Minority Variants during Virus Adaptation Determines Virus Fitness and Phenotype.

VP3.notes: Mutations in VP3 were found to contribute to virus fitness in A549 cells.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several mutations in the VP3 capsid protein, including E76G, N63Y, D138G, and Q234K, which contributed to increased fitness of Coxsackie virus B3 in A549 cells. These mutations were shown to interact synergistically to enhance viral fitness.
full_output.methodology: Deep sequencing, reverse genetics, and fitness assays were used to analyze viral adaptation and identify mutations contributing to increased fitness in A549 cells.

full_output.paper_title: Disruption of Transcriptional Coactivator Sub1 Leads to Genome-Wide Re-distribution of Clustered Mutations Induced by APOBEC in Active Yeast Genes.

SUB1.notes: Disruption of the SUB1 gene reduces APOBEC-induced mutagenesis.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: increased mutation densities in promoter/5'-UTR regions

sub1.notes: Disruption of sub1 leads to increased mutation densities in promoter/5'-UTR regions.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that disruption of the transcription initiation factor Sub1 significantly reduces APOBEC-induced mutagenesis, indicating its role in protecting ssDNA from deamination.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of yeast mutants, mutagenesis experiments, and RNA sequencing to analyze transcriptional profiles.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that the primary resistance of Helicobacter pylori to clarithromycin, metronidazole, amoxicillin, and tetracycline remained low in Taiwan, while levofloxacin resistance increased significantly. The low resistance rates were attributed to reduced antibiotic consumption following a national policy, but rising levofloxacin resistance was linked to increased fluoroquinolone use.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antibiotic resistance in H. pylori strains from treatment-naïve and treatment-failure cases using agar dilution tests and evaluated antibiotic consumption through the Taiwan National Health Insurance database.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative genome analysis of rice-pathogenic Burkholderia provides insight into capacity to adapt to different environments and hosts.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the comparative genome analysis of rice-pathogenic Burkholderia species, identifying unique genes involved in toxin production and CRISPR-mediated immune systems. It highlighted the diversity of secretion systems, QS systems, and toxin production genes among the species.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome shotgun sequencing, comparative genomics, pan-genome analysis, and CRISPR-Cas system analysis were employed.

full_output.paper_title: Cross-species chimeras reveal BamA POTRA and β-barrel domains must be fine-tuned for efficient OMP insertion.

BamA.encodes: outer membrane protein insertion machine component
BamA.notes: Mutations at the POTRA-β-barrel interface improve function of BamA chimeras
BamA.evidence_note: The paper describes mutations in BamA that improve the function of chimeric proteins, but does not explicitly state that these mutations confer resistance to antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the BamA protein that enhance the functionality of chimeric constructs, allowing them to rescue BamA depletion in E. coli. These mutations occur in the POTRA 5 domain and the β-barrel domain of BamA, improving interactions between these regions.
full_output.methodology: The study uses genetic engineering, western blotting, and growth assays to analyze the functionality of BamA chimeras and identify beneficial mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Expression of heterologous sigma factors enables functional screening of metagenomic and heterologous genomic libraries.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that expressing the Lpl rpoD sigma factor in E. coli enhances the recognition of heterologous promoters, enabling the functional screening of metagenomic and heterologous genomic libraries. This approach was used to identify genetic loci in L. plantarum that confer ethanol tolerance in E. coli.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized GFP-trap assays, RNA-seq, and microbial culturing techniques to evaluate promoter recognition and gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of agar dilution and broth microdilution methods to determine the disinfectant susceptibility.

qacEΔ1.encodes: SMR family small multidrug resistance protein

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the qacEΔ1 gene as a key factor in quaternary ammonium compound resistance, showing a strong association with high MICs in various bacterial species.
full_output.methodology: Agar dilution and broth microdilution methods were used to determine MICs, along with PCR amplification for gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Pattern of multiresistant to antimicrobials and heavy metal tolerance in bacteria isolated from sewage sludge samples from a composting process at a recycling plant in southern Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant bacteria in sewage sludge and compost samples, with high resistance to nitrofurantoin and β-lactams, and notable tolerance to heavy metals like copper and zinc.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial resistance was assessed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion assay, while heavy metal tolerance was determined via microdilution techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Nitric Oxide Mediates Biofilm Formation and Symbiosis in Silicibacter sp. Strain TrichCH4B.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SiliNOS as a nitric oxide synthase and SiliH-NOX as a heme-nitric oxide/oxygen binding protein in Silicibacter sp. strain TrichCH4B, highlighting their roles in NO signaling and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biochemical assays, genetic analysis, and molecular biology techniques to characterize the NO signaling pathway in Silicibacter sp. strain TrichCH4B.

full_output.paper_title: LegK2 Inhibits ARP2/3 Complex Activity to Control Actin Polymerization and Endocytic Pathway Evasion in Legionella pneumophila

mutations_found.validated_by: expression of kinase-dead variant in mammalian cells
expression of kinase-dead variant in mammalian cells

legK2.notes: Kinase-dead variants of LegK2 (K112M and K112M/D209N) fail to inhibit actin polymerization and endocytic pathway evasion.
legK2.evidence_note: The paper describes the role of LegK2 in inhibiting actin polymerization and endocytic pathway evasion, but does not provide evidence that LegK2 confers resistance to antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: LegK2, a protein kinase from Legionella pneumophila, inhibits ARP2/3 complex activity, thereby controlling actin polymerization on the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCV) and preventing fusion with late endosomes, allowing the bacteria to evade endocytic degradation.
full_output.methodology: Expression of LegK2 and its mutants in mammalian cells, immunofluorescence microscopy, and biochemical assays to assess actin polymerization and endocytic pathway evasion.

full_output.paper_title: Nordihydroguaiaretic Acid Disrupts the Antioxidant Ability of Helicobacter pylori through the Repression of SodB Activity In Vitro.

fecA1.validation_method: experimental validation through gene deletion and SodB activity measurement

sodB.validation_method: experimental validation through gene overexpression and activity measurement

full_output.key_findings: NDGA disrupts SodB activity in H. pylori by repressing intracellular Fe2+ levels via FecA1 inhibition, leading to increased H2O2 and metronidazole sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: In silico screening, intracellular Fe2+ measurement, SOD activity assay, MIC determination, and H2O2 disk assays.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and functional analysis of betaine aldehyde dehydrogenase from Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the betaine aldehyde dehydrogenase (Sa BADH) from Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating its specific activity towards betaine aldehyde and its role in osmoregulation and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Expression, purification, enzymatic activity assays, SPR, crystallography, and structural analysis.

full_output.paper_title: L-arginine destabilizes oral multi-species biofilm communities developed in human saliva.
full_output.key_findings: L-arginine monohydrochloride (LAHCl) destabilizes oral multi-species biofilms, altering their architecture and community composition without direct antimicrobial effects. It enhances the antimicrobial efficacy of cetylpyridinium chloride (CPC).
full_output.methodology: Used static microplate and controlled-flow microfluidic systems to analyze biofilm architecture, viability, and community composition.

full_output.paper_title: An Atypical Mitochondrial Carrier That Mediates Drug Action in Trypanosoma brucei.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TbMCP14 as a mitochondrial carrier protein involved in the action of choline analogs and pentamidine in Trypanosoma brucei, with its expression affecting drug susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: RNAi-mediated gene silencing and over-expression, metabolomic analysis, and mitochondrial membrane potential measurements.

full_output.paper_title: Rational design of antibiotic treatment plans: a treatment strategy for managing evolution and reversing resistance.

blaTEM-1.validation_method: growth rate measurements in presence of β-lactam antibiotics
blaTEM-1.evidence_note: The paper describes blaTEM-1 as the wild type genotype and shows that mutations in this gene confer resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.

blaTEM-50.validation_method: growth rate measurements in presence of β-lactam antibiotics

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the wild-type TEM-1 beta-lactamase and its variant TEM-50, which confers resistance to penicillins, cephalosporins, and β-lactamase inhibitors. It explores how antibiotic treatment plans can reverse resistance by targeting specific amino acid substitutions in TEM genotypes.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis was used to create 16 variant genotypes of the TEM-50 beta-lactamase, and growth rates were measured in the presence of 15 β-lactam antibiotics to assess resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: A novel ABCG-like transporter of Trypanosoma cruzi is involved in natural resistance to benznidazole.

TcABCG1.mechanism: over-expression leads to increased resistance to benznidazole
TcABCG1.validation_method: transfection studies and measurement of IC50 values

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TcABCG1, a novel ABCG-like transporter in Trypanosoma cruzi, which is over-expressed in benznidazole-resistant strains and contributes to natural resistance against the drug.
full_output.methodology: Transfection studies, real-time PCR, and IC50 measurements were used to validate the role of TcABCG1 in benznidazole resistance.
full_output.sample_size: Eight T. cruzi strains from different discrete typing units (DTUs)

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies gelE and sprE genes in Enterococcus faecalis as critical for collagen degradation and MMP9 activation, contributing to anastomotic leak.
full_output.methodology: Experimental analysis using bacterial mutants, complementation, and enzymatic assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of Escherichia coli O157:H7 in Egyptian sheep, with 8.7% of the 150 sampled animals being carriers. The investigation focused on the molecular characterization of the isolates, revealing the presence of virulence genes such as eae, stx1, stx2, and hlyA.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR for the molecular characterization of E. coli O157:H7 isolates, along with biochemical and serotyping methods for identification.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of antibiotic resistance genes of wastewater and surface water in livestock farms of Jiangsu Province, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 22 antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in wastewater and surface water samples from livestock farms in Jiangsu Province, China. Key findings include the high prevalence of sul1, sul2, and tetM, along with other ARGs such as ermB, qnrS, and aac, which were detected in all samples. The study highlights the significant presence of ARGs in aquatic environments near livestock farms, emphasizing the need for monitoring and managing antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) was used to analyze the prevalence, abundance, and distribution of 22 ARGs in wastewater and surface water samples collected from 12 livestock farms in Jiangsu Province.
full_output.sample_size: 28 samples (11 surface water samples, 17 wastewater samples)

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of an Enterococcus gallinarum Isolate Carrying a Dual vanA and vanB Cassette.

vanA.mechanism: expression of the vanA operon on plasmid pA6981

vanB.mechanism: integration of the vanB operon into the bacterial chromosome

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies an Enterococcus gallinarum isolate carrying both vanA and vanB genes, which confer high-level resistance to vancomycin and teicoplanin. The vanA gene was found on a plasmid, while the vanB gene was integrated into the chromosome.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify and characterize the vanA and vanB genes.

full_output.paper_title: EGFR Mutations and Resistance to Irreversible Pyrimidine-Based EGFR Inhibitors.

EGFR.notes: Mutations identified in EGFR that confer resistance to irreversible pyrimidine-based EGFR inhibitors.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies EGFR mutations L718Q, L844V, and C797S that confer resistance to irreversible pyrimidine-based EGFR inhibitors such as WZ4002, CO-1686, and AZD9291.
full_output.methodology: The study uses an ENU mutagenesis screen and functional testing to identify and characterize EGFR mutations that confer resistance to EGFR inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Klebsiella Pneumoniae in Septicemic Neonates with Special Reference to Extended Spectrum β-lactamase, AmpC, Metallo β-lactamase Production and Multiple Drug Resistance in Tertiary Care Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of AmpC and MBL co-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates and a high rate of multiple drug resistance (MDR) among the isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used CLSI disk method, AmpC cefoxitin screen, and imipenem, meropenem, ceftazidime disk screen for detecting β-lactamases, and Kirby-Bauer's disk diffusion method for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Crystallization of Membrane Proteins Involved in Heavy-Metal and Multidrug Efflux
full_output.key_findings: This study reports the crystallization and structural determination of several membrane proteins involved in heavy-metal and multidrug efflux, including CusC, MtrE, CmeC, CusA, CusB, and MtrD. These structures provide insights into the mechanisms of efflux-mediated antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Protein expression, purification, and crystallization followed by X-ray diffraction analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Antimycobacterial and anti-inflammatory activities of substituted chalcones focusing on an anti-tuberculosis dual treatment approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified chalcones 4 and 5 as promising antimycobacterial and anti-inflammatory agents, showing strong inhibition of NO and TNF-α production and effective growth inhibition of M. tuberculosis strains.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the anti-inflammatory and antimycobacterial effects of forty synthetic chalcones through in vitro assays, including NO and TNF-α production inhibition, MIC determination, and cytotoxicity testing.

full_output.paper_title: Global transcriptome analysis reveals small RNAs affecting Neisseria meningitidis bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 8 new sRNAs in Neisseria meningitidis that are differentially expressed under various stress conditions and are involved in regulating metabolic processes and bacterial fitness during infection.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome analysis using microarrays and validation by Northern blot and primer extension.

full_output.paper_title: Activity of Antibiotics against Mycobacterium Species Commonly Found in Laboratory Zebrafish.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antibiotic susceptibility of various Mycobacterium species isolated from zebrafish, identifying effective antibiotics for treating mycobacteriosis. It highlights variations in susceptibility among different species and strains, emphasizing the importance of species-specific treatment strategies.
full_output.methodology: The study used commercial MIC panels to assess the minimum inhibitory concentrations of antibiotics against Mycobacterium isolates from zebrafish.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus Survives with a Minimal Peptidoglycan Synthesis Machine but Sacrifices Virulence and Antibiotic Resistance.

pbp2.mechanism: bi-functional penicillin-binding protein with transpeptidase and transglycosylase activities

full_output.key_findings: The study identified that Staphylococcus aureus can survive with a minimal peptidoglycan synthesis machinery consisting of only PBP1 and PBP2, but this strain exhibits increased susceptibility to cell wall-targeting antibiotics and reduced virulence.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, gene deletion, MIC testing, and growth analysis were used to investigate the role of peptidoglycan synthesis enzymes in S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Enhanced horizontal transfer of antibiotic resistance genes in freshwater microcosms induced by an ionic liquid.

aphA.validation_method: tracking plasmid RP4 abundance via aphA gene quantification

full_output.key_findings: The ionic liquid [BMIm][PF6] enhances the horizontal transfer of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) mediated by plasmid RP4 in freshwater microcosms, leading to increased resistance to ampicillin, kanamycin, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Experimental setup involving plasmid RP4 horizontal transfer in microcosms, tracking gene abundance via qPCR, and assessing cell membrane permeability using flow cytometry.

full_output.paper_title: Coordination of peptidoglycan synthesis and outer membrane constriction during Escherichia coli cell division.
full_output.key_findings: CpoB coordinates peptidoglycan synthesis and outer membrane constriction during cell division in E. coli by interacting with PBP1B and TolA.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, biochemical assays, and fluorescence microscopy were used to investigate the role of CpoB in cell division.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular identification and functional characterization of the first Nα-acetyltransferase in plastids by global acetylome profiling.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes AtNAA70, the first organellar-localized Nα-acetyltransferase in eukaryotes, demonstrating its Nα-acetyltransferase activity towards E. coli proteins and its ability to acetylate internal lysine residues.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a combination of bioinformatics, structural modeling, subcellular localization experiments, and proteomics to identify and functionally characterize AtNAA70.

full_output.paper_title: Draft Genome Sequence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Strain E186hv of Beijing B0/W Lineage with Reduced Virulence.

katG.notes: associated with isoniazid resistance

pncA.notes: associated with pyrazinamide resistance

rpoB.notes: associated with rifampin resistance

gyrA.notes: associated with ofloxacin resistance

full_output.paper_title: Parallel evolutionary pathways to antibiotic resistance selected by biocide exposure.

ramR.notes: Mutations in ramR lead to de-repression of the AcrAB-TolC MDR efflux system.

gyrA.notes: Mutation in gyrA leads to reduced susceptibility to quinolones.

fabI.notes: Mutation in fabI leads to triclosan resistance.

rpoA.notes: Mutation in rpoA contributes to decreased susceptibility to nalidixic acid and chloramphenicol.

zur.encodes: putative regulatory protein controlling zinc uptake systems
zur.notes: Mutation in zur leads to loss of function and contributes to triclosan resistance.

full_output.key_findings: Exposure to biocides selects for antibiotic-resistant mutants with mutations in ramR, gyrA, fabI, rpoA, and zur, leading to decreased susceptibility to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing and phenotypic characterization of mutants selected after biocide exposure.

full_output.paper_title: An ace up their sleeve: a transcriptomic approach exposes the AceI efflux protein of Acinetobacter baumannii and reveals the drug efflux potential hidden in many microbial pathogens.

aceI.validation_method: biochemical approaches and fluorescence transport assays
aceI.evidence_note: The paper describes the characterization of AceI as a chlorhexidine resistance protein that functions via an active efflux mechanism. It also shows that AceI homologs from other species confer resistance to chlorhexidine, benzalkonium, acriflavine, and proflavine when expressed in E. coli.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AceI as a novel multidrug efflux pump in Acinetobacter baumannii, which provides resistance to chlorhexidine, benzalkonium, acriflavine, and proflavine. AceI is part of the PACE family of multidrug efflux systems, which are conserved in various bacterial species.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis and biochemical experiments were used to characterize AceI and its homologs.

full_output.paper_title: The prevalence of Escherichia coli strains with extended spectrum beta-lactamases isolated in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaCTX-M and blaTEM genes as the primary mechanisms of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) production in Escherichia coli isolates from Shandong Province, China. The most prevalent ESBL types were CTX-M-14 and CTX-M-15, along with TEM-1 and TEM-135.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to identify ESBL genes in E. coli isolates.

mecA.notes: Mutations in the non-penicillin-binding domain of PBP2a were associated with increased ceftaroline MICs.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the mecA gene, particularly N146K, which were associated with increased ceftaroline MICs in Staphylococcus aureus isolates, highlighting the importance of monitoring resistance mechanisms in clonal lineages ST228 and ST239.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing via broth microdilution, disc diffusion, and Etest, along with molecular characterization of mecA gene mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Eh CP5-mediated activation of α5β1 integrin induces ATP release and NLRP3 inflammasome activation
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Eh CP5 as a crucial factor in activating the NLRP3 inflammasome through α5β1 integrin, leading to ATP release and subsequent inflammasome activation. Mutations in the RGD sequence of Eh CP5 and inhibition of its cysteine protease activity prevent this process.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular biology techniques including siRNA, Western blotting, flow cytometry, and ATP measurements to investigate the role of Eh CP5 in NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, Antimicrobial and Hypoglycemic Activities of Novel N-(1-Adamantyl)carbothioamide Derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: The paper describes the synthesis and evaluation of novel N-(1-adamantyl)carbothioamide derivatives for antimicrobial and hypoglycemic activities. Compounds 5c, 5d, 5e, 6, 7, 10a, 10b, 15a, 15f, and 15g showed potent antibacterial activity against various bacterial strains, while compounds 5c, 6, 8b, 9, 14a, and 15b exhibited hypoglycemic effects in diabetic rats.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, agar disc-diffusion method for antimicrobial activity, and oral hypoglycemic activity testing in diabetic rats.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of pneumococcal colonization determinants in the stringent response pathway facilitated by genomic diversity.

SP_1645.validation_method: genetic manipulation and surface killing assay

SP_1097.validation_method: genetic manipulation and surface killing assay

mutations_found.validated_by: genetic manipulation and surface killing assay

SP_1645.evidence_note: The SP_1645:C1019T variation was shown to reduce resistance to neutrophil-killing through genetic manipulation and surface killing assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SP_1645 and SP_1097 as genes involved in the stringent response pathway that affect pneumococcal resistance to neutrophil-killing and colonization competitiveness.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, genetic manipulation, and surface killing assays were used to analyze the role of SP_1645 and SP_1097 in pneumococcal resistance and colonization.

full_output.paper_title: Yersinia enterocolitica Isolates from Wild Boars Hunted in Lower Saxony, Germany.

ail.encodes: outer membrane protein that promotes attachment and invasion
ail.validation_method: PCR detection of the chromosomal gene ail

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the ail gene in two Y. enterocolitica isolates of BT 1A, indicating potential virulence, and noted that most isolates belonged to biotype 1A, while enteropathogenic bioserotypes 4/O:3 and 2/O:9 were not identified.
full_output.methodology: PCR and molecular analysis for virulence markers, MALDI-TOF MS, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Lipid metabolism and Type VII secretion systems dominate the genome scale virulence profile of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in human dendritic cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes involved in lipid synthesis, cholesterol metabolism, and phagosomal maturation that are crucial for Mycobacterium tuberculosis survival in human dendritic cells. These include genes related to the synthesis of pDIMs, PGLs, sulfolipids, and cholesterol metabolism, as well as genes involved in the regulation of phagosomal maturation.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis and fitness analysis in human dendritic cells.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of dfrA14 in two distinct plasmids conferring trimethoprim resistance in Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae.

dfrA14.validation_method: plasmid isolation and sequencing, PCR, MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies dfrA14 in two distinct plasmids conferring trimethoprim resistance in Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae, marking the first description of this gene in the Pasteurellaceae family.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid isolation, PCR, and MIC testing were used to characterize the genetic basis of trimethoprim resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Within-host diversity of MRSA antimicrobial resistances.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified variations in antimicrobial resistance (AMR) profiles and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) among MRSA isolates from nasal carriers, highlighting the role of bacteriophages in gene transfer and the importance of sampling multiple colonies to accurately detect AMR.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 38 MRSA carriers, examining 20 colonies per patient for AMR profiles and genetic variation, along with whole-genome sequencing and phage isolation.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of two novel regulatory genes involved in pristinamycin biosynthesis and elucidation of the mechanism for AtrA-p-mediated regulation in Streptomyces pristinaespiralis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two novel regulatory genes, atrA-p and SSDG_02492, involved in pristinamycin biosynthesis in Streptomyces pristinaespiralis. AtrA-p was shown to positively regulate pristinamycin production by activating the transcription of spbR and papR5, while SSDG_02492, an orphan histidine kinase, was found to be essential for normal pristinamycin production.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized transposon mutagenesis, gene deletion, and complementation experiments, along with transcriptional analysis and electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSAs) to investigate the roles of the identified genes in pristinamycin biosynthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence and spread of O16-ST131 and O25b-ST131 clones among faecal CTX-M-producing Escherichia coli in healthy individuals in Hunan Province, China.

gyrA.notes: gyrA 1A

parC.notes: parC 1b

full_output.key_findings: The study identified O16-ST131 and O25b-ST131 clones among faecal CTX-M-producing E. coli in healthy individuals in Hunan Province, China. It found that O25b-ST131 isolates had higher resistance to ciprofloxacin compared to O16-ST131. Mutations in gyrA and parC were associated with ciprofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR analysis, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and PFGE analysis were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity and mutagenesis of sponge-associated Pseudomonas fluorescens H41.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pvdL and pvdD genes involved in the biosynthesis of pyoverdine, which are linked to the antimicrobial activity of Pseudomonas fluorescens H41.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis and functional screening of mutants to identify genes associated with antimicrobial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Global in vitro activity of tigecycline and comparator agents: Tigecycline Evaluation and Surveillance Trial 2004-2013.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of tigecycline and other antimicrobial agents against various pathogens, highlighting trends in susceptibility and resistance over time.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility was determined using CLSI guidelines, with MICs calculated via broth microdilution.

full_output.paper_title: Structural basis for dynamic mechanism of nitrate/nitrite antiport by NarK.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: did not restore the nitrate-transport activity to the same level as that of wild-type NarK

NarK.notes: Mutants analyzed show loss of nitrate-uptake activity or complementation.
NarK.evidence_note: The paper describes the structural and functional analysis of NarK, demonstrating its role as a nitrate/nitrite antiporter. Mutations in NarK, such as G408A, G418A, G363A, G365A, G367A, G268A, F147A, F267A, R89K, Y263F, and R305K, were shown to affect nitrate-uptake activity or complementation, indicating their impact on the function of NarK.

full_output.key_findings: NarK is a nitrate/nitrite antiporter, and mutations in specific glycine residues and substrate-binding site residues significantly affect its nitrate-uptake activity.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, mutational analysis, and MD simulations were used to determine the structural and functional properties of NarK.

full_output.paper_title: Mutated and hypermutated genes of persistent measles viruses which caused lethal human brain diseases.

mutations_found.nucleotide_position: near the end of the open reading frame
mutations_found.effect_on_function: most likely compromising efficient viral budding
mutations_found.validated_by: sequencing and analysis of persistent MV strains

F.notes: The F protein's intracellular domain was partially deleted in three of four persistent viruses, potentially affecting viral budding.

mutations_found.validated_by: sequencing of the H gene of cell line IP-3-Ca

H.notes: The H protein of the SSPE cell line showed a cluster of 16 amino acid changes, potentially affecting hemadsorption.

full_output.key_findings: Persistent measles viruses exhibit mutations in the F and H genes, including partial deletions in the F protein's intracellular domain and hypermutations in the H gene, which may affect viral budding and hemadsorption.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of MV genes from cell lines and brain tissue, analysis of mutations in persistent and lytic strains.
full_output.sample_size: four persistent MV strains and seven persistent MV strains

full_output.paper_title: Peptide macrocyclization by a bifunctional endoprotease.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a bifunctional endoprotease from jack bean (CeAEP1) capable of performing both cleavage and intramolecular transpeptidation to produce the macrocyclic peptide SFTI-1. This enzyme demonstrates the ability to excise and macrocycle SFTI-1 from its precursor, highlighting the role of AEPs in the biosynthesis of cyclic peptides in plants.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in situ and in vitro assays, along with recombinant expression of AEPs, to investigate the enzymatic activity of AEPs in the biosynthesis of SFTI-1.

full_output.paper_title: PqsE of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Acts as Pathway-Specific Thioesterase in the Biosynthesis of Alkylquinolone Signaling Molecules.

pqsE.validation_method: in vitro reconstitution of biosynthetic pathway and enzyme assays

full_output.key_findings: PqsE acts as a pathway-specific thioesterase in the biosynthesis of alkylquinolone signaling molecules in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, hydrolyzing the intermediate 2-aminobenzoylacetyl-CoA to form 2-aminobenzoylacetate.
full_output.methodology: In vitro reconstitution of biosynthetic pathway, enzyme assays, and analysis of mutant strains.

full_output.paper_title: Four decades of transmission of a multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis outbreak strain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis that confer resistance to multiple antibiotics, including isoniazid, streptomycin, rifampicin, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, kanamycin, and fluoroquinolones. These mutations were found in a multidrug-resistant outbreak strain that has been circulating for over four decades.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of 252 clinical isolates, phylogenetic analysis, and drug susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance mutations and track the evolution of the outbreak strain.

full_output.paper_title: The Amino Acid Arginine 210 of the Response Regulator HrpG of Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri Is Required for HrpG Function in Virulence.

mutations_found.validated_by: plant infiltration assays, RT-qPCR, EMSA, in vitro transcription assays

hrpG.evidence_note: The paper describes a point mutation (R210C) in the response regulator HrpG of Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri, which leads to a dominant negative effect, reducing virulence and impairing the ability to trigger HR in non-host plants. The mutation does not affect DNA binding but impairs transcriptional activation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a point mutation (R210C) in the response regulator HrpG of Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri, which significantly reduces virulence and the ability to induce hypersensitive response (HR) in non-host plants.
full_output.methodology: Plant infiltration assays, RT-qPCR, EMSA, in vitro transcription assays, and protein purification techniques were used to investigate the effects of the R210C mutation in HrpG.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and prognosis of coagulase-negative staphylococcal endocarditis: impact of vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the importance of vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) in predicting mortality in coagulase-negative staphylococcal (CoNS) infective endocarditis (IE). Patients with CoNS isolates having vancomycin MICs ≥2 μg/mL had significantly higher mortality rates compared to those with lower MICs.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the epidemiology, antibiotic susceptibility profiles, and outcomes of 103 patients with CoNS IE, focusing on the impact of vancomycin MIC on mortality.

full_output.paper_title: Atypical Role for PhoU in Mutagenic Break Repair under Stress in Escherichia coli.

phoU.notes: PhoU mutations lead to reduced mutagenic break repair (MBR) in E. coli.

full_output.key_findings: PhoU mutations lead to reduced mutagenic break repair (MBR) in E. coli, indicating a novel role for PhoU in regulating mutagenesis under stress.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screens, stress-induced Lac-reversion assays, whole-genome sequencing, and mutagenesis assays.

full_output.paper_title: A mass spectrometry-based assay for improved quantitative measurements of efflux pump inhibition.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a mass spectrometry-based assay to measure efflux pump inhibition, demonstrating that flavonoids like quercetin, apigenin, and others exhibit efflux pump inhibitory activity, with IC50 values ranging from 19 to 75 μg/mL. The method overcame issues of optical interference seen in fluorescence-based assays.
full_output.methodology: The study used a mass spectrometry-based assay to measure efflux pump inhibition, comparing results with traditional fluorescence-based methods and validating with known efflux pump inhibitors like piperine and CCCP.

full_output.paper_title: What It Takes to Be a Pseudomonas aeruginosa? The Core Genome of the Opportunistic Pathogen Updated.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes in the core genome of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, including ampC, mexAB-oprM, mexCD-oprJ, mexXY, mexEF-oprN, gyrA, gyrB, parC, and parE, which contribute to resistance against beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, tetracyclines, chloramphenicol, and trimethoprim.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and analysis of 17 Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains to determine the core genome and identify AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogeographical analysis of the dominant multidrug-resistant H58 clade of Salmonella Typhi identifies inter- and intracontinental transmission events.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes multidrug-resistant (MDR) genes and mutations in the H58 clade of Salmonella Typhi, highlighting the role of specific resistance genes and quinolone resistance mutations in the spread of MDR typhoid.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis of 1,832 S. Typhi isolates to identify resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies point mutations in the quinolone resistance determining region (QRDR) of the gyrA gene in Salmonella Typhi isolates from India, which are associated with increased minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of fluoroquinolones.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a sequential transfection method in B. bovis using blasticidin-S/deaminase (bsd) and WR99210/human dihydrofolate reductase (hdhfr) selection systems. This method enabled the complementation of the Bbtpx-1 gene, restoring resistance to nitrosative stress in Bbtpx-1 knockout parasites.
full_output.methodology: Transfection with plasmids carrying bsd and hdhfr genes, followed by drug selection and verification through PCR, sequencing, and phenotypic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial activity and safety evaluation of Enterococcus faecium KQ 2.6 isolated from peacock feces.
full_output.key_findings: E. faecium KQ 2.6 was found to be resistant to vancomycin and polymyxin B, while lacking several virulence genes such as gelE, esp, asa1, cylA, efaA, and hyl.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity was assessed using agar well diffusion and disk diffusion tests, and virulence genes were detected via PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Importance of Real-Time Assays To Distinguish Multidrug Efflux Pump-Inhibiting and Outer Membrane-Destabilizing Activities in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that PAβN primarily functions as an inhibitor of the AcrAB and AcrEF multidrug efflux pumps in Escherichia coli, distinguishing its effect from outer membrane destabilization.
full_output.methodology: MIC assays, real-time efflux assays, and nitrocefin hydrolysis assays were used to evaluate the effects of PAβN on efflux pump activity and outer membrane integrity.

full_output.paper_title: Bacillus anthracis Overcomes an Amino Acid Auxotrophy by Cleaving Host Serum Proteins.
full_output.key_findings: Bacillus anthracis utilizes the secreted metalloprotease InhA1 to cleave host serum proteins, including hemoglobin and serum albumin, to obtain essential amino acids like valine, overcoming amino acid auxotrophy.
full_output.methodology: Defined medium (BSM) and proteolysis assays were used to study the role of InhA1 in cleaving host serum proteins for amino acid acquisition.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility of travel-related Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi isolates detected in Switzerland (2002-2013) and molecular characterization of quinolone resistant isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified qnrS1 as a plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance gene in Salmonella Typhi isolates and characterized mutations in gyrA and parC associated with quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and disk diffusion susceptibility testing were used to analyze antimicrobial resistance in Salmonella Typhi isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial susceptibility profile of listeria species from ready-to-eat foods of animal origin in Gondar Town, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 24 (6.25%) of the food samples contained Listeria monocytogenes, with 16 (66.7%) showing resistance to penicillin, 12 (50%) to nalidixic acid, 9 (37.5%) to tetracycline, and 4 (16.6%) to chloramphenicol. Four (16.7%) isolates were multidrug resistant. All isolates were sensitive to amoxicillin, cephalothin, cloxacillin, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprime, gentamicin, and vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Culture, biochemical tests, and disc diffusion assay were used for identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of Listeria species.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic environment of OXA-2 beta-lactamase producing Gram-negative bacilli from a tertiary referral hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaOXA-2 gene encoding a beta-lactamase that hydrolyzes cloxacillin and oxacillin, and is located within class I integron in various Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, transformation, conjugation, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Densities and antimicrobial resistance of Escherichia coli isolated from marine waters and beach sands.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli isolates from marine waters and beach sands, highlighting higher resistance frequencies in contaminated beach sands compared to water samples.
full_output.methodology: The study used membrane filter techniques and agar disc diffusion methods to enumerate E. coli and assess antimicrobial susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of daptomycin in combination with β-lactams, gentamicin, rifampin, and tigecycline against daptomycin-nonsusceptible enterococci.

liaFSR.encodes: three-component regulatory system involved in cell membrane stress response
liaFSR.notes: Mutations in liaFSR and clsA/clsB are associated with daptomycin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the liaFSR system and clsA/clsB genes associated with daptomycin resistance in enterococci, highlighting the importance of these genetic alterations in reducing susceptibility to daptomycin.
full_output.methodology: The study used time-kill assays, mutational analysis, and BODIPY-daptomycin binding studies to evaluate the effects of daptomycin combinations on daptomycin-nonsusceptible enterococci.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of aztreonam-avibactam against a global collection of Gram-negative pathogens from 2012 and 2013.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of aztreonam-avibactam against a global collection of Gram-negative pathogens, demonstrating its effectiveness against isolates producing various β-lactamases, including metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs).
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution methodology to determine the minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of aztreonam-avibactam and comparator antimicrobials against clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: N-Acetyltransferase Genotypes and the Pharmacokinetics and Tolerability of para-Aminosalicylic Acid in Patients with Drug-Resistant Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified NAT1 and NAT2 genotypes influencing the pharmacokinetics and tolerability of para-aminosalicylic acid (PAS) in patients with drug-resistant tuberculosis. Specific alleles such as NAT1*14, NAT1*3, and NAT2*5 were associated with altered PAS clearance and exposure.
full_output.methodology: The study used a randomized, two-period, open-label, crossover design with pharmacokinetic modeling and genotyping to assess the impact of NAT1 and NAT2 alleles on PAS concentrations and tolerability.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus metabolic adaptations during the transition from a daptomycin susceptibility phenotype to a daptomycin nonsusceptibility phenotype.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in mprF and yycG as key factors in the development of daptomycin nonsusceptibility in Staphylococcus aureus, highlighting their roles in altering cell wall synthesis and metabolic pathways.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized NMR metabolomics, growth analysis, and genetic analysis to investigate metabolic and physiological changes in daptomycin-susceptible and -nonsusceptible S. aureus strains.

full_output.paper_title: Planctomycetes do possess a peptidoglycan cell wall.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that Planctomycetes possess a peptidoglycan cell wall and have the genomic potential to produce beta-lactamases that could confer resistance against beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatic analysis, biochemical analysis, and microscopic techniques were used to investigate the presence of peptidoglycan and beta-lactamase genes in Planctomycetes.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm Formation and β-Lactamase Production in Burn Isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the pslA gene as being strongly associated with biofilm formation in P. aeruginosa burn isolates. Additionally, it found that biofilm formation correlates with the production of MBL and AmpC β-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of the pslA gene, biofilm formation assay using microtiter plates, and screening for β-lactamase production using various biochemical tests.

full_output.paper_title: The Tipper-Strominger Hypothesis and Triggering of Allostery in Penicillin-Binding Protein 2a of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that ceftaroline triggers allostery in PBP2a of MRSA, leading to conformational changes that enhance the efficacy of other β-lactam antibiotics through synergy.
full_output.methodology: Fluorescence spectroscopy, MIC testing, and genetic manipulation of PBP2a.

full_output.paper_title: The MazEF Toxin-Antitoxin System Alters the β-Lactam Susceptibility of Staphylococcus aureus.

mazF.validation_method: experimental validation through gene disruption and complementation studies

full_output.key_findings: The mazEF toxin-antitoxin system regulates β-lactam susceptibility in Staphylococcus aureus through mRNA cleavage, with deletion of mazEF leading to increased susceptibility to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, primer extension, and MIC testing were used to investigate the role of mazEF in β-lactam susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic profiles of Propionibacterium acnes and identification of a unique transposon with novel insertion sequences in sarcoid and non-sarcoid isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a unique transposon in Propionibacterium acnes isolates, including a novel insertion sequence and extrinsic genes, some of which are involved in arsenic resistance and resolvase functions.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, PCR detection, and bioinformatics analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenemase producing bacteria in the food supply escaping detection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified OXA-48 carbapenemase-producing bacteria in seafood products from China and Korea, highlighting the potential for these genes to enter the food supply undetected.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic screening, PCR, DNA sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize carbapenemase-producing bacteria.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the ESBL genes blaCTX-M-15, blaTEM-1, and blaSHV-63 in the outbreak strain of Klebsiella pneumoniae, which conferred resistance to ampicillin, cefotaxime, and ceftazidime.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and susceptibility testing of K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial swarms recruit cargo bacteria to pave the way in toxic environments.

full_output.methodology: Co-inoculation experiments, fluorescence microscopy, and selective viable counts.

full_output.paper_title: Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeat-Dependent, Biofilm-Specific Death of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Mediated by Increased Expression of Phage-Related Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the CRISPR system interacting with the DMS3-42 protospacer leads to the overexpression of pyocin and PA14_52530 genes, causing biofilm-specific cell death in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR manipulation, qRT-PCR, RNA-Seq, and pyocin killing assays were used to validate the findings.

This system is conserved in several Proteobacteria, including uropathogenic E. coli and Brucella spp.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic characterization of gene deletions, chemogenomic profiling, transcriptome sequencing, qPCR, and Western blotting.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid quantification of mutant fitness in diverse bacteria by sequencing randomly bar-coded transposons.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces RB-TnSeq, a method for rapid quantification of mutant fitness in diverse bacteria using randomly bar-coded transposons. It identifies genes involved in carbon utilization and metabolic pathways through high-throughput mutant fitness profiling.
full_output.methodology: RB-TnSeq combines transposon mutagenesis with bar-code sequencing to analyze mutant fitness in bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Quorum-Sensing Inhibitors Disrupting Signaling between Rgg and Short Hydrophobic Peptides in Streptococci.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cyclosporine A and valspodar as inhibitors of the Rgg-SHP quorum-sensing pathway in Streptococcus species, effectively blocking biofilm development and Rgg-mediated transcription without affecting bacterial growth.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening using fluorescence polarization assay and luciferase reporter assays to identify compounds that inhibit Rgg3-SHP interactions.

full_output.paper_title: Gut Colonization of Healthy Children and Their Mothers With Pathogenic Ciprofloxacin-Resistant Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that ciprofloxacin-resistant Escherichia coli, particularly ST131-H30 and ST405 clones, are common in the gut flora of healthy children and their mothers. These isolates exhibited multiple antibiotic resistances and virulence factors characteristic of extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a prospective cohort analysis of stool specimens from healthy twins and their mothers to identify ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli, followed by molecular characterization and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Environmentally co-occurring mercury resistance plasmids are genetically and phenotypically diverse and confer variable context-dependent fitness effects.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mercury resistance plasmids pQBR55, pQBR57, and pQBR103, which confer mercury resistance and vary in their fitness effects depending on environmental context.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing and comparative analysis of plasmid genomes, along with fitness assays in different environmental conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Longitudinal Sequence and Functional Evolution within Glycoprotein E2 in Hepatitis C Virus Genotype 3a Infection.
