full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the ATP binding and hydrolysis properties of ABCB10 and identifies mutations in conserved residues of the NBD that affect these activities. It also reveals that glutathione regulates ABCB10 ATP binding and hydrolysis activity.
full_output.methodology: Mutagenesis, photolabeling, Western blotting, and autoradiography were used to analyze ABCB10's ATP binding and hydrolysis properties and the effects of mutations.

full_output.paper_title: A Pipeline for Screening Small Molecules with Growth Inhibitory Activity against Burkholderia cenocepacia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several small molecules with growth inhibitory activity against Burkholderia cenocepacia K56-2, highlighting their potential as antibacterial agents. Key compounds included MAC-0036650, MAC-0040599, MAC-0041192, MAC-0044103, MAC-0151023, and MAC-0164811, which showed effective MIC values against B. cenocepacia and other Bcc strains.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening of small molecules using a whole-cell assay, followed by secondary screening, MIC determination, and in vivo testing in C. elegans.
full_output.sample_size: 30,259 compounds tested in the primary screen

full_output.paper_title: Screening of Probiotic Candidates in Human Oral Bacteria for the Prevention of Dental Disease.
full_output.key_findings: Four probiotic strains were selected based on their low cariogenic potential and lower risk of infective endocarditis.
full_output.methodology: Screening of oral isolates for probiotic properties including VSC production, WIG production, antibacterial activity, adherence to S-HA and oral epithelial cells, and risk of infective endocarditis.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the roles of CcrA and CcrB in the excision and integration of the staphylococcal cassette chromosome mec (SCC mec ), highlighting the importance of specific amino acid residues in these processes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized plasmid models, site-directed mutagenesis, and recombination assays to investigate the functions of CcrA and CcrB.

full_output.paper_title: The RNA Helicase DeaD Stimulates ExsA Translation To Promote Expression of the Pseudomonas aeruginosa Type III Secretion System.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies DeaD as a novel extrinsic regulator of the Pseudomonas aeruginosa type III secretion system (T3SS), showing that it promotes ExsA translation at a posttranscriptional level.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screens, transposon mutagenesis, in vitro translation assays, and molecular biology techniques were used to investigate the role of DeaD in T3SS gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: A genetically amenable platensimycin- and platencin-overproducer as a platform for biosynthetic explorations: a showcase of PtmO4, a long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes ptmO4, a long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase, which catalyzes β-oxidation of diterpenoid intermediates in the biosynthesis of platensimycin (PTM) and platencin (PTN).
full_output.methodology: Gene inactivation, complementation, and structural elucidation of congeners through fermentation and spectroscopic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of the replication region in pBCNF5603, a bacteriocin-encoding plasmid, in the enterotoxigenic Clostridium perfringens strain F5603.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the replication region of the bacteriocin-encoding plasmid pBCNF5603 in Clostridium perfringens strain F5603, highlighting the presence of a rep gene homologous to PCP63 on pCP13 and the identification of potential plasmid replication and partitioning regions.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing and comparative genomics were used to analyze the replication region of pBCNF5603.

full_output.paper_title: Frequency and Distribution of Single-Nucleotide Polymorphisms within mprF in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Clinical Isolates and Their Role in Cross-Resistance to Daptomycin and Host Defense Antimicrobial Peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the mprF gene of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) clinical isolates, which are associated with daptomycin resistance and cross-resistance to host defense antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.methodology: The study used sequencing of the mprF gene, MIC testing, and assessments of surface charge and phospholipid profiles to determine the role of mprF SNPs in daptomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: In Vivo Efficacy of Antimicrobials against Biofilm-Producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy of antibiotics against biofilm-forming Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a murine tumor model, demonstrating that colistin-tobramycin combination therapy was more effective against biofilm-forming wild-type bacteria than individual antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used a murine tumor model to assess the in vivo efficacy of antibiotics against biofilm-forming Pseudomonas aeruginosa, including CFU counting and histological analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution of different efflux pump genes in clinical isolates of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii and their correlation with antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that the upregulation of adeB, adeJ, and macB genes is responsible for tigecycline resistance, while increased abeS expression is strongly related to amikacin resistance in multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used quantitative reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction to analyze the expression of efflux pump genes in clinical isolates of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of antimicrobial susceptibility of Salmonella isolates: First identification of a plasmid carrying qnrD or oqxAB in Taiwan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the first plasmid carrying qnrD or oqxAB in Salmonella isolates in Taiwan, highlighting their role in quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of MERS-CoV 3CL pro and Its Inhibition by Peptidomimetic Compounds
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the MERS-CoV 3CL pro enzyme, highlighting its lower enzymatic efficiency and weak dimerization compared to other coronavirus 3CL pro enzymes. It identifies peptidomimetic compounds 6-9 as effective inhibitors of MERS-CoV 3CL pro with K_I values less than 10 μM.
full_output.methodology: Enzymatic activity assays, kinetic studies, analytical ultracentrifugation, and x-ray crystallography were used to analyze MERS-CoV 3CL pro and its inhibition by peptidomimetic compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Tenebrionid secretions and a fungal benzoquinone oxidoreductase form competing components of an arms race between a host and pathogen.

BbbqrA.validation_method: gene knockout and overexpression experiments, enzyme activity assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies BbbqrA, a NAD(P)H:1,4-benzoquinone oxidoreductase in Beauveria bassiana, which plays a critical role in detoxifying benzoquinone secretions from the tenebrionid beetle Tribolium castaneum, highlighting a coevolutionary arms race between the host and pathogen.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression analysis, enzyme activity assays, gene knockout and overexpression experiments, and heterologous expression in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: A Genome-Wide Screen Reveals that the Vibrio cholerae Phosphoenolpyruvate Phosphotransferase System Modulates Virulence Gene Expression.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ptsI and ptsH, encoding the enzyme I (EI) and Hpr components of the V. cholerae phosphoenolpyruvate phosphotransferase system (PTS), as crucial for TcpA and cholera toxin (CT) production. Disruption of these genes reduces TcpA expression and CT production, impairing intestinal colonization.
full_output.methodology: A transposon insertion site (TIS) sequencing-based screen was used to identify regulators of tcpA expression, followed by immunoblotting, flow cytometry, and qRT-PCR to validate findings.

full_output.paper_title: Persistent Staphylococcus aureus isolates from two independent cases of bacteremia display increased bacterial fitness and novel immune evasion phenotypes.

mprF.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and correlation with persistence-associated phenotypes

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mprF gene mutations as a key factor in the persistence of Staphylococcus aureus during bacteremia, contributing to increased bacterial fitness and immune evasion.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic analysis of S. aureus isolates from persistent and resolved bacteremia cases.

full_output.paper_title: Ligand-Induced Proton Transfer and Low-Barrier Hydrogen Bond Revealed by X-ray Crystallography.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals the formation of a low-barrier hydrogen bond (LBHB) between Ser70 and Lys73 in CTX-M β-lactamase, induced by non-covalent ligand binding, providing insights into enzyme catalysis and proton transfer mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography and QM/MM calculations were used to analyze protonation states and hydrogen bonding networks in CTX-M β-lactamase.

full_output.paper_title: A Lipid Transfer Protein Increases the Glutathione Content and Enhances Arabidopsis Resistance to a Trichothecene Mycotoxin.

full_output.methodology: Transgenic Arabidopsis and yeast strains were created, and resistance to trichothecin was assessed via MIC testing and ROS measurement.

full_output.paper_title: Shifts in the Antibiotic Susceptibility, Serogroups, and Clonal Complexes of Neisseria meningitidis in Shanghai, China: A Time Trend Analysis of the Pre-Quinolone and Quinolone Eras.

gyrA.mechanism: point mutation leading to ciprofloxacin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identified two predominant ciprofloxacin-nonsusceptible clones, China CC4821-R1-C/B and China CC5-R14-A, which acquired resistance through point mutations in the gyrA gene.

full_output.paper_title: PC, a Novel Oral Insecticidal Toxin from Bacillus bombysepticus Involved in Host Lethality via APN and BtR-175.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PC, a novel insecticidal toxin from Bacillus bombysepticus, which interacts with BmAPN4 and BtR-175 to cause pathogenicity in silkworms. Knockout of BtR-175 increases silkworm resistance to PC.
full_output.methodology: The study uses biochemical purification, binding assays, and CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing to analyze the interaction of PC with BmAPN4 and BtR-175.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiofilm Activity of the Brown Alga Halidrys siliquosa against Clinically Relevant Human Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity of organic extracts from the brown alga Halidrys siliquosa against various clinically relevant human pathogens, demonstrating significant activity against Gram-positive bacteria such as Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species, as well as some Gram-negative bacteria like Stenotrophomonas maltophilia and Chromobacterium violaceum.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-Wide Identification of Klebsiella pneumoniae Fitness Genes during Lung Infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several genes crucial for K. pneumoniae lung fitness, including rfaH, involved in capsule and LPS synthesis, and ilvC, ilvD, copA, and aroE, involved in branched-chain amino acid synthesis, copper efflux, and aromatic amino acid synthesis, respectively.

full_output.paper_title: Cyclic Rhamnosylated Elongation Factor P Establishes Antibiotic Resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

Mutants lacking efp, earP, or rmlC showed increased antibiotic sensitivity.

full_output.paper_title: Temperate and lytic bacteriophages programmed to sensitize and kill antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the use of CRISPR-Cas systems delivered by temperate phages to sensitize antibiotic-resistant bacteria and destroy resistance-conferring plasmids, thereby reducing the prevalence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas system delivery by λ phage, transformation efficiency assays, and lytic phage growth efficiency assays.

full_output.paper_title: Mycoplasma genitalium infection: current treatment options, therapeutic failure, and resistance-associated mutations.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the emergence of macrolide resistance in Mycoplasma genitalium due to mutations in the 23S rRNA gene, particularly at position 2058 (A2058T), which is associated with azithromycin treatment failure.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of 23S rRNA gene and PCR assays to detect resistance mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Diffusion and persistence of multidrug resistant Salmonella Typhimurium strains phage type DT120 in southern Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes multidrug resistant Salmonella Typhimurium strains phage type DT120 in southern Italy, identifying various resistance genes including aadA2, floR, tet(G), blaPSE-1, sul1, blaOXA-30, catA1, aadA1, dfrA1, strAB, blaTEM, sul2, tet(B), tet(A), and dfrA12.

full_output.paper_title: Antiviral, Antifungal and Antibacterial Activities of a BODIPY-Based Photosensitizer.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial photodynamic inactivation (aPDI) effects of DIMPy-BODIPY against various bacteria, yeasts, and viruses, demonstrating significant reductions in viability at low concentrations.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro assays to assess the effectiveness of DIMPy-BODIPY in photodynamically inactivating various microorganisms.

full_output.paper_title: Replication and Active Partition of Integrative and Conjugative Elements (ICEs) of the SXT/R391 Family: The Line between ICEs and Conjugative Plasmids Is Getting Thinner.

full_output.paper_title: Sequence Polymorphism of Cytochrome b Gene in Theileria annulata Tunisian Isolates and Its Association with Buparvaquone Treatment Failure.

cyt_b.notes: Mutations in the cytochrome b gene were associated with buparvaquone resistance in Theileria annulata.

full_output.paper_title: A Multidrug-resistant Engineered CAR T Cell for Allogeneic Combination Immunotherapy.

dCK.mechanism: inactivation of dCK gene leads to resistance to purine nucleotide analogues
dCK.validation_method: TALEN-mediated gene inactivation and in vitro resistance testing

full_output.key_findings: Defensin 1 from Tribolium castaneum exhibits antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating synergy with telavancin and daptomycin, and does not cause hemolysis of human erythrocytes.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, checkerboard assay, membrane permeabilization assay, and C. elegans infection model.

full_output.paper_title: Soluble Expression of (+)-γ-Lactamase in Bacillus subtilis for the Enantioselective Preparation of Abacavir Precursor.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of MAIT Cell Development and Function in MR1-Deficient and MR1-Sufficient Mice
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the development and function of MAIT cells in MR1-deficient and MR1-sufficient mice, highlighting the critical role of MR1 in the expansion and functionality of MAIT cells, particularly in response to mycobacterial infections.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MR1/RL tetramers, flow cytometry, and cytokine assays to analyze MAIT cell subsets and their functional responses in various tissues of transgenic and wild-type mice.

full_output.paper_title: Aeromonas punctata derived depolymerase improves susceptibility of Klebsiella pneumoniae biofilm to gentamicin.

full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and characterization of a depolymerase from Aeromonas punctata, assessment of its enzymatic activity, and evaluation of its effectiveness in disrupting K. pneumoniae biofilms and enhancing gentamicin efficacy through various microbiological techniques including microscopic examination, enzyme kinetics, and biofilm susceptibility assays.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Types of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Methicillin-Sensitive S. aureus Strains Causing Skin and Soft Tissue Infections and Nasal Colonization, Identified in Community Health Centers in New York City.

full_output.paper_title: Transmitted Extended-Spectrum Extensively Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis in Beijing, China, with Discordant Whole-Genome Sequencing Analysis Results.

The study highlights discrepancies between whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic testing results, indicating potential limitations in relying solely on WGS for resistance detection.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance Profile and Genotypic Characteristics of Streptococcus suis Capsular Type 2 Isolated from Clinical Carrier Sows and Diseased Pigs in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Streptococcus suis serotype 2, including ermB, mefA, tetM, and tetO, which confer resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, and tetracyclines. The presence of these genes was associated with resistance phenotypes observed in isolates from both healthy sows and diseased pigs.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and validate AMR genes in S. suis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Multidrug Resistant Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase-Producing Escherichia coli among Uropathogens of Pediatrics in North of Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified TEM, SHV, CTX, and VEB beta-lactamase genes as the primary drivers of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase production in E. coli isolates from pediatric patients in northern Iran, with TEM being the most prevalent. These genes conferred resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR and MIC testing were used to identify ESBL genes and assess antimicrobial resistance in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence of Multidrug Resistant Extended Spectrum Beta-Lactamase-Producing Bacteria on Iceberg Lettuce Retailed for Human Consumption.

blaSHV.evidence_note: The bla SHV gene was detected in K. pneumoniae isolate T1 and showed 99% relatedness to bla SHV genes found in clinical isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified ESBL-producing bacteria on iceberg lettuce, including K. pneumoniae isolates carrying SHV-type and TEM-type beta-lactamase genes, as well as S. marcescens with a CTX-M-1 beta-lactamase. These genes confer resistance to cefotaxime.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolation, PCR, sequencing, and conjugation experiments were used to characterize AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Activity of Imipenem and Colistin against a Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolate Coproducing SHV-31, CMY-2, and DHA-1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of blaSHV-31, blaCMY-2, and blaDHA-1 genes in a carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae isolate, along with mutations in ompK35 and loss of ompK36, contributing to resistance against multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and time-kill assays were used to analyze resistance mechanisms and evaluate antimicrobial combinations.

full_output.paper_title: Discrepancies in Drug Susceptibility Test for Tuberculosis Patients Resulted from the Mixed Infection and the Testing System.

katG.notes: The AGC315AAC and AGC315ACC mutations were identified in 13 paired isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the katG gene, particularly at codon 315 (AGC vs. AAC and AGC vs. ACC), which are associated with isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.
full_output.methodology: Sequence analysis of the katG gene and determination of MICs using broth microdilution and L-J proportion methods.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae: Progressive Spread and Four-Year Period of Observation in a Cardiac Surgery Division.

blaVIM-1.evidence_note: The paper states that 9/98 MBL-producing strains carried the bla VIM-1 gene.

blaKPC-2.evidence_note: The paper states that 89/98 isolates were positive for bla KPC-2.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaVIM-1 and blaKPC-2 as the primary carbapenem resistance genes in CRKP isolates, with blaKPC-2 being more prevalent.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, MLST, and PFGE were used to characterize CRKP isolates.

full_output.paper_title: An outbreak of colistin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae in the Netherlands (July to December 2013), with inter-institutional spread.

blaSHV-12.evidence_note: The paper mentions the presence of bla SHV-12 genes in the isolates.

aac(6')-Ib.evidence_note: The paper mentions the presence of the aac(6')-Ib gene in KPC-KP isolates, indicating its role in aminoglycoside resistance.

aph(3')-Ia.evidence_note: The gene aph(3')-Ia was identified in the resistome analysis of KPC-KP isolates, indicating its presence in the context of aminoglycoside resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes an outbreak of colistin-resistant KPC-producing K. pneumoniae ST258 in the Netherlands, highlighting the presence of multiple resistance genes including blaKPC-2, blaSHV-12, and various other AMR genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and molecular typing techniques were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes and resistance mechanisms in the outbreak isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Three Dimensional Checkerboard Synergy Analysis of Colistin, Meropenem, Tigecycline against Multidrug-Resistant Clinical Klebsiella pneumonia Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the resistance mechanisms in multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, focusing on the role of porin genes ompK35 and ompK36. Mutations in these genes, including stop codons, insertions, deletions, and substitutions, were associated with increased resistance to meropenem.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of porin genes and susceptibility testing of clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Structure and inhibition studies of a type II beta-carbonic anhydrase psCA3 from Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes psCA3, a type II beta-carbonic anhydrase from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, determining its structure and identifying inhibitors such as sulfamide, sulfamic acid, phenylboronic acid, and phenylarsonic acid. Acetazolamide showed significant inhibitory effects on P. aeruginosa growth.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, kinetic analysis, and in vivo inhibition studies.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of clarithromycin-resistant Helicobacter pylori strains in a dyspeptic patient population in Sri Lanka by polymerase chain reaction-restriction fragment length polymorphism.

23S rRNA.notes: A2143G mutation was not detected.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the predominance of the A2142G point mutation in the 23S rRNA gene of H. pylori strains associated with clarithromycin resistance in Sri Lanka.
full_output.methodology: In-house urease test and PCR amplification of the glmM gene were used to confirm H. pylori infection, followed by analysis of point mutations in the 23S rRNA gene using PCR-RFLP.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations at embB306 codon and their association with multidrug resistant M. tuberculosis clinical isolates.

embB.notes: The embB306 mutation is associated with ethambutol resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The embB306 mutation is significantly associated with ethambutol resistance in M. tuberculosis clinical isolates, with a higher frequency observed in ethambutol-resistant isolates compared to susceptible ones.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic drug susceptibility testing was performed on 354 M. tuberculosis isolates using standard proportion method and multiplex-allele-specific polymerase chain reaction assay.

full_output.paper_title: In Vivo Selection of Pan-Drug Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii during Antibiotic Treatment.

armA.evidence_note: The paper states that the PDR A. baumannii AB003 isolate harbored the armA gene and showed resistance to aminoglycosides.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel mutation in the pmrB gene (Glu229Asp) and the acquisition of the armA gene as mechanisms contributing to colistin and aminoglycoside resistance in a pan-drug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolate.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry.

full_output.paper_title: Reversing resistance: The next generation antibacterials.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the rise of antibiotic resistance and highlights the development of new antibiotics targeting various bacterial mechanisms, including cell wall synthesis, DNA replication, and protein synthesis.
full_output.methodology: The paper provides a comprehensive review of current and emerging antibiotics, focusing on their mechanisms of action and resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Utility of Line Probe Assay for the Early Detection of Multidrug-Resistant Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the line probe assay (LPA) for the early detection of multidrug-resistant pulmonary tuberculosis, demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity for detecting rifampicin and isoniazid resistance. Mutations in rpoB (S531L), katG (S315T1 and S315T2), and inhA (C15T, A16G, T8C, T8A) were identified as key resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Line probe assay (LPA) and conventional 1% proportion method (PM) were used for drug susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Study of Antibiotic Resistance Pattern in Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus with Special Reference to Newer Antibiotic.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that none of the MRSA isolates were resistant to ceftaroline, telavancin, teicoplanin, or vancomycin, but 2.28% were resistant to linezolid and 5.56% to daptomycin. Additionally, 100% resistance was noted to fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides, and lincosamides.
full_output.methodology: The study used disk diffusion method for antibiotic susceptibility testing and D-test for inducible clindamycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Within-Farm Changes in Dairy Farm-Associated Salmonella Subtypes and Comparison to Human Clinical Isolates in Michigan, 2000-2001 and 2009.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified changes in the distribution and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) of Salmonella subtypes on Michigan dairy farms between 2000-2001 and 2009. It noted a decrease in multidrug-resistant (MDR) Salmonella subtypes and an increase in pansusceptible strains, indicating potential improvements in farm management practices and reduced AMR prevalence.
full_output.methodology: The study used longitudinal sampling of dairy farms, serotyping, multilocus sequence typing (MLST), and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) to analyze Salmonella subtypes and their AMR profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity of SCCmec elements in Staphylococci isolated from public washrooms.

mecA.validation_method: detection of mecA gene and SCC mec typing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified diverse SCCmec elements in various staphylococcal species from public washrooms, highlighting the presence of mecA-mediated oxacillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization, SCCmec typing, MIC testing, and MLST/spa typing.

full_output.paper_title: Point-of-care multiplex PCR promises short turnaround times for microbial testing in hospital-acquired pneumonia--an observational pilot study in critical ill patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the performance of a point-of-care multiplex PCR system for detecting pathogens and antibiotic resistance markers in hospital-acquired pneumonia. The system showed significantly shorter turnaround times compared to conventional microbiological diagnostics, although its performance was limited by frequent test failures and non-concordant results.
full_output.methodology: Observational pilot study comparing the Unyvero multiplex PCR system with conventional microbiological diagnostics in critically ill patients with hospital-acquired pneumonia.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro antimicrobial susceptibility testing of human Brucella melitensis isolates from Qatar between 2014 - 2015.

rpoB.notes: Mutations in rpoB gene were analyzed for rifampicin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified B. melitensis as the causative agent of brucellosis in Qatar and found no resistant isolates among conventional antimicrobial agents, although 48% of strains showed elevated rifampicin MICs (>1 mg/L). No rpoB mutations were found in strains with high rifampicin MICs.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using E-test strips and PCR analysis of the rpoB gene for rifampicin-resistant strains.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium and Salmonella enterica serovar 4,[5],12:i:- isolates from pigs presenting with diarrhea in Korea

fljA.notes: FljA is involved in flagellar phase variation

fljB.notes: FljB is involved in flagellar phase variation

hin.encodes: H inversion: regulation of flagellar gene expression
hin.notes: Hin is involved in flagellar phase variation

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium and Salmonella enterica serovar 4,[5],12:i:- isolates from pigs in Korea, highlighting differences in flagellar gene expression and antimicrobial resistance patterns.
full_output.methodology: PCR analysis, MLVA, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and serotyping were used to characterize the isolates.
full_output.sample_size: 50 S. Typhimurium isolates and 4 S. 4,[5],12:i:- isolates

full_output.paper_title: SarA based novel therapeutic candidate against Staphylococcus aureus associated with vascular graft infections.

sarA.encodes: DNA-binding protein SarA; a 14.7 kDa winged helix turn helix transcriptional activator

mutations_found.effect_on_function: The SarABI forms hydrogen bond with glutamic acid and arginine at 88 and 89 positions respectively.
mutations_found.origin: The SarABI was synthesized by the condensation of commercially available 2,4 difluorobenzyl bromide and 4-aminocyclohexanol (Sigma-Aldrich)

sarA.notes: Mutations in sarA were not explicitly mentioned, but the gene was targeted by SarABI.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified SarABI, a novel inhibitor targeting SarA, which effectively reduced biofilm formation and virulence gene expression in Staphylococcus aureus without exhibiting antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: Molecular docking, in vitro biofilm inhibition assays, qRT-PCR, and animal infection models were used to evaluate SarABI's efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of in-feed administration and withdrawal of tylosin phosphate on antibiotic resistance in enterococci isolated from feedlot steers.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that tylosin phosphate administration increased the proportion of erythromycin and tylosin resistant enterococci, but withdrawal reduced their prevalence. The resistance was primarily mediated by the erm(B) gene and msrC gene.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Insight into the mobilome of Aeromonas strains.

blaOXA-10.genetic_context: Tn 21 : qacH , bla OXA-10 , aadA1 , sul1 , intI
blaOXA-10.evidence_note: bla OXA-10 is located on the pR148 plasmid, which is part of the IncA/C group.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various antibiotic resistance genes (ARG) in Aeromonas strains, highlighting the presence of beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, tetracycline resistance genes, and others. These genes are often located on plasmids and contribute to multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid characterization and analysis of mobile genetic elements.

full_output.paper_title: Architecture and roles of periplasmic adaptor proteins in tripartite eﬄux assemblies.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the structural and functional roles of periplasmic adaptor proteins (PAPs) in tripartite efflux assemblies, highlighting their importance in linking inner membrane transporters with outer membrane factors (OMFs) to facilitate multidrug efflux.
full_output.methodology: Structural and functional analysis of PAPs and their interactions with OMFs and transporters.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of carbapenem non-susceptible Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates in Eastern Algeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla PSE-1 and aac(3)-II as the genes responsible for carbapenem and gentamicin resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates in Eastern Algeria.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect resistance genes, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: A Thermophilic Phage Endolysin Fusion to a Clostridium perfringens-Specific Cell Wall Binding Domain Creates an Anti-Clostridium Antimicrobial with Improved Thermostability.

PlyGVE2CpCWB.validation_method: plate lysis (spot) assay, MIC assay, SDS-PAGE, mass spectrometry

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the creation of a thermostable chimeric endolysin, PlyGVE2CpCWB, which effectively lysed Clostridium perfringens in both plate and liquid cultures. The protein showed optimal activity at pH 8.0 and remained active under various salinity conditions. It exhibited improved thermostability compared to the parental endolysin PlyCP26F, making it suitable for use in poultry feed.
full_output.methodology: Gene synthesis, cloning, protein expression, purification, and activity assays including plate lysis, MIC determination, SDS-PAGE, and mass spectrometry.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium avium Subspecies paratuberculosis Recombinant Proteins Modulate Antimycobacterial Functions of Bovine Macrophages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis recombinant proteins, including MAP0261c, MAP0584, MAP2322c, MAP3615c, MAP0981c, and MAP3837c, which modulate antimycobacterial functions in bovine macrophages by influencing cytokine expression and MAPKp38 activation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized recombinant proteins derived from M. paratuberculosis lipoproteins, tested their effects on cytokine expression and MAPKp38 activation in bovine macrophages, and assessed their impact on M. avium survival.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the Enterococcus faecalis Biofilm-Associated Virulence Factors AhrC and Eep in Rat Foreign Body Osteomyelitis and In Vitro Biofilm-Associated Antimicrobial Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that neither ahrC nor eep directly contribute to Enterococcus faecalis biofilm-associated antimicrobial resistance. Surface colonization alone was sufficient for E. faecalis cells to acquire the biofilm antimicrobial resistance phenotype.
full_output.methodology: The study used a rat model of acute foreign body osteomyelitis and in vitro biofilm assays to evaluate the role of ahrC and eep in biofilm formation and antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology and characterization of an outbreak causing Klebsiella pneumoniae clone carrying chromosomally located bla(CTX-M-15) at a German University-Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a chromosomal insertion of bla(CTX-M-15) in a Klebsiella pneumoniae ST101 strain, highlighting the potential for chromosomal locations to serve as reservoirs for the spread of bla(CTX-M-15) encoding transposition units.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, PCR, and PFGE analysis were used to characterize the chromosomal location of bla(CTX-M-15) in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study found high in vitro susceptibility to the novel spiropyrimidinetrione ETX0914 among 873 clinical Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from 21 European countries, with no cross-resistance to other antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: The study determined the minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of ETX0914 using agar dilution method and compared them with those of ceftriaxone, cefixime, azithromycin, and ciprofloxacin.

full_output.paper_title: Mobile genetic elements related to the diffusion of plasmid-mediated AmpC β-lactamases or carbapenemases from Enterobacteriaceae: findings from a multicenter study in Spain.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various plasmid-mediated AmpC β-lactamases (bla CMY-2, bla DHA-1, bla ACC-1, bla FOX-3) and carbapenemases (bla VIM-1, bla IMP-22, bla IMP-28) in Enterobacteriaceae isolates, highlighting their association with mobile genetic elements and their role in the spread of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid analysis, S1-PFGE, Southern hybridization, PCR, and sequencing were used to characterize the genetic context of the resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: pKBuS13, a KPC-2-encoding plasmid from Klebsiella pneumoniae sequence type 833, carrying Tn4401b inserted into an Xer site-specific recombination locus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pKBuS13, a plasmid carrying the blaKPC-2 gene, which confers resistance to carbapenems in Klebsiella pneumoniae ST833. The plasmid's instability and insertion of Tn4401b into an Xer recombination locus are noted.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization, plasmid sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of ceftiofur injection on gut microbiota and Escherichia coli resistance in pigs.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the blaCTX-M-1 gene, which confers resistance to ceftiofur and other extended-spectrum cephalosporins in Escherichia coli isolated from pigs.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, sequencing, and qPCR to characterize the blaCTX-M-1 gene and its resistance profile in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Insights into the mechanism of inhibition of novel bacterial topoisomerase inhibitors from characterization of resistant mutants of Staphylococcus aureus.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA and gyrB were identified in resistant mutants of S. aureus.

gyrB.notes: Mutations in gyrB were identified in resistant mutants of S. aureus.

parC.notes: Mutations in parC were identified in resistant mutants of S. aureus.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple mutations in the DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV subunits of Staphylococcus aureus that confer resistance to novel bacterial topoisomerase inhibitors (NBTIs) such as AZ6142, AZ0217, and MCHEM18. These mutations were located in the binding pocket and DNA-binding cleft, affecting the interaction with the inhibitors and leading to increased minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs).
full_output.methodology: The study characterized resistant mutants of S. aureus to identify mutations in DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV subunits that confer resistance to NBTIs. Whole-genomic DNA was sequenced to detect mutations, and MICs were determined to assess resistance levels.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic effect of membrane-active peptides polymyxin B and gramicidin S on multidrug-resistant strains and biofilms of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the synergistic effect of polymyxin B (PMB) and gramicidin S (GS) against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains and biofilms, showing that their combination significantly enhances antimicrobial efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study used checkerboard assays, resazurin assays, and crystal violet staining to evaluate the synergistic effects of PMB and GS on P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Mutation landscape of acquired cross-resistance to glycopeptide and β-lactam antibiotics in Enterococcus faecium.

These mutations affect various aspects of peptidoglycan synthesis and regulatory pathways, leading to high-level resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and functional analysis of mutants to identify mutations associated with resistance to ampicillin and glycopeptides.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterisation of new organisation of plnEF and plw loci of bacteriocin genes harbour concomitantly in Lactobacillus plantarum I-UL4.
full_output.key_findings: Lactobacillus plantarum I-UL4 was identified as a novel multiple bacteriocin producer that harbors both plw and plnEF loci, contributing to its broad inhibitory spectrum against various Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the plnEF and plw loci in Lactobacillus plantarum I-UL4.

full_output.paper_title: Links between Anr and Quorum Sensing in Pseudomonas aeruginosa Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that Anr activity is crucial for the expression of metabolic pathways and virulence-related genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms, especially in quorum sensing (QS) mutants. Anr regulates the production of CupA fimbriae and 4-hydroxy-2-alkylquinolines (HAQs), which are important for biofilm formation and interspecies interactions.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized transcriptome sequencing (RNA-Seq) and NanoString analysis to investigate the Anr regulon in P. aeruginosa strains under low-oxygen conditions, alongside Western blot analysis and genetic manipulation techniques.

full_output.paper_title: AmpC-BETA Lactamases among Enterobacteriaceae Isolated at a Tertiary Hospital, South Western Uganda.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several plasmid-mediated AmpC beta-lactamase genes, including EBC, FOX, ACC, CIT, MOX, and DHA, among Enterobacteriaceae isolates. EBC was the most common genotype, followed by FOX, while MOX was the least detected. The prevalence of AmpC-producing isolates was high, particularly in urine samples and E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and disc diffusion tests were used to identify and characterize AmpC beta-lactamase genes in Enterobacteriaceae isolates.

full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and MIC testing were used to characterize resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: A Macrophage Subversion Factor Is Shared by Intracellular and Extracellular Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mgtC as a critical virulence determinant in P. aeruginosa, demonstrating its role in resisting macrophage killing and contributing to virulence in a zebrafish infection model.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and fine-mapping of a new resistance gene, Xa40, conferring resistance to bacterial blight races in rice (Oryza sativa L.).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a new resistance gene, Xa40, which confers resistance to bacterial blight races in rice, particularly the K3a race. The gene was fine-mapped to a specific region on chromosome 11 and validated through genetic analysis and RT-PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Catch me if you can: a biotinylated proteoliposome affinity assay for the investigation of assembly of the MexA-MexB-OprM efflux pump from Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: First detection of Aspergillus fumigatus azole-resistant strain due to Cyp51A TR46/Y121F/T289A in an azole-naive patient in Spain.

full_output.paper_title: Risk and Prognostic Factors for Multidrug-Resistant Acinetobacter Baumannii Complex Bacteremia: A Retrospective Study in a Tertiary Hospital of West China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies carbapenem use and ICU admission as independent risk factors for multidrug-resistant (MDR) Acinetobacter baumannii complex bacteremia. full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical data from patients with A. baumannii complex bacteremia, including susceptibility testing and statistical analysis of risk factors.

full_output.paper_title: Multi-resistant gram negative enteric bacteria causing urinary tract infection among malnourished underfives admitted at a tertiary hospital, northwestern, Tanzania.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant Gram-negative enteric bacteria, including Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, causing urinary tract infections in malnourished children. These isolates showed high resistance to ampicillin, amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, gentamicin, and third-generation cephalosporins, with all isolates exhibiting an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) phenotype.
full_output.methodology: Urinary tract infections were diagnosed through urine culture and susceptibility testing using the disk diffusion method.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in Salmonella strains from food of animal origin in southern Italy, with notable resistance to sulfonamides, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of 614 Salmonella strains from food samples using disk diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: The DNA Methyltransferase DNMT1 and Tyrosine-Protein Kinase KIT Cooperatively Promote Resistance to 5-Aza-2'-deoxycytidine (Decitabine) and Midostaurin (PKC412) in Lung Cancer Cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies DNMT1 and KIT as key players in promoting resistance to decitabine and PKC412 in lung cancer cells through their reciprocal regulation and involvement in DNA hypermethylation and kinase signaling reactivation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized cell culture, siRNA transfection, Western blot, qPCR, and in vivo tumor xenograft models to investigate the roles of DNMT1 and KIT in drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of Remel Spectra CRE Agar for Detection of Carbapenem-Resistant Bacteria from Rectal Swabs Obtained from Residents of a Long-Term-Care Facility.

blaKPC.validation_method: multiplex PCR and modified Hodge test

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of Remel Spectra CRE agar for detecting carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) and found that it detected KPC-type CRE in 97.2% of cases, demonstrating its utility as a fast and reliable method for CRE detection.
full_output.methodology: The study compared Remel Spectra CRE agar with the CDC standard methodology for isolating CRE from rectal swabs, utilizing multiplex PCR and modified Hodge tests for confirmation.

full_output.paper_title: Biophysical separation of Staphylococcus epidermidis strains based on antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the aac(6')-aph(2'') gene as responsible for gentamicin resistance in Staphylococcus epidermidis, demonstrating the use of g-iDEP for separating resistant and susceptible strains based on their electrophoretic and dielectrophoretic mobilities.
full_output.methodology: The study uses gradient insulator-based dielectrophoresis (g-iDEP) to separate gentamicin-resistant and susceptible strains of Staphylococcus epidermidis, analyzing their electrophoretic and dielectrophoretic mobilities.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Characterization of Novel Synthetic Thiazole Compounds against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antibacterial activity of six novel synthetic thiazole compounds against methicillin-sensitive and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius, showing potent bactericidal effects and the ability to re-sensitize resistant strains to oxacillin.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution, time-kill assays, and combination therapy assessments to evaluate the antibacterial activity of thiazole compounds against S. pseudintermedius isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Preterm infant gut colonization in the neonatal ICU and complete restoration 2 years later.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the bacterial antibiotic-resistant high-risk lineages colonizing preterm infants during their NICU stay and their persistence in faeces after 2 years. It identifies Enterococcus faecalis ST64 and Enterococcus faecium ST18 clones as prevalent in the NICU, while multidrug-resistant high-risk clones were not recovered from the faecal samples of the 2-year-olds.
full_output.methodology: The study used culture analysis, 16S rDNA sequencing, MALDI-TOF, antibiotic susceptibility testing, genetic diversity analysis (RAPD, PFGE, MLST), and PCR for virulence factors.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro susceptibilities of clinical isolates of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae to fosfomycin and tigecycline.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro susceptibility of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (CPE) isolates to fosfomycin and tigecycline, revealing that 88.8% of CPE isolates were susceptible to fosfomycin and 66.6% to tigecycline.
full_output.methodology: Disc diffusion tests were performed according to CLSI guidelines, with susceptibility interpreted using CLSI breakpoints and EUCAST criteria.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Heterogeneity of Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Associated with Variation in Severity of Illness among Children with Acute Hematogenous Osteomyelitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified genomic heterogeneity among MRSA isolates from children with osteomyelitis, highlighting differences in virulence genes and SNPs. It found a higher occurrence of virulence genes in study isolates compared to reference strains and identified strain-specific SNPs.
full_output.methodology: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) and optical mapping were used to analyze MRSA isolates from children with osteomyelitis.

full_output.paper_title: APR-246 overcomes resistance to cisplatin and doxorubicin in ovarian cancer cells.
full_output.key_findings: APR-246 resensitizes cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer cells to cisplatin and doxorubicin by decreasing intracellular glutathione levels and restoring wild-type p53 function.
full_output.methodology: Cell viability assays, western blotting, and analysis of glutathione levels were used to assess the effects of APR-246 on ovarian cancer cells.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal Evolution and Blast Crisis Correlate with Enhanced Proteolytic Activity of Separase in BCR-ABL b3a2 Fusion Type CML under Imatinib Therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the b3a2 fusion type of p210BCR-ABL is associated with a higher likelihood of acquiring unbalanced additional cytogenetic abnormalities (ACA) and progressing to blast crisis under imatinib therapy. It also reveals that imatinib treatment leads to a decrease in Separase protein levels but an increase in its proteolytic activity specifically in b3a2 CML cell lines.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 1151 CML patients and conducted experiments on CML cell lines to assess the effects of imatinib on Separase expression and activity.

tcrYAZB.encodes: negative transcriptional regulator, copper chaperone, and two P1B-type ATPases
tcrYAZB.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a 'copper pathogenicity island' containing genes like pco and sil that confer copper and silver resistance, respectively, in bacteria isolated from copper- and zinc-fed pigs. Additionally, a yersiniabactin synthesis cluster and tcrYAZB determinant were found to contribute to copper resistance in Enterococcus species.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing of bacterial strains isolated from pigs, followed by functional analysis of identified resistance genes.
full_output.sample_size: Several strains of Escherichia coli, Salmonella enterica, and Enterococcus faecium and faecalis.

full_output.paper_title: Cornus mas (Linnaeus) Novel Devised Medicinal Preparations: Bactericidal Effect against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of novel medicinal preparations from Cornus mas L. fruits that exhibit potent bactericidal activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The bactericidal effect is attributed to the presence of 200 mM sodium bromide during the extraction process.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized novel extraction methodologies, including A.A.L.E.P. and A.O.E.P., to produce medicinal preparations from Cornus mas L. fruits. Antimicrobial effectiveness tests were conducted to evaluate the bactericidal activity of these preparations against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the invasive, multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium strain D23580, highlighting its enhanced acid stress resistance, motility, and tissue colonization abilities in a murine model. It also notes differences in biochemical profiles compared to other Salmonella strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used a murine model to assess the virulence and pathogenicity of D23580, including tissue distribution, acid stress resistance, motility, and biochemical profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Asian Citrus Psyllid Expression Profiles Suggest Candidatus Liberibacter Asiaticus-Mediated Alteration of Adult Nutrition and Metabolism, and of Nymphal Development and Immunity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified differentially expressed genes in Asian citrus psyllid (ACP) adults and nymphs infected or uninfected with Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (CLas), highlighting changes in gene expression related to nutrition, metabolism, development, and immunity.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis using Illumina sequencing and bioinformatics tools to compare gene expression in CLas-infected and uninfected ACP.
full_output.sample_size: 100 CLas-infected and uninfected ACP adults, 225 CLas-infected and uninfected ACP nymphs

full_output.paper_title: Nitric Oxide Synthase as a Target for Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: increased hydrophobicity of Ile-218 over the analogous mNOS Val residue improves inhibitor binding to bNOS

I218V.notes: Mutation in the active site of bNOS affecting inhibitor binding
I218V.evidence_note: The paper describes the I218V mutation in bsNOS and its effect on inhibitor binding, but does not explicitly state that this mutation confers resistance to any specific drug.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two potent bacterial nitric oxide synthase (bNOS) inhibitors, 19 and 32, which show antimicrobial activity against MRSA. The research highlights the importance of the Ile-218 residue in bNOS for inhibitor binding and suggests that targeting bNOS could be a novel strategy for combating MRSA.
full_output.methodology: The study employed biochemical assays, crystallography, and mutagenesis to characterize bNOS inhibitors and their effects on MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and drug resistance profile of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolated from pulmonary tuberculosis patients attending two public hospitals in East Gojjam zone, northwest Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 20.23% of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates were resistant to at least one anti-TB drug, with streptomycin resistance being the most common. Rifampicin resistance was higher than previous reports, indicating a potential rise in MDR-TB cases.
full_output.methodology: Drug susceptibility testing (DST) was performed using the indirect proportion method on Middlebrook 7H10 agar media for first-line drugs: isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, and streptomycin.

full_output.paper_title: Aii20J, a wide-spectrum thermostable N-acylhomoserine lactonase from the marine bacterium Tenacibaculum sp. 20J, can quench AHL-mediated acid resistance in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: Aii20J, a metallo-beta-lactamase from Tenacibaculum sp. 20J, effectively quenches AHL-mediated acid resistance in E. coli by degrading AHLs, demonstrating high thermostability and broad substrate specificity.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, heterologous expression, enzyme purification, and functional assays with AHL biosensors and HPLC-MS analysis.

katG.notes: associated with increased transmission

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the katG Ser315Thr mutation as being significantly associated with increased transmission of multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis, whereas the combination of katG Ser315Thr and rpsL Lys43Arg mutations was associated with decreased transmission.
full_output.methodology: Case-control study analyzing drug resistance mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains from households in Lima, Peru.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Lactococcus-Specific Bacteriocins Produced by Lactococcal Isolates, and the Discovery of a Novel Bacteriocin, Lactococcin Z.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel class IId bacteriocin, lactococcin Z, produced by Lactococcus lactis strain QU 7, which exhibits antimicrobial activity against Lactococcus lactis strains.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation of bacteriocin-producing strains, purification of lactococcin Z, and structural analysis including amino acid sequencing and mass spectrometry.

full_output.paper_title: Interspecies gene transfer provides soybean resistance to a fungal pathogen.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PING genes involved in postinvasion nonhost resistance (NHR) in Arabidopsis thaliana against Phakopsora pachyrhizi. These genes, when transferred to soybean, confer resistance to Asian soybean rust disease.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome analysis, gene silencing, and transgenic overexpression experiments were conducted to identify and validate the role of PING genes in conferring resistance to P. pachyrhizi in soybean.

full_output.paper_title: Thiophenecarboxamide Derivatives Activated by EthA Kill Mycobacterium tuberculosis by Inhibiting the CTP Synthetase PyrG.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pyrG and ethA as critical genes involved in the activation and resistance to thiophenecarboxamide derivatives 7947882 and 7904688 in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Mutations in pyrG, particularly T557G (Val186Gly), confer resistance to these compounds by altering the ATP-binding site.
full_output.methodology: Genetic validation, biochemical assays, and whole-genome sequencing were used to identify and characterize the roles of pyrG and ethA in the resistance mechanism of 7947882 and 7904688.

mutations_found.validated_by: experimental validation through evaluation of antibacterial activity and structural studies

dhfr.notes: The F98Y mutation in dhfr is a key resistance mechanism against trimethoprim.
dhfr.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the F98Y mutation in DHFR confers resistance to trimethoprim.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the F98Y mutation in dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) as a key resistance mechanism against trimethoprim in Staphylococcus aureus. The research explores the structural and functional implications of this mutation, highlighting its impact on cofactor binding and enzyme inhibition.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized structural biology techniques, enzymatic inhibition assays, and antibacterial activity evaluations to characterize the resistance mechanism conferred by the F98Y mutation in DHFR.

full_output.paper_title: Lipopolysaccharide Phosphorylation by the WaaY Kinase Affects the Susceptibility of Escherichia coli to the Human Antimicrobial Peptide LL-37.
full_output.key_findings: Inactivation of the waaY gene, which encodes a kinase responsible for heptose II phosphorylation in the LPS inner core, leads to decreased susceptibility to LL-37 in E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, RT-PCR, MIC assays, flow cytometry, and complementation experiments were used to investigate the role of waaY in LL-37 susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: A novel point mutation promotes growth phase-dependent daptomycin tolerance in Staphylococcus aureus.

pitA6.validation_method: mutant strain construction and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: A single point mutation in the putative inorganic phosphate transporter gene pitA (pitA6) leads to growth phase-dependent daptomycin tolerance in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, mutant strain construction, and MIC testing

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in genes for the F420 biosynthetic pathway and a nitroreductase enzyme are the primary resistance determinants in spontaneous in vitro-selected PA-824-resistant mutants of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in genes involved in the F420 biosynthetic pathway and a nitroreductase enzyme as the primary resistance determinants in PA-824-resistant mutants of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of target genes and determination of MICs.

full_output.paper_title: Correlation between GyrA substitutions and ofloxacin, levofloxacin, and moxifloxacin cross-resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA QRDR correlate with increased MICs for fluoroquinolones.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific GyrA substitutions that correlate with resistance to ofloxacin, levofloxacin, and moxifloxacin in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, highlighting the importance of gyrA mutations in fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used sequencing and MIC testing to evaluate the correlation between GyrA mutations and fluoroquinolone resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Differences in antibiotic-induced oxidative stress responses between laboratory and clinical isolates of Streptococcus pneumoniae.

parC.notes: Mutation in parC confers resistance to ciprofloxacin

gyrA.notes: Mutation in gyrA confers resistance to ciprofloxacin

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the parC and gyrA genes that confer resistance to ciprofloxacin in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The study used cloning and MIC testing to validate the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Variation in resistance traits, phylogenetic backgrounds, and virulence genotypes among Escherichia coli clinical isolates from adjacent hospital campuses serving distinct patient populations.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M and bla CTX-M-15 genes as significant contributors to extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) production in Escherichia coli isolates, particularly in the ST131-H30Rx subclone.
full_output.methodology: Molecular methods including PCR, sequencing, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis were used to characterize E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: An in vitro combined antibiotic-antibody treatment eliminates toxicity from Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies tigecycline (TGC) as an antibiotic that effectively inhibits the growth of all tested Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) isolates without inducing Shiga toxin (Stx) production. TGC, when combined with neutralizing antibodies against Stx1 and Stx2, fully protects Vero cells from Stx toxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study used an antibiotic array to screen 42 STEC isolates for susceptibility, ELISA to measure Stx levels, and Vero cell cytotoxicity assays to evaluate the effectiveness of TGC and antibodies in neutralizing Stx toxicity.

full_output.paper_title: Multicenter retrospective study of cefmetazole and flomoxef for treatment of extended-spectrum-β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the efficacy of cefmetazole and flomoxef for treating extended-spectrum-beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli (ESBL-EC) bacteremia, suggesting they may be viable alternatives to carbapenems in certain patient populations.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective multicenter study analyzing patient outcomes and antimicrobial susceptibility data.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of IncI1 Sequence Type 71 Epidemic Plasmid Lineage Responsible for the Recent Dissemination of CTX-M-65 Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase in the Bolivian Chaco Region
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the IncI1 ST71 plasmid lineage as the primary driver of CTX-M-65 dissemination in the Bolivian Chaco region, highlighting the role of this plasmid in conferring resistance to multiple β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid sequencing, PCR, and conjugation experiments were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms and dissemination potential of the IncI1 ST71 plasmid.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa High-Level Resistance to Polymyxins and Other Antimicrobial Peptides Requires cprA, a Gene That Is Disrupted in the PAO1 Strain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cprA as a gene essential for high-level resistance to polymyxins and other antimicrobial peptides in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The cprA gene is disrupted in the PAO1 strain, leading to reduced resistance.
full_output.methodology: Deletion analysis, allelic replacement, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to validate the role of cprA in polymyxin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Interactions between QnrB, QnrB mutants, and DNA gyrase.

qnrB.validation_method: bacterial two-hybrid assay and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the interactions between QnrB, a plasmid-encoded quinolone resistance protein, and DNA gyrase subunits, revealing that QnrB protects gyrase from quinolone inhibition and that specific structural features of QnrB are crucial for this resistance mechanism.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial two-hybrid assay and MIC testing were used to evaluate protein-protein interactions and resistance phenotypes.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analysis of diversity, population structure, virulence, and antimicrobial resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae, an urgent threat to public health.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple beta-lactamase genes (blaSHV, blaOKP, blaLEN), fosA, and oqxAB as key contributors to antimicrobial resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting the widespread presence of these genes in human-associated lineages.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of over 300 K. pneumoniae isolates using whole-genome sequencing and pangenome-wide association studies.

full_output.paper_title: Expression of the multidrug transporter P-glycoprotein is inversely related to that of apoptosis-associated endogenous TRAIL.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies an inverse relationship between P-glycoprotein (Pgp) expression and endogenous TRAIL expression, highlighting the role of Pgp in modulating TRAIL levels and affecting sensitivity to TRAIL-mediated apoptosis.
full_output.methodology: The study used a TET-off system to regulate Pgp expression, combined with RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and functional assays to analyze the relationship between Pgp and TRAIL.

full_output.paper_title: Acyl acceptor recognition by Enterococcus faecium L,D-transpeptidase Ldtfm.

Ldtfm.notes: Residues K372, R437, and W425 are critical for acyl acceptor binding and l,d-transpeptidase activity.
Ldtfm.evidence_note: The paper describes mutations in Ldtfm that impair interaction with the acyl acceptor, but does not explicitly state that these mutations confer resistance to any specific drug.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies critical residues (K372, R437, and W425) in the L,D-transpeptidase Ldtfm of Enterococcus faecium that are essential for acyl acceptor binding and l,d-transpeptidase activity.
full_output.methodology: NMR spectroscopy, site-directed mutagenesis, and cross-linking assays were used to characterize the interaction of Ldtfm with acyl acceptors.

full_output.paper_title: Individual Constituents from Essential Oils Inhibit Biofilm Mass Production by Multi-Drug Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that carvacrol, citral, and (+)-limonene inhibit biofilm mass production by multi-drug resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains, with carvacrol being the most effective compound.
full_output.methodology: The study used crystal violet staining to evaluate biofilm mass formation and determined minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of the compounds against S. aureus strains.

full_output.paper_title: Expression of Genes for Drug Transporters in the Human Female Genital Tract and Modulatory Effect of Antiretroviral Drugs.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the expression of drug transporters in cervicovaginal cell lines and tissues, focusing on the effects of antiretroviral drugs (darunavir, dapivirine, and tenofovir) on transporter expression. Key findings include the modulation of MRP1, MRP5, MRP7, CNT3, OCT3, and other transporters by these drugs.
full_output.methodology: The study used real-time PCR to analyze gene expression of drug transporters in various cervicovaginal cell lines and tissues, assessing the effects of antiretroviral drugs on transporter expression.

full_output.paper_title: Click Chemistry in Lead Optimization of Boronic Acids as β-Lactamase Inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of a new class of boronic acid inhibitors targeting class C β-lactamases, demonstrating potent inhibition against P99 and PDC-3 enzymes with low nanomolar K_i values.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and testing of new boronic acid inhibitors against class C β-lactamases using enzymatic inhibition assays and MIC determination.

full_output.paper_title: Transmission of Multidrug-Resistant and Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis within Households: A Prospective Cohort Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDRTB) has a lower relative fitness compared to drug-susceptible tuberculosis, as evidenced by a reduced incidence of tuberculosis disease among household contacts of MDRTB index cases.
full_output.methodology: Prospective cohort study with multivariate Cox regression analysis to assess the relative fitness of MDRTB and drug-susceptible tuberculosis.
full_output.sample_size: 1,055 household contacts of 213 MDRTB index cases and 2,362 household contacts of 487 drug-susceptible index cases

full_output.paper_title: Development of a multiplex PCR system and its application in detection of blaSHV, blaTEM, blaCTX-M-1, blaCTX-M-9 and blaOXA-1 group genes in clinical Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli strains.

blaSHV.source: Development of a multiplex PCR system and its application in detection of blaSHV, blaTEM, blaCTX-M-1, blaCTX-M-9 and blaOXA-1 group genes in clinical Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli strains.

blaCTX-M-1.source: Development of a multiplex PCR system and its application in detection of blaSHV, blaTEM, blaCTX-M-1, blaCTX-M-9 and blaOXA-1 group genes in clinical Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a multiplex PCR system for the simultaneous detection of blaSHV, blaTEM, blaCTX-M-1, blaCTX-M-9, and blaOXA-1 group genes in clinical Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli strains, demonstrating high specificity and sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR system development and validation using reference strains and clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance to Isoniazid and Ethionamide in Mycobacterium tuberculosis: Genes, Mutations, and Causalities.
