full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple copy number variations and single nucleotide polymorphisms in genes associated with oxaborole resistance in Trypanosoma brucei, indicating a complex genetic basis for resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing of oxaborole-resistant and revertant T. brucei cell lines, along with chemical proteomic profiling.
full_output.sample_size: Five T. brucei lines including parental, resistant, and revertant clones.

full_output.paper_title: Drug-protein hydrogen bonds govern the inhibition of the ATP hydrolysis of the multidrug transporter P-glycoprotein.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: switch from inhibition to stimulation of ATPase activity

P-gp.notes: Mutation of Y307 leads to switch from inhibition to stimulation of ATPase activity

full_output.paper_title: Rapid antibiotic-resistance predictions from genome sequence data for Staphylococcus aureus and Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

mecA.mechanism: mediates resistance to β-lactam antibiotics by altering the target site

rpoB.notes: Mutation in rpoB gene associated with rifampicin resistance.

fusA.notes: Mutation in fusA gene associated with linezolid resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents Mykrobe predictor, a software tool that rapidly predicts antibiotic resistance from genome sequence data for Staphylococcus aureus and Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It identifies resistance genes such as mecA and detects mutations like S84L in gyrA that confer resistance to specific antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and computational analysis combined with phenotypic testing to validate resistance predictions.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic regimen based on population analysis of residing persister cells eradicates Staphylococcus epidermidis biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified three subpopulations within S. epidermidis biofilms: normal cells, dormant cells, and tolerant-but-killable (TBK) cells. It demonstrated that antibiotic regimens targeting dormant cells can effectively eradicate biofilms.
full_output.methodology: The study used population analysis, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and scanning electron microscopy to analyze biofilm subpopulations and evaluate antibiotic efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: New Clinical Strain of Neisseria gonorrhoeae with Decreased Susceptibility to Ceftriaxone, Japan.

mutations_found.validated_by: sequencing results of the penA gene
sequencing results of the penA gene
sequencing results of the penA gene

penA.notes: The strain GU140106 has the same A311V and T483S substitutions as strain H041, but it has substitution V316T instead of V316P.
penA.evidence_note: The presence of substitutions A311V, V316P, and T483S was reported to be responsible for resistance to ceftriaxone ( 7 ).

full_output.key_findings: A new clinical strain of Neisseria gonorrhoeae (GU140106) with decreased susceptibility to ceftriaxone was identified. The strain exhibited substitutions in the penA gene encoding penicillin-binding protein 2, namely A311V, V316T, and T483S, which are associated with reduced susceptibility to ceftriaxone.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of the penA gene and determination of minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) for various antimicrobial agents.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of Outcomes among Adult Patients with Nosocomial Bacteremia Caused by Methicillin-Susceptible and Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that HA-MRSA-S bacteremia was an independent risk factor for higher in-hospital mortality compared to MSSA, while CA-MRSA-S did not show a significant increase in mortality. Resistance to linezolid and daptomycin was observed in MRSA isolates.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing clinical and microbiological data from patients with nosocomial S. aureus bacteremia.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Penicillin-Type Analogues Bearing a Variable Substituted 2-Azetidinone Ring at Position 6: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reports the synthesis and biological evaluation of novel penicillin-type analogues with a substituted 2-azetidinone ring at position 6. These compounds exhibited good antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacteria, particularly Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis, with 12a showing the highest activity. However, none of the compounds showed significant activity against Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized through a series of chemical reactions involving the Staudinger reaction and subsequent coupling with 6-APA. Antimicrobial activity was determined using the broth microdilution method to calculate MIC and MLD values.

full_output.key_findings: The study found a higher prevalence of primary Helicobacter pylori resistance to levofloxacin, metronidazole, and clarithromycin in HIV-positive patients compared to HIV-negative patients.
full_output.methodology: Prospective collection of data from HIV-positive and HIV-negative patients undergoing upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, with antibiotic susceptibility testing using disk diffusion and agar dilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Draft genome sequence of Inquilinus limosus strain MP06, a multidrug-resistant clinical isolate.
full_output.key_findings: The draft genome sequence of Inquilinus limosus strain MP06 reveals multidrug resistance mechanisms, including efflux pumps and penicillin-binding proteins, contributing to resistance against various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome shotgun sequencing and genome annotation.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility profile of bacilli isolated from the skin of healthy humans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antibiotic resistance profiles of bacilli isolated from human skin, highlighting resistance to several broad-spectrum antibiotics, including ceftazidime, nalidixic acid, ampicillin, and tetracycline. Notably, Dermabactor isolates showed resistance to vancomycin, which was previously reported as susceptible.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility was determined using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic effects of sulbactam in multi-drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro efficacy of antibiotic combinations involving sulbactam against multi-drug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii strains, identifying synergistic effects in certain combinations.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility tests and Etest were used to assess the efficacy of antibiotic combinations against A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and genetic diversity of Escherichia coli isolated from humans and foods.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 34.6% of E. coli isolates were antimicrobial resistant, with tetracycline resistance being the most frequent. High levels of multidrug resistance were observed, particularly in isolates from humans and foods of animal origin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method, and genetic diversity was assessed via pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE).

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of Escherichia coli and Salmonella spp. from free-ranging wild animals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various virulence genes in E. coli strains isolated from free-ranging wild animals, highlighting differences in virulence gene profiles and antimicrobial resistance patterns between animals from different geographical locations. Resistance to multiple antimicrobial classes was observed in strains from areas with higher anthropogenic impact.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using disk diffusion method.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC-2 as a gene conferring resistance to carbapenems in tigecycline-nonsusceptible Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.
full_output.methodology: Polymerase chain reaction and sequencing were used to identify carbapenemase and 16S rRNA methylase genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Review article: the global emergence of Helicobacter pylori antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the global emergence of antibiotic resistance in Helicobacter pylori, highlighting increasing resistance rates to clarithromycin, metronidazole, and levofloxacin, among others, and emphasizes the need for localized resistance testing to guide treatment.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of resistance data from various regions.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive Characterization of Escherichia coli O104:H4 Isolated from Patients in the Netherlands.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in EAEC Stx2a+ O104:H4 isolates, including bla TEM-1, bla CTX-M-15, dfrA7, sul1, sul2, and tetA, which conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as ampicillin, cefotaxime, ceftazidime, cefepime, cefuroxime, trimethoprim, sulfamethoxazole, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic resistance testing were used to characterize the AMR genes and mutations in the isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Seven isolates from 2011 and 2013, including those from a HUS patient and her friend.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and Functional Characterization of qnr-Encoding Plasmids from Municipal Wastewater Biosolid Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two types of plasmids harboring qnr genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from municipal wastewater biosolids. One plasmid, pKPSH-11XL, was a large multidrug-resistant IncF plasmid containing qnrB, beta-lactamase genes, tetracycline resistance genes, aminoglycoside resistance genes, and chloramphenicol resistance genes. Another group of smaller plasmids contained qnrS and other resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, transformation, and MIC testing were used to characterize the plasmids and their resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic Heterogeneity Affects Stenotrophomonas maltophilia K279a Colony Morphotypes and β-Lactamase Expression.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla L1 and bla L2 as the primary β-lactam resistance genes in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia K279a, demonstrating their upregulation in response to ampicillin and their role in phenotypic heterogeneity.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq, promoter fusions, and whole genome sequencing were used to analyze gene expression and identify resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Resistance Determinants, In Vitro Time-Kill Curve Analysis and Pharmacodynamic Functions for the Novel Topoisomerase II Inhibitor ETX0914 (AZD0914) in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

gyrB.mechanism: Mutations in gyrB (D429N, D429A, K450T) confer resistance to ETX0914

mutations_found.protein_change: Aspartic acid to Alanine at position 429

gyrB.notes: Mutations in gyrB result in reduced susceptibility to ETX0914

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the D429A mutation in GyrB as a resistance mechanism to ETX0914 and demonstrates that inactivation of the MtrCDE efflux pump restores susceptibility to wild-type levels in resistant mutants.
full_output.methodology: Mutant selection, susceptibility testing, time-kill curve analysis, and pharmacodynamic modeling.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin Resistant Staphylococci: Prevalence and susceptibility patterns in a burn center in Ahvaz from 2013-2014.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and coagulase-negative staphylococci (MRCoNS) in a burn center in Ahvaz, Iran. The mecA gene was identified as the primary determinant of methicillin resistance in these isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR and Etest were used to detect methicillin resistance and the mecA gene in staphylococcal isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Safety Evaluation of the Coagulase-Negative Staphylococci Microbiota of Salami: Superantigenic Toxin Production and Antimicrobial Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various staphylococcal enterotoxin genes (sea, seb, sec, sed, see, seg, seh, sei, selm, seln, selo, and tstH1) in coagulase-negative staphylococci (CNS) strains isolated from salami. These strains exhibited multiresistance to several antimicrobials, including β-lactams, vancomycin, and linezolid.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, real-time RT-PCR, ELISA, and sequencing to identify and characterize enterotoxin genes and antimicrobial resistance in CNS strains from salami.

full_output.paper_title: Expression and Functions of CreD, an Inner Membrane Protein in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CreD as a critical inner membrane protein involved in maintaining cell envelope integrity in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia. Deletion of creD leads to morphological abnormalities, compromised cell envelope integrity, and increased outer membrane permeability, triggering the σ E -mediated envelope stress response.
full_output.methodology: The study uses molecular genetics, transcriptional fusion assays, and various biochemical and microbiological techniques to analyze the role of CreD in S. maltophilia.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and Antimicrobial Resistance of Microbes Causing Bloodstream Infections in Unguja, Zanzibar.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the presence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacteriaceae, including Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli, causing bloodstream infections in Unguja, Zanzibar. Multidrug-resistant Salmonella Typhi isolates were also identified.
full_output.methodology: Blood cultures and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted on patients with bloodstream infections.

full_output.paper_title: Biochemical and Computational Analysis of the Substrate Specificities of Cfr and RlmN Methyltransferases.

cfr.mechanism: methylation of C8 at 23S rRNA position A2503
cfr.role_in_paper: The cfr gene was reported in 2000 and identified on plasmid pSCFS1 from Staphylococcus sciuri causing resistance to florfenicol and chloramphenicol
cfr.validation_method: RNA primer extension analysis and MIC analysis
cfr.genetic_context: plasmids or in relation with transposon sequences
cfr.evidence_note: The cfr gene was reported in 2000 and identified on plasmid pSCFS1 from Staphylococcus sciuri causing resistance to florfenicol and chloramphenicol

full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the substrate specificities of Cfr and RlmN methyltransferases, focusing on their roles in modifying 23S rRNA at adenine 2503. Cfr methylates both C8 and C2, while RlmN only methylates C2. The research revealed differences in their binding affinities and structural preferences, highlighting the distinct functionalities of these enzymes despite their sequence similarities.
full_output.methodology: The study combined biochemical experiments and computational modeling to analyze the substrate specificities of Cfr and RlmN methyltransferases.

full_output.paper_title: Outbreak of a beta-lactam resistant non-typeable Haemophilus influenzae sequence type 14 associated with severe clinical outcomes.

ftsI.notes: The mutation in the ftsI gene encoding penicillin-binding protein (PBP) 3 was associated with high MIC-values of ampicillin, cefuroxime and cefotaxime.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a beta-lactam resistant non-typeable Haemophilus influenzae sequence type 14 with a mutation in the ftsI gene encoding penicillin-binding protein (PBP) 3, which conferred resistance to ampicillin, cefuroxime, and cefotaxime.
full_output.methodology: The study performed MIC testing, molecular typing, and phylogenetic analysis to characterize the outbreak strain.

full_output.paper_title: Crystal Structure of OXA-58 with the Substrate-Binding Cleft in a Closed State: Insights into the Mobility and Stability of the OXA-58 Structure.

blaOXA-58.validation_method: structural analysis and enzymatic activity measurements

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the OXA-58 beta-lactamase from Acinetobacter baumannii, revealing its structure and the role of specific residues in its stability and activity.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis and enzymatic activity measurements of OXA-58 and its mutants.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the intrinsic and acquired antibiotic resistance mechanisms in Clostridium difficile, including tetracycline resistance mediated by tet(M), macrolide/lincosamide/streptogramin B resistance mediated by erm(B), chloramphenicol resistance mediated by catP, and multidrug resistance mediated by cfr.
full_output.methodology: Experimental validation of antibiotic resistance genes and mutations in Clostridium difficile.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of novel cyclic lipopeptides from a positional scanning combinatorial library with enhanced antibacterial and antibiofilm activities.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cyclic lipopeptide 3 as a novel compound with enhanced antibacterial and antibiofilm activities against ESKAPE pathogens, demonstrating effectiveness against both planktonic and biofilm-forming bacteria without significant toxicity.
full_output.methodology: Combinatorial library screening, MIC testing, biofilm disruption assays, and in vivo wound infection models were used to evaluate the antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of cyclic lipopeptides.

full_output.paper_title: Non-Typhoidal Salmonella in poultry meat and diarrhoeic patients: prevalence, antibiogram, virulotyping, molecular detection and sequencing of class I integrons in multidrug resistant strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes, including aac(3)-Id, aadA2, aadA4, aadA7, dfrA15, lnuF, sat, and estX, in multidrug-resistant Salmonella strains isolated from poultry meat and diarrheic patients in Egypt.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect and characterize AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemic spread of Pandoraea pulmonicola in a cystic fibrosis center.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes an epidemic spread of Pandoraea pulmonicola in a cystic fibrosis center, highlighting its resistance to multiple antibiotics including beta-lactams, ciprofloxacin, and colistin, while showing susceptibility to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial identification using ARDRA, 16S rDNA sequencing, and MALDI-TOF MS, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing via disk diffusion and E-test methods.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Interactions of Antibiotic Combinations of Colistin, Tigecycline, and Doripenem Against Extensively Drug-Resistant and Multidrug-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the synergistic activity of colistin, doripenem, and tigecycline combinations against extensively drug-resistant (XDR) and multidrug-resistant (MDR) Acinetobacter baumannii. The colistin-doripenem combination showed the highest rate of synergy and bactericidal activity, while the doripenem-tigecycline combination had the lowest synergy rate and higher antagonistic interactions.
full_output.methodology: Time-kill assays were performed for 69 clinical isolates of A. baumannii using colistin, doripenem, and tigecycline combinations.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Synergistic Effects of Antimicrobial Combinations on Extensively Drug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified metallo-beta-lactamases (blaIMP-1, blaVIM-2, blaSIM-1) and OXA-23 carbapenemases in XDR P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii isolates, highlighting their role in carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of AMR genes and in vitro synergy testing of antimicrobial combinations.
full_output.sample_size: 77 XDR GNFB isolates (43 P. aeruginosa and 34 A. baumannii)

full_output.paper_title: Xpert CARBA-R Assay for the Detection of Carbapenemase-Producing Organisms in Intensive Care Unit Patients of a Korean Tertiary Care Hospital

blaVIM.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the CARBA-R assay detects blaVIM, blaIMP, blaNDM, blaKPC, and blaOXA-48-like alleles.

full_output.key_findings: The Xpert CARBA-R assay detected carbapenemase-producing organisms (CPO) in ICU patients, identifying blaVIM, blaIMP, and blaKPC genes as responsible for carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used the Xpert CARBA-R assay and conventional culture methods to detect CPO in clinical stool and rectal swab samples.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations That Enhance the Ciprofloxacin Resistance of Escherichia coli with qnrA1.

qnrA1.validation_method: experimental validation through MIC testing and sequencing

mutations_found.position_in_molecule: upstream of the marR start codon
mutations_found.origin: mutants selected from J53(pMG252) with qnrA1

marR.notes: mutation in the MarR binding site
marR.evidence_note: The paper describes mutations in marR that lead to increased expression of marA and soxS, which in turn increase the expression of the AcrAB pump, leading to increased ciprofloxacin resistance. The specific mutation TA to AC 22 bp upstream from the marR start codon is mentioned.

mutations_found.origin: mutants with increased expression of soxS

soxR.evidence_note: The paper states that two strains with SoxR mutations had 10- to 12-fold overexpression of soxS, establishing that in these mutants, SoxR was constitutively active.

gyrA.notes: mutation in the quinolone resistance-determining region

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in marR and soxR that enhance ciprofloxacin resistance in E. coli with qnrA1 by increasing the expression of efflux pumps. Additionally, mutations in rfaE and rfaD were linked to novobiocin hypersusceptibility, and decreased ompF expression contributed to reduced ciprofloxacin susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study used MIC testing, whole-genome sequencing, and RT-qPCR to analyze mutations and gene expression in E. coli mutants.

full_output.paper_title: In Vivo Characterization of the Activation and Interaction of the VanR-VanS Two-Component Regulatory System Controlling Glycopeptide Antibiotic Resistance in Two Related Streptomyces Species.

vanR.notes: The T69S mutation in the REC domain of VanRst allows activation independent of VanS.
vanR.evidence_note: The paper states that the T69S mutation in the REC domain of VanRst allows activation independent of VanS.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the VanR-VanS two-component system in Streptomyces coelicolor and Streptomyces toyocaensis, highlighting the role of specific amino acid residues in the REC domain of VanR in determining glycopeptide resistance. A T69S mutation in VanR was found to enable VanR activation without the need for VanS.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized site-directed mutagenesis, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and gene expression analysis to investigate the functionality of the VanR-VanS system.

full_output.paper_title: Impairment of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Biofilm Resistance to Antibiotics by Combining the Drugs with a New Quorum-Sensing Inhibitor.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that the quorum-sensing inhibitor C11 significantly reduces the expression of quorum-sensing (QS) regulatory genes (rhlR, rhlI, lasR, lasI) and QS-regulated virulence genes (rhlA, lasB) in Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms, thereby impairing biofilm resistance to antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized quantitative reverse transcriptase PCR (qRT-PCR) to analyze gene expression and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) to assess biofilm structure and viability.

full_output.paper_title: The Staphylococcus aureus Chaperone PrsA Is a New Auxiliary Factor of Oxacillin Resistance Affecting Penicillin-Binding Protein 2A.
full_output.key_findings: PrsA is a chaperone protein that contributes to oxacillin resistance by influencing the membrane levels of PBP2A in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, western blot, and MIC assays were used to investigate the role of PrsA in oxacillin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: A cell wall damage response mediated by a sensor kinase/response regulator pair enables beta-lactam tolerance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the WigKR two-component system as critical for Vibrio cholerae's tolerance to beta-lactam antibiotics. WigKR is involved in responding to cell wall damage and regulating cell wall synthesis, enabling the bacterium to recover from the spherical, non-dividing state induced by antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic screens, mutant analysis, RNA sequencing, and biochemical assays to investigate the role of the WigKR system in beta-lactam tolerance and cell wall homeostasis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaCTX-M-15 and blaSHV-28 genes as the primary mechanisms of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) production in Enterobacteriaceae isolates from nursing home residents.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify ESBL-producing organisms.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli Population Structure and Antibiotic Resistance at a Buffalo/Cattle Interface in Southern Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline, trimethoprim, and amoxicillin resistance genes (tet, dfrA, and blaTEM-1) in E. coli strains from buffalo and cattle populations in Zimbabwe, highlighting the role of human-animal interfaces in the dissemination of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used phenotypic and genotypic characterization techniques, including PCR and sequencing, to analyze antibiotic resistance in E. coli strains from buffalo and cattle populations.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro selection of miltefosine resistance in promastigotes of Leishmania donovani from Nepal: genomic and metabolomic characterization.

LdMT.notes: Mutations in LdMT contribute to miltefosine resistance.
LdMT.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that mutations in LdMT, including E197D, A691P, and ΔLdMT, confer resistance to miltefosine. The organisms observed are Leishmania donovani. The effect on function is loss of function, and the mutations are validated by genomic analysis and PCR verification.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the LdMT gene, including a deletion (ΔLdMT) and missense mutations (E197D and A691P), as key contributors to miltefosine resistance in Leishmania donovani.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, PCR verification, and metabolomic profiling were used to characterize miltefosine resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Co-Carriage of blaKPC-2 and blaNDM-1 in Clinical Isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Associated with Hospital Infections from India.

blaKPC-2.validation_method: PCR, sequencing, cloning, transformation assay, Southern hybridization
blaKPC-2.genetic_context: bla KPC-2 was present in two different locations within the host. In first, it was not associated with any mobile genetic element, whereas the second one was class 1 integron mediated attaining reverse orientation
blaKPC-2.evidence_note: The antibiotic susceptibility was done by Kirby Bauer disc-diffusion method against antibiotics viz. piperacillin-tazobactam (100/10 μg), amikacin (30 μg), gentamicin (10 μg), ciprofloxacin (5 μg), polymixin B (300 units), netilmicin (30 μg) and carbenicillin (100 μg) (Hi-Media, Mumbai, India). Minimum inhibitory concentration was performed by agar dilution method against imipenem, ertapenem, meropenem, cefepime & aztreonam and the results were compared with standard CLSI guidelines [14]. full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the first detection of integron-mediated blaKPC-2 coexisting with blaNDM-1 in Pseudomonas aeruginosa from India, highlighting the emergence of multidrug-resistant isolates carrying these carbapenemase genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, cloning, transformation assay, Southern hybridization, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Protocol: a 'One health' two year follow-up, mixed methods study on antibiotic resistance, focusing children under 5 and their environment in rural India.
full_output.key_findings: The study aimed to investigate antibiotic resistance in children and their environment in rural India, focusing on E. coli isolates from various sources. It highlighted the importance of integrated approaches to understand the spread of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study employed a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative surveys, qualitative interviews, and microbiological analyses to assess antibiotic resistance patterns in E. coli from children, animals, and environmental samples.

full_output.paper_title: Excision of staphylococcal cassette chromosome mec in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus assessed by quantitative PCR.

mecA.mechanism: confers resistance to β-lactam antibiotics by encoding a low-affinity penicillin-binding protein that prevents effective binding of β-lactam antibiotics
mecA.role_in_paper: central to the study of SCC mec excision and methicillin resistance
mecA.validation_method: demonstrated through the study of SCC mec excision and its impact on methicillin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the excision rate of the staphylococcal cassette chromosome mec (SCC mec) in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strain N315 using a quantitative PCR-based method, revealing an excision rate of approximately 2 × 10−6 under standard growth conditions.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR was used to measure the rate of SCC mec excision by amplifying the chromosome-chromosome junction and the circularized SCC mec resulting from excision.

full_output.paper_title: First identification of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius strains among coagulase-positive staphylococci isolated from dogs with otitis externa in Trinidad, West Indies.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius isolates carrying the mecA gene, marking the first report of such organisms in the Caribbean.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius strains.

full_output.paper_title: β-Lactamases Encoded by blaCTX-M Group I Genes as Determinants of Resistance of Esbl-Positive Enterobacteriaceae in European Soldiers in Tropical Mali.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaTEM-1 and blaCTX-M group I as significant contributors to β-lactam resistance in ESBL-positive Enterobacteriaceae isolated from European soldiers in Mali.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and characterize β-lactamase genes in ESBL-positive Enterobacteriaceae.

full_output.paper_title: Insights into the Mechanism of Action of Bactericidal Lipophosphonoxins.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies lipophosphonoxins (LPPOs) as a new class of bactericidal compounds that target the bacterial cell membrane, causing pore formation and cell death. These compounds showed selective cytotoxicity toward Gram-positive bacteria and did not select for resistant strains easily.
full_output.methodology: The study used microbiological assays, electron microscopy, HPLC, and lipid bilayer experiments to investigate the mechanism of action of LPPOs.

full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and characterize carbapenemase genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: ISPpu22, a novel insertion sequence in the oprD porin gene of a carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate from a burn patient in Tehran, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a novel insertion sequence, IS Ppu 22, within the oprD gene of a carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa isolate, leading to resistance through oprD mutation and AmpC overproduction. Additionally, the isolate carried the blaOXA-10 gene, contributing to resistance.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and molecular methods, including PCR, sequencing, and MIC testing, were used to analyze resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Next-Generation Sequencing of Plasmodium vivax Patient Samples Shows Evidence of Direct Evolution in Drug-Resistence Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the dhfr gene associated with pyrimethamine resistance in Plasmodium vivax and highlights the evolutionary dynamics of drug resistance genes in the parasite.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and genotyping of P. vivax isolates from the Peruvian Amazon to identify drug resistance-associated mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and Trends of Staphylococcus aureus Bacteraemia in Hospitalized Patients in South Africa, 2010 to 2012: Laboratory-Based Surveillance Mapping of Antimicrobial Resistance and Molecular Epidemiology.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in South Africa, with SCC mec type III and IV being the most common. The mecA gene was found in all MRSA isolates, contributing to methicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Laboratory-based sentinel site surveillance, including phenotypic susceptibility testing, PCR screening for mecA and mecC genes, SCC mec typing, spa-typing, and multilocus sequence typing (MLST).

full_output.paper_title: Recombinant expression, antimicrobial activity and mechanism of action of tritrpticin analogs containing fluoro-tryptophan residues.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the recombinant production of tritrpticin and its analogs containing fluoro-tryptophan residues, demonstrating their antimicrobial activity against E. coli. The fluoro-Trp residues were incorporated at high levels using a combination of calmodulin as a fusion protein and glyphosate as an inhibitor of aromatic amino acid synthesis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized recombinant expression in E. coli, purification techniques, and various biochemical assays including fluorescence spectroscopy, NMR, and membrane permeability tests.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Susceptibility Profiles of Dairy Leuconostoc, Analysis of the Genetic Basis of Atypical Resistances and Transfer of Genes In Vitro and in a Food Matrix.

erm(B).evidence_note: The erm(B) gene was amplified in Leuconostoc mesenteroides subsp. dextranicum LbE15 and was associated with a plasmid.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Leuconostoc strains, including erm(B) for erythromycin resistance, tet(S) for tetracycline resistance, and others like aadE, aphA-3, sat4, and vat(E) for aminoglycoside and virginiamycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic resistance testing, PCR, hybridization, and genome sequencing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes.

mutations_found.validated_by: toeprinting analysis and in vivo testing

ermBL.notes: Mutations of Arg7 of ErmBL can alter the cofactor recognition properties of the ribosome-ErmBL complex by primarily narrowing the small molecule specificity or abolishing ribosome stalling.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the C-terminal residue of the ErmBL nascent peptide plays a crucial role in determining the specificity of antibiotic recognition and ribosome stalling. Mutations in Arg7 and Asp10 of ErmBL affect the ability of the ribosome to distinguish between different macrolide antibiotics, thereby influencing the activation of resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized toeprinting assays, in vivo testing, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the role of the ErmBL nascent peptide in antibiotic recognition and ribosome stalling.

full_output.paper_title: Structural basis of lantibiotic recognition by the nisin resistance protein from Streptococcus agalactiae.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the nisin resistance protein Sa NSR from Streptococcus agalactiae, elucidating its structural basis for recognizing and resisting nisin, a lantibiotic. Key findings include the identification of the TASSAEM region and critical residues involved in nisin binding and catalytic activity.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography, molecular dynamics simulations, and mutagenesis studies were employed to analyze the structure and function of Sa NSR.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the processing of nonconjugative resistance plasmids by the conjugation nicking enzyme NES from Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating that NES can bind, cleave, and religate oriT sequences from plasmids like pSK156 and pCA347, although with reduced efficiency compared to its cognate pSK41 oriT.
full_output.methodology: The study used biochemical assays, structural modeling, and genetic analyses to investigate the role of NES in plasmid transfer and its interaction with various oriT sequences.

full_output.paper_title: Strong and Nonspecific Synergistic Antibacterial Efficiency of Antibiotics Combined with Silver Nanoparticles at Very Low Concentrations Showing No Cytotoxic Effect.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) significantly enhance the antibacterial efficacy of various antibiotics against Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Staphylococcus aureus at very low concentrations without causing cytotoxic effects.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized the microdilution method to evaluate the synergistic effects of antibiotics combined with AgNPs against different bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Crystal Structures of KPC-2 and SHV-1 β-Lactamases in Complex with the Boronic Acid Transition State Analog S02030
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the crystal structures of KPC-2 and SHV-1 β-lactamases in complex with the boronic acid transition state analog S02030, highlighting their roles in conferring resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis of protein-inhibitor complexes using X-ray crystallography.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the combinatorial pharmacodynamics of ceftolozane-tazobactam against β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli strains, demonstrating that tazobactam enhances the bactericidal activity of ceftolozane against various β-lactamase variants.
full_output.methodology: Time-kill studies and pharmacodynamic analyses were conducted against four E. coli strains with different β-lactamase profiles.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified and characterized the resistance mechanisms of KPC-2 and SHV-1 beta-lactamases, demonstrating the effectiveness of boronic acid transition state inhibitors (BATSIs) in restoring susceptibility to beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biochemical assays, molecular modeling, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to evaluate the efficacy of BATSIs against KPC-2 and SHV-1 beta-lactamases.

full_output.paper_title: Pneumonia Caused by Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus: Does Vancomycin Heteroresistance Matter?
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the presence of heterogeneous vancomycin-intermediate S. aureus (hVISA) was independently associated with increased inpatient mortality in patients with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) pneumonia. hVISA was determined by the 48-h population analysis profile area under the curve (PAP-AUC).
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing patients with MRSA pneumonia, using the 48-h PAP-AUC method to identify hVISA, and comparing clinical outcomes between hVISA and vancomycin-susceptible S. aureus (VSSA) infections.

full_output.paper_title: Chromosomally and Extrachromosomally Mediated High-Level Gentamicin Resistance in Streptococcus agalactiae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the aac(6')-Ie-aph(2")-Ia gene as responsible for high-level gentamicin resistance in Streptococcus agalactiae, which can be transferred via plasmid pIP501.
full_output.methodology: PCR, plasmid purification, DNA sequencing, and MIC testing were used to identify and validate the resistance mechanism.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the class C beta-lactamase CHE-1 from Enterobacter cloacae, which shows reduced sensitivity to beta-lactamase inhibitors like BAL29880 and LK157 compared to the P99 enzyme.
full_output.methodology: Purification and kinetic analysis of the CHE-1 enzyme.

full_output.paper_title: Optimized In Vitro Antibiotic Susceptibility Testing Method for Small-Colony Variant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study optimized in vitro antibiotic susceptibility testing methods for small-colony variant (SCV) Staphylococcus aureus, highlighting the importance of growth media supplementation with thymidine, hemin, and menadione to support SCV growth and stability. It found that SCVs were typically nonsusceptible to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or aminoglycosides based on their auxotrophy type, and mecA-positive SCVs were invariably resistant to cefoxitin.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated various growth media and tested antibiotic susceptibility using disk diffusion and Etest methods on 86 SCVs and 28 isogenic NCs, along with MIC determinations for select antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Small angle X-ray scattering as a high-throughput method to classify antimicrobial modes of action.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores the use of small angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) as a high-throughput method to classify the mode of action of antimicrobial agents, demonstrating its ability to detect ultrastructural changes in E. coli cells induced by various antibiotics and a short cationic antimicrobial peptide.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized SAXS and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to analyze ultrastructural changes in E. coli cells treated with different antibiotics and a short cationic antimicrobial peptide.

full_output.paper_title: Drug use and antimicrobial resistance among Escherichia coli and Enterococcus spp. isolates from chicken and turkey flocks slaughtered in Quebec, Canada.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of antimicrobial resistance in E. coli and Enterococcus spp. isolates from chicken and turkey flocks in Quebec, Canada. Resistance to tetracycline, streptomycin, and sulfisoxazole was detected in >90% of E. coli isolates, while resistance to bacitracin, erythromycin, lincomycin, quinupristin-dalfopristin, and tetracycline was observed in both chicken and turkey flocks for Enterococcus spp. isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial resistance in E. coli and Enterococcus spp. isolates from chicken and turkey flocks using minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing and examined the association between antimicrobial use and resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Klebsiella pneumoniae: Development of Carbapenem Resistance due to Acquisition of bla NDM-1 During Antimicrobial Therapy in Twin Infants with Pneumonia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the acquisition of the blaNDM-1 gene in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from twin infants with pneumonia, leading to carbapenem resistance during meropenem therapy.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and conjugation experiments were used to detect and characterize the blaNDM-1 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of a SUMO E2 Conjugating Enzyme Involved in Resistance to Clavibacter michiganensis Subsp. michiganensis in Solanum peruvianum, Through a Tomato Mottle Virus VIGS Assay.
full_output.key_findings: The SUMO E2 conjugating enzyme SCE I plays an important role in the innate immunity of Solanum peruvianum against Clavibacter michiganensis subsp. michiganensis (Cmm). Silencing of SCE I led to increased Cmm colonization and disease symptoms, indicating its involvement in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: VIGS assay using a Tomato Mottle Virus vector to silence SCE I in Solanum peruvianum, followed by assessment of Cmm infection and colonization.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility and pathogenic genes of Staphylococcus aureus isolated from the oral cavity of patients with periodontitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaZ, aph(3')-IIIa, and tem genes as responsible for penicillin, gentamicin, and ampicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from periodontitis patients.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect resistance genes and assess antimicrobial resistance patterns.

full_output.key_findings: The study focused on synthesizing and evaluating polymyxin B analogs to enhance antimicrobial activity and reduce nephrotoxicity. Several compounds showed improved activity against polymyxin-resistant strains with lower cytotoxicity compared to existing polymyxins.
full_output.methodology: The research involved chemical synthesis of polymyxin B analogs, followed by biological activity testing against bacterial strains and cytotoxicity assessments in human cell lines.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Isolated from Australian Veterinarians.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in MRSA isolates from Australian veterinarians, including erm(A), erm(C), aadD, aacA-aphD, tet(M), tet(K), dfrA, msr(A), mph(C), and vat(B). These genes were associated with resistance to erythromycin, gentamicin, tetracycline, trimethoprim, and virginiamycin.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular typing techniques, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and microarray analysis to identify AMR genes in MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical features, Outcomes and Molecular Profiles of Drug Resistance in Tuberculous Meningitis in non-HIV Patients.

full_output.methodology: Genotypic assays and MTBDRsl assays were used to detect drug resistance mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a BNA-PCR system to detect clarithromycin resistance in Mycobacterium avium-M. intracellulare complex (MAC) isolates, identifying point mutations at positions 2058 and 2059 in domain V of the 23S rRNA gene as a key resistance mechanism.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR with BNA probes was used to detect point mutations in the 23S rRNA gene associated with clarithromycin resistance in MAC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Apramycin treatment affects selection and spread of a multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli strain able to colonize the human gut in the intestinal microbiota of pigs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes in the multidrug-resistant E. coli strain 912, including aac(3)-IV, blaTEM-1, sul2, aph(4), tet(X), and strA/B, which confer resistance to various antibiotics such as gentamicin, apramycin, sulfonamides, aminoglycosides, tetracyclines, and streptomycin.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, PCR, and determination of minimum inhibitory concentration were used to identify and validate AMR genes in the E. coli strain.

full_output.paper_title: Drug resistance characteristics and cluster analysis of M. tuberculosis in Chinese patients with multiple episodes of anti-tuberculosis treatment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various mutations in genes such as rpoB, katG, gyrA, rrs, and pncA that confer resistance to first- and second-line anti-tuberculosis drugs in M. tuberculosis isolates from patients with multiple treatment histories.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic drug susceptibility testing and DNA sequencing were used to analyze drug resistance mechanisms in M. tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Association of doripenem resistance with OXA-type carbapenemases in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activities of Methanol, Ethanol and Supercritical CO2 Extracts of Philippine Piper betle L. on Clinical Isolates of Gram Positive and Gram Negative Bacteria with Transferable Multiple Drug Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activities of ethanol, methanol, and supercritical CO2 extracts of Piper betle against multiple drug resistant (MDR) bacteria, including MRSA, VRE, CRE, ESβL-producing Enterobacteriaceae, and MβL-producing P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii. The extracts showed significant antibacterial activity, with the ethanol extract demonstrating the highest potency.
full_output.methodology: The study used disc diffusion and broth microdilution methods to assess the antimicrobial activity of the extracts against MDR bacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Unearthing the Antibacterial Mechanism of Medicinal Clay: A Geochemical Approach to Combating Antibiotic Resistance.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized antimicrobial susceptibility testing, metal solubility analysis, speciation modeling, bioimaging techniques, and genetic responses evaluation to investigate the antibacterial mechanism of Oregon Blue clay.
