full_output.key_findings: The study identified hypermutator Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from patients with cystic fibrosis in Australia, highlighting the role of mutations in mutL and mutS in the hypermutator phenotype and increased antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and mutation frequency analysis were used to characterize the hypermutator isolates and identify mutations in mutL and mutS.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial Cytological Profiling as a Tool To Study Mechanisms of Action of Antibiotics That Are Active against Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified that the compound NSC145612 inhibits the growth of Acinetobacter baumannii by targeting RNA transcription, and resistant mutants were found to have mutations in the rpoB gene, which is responsible for rifampin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial cytological profiling (BCP) was used to analyze the mechanism of action of antibiotics, and resistant mutants were isolated and characterized through genome sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae colonising the gut of adult rural population in South India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug resistance genes including blaCTX-M, blaCIT, blaKPC-1, and blaNDM-1 in Enterobacteriaceae colonizing the gut of adult rural populations in South India.
full_output.methodology: Faecal samples were screened for Enterobacteriaceae resistant to commonly used antibiotics using standard methods, followed by phenotypic detection of ESBL, AmpC, and carbapenemases, and polymerase chain reaction to detect specific resistance genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified SCCmec types II and V as predominant among methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci (MR-CoNS) in the northeastern region of India. The mecA gene was detected in 53.84% of the MR-CoNS isolates.
full_output.methodology: Environmental and food samples were analyzed using cefoxitin disc and PCR techniques for mecA and mecC gene detection, followed by SCCmec typing and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptional Response of AcrEF-TolC against Fluoroquinolone and Carbapenem in Escherichia coli of Clinical Origin
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights that AcrEF-TolC plays a significant role in fluoroquinolone resistance in clinical isolates of Escherichia coli, alongside qnr genes and gyr region mutations.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptional analysis of AcrEF-TolC in clinical isolates exposed to fluoroquinolones and carbapenems.

full_output.paper_title: Sub-inhibitory concentration of ertapenem induces overexpression of regulator of antibiotic resistance A in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: RarA, a global regulator of the AraC-type family, was found to induce overexpression of the AcrAB-TolC efflux pump in Escherichia coli, leading to increased resistance against carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR and zone of inhibition analysis were used to assess the impact of RarA on carbapenem resistance in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Microcin PDI Inhibits Antibiotic-Resistant Strains of Escherichia coli and Shigella through a Mechanism of Membrane Disruption and Protection by Homotrimer Self-Immunity.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of mcr-5-Harboring Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica Serovar Typhimurium Isolates from Animal and Food Origin in Germany.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes mcr-5-harboring Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium isolates from Germany, identifying five distinct plasmid types carrying mcr-5.1 and confirming the mobility of the gene through conjugation.
full_output.methodology: PCR screening, whole-genome sequencing, plasmid analysis, and conjugation experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies KKL-40, a small-molecule inhibitor of trans-translation, as effective against Staphylococcus aureus and other Gram-positive bacteria, and shows that it synergizes with the antimicrobial peptide LL-37. full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution assays, synergy assays, and cytotoxicity tests to evaluate the antimicrobial activity and resistance profile of KKL-40.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity Evaluation of Tebipenem (SPR859), an Orally Available Carbapenem, against a Global Set of Enterobacteriaceae Isolates, Including a Challenge Set of Organisms.

full_output.methodology: In vitro antimicrobial susceptibility testing using broth microdilution and agar dilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel VIM-Type Metallo-β-Lactamase Variant, VIM-60, with Increased Hydrolyzing Activity against Fourth-Generation Cephalosporins in Pseudomonas aeruginosa Clinical Isolates in Japan.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli Harboring mcr-1 in a Cluster of Liver Transplant Recipients: Detection through Active Surveillance and Whole-Genome Sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1-positive Escherichia coli ST117 in a cluster of liver transplant recipients, highlighting the potential for silent dissemination of colistin resistance through asymptomatic colonization.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize mcr-1-positive isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Effect of Colistin Combined with PFK-158 against Colistin-Resistant Enterobacteriaceae.

full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the synergistic effects of colistin with PFK-158 using in vitro checkerboard assays, time-kill studies, and in vivo mouse infection models.

full_output.methodology: The study involved molecular analysis of E. faecalis isolates, including sequencing of the pbp4 gene and its promoter region, and comparison with a reference strain.

full_output.paper_title: Chemical disarming of isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies C10 as a small molecule that potentiates the activity of isoniazid (INH) and prevents the selection for INH-resistant mutants. full_output.paper_title: Microbiological profile and antibiotic susceptibility pattern of Gram-positive isolates at a tertiary care hospital.

MRSA isolates showed reduced sensitivity to several antibiotics including ciprofloxacin, erythromycin, clindamycin, and co-trimoxazole, while showing high susceptibility to linezolid, vancomycin, and teicoplanin. VRE prevalence was noted at 7.5%, with some isolates showing resistance to linezolid as well.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and risk factors of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and vancomycin-resistant enterococci infections in Zhejiang China from 2015 to 2017.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the epidemiology and risk factors of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) in Zhejiang China from 2015 to 2017. It found that MRSA and VRE detection rates decreased over time, with certain risk factors such as age over 75 years, ICU admission, and tertiary hospitals being significantly associated with higher detection rates. No vancomycin-resistant isolates were found in MRSA, and resistance rates to various antibiotics varied among different bacterial species.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting and analyzing bacterial isolates from multiple hospitals in Zhejiang China, conducting antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and performing statistical analysis to identify risk factors associated with MRSA and VRE detection.
full_output.sample_size: Data from 86 hospitals across 11 cities in Zhejiang China

full_output.paper_title: Salmonellosis: Serotypes, prevalence and multi-drug resistant profiles of Salmonella enterica in selected poultry farms, Kwara State, North Central Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of multidrug resistance in Salmonella isolates from poultry farms in Kwara State, Nigeria, with all isolates showing resistance to ampicillin, ceftazidime, and cefotaxime. Notably, Salmonella enterica ser. 6.7:d:- and S. Agama were the most prevalent serovars, highlighting the need for improved antimicrobial stewardship.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and serotyping of Salmonella from poultry samples, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Ouabain potentiates the antimicrobial activity of aminoglycosides against Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Ouabain enhances the antimicrobial activity of aminoglycosides against Staphylococcus aureus by reducing the MIC of gentamycin, amikacin, and kanamycin, and promoting cell death through increased membrane permeability and intracellular accumulation of aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: In vitro antimicrobial effect of ouabain combined with aminoglycosides was determined using checkerboard, Gentamycin uptake, and biofilm assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and antibiotic-modifying activities of fractions and compounds from Albizia adianthifolia against MDR Gram-negative enteric bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several compounds from Albizia adianthifolia with antibacterial activity against MDR Gram-negative bacteria, including stearic acid, a mixture of stigmasterol and β-sitosterol, β-sitosterol 3-O-β-D-glucopyranoside, palmatin, homomangiferin, and mangiferin. These compounds showed significant inhibitory effects against various bacterial strains, particularly demonstrating strong activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and characterization of compounds from Albizia adianthifolia roots through chromatography techniques, followed by antibacterial testing using MIC and MBC assays. The compounds were also tested in combination with antibiotics to assess synergistic effects.

full_output.paper_title: Profiling interactions of vaborbactam with metallo-β-lactamases.
full_output.key_findings: Vaborbactam shows weak inhibition of metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs) from all three subclasses (B1, B2, and B3), with lower potency compared to its inhibition of serine-β-lactamases (SBLs).
full_output.methodology: Experimental analysis of vaborbactam's interaction with various β-lactamases using biochemical assays and structural modeling.

full_output.paper_title: Development of antiseptic adaptation and cross-adapatation in selected oral pathogens in vitro.
full_output.key_findings: Oral pathogens developed increased resistance to antiseptics (chlorhexidine and cetylpyridinium chloride) and exhibited cross-adaptation to antibiotics. Changes in cell surface hydrophobicity and proteomic alterations were observed.
full_output.methodology: In vitro exposure of oral pathogens to antiseptics followed by MIC measurements and proteomic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Stable pantothenamide bioisosteres: novel antibiotics for Gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes stable pantothenamide bioisosteres that exhibit antibiotic activity against Gram-positive bacteria, targeting a unique biochemical pathway. These compounds show improved stability and activity against staphylococci and streptococci.
full_output.methodology: The research involved the synthesis and evaluation of pantothenamide derivatives, assessing their stability, antimicrobial activity, and toxicity in various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: CA-MRSA and HA-MRSA coexist in community and hospital settings in Uganda.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that CA-MRSA and HA-MRSA coexist in children in the community in eastern Uganda, with a high MRSA carriage rate of 5.7%. Both types showed multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed MRSA isolates from children using SCC mec typing, spa typing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Reaching the End of the Line: Urinary Tract Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The review discusses the challenges posed by urinary tract infections (UTIs), emphasizing the role of uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) and the increasing difficulty in treating UTIs due to antibiotic resistance. It highlights the importance of understanding UPEC pathogenesis and the development of alternative treatments such as vaccines and small-molecule inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature on UTIs, focusing on UPEC pathogenesis, antibiotic resistance, and emerging treatment strategies.

full_output.paper_title: The mechanism of error induction by the antibiotic viomycin provides insight into the fidelity mechanism of translation.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals how viomycin reduces the fidelity of mRNA decoding by stabilizing ternary complexes on the ribosome, preventing the discrimination between cognate and near-cognate tRNAs, and thus inducing translational errors.
full_output.methodology: The study used pre-steady state kinetics and mean time analysis on a cell-free protein synthesis system derived from E. coli components to investigate the effects of viomycin on translational accuracy.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-activity relationships of potentiators of the antibiotic activity of clarithromycin against Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified compound 16 as a potent potentiator of clarithromycin activity against E. coli ATCC 25922, enhancing its efficacy by 32-fold through mechanisms involving outer membrane permeabilization and efflux pump inhibition.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of various compounds for their ability to potentiate clarithromycin activity against E. coli ATCC 25922 using MIC-based assays, fluorescence-based permeabilization assays, and efflux pump inhibition studies.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance and virulence determinants of faecal Salmonella spp. isolated from slaughter animals in Benin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant Salmonella spp. carrying virulence genes including invA, spvR, spvC, fimA, and stn. These genes are associated with invasion, systemic infection, adhesion, and stress response.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: NanoARG: A web service for analyzing antibiotic resistance genes from nanopore metagenomes
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various antibiotic resistance genes, including beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, tetracycline resistance genes, sulfonamide resistance genes, and macrolide resistance genes, using nanopore metagenomic sequencing.
full_output.methodology: Nanopore metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify and characterize antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Eukaryotic cell culture media affect macrolide minimum inhibitory concentrations but not resistance interpretation for foodborne pathogens.

full_output.methodology: Cloning of the ermE gene into E. coli plasmids and detection of methylase activity in resistant cells.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting ADP-ribosylation as an antimicrobial strategy.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the role of ADP-ribosylation in bacterial pathogenesis and highlights the potential of targeting ADP-ribosylation as an antimicrobial strategy. It covers the mechanisms of ADP-ribosylation, the enzymes involved, and the implications for antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature on ADP-ribosylation in bacterial systems and its potential as an antimicrobial target.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Cells Translocated with Yersinia Yops in Infected Tissues Using β-Lactamase Fusions.

full_output.paper_title: An agonist of the MscL channel affects multiple bacterial species and increases membrane permeability and potency of common antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the compound 011A increases membrane permeability and potentiates the effect of antibiotics by activating the MscL channel in multiple bacterial species, including Staphylococcus aureus and Mycobacterium smegmatis. full_output.paper_title: Pulmonary Mycobacterium abscessus Subspecies abscessus Disease That Showed a Discrepancy Between the Genotype and Phenotype of Clarithromycin Resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic & genotypic profile of antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas species in hospitalized patients.

full_output.methodology: The study used phenotypic and genotypic methods including disc-diffusion, E-test, and PCR-based detection of beta-lactamase-encoding genes to analyze antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic & genotypic study of antimicrobial profile of bacteria isolates from environmental samples.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes including tetracycline resistance genes (tetA, tetB, tetC, tetD, tetE, tetG, tetM, tetS), sulfonamide resistance genes (sul1, sul2, sul3), beta-lactamase genes (blaTEM, blaCTX-M), quinolone resistance genes (qnrA, qnrB, qnrS), and chloramphenicol resistance genes (cat1, cat2, cmlA) in Gram-negative bacteria from environmental samples.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and characterize AMR genes in bacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization & epidemiology of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii collected across India.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from India, identifying bla OXA-51-like, bla OXA-23-like, bla NDM-like, bla PER-like, and bla TEM-like genes as major contributors to carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and multilocus sequence typing were used to analyze AMR genes and genetic diversity.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance, virulence & plasmid profiles among clinical isolates of Shigella serogroups.

gyr B.notes: novel mutation associated with quinolone resistance

par C.notes: novel mutations associated with quinolone resistance
par C.evidence_note: The paper mentions 'novel mutations in gyr B, par C and par E genes' and 'mutations were observed at codon 83 in the gyr A gene and at codon 80 in the par C gene which resulted in the replacement of serine by leucine and isoleucine, respectively.' Additionally, 'novel mutations were observed in gyr B (Gln776 to Leu) and par C (Gln506 to Leu and Arg86 to Cys) genes.'

par E.notes: novel mutation associated with quinolone resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes including bla OXA-1, bla TEM-1B, qnr S1, dfr A1, aad A1, sul II, tet B, and cat A1 in Shigella isolates. Additionally, novel mutations in gyr A, gyr B, par C, and par E genes were observed, contributing to quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in Shigella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Heterogeneity of macrolide-lincosamide-streptogramin phenotype & conjugal transfer of erm(B) in Pediococcus pentosaceus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the erm(B) and msr(C) genes in Pediococcus pentosaceus isolates, which confer resistance to macrolide-lincosamide-streptogramin B antibiotics. The erm(B) gene was successfully transferred to Enterococcus faecalis via conjugation.
full_output.methodology: PCR, Southern hybridization, conjugation experiments, and MIC testing were used to characterize AMR genes and their transferability.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic-resistant Enterobacteriaceae in healthy gut flora: A report from north Indian semiurban community.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 70.5% of Enterobacteriaceae isolates from stool samples were antibiotic-resistant, with the most common resistance genes being TEM, SHV, OXA-1, CTXM-1, CTXM-2, CTXM-9, and CTXM-8/25, primarily conferring resistance to cephalosporins and beta-lactams. Low levels of carbapenem resistance were observed, with VIM detected in only one isolate.
full_output.methodology: Stool samples were analyzed using MALDI-TOF MS for identification and disc diffusion for susceptibility testing. Multiplex PCR was used to detect resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: CTX-M type extended-spectrum β-lactamase in Escherichia coli isolated from extra-intestinal infections in a tertiary care hospital in south India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaCTX-M-15 as the dominant extended-spectrum β-lactamase gene in E. coli isolates from extra-intestinal infections in a tertiary care hospital in South India.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology & therapeutic options of carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Carbapenem resistance in Gram-negative bacteria is rising, with bla_NDM being the most prevalent gene, followed by bla_VIM. Fosfomycin showed high efficacy against carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae, while colistin was effective against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter spp.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Presence & mobility of antimicrobial resistance in Gram-negative bacteria from environmental samples in coastal Karnataka, India
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes, including blaCTX-M, blaTEM, tetA, qnrA, qnrS, and sul, in Gram-negative bacteria from environmental samples in coastal Karnataka, India. These genes were found to be mobile through plasmids and phages, highlighting their potential for horizontal gene transfer.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR-based detection of AMR genes, and analysis of plasmid and phage DNA.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of phylogenetically diverse and fluoroquinolone resistant Salmonella Enteritidis as a cause of invasive nontyphoidal Salmonella disease in Ghana.

gyrA.notes: Mutations promoted from gene entry 'gyrA' (model emitted mutations_found inside genes).

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies fluoroquinolone resistance in Salmonella Enteritidis isolates from Ghana, primarily due to gyrA mutations at codon 87. These mutations were found in isolates belonging to the global epidemic clade, indicating both local emergence and potential importation of resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and Etest MIC determination were used to identify and characterize AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Biochemical changes associated with alpha-difluoromethylornithine uptake and resistance in Trypanosoma brucei.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that resistance to alpha-difluoromethylornithine (DFMO) in Trypanosoma brucei is not due to increased ornithine decarboxylase (ODC) activity or gene amplification, but rather to elevated intracellular ornithine levels that compete with DFMO for ODC binding, thereby protecting the enzyme from inactivation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biochemical assays, including ODC activity measurements, radiolabeling experiments, and nucleic acid analysis to investigate DFMO resistance mechanisms in T. brucei.

GSTP1.validation_method: protein overexpression and cell viability assays

full_output.key_findings: GST P1-1 mediates cisplatin resistance by sequestering and inactivating cisplatin through its cysteine residues, particularly C101. Mutations at C47 and C101 reduce this protective effect.
full_output.methodology: Protein overexpression, cell viability assays, ESI-MS, and X-ray crystallography.

full_output.paper_title: Microevolution of antimicrobial resistance and biofilm formation of Salmonella Typhimurium during persistence on pig farms.

sopE.encodes: type III secretion system effector protein

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes multiple antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in Salmonella Typhimurium and S. 4,[5],12:i:- strains, highlighting the presence of genes such as blaTEM, strA, strB, sul2, tetA, aadA1, aph, cmI, dfrA12, mefB, qacH, and SGI-4, which confer resistance to various antibiotics and heavy metals. Additionally, the study identifies the acquisition of plasmids carrying AMR genes on certain farms, contributing to the persistence of these strains on pig farms.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella strains isolated from pig farms.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of C-nucleoside Antimicrobials from Streptomyces albus DSM 40763: Strepturidin is Pseudouridimycin.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the biosynthesis of pseudouridimycin (PUM) and identifies a gene cluster (sap) involved in its production. The compound PUM was found to inhibit bacterial RNA polymerase, showing selective antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, bioinformatics analysis, and biochemical characterization were used to identify and analyze the sap gene cluster and its role in PUM biosynthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm formation by multidrug resistant Enterobacteriaceae strains isolated from solid organ transplant recipients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes, including blaCTX-M, blaSHV, blaOXA-48, and AmpC, in multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae strains isolated from solid organ transplant recipients.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to characterize antibiotic resistance genes in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and prioritization of macrolide resistance genes with hypothetical annotation in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and prioritizes hypothetical genes associated with macrolide resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae, focusing on domains of unknown function (DUFs) that may play roles in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The research employed gene expression analysis, differential expression, and bioinformatics tools to identify and prioritize genes linked to macrolide resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic amplification of chromosome 7 in the Doxorubicin resistant K562 cell line.

ABCB1.validation_method: array-based comparative genomic hybridization (aCGH) and qRT-PCR

full_output.key_findings: Genomic amplification of chromosome 7, specifically the 7q21.12 region containing the ABCB1 gene, leads to overexpression of ABCB1 and multidrug resistance (MDR) in the Doxorubicin-resistant K562 cell line.
full_output.methodology: Array-based comparative genomic hybridization (aCGH) and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) were used to analyze genomic amplification and gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility patterns of Staphylococcus aureus strains isolated at the Yaounde Central Hospital, Cameroon: a retro prospective study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains were highly resistant to several antibiotics including cefoxitin, cotrimoxazole, vancomycin, lincomycin, tobramycin, doxycycline, kanamycin, and erythromycin, with rifampicin showing high susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antibiotic susceptibility patterns of 250 S. aureus strains using disk diffusion method and EUCAST guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Persister cells are not slow growers but undergo SOS-induced filamentation and recovery

lexA.encodes: transcriptional repressor of the SOS response

mutations_found.validated_by: MIC testing and fluorescence reporter assay

lexA.notes: Mutations in the SOS regulon affect persister cell formation

mutations_found.validated_by: MIC testing and fluorescence reporter assay

sulA.notes: SulA deletion impacts persister cell recovery

mutations_found.validated_by: MIC testing and fluorescence reporter assay

tisAB.notes: TisAB deletion does not alter persister cell frequency

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the behavior of persister cells to ofloxacin in Escherichia coli, highlighting that these cells are not necessarily slow growers and can originate from metabolically active cells. It also shows that persister cells undergo filamentation and resume growth after antibiotic removal, with variations in SOS response induction and DNA damage levels.
full_output.methodology: Single-cell imaging and fluorescence microscopy were used to track persister cells in real-time, along with SOS response monitoring using a psulA::gfp reporter.

full_output.paper_title: An MLST approach to support tracking of plasmids carrying OXA-48-like carbapenemase.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the OXA-48-like carbapenemase genes blaOXA-48, blaOXA-181, and blaOXA-244 in various Enterobacteriaceae isolates, highlighting the diversity of plasmid backgrounds and the importance of MLST in tracking their spread.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, plasmid mapping, and MLST were used to characterize the resistance genes and their genetic environments.

full_output.paper_title: The YIN and YANG of lipoproteins in developing and preventing infectious arthritis by Staphylococcus aureus.

lgt.mechanism: loss of function leads to immune evasion

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that lipoproteins from Staphylococcus aureus can induce arthritis through TLR2, while a mutant lacking the lgt gene (which affects lipoprotein lipidation) causes more severe inflammation due to immune evasion. Coinjection of lipoproteins with S. aureus enhances bacterial elimination.
full_output.methodology: In vivo infection experiments, flow cytometry, and molecular biology techniques were used to analyze the role of lipoproteins and the lgt gene in arthritis development and immune response.

full_output.paper_title: Serotype-specific evolutionary patterns of antimicrobial-resistant Salmonella enterica.

aac(6')-Iaa.mechanism: chromosomal-encoded aminoglycoside acetyltransferase that acetylates tobramycin, kanamycin, and amikacin

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes, including aadB, cmlA, blaCARB, sulI, aadA, tetRG, tetG, strB, sulII, strA, tetA, tetR, and blaCMY, which are significantly over- or under-represented in different Salmonella serotypes.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide analysis and annotation of 90 AMR S. enterica isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic determination of resistance and heteroresistance to clarithromycin in Helicobacter pylori isolates from antrum and corpus of Colombian symptomatic patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of clarithromycin resistance in H. pylori isolates from Colombian patients, with 38.1% of isolates showing resistance. Mutations in the 23S rDNA gene, specifically A2142G and A2143G, were associated with resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing of the 23S rDNA gene to detect mutations associated with clarithromycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Lugdunin amplifies innate immune responses in the skin in synergy with host- and microbiota-derived factors.
full_output.key_findings: Lugdunin enhances innate immune responses in the skin, leading to reduced Staphylococcus aureus colonization through the induction of antimicrobial peptides like LL-37 and CXCL8, and synergistic interactions with host and microbiota-derived factors.
full_output.methodology: Experimental analysis of lugdunin's effects on keratinocytes and mouse skin, including cytokine expression, immune cell recruitment, and antimicrobial synergy studies.

full_output.paper_title: Minimal exposure of lipid II cycle intermediates triggers cell wall antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that the in vivo efficacy gap of cell wall antibiotics is due to the asymmetric distribution of lipid II cycle intermediates, which leads to inefficient sequestration of lipid carriers by antibiotics targeting small pools. Cooperative drug-target interactions, such as those seen in vancomycin, significantly enhance antibiotic efficacy by overcoming this buffering effect.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a computational model of the lipid II cycle to predict antibiotic efficacy and validate findings with experimental data on antibiotic binding and cell wall synthesis rates.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that urban wildlife in Nairobi carry high levels of multidrug-resistant E. coli, with resistance to multiple antibiotic classes, including beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, and aminoglycosides. However, no specific AMR genes or mutations were experimentally characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: The study used antimicrobial susceptibility testing of E. coli isolates from wildlife, humans, livestock, and environmental samples to assess resistance patterns.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline- and erythromycin-resistant bacteria in aerosols and manures from animal farms in China, highlighting the diversity and potential health risks associated with these resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study used high-throughput sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene to analyze bacterial communities in aerosols and manures from different animal farms.

full_output.paper_title: High Prevalence of USA300 Among Clinical Isolates of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus on St. Kitts and Nevis, West Indies.

mph(C).encodes: macrolide, lincosamide, and streptogramin B resistance
mph(C).evidence_note: The paper mentions that 'nearly all isolates carried genes encoding resistance to streptomycin [ant(6)-Ia], amikacin and other aminoglycosides [aph(3')-III], fosfomycin (fosD), macrolides, lincosamides and streptogramins [mph(C) and mrs(A)], and penicillin (blaZ)'.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) on St. Kitts and Nevis, with the USA300-NAE lineage being the dominant clone. Several AMR genes were detected, including those conferring resistance to streptomycin, amikacin, fosfomycin, macrolides, lincosamides, streptogramin B, penicillin, trimethoprim, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and in silico analysis were used to identify AMR genes and assess genetic diversity among MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity, Virulence, and Clinical Significance of Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase- and pAmpC-Producing Escherichia coli From Companion Animals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) and plasmid-mediated AmpC (pAmpC) genes in E. coli isolates from companion animals, highlighting the prevalence of bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-14, and bla CTX-M-55 as the most common ESBL genotypes, along with bla CMY-2 as the primary pAmpC gene. These findings underscore the clinical significance of these resistance mechanisms in veterinary settings.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR product sequencing to characterize ESBL and pAmpC genes in E. coli isolates from companion animals.

full_output.paper_title: The Emergence of Chromosomally Located bla (CTX-M-55) in Salmonella From Foodborne Animals in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the chromosomal location of bla CTX-M-55 in Salmonella isolates from foodborne animals in China, highlighting its association with resistance to cephalosporins and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the presence and characteristics of bla CTX-M-55 in Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: 3-Benzyl-Hexahydro-Pyrrolo[1,2-a]Pyrazine-1,4-Dione Extracted From Exiguobacterium indicum Showed Anti-biofilm Activity Against Pseudomonas aeruginosa by Attenuating Quorum Sensing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 3-Benzyl-hexahydro-pyrrolo[1,2-a]pyrazine-1,4-dione as a compound with anti-quorum sensing and anti-biofilm activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa without affecting planktonic growth.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular identification, GC-MS, and bioassays to characterize the active compound and its effects on P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Genome Analysis of Uropathogenic Morganella morganii Strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified hemolysin genes hpmA and hlyA in uropathogenic Morganella morganii strains, with hlyA being associated with hemolytic activity and cytotoxicity towards T-24 bladder carcinoma cells.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR amplification, and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify and characterize hemolysin genes in M. morganii strains.
full_output.sample_size: Three strains (MM 1, MM 4, MM 190) isolated from urine samples of patients with community-acquired urinary tract infections.

full_output.paper_title: Conjugative Transfer of the pVA1-Type Plasmid Carrying the pirAB(vp) Genes Results in the Formation of New AHPND-Causing Vibrio.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the conjugative transfer of the pVA1-type plasmid carrying the pirAB(vp) genes, which leads to the formation of new AHPND-causing Vibrio strains. This plasmid was successfully transferred from V. parahaemolyticus to V. campbellii, resulting in the acquisition of virulence properties.
full_output.methodology: Conjugation experiments, PCR, RT-PCR, and challenge studies were used to validate the transfer and functionality of the pVA1-type plasmid.
full_output.sample_size: Various Vibrio strains from different locations were analyzed.

full_output.paper_title: Selection and characterization of ultrahigh potency designed ankyrin repeat protein inhibitors of C. difficile toxin B.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes DARPins, including 1.4E, U3, and the dimeric DLD-4, which effectively neutralize C. difficile toxin B by interfering with its interaction with cellular receptors CSPG4 and FZD2.
full_output.methodology: Phage panning, ELISA, cell viability assays, and in vivo mouse models were used to characterize the DARPins.

full_output.paper_title: A novel Zn chelate (TSOL) that moves systemically in citrus plants inhibits growth and biofilm formation of bacterial pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimicrobial properties of a novel Zn-chelate, TSOL, against Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri (Xcc) and Liberibacter crescens (Lcr), demonstrating its ability to inhibit growth and biofilm formation. TSOL shows superior systemic movement in citrus plants compared to ZnO.
full_output.methodology: The study uses in vitro batch cultures and microfluidic chambers to assess the antimicrobial effects of TSOL and ZnO on Xcc and Lcr, along with plant uptake experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Synthetic Phosphodiester-Linked 4-Amino-4-deoxy-l-arabinose Derivatives Demonstrate that ArnT is an Inverting Aminoarabinosyl Transferase.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the ArnT enzyme from Burkholderia cenocepacia as an inverting aminoarabinosyl transferase that specifically accepts the alpha-neryl derivative of 4-amino-4-deoxy-l-arabinose phosphate for the transfer of Ara4N onto lipid A.
full_output.methodology: Enzymatic assay using crude membranes from E. coli expressing ArnT, TLC, and LC-ESI-QTOF mass spectrometry.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence and ecological determinants of the contamination of floodplain wetlands with Klebsiella pneumoniae and pathogenic or antibiotic-resistant Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the occurrence and resistance profiles of Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae in floodplain wetlands, highlighting the presence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing E. coli and their resistance to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study involved sampling and analyzing water from 16 wetlands and three rivers, measuring bacterial concentrations, and assessing antibiotic resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Dual β-lactam combination therapy for multi-drug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection: enhanced efficacy in vivo and comparison with monotherapies of penicillin-binding protein inhibition.

full_output.paper_title: Nanopore metagenomics enables rapid clinical diagnosis of bacterial lower respiratory infection.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a NDM-7 carbapenemase-producing Escherichia coli ST410 clinical strain isolated from a urinary tract infection in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel NDM-7 carbapenemase-producing E. coli ST410 strain isolated from a urinary tract infection in China, highlighting the potential for horizontal transmission of carbapenem resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Proteomics-based discrimination of differentially expressed proteins in antibiotic-sensitive and antibiotic-resistant Salmonella Typhimurium, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Monitoring antimicrobial resistance trends in commensal Escherichia coli from livestock, the Netherlands, 1998 to 2016.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed antimicrobial resistance (AMR) trends in commensal Escherichia coli from livestock in the Netherlands from 1998 to 2016, identifying significant increases in resistance before 2009 and subsequent decreases after 2009, particularly in broilers and pigs. Colistin resistance was sporadic and showed a significant decrease in broilers but not in pigs.
full_output.methodology: The study used Poisson regression to analyze trends in resistant counts of E. coli isolates from broilers, pigs, and veal calves, considering changes in sampling strategies and antimicrobial use interventions.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae and Aeromonas spp. present in wastewater treatment plant effluent and nearby surface waters in the US.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance, Virulence Factors, and Pathotypes of Escherichia coli Isolated from Drinking Water Sources in Jordan.

full_output.paper_title: Assessment of a newly developed immunochromatographic assay for NDM-type metallo-β-lactamase producing Gram-negative pathogens in Myanmar.

full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and sequencing to identify blaNDM genes in bacterial isolates and developed an immunochromatographic assay for detection of NDM-producing bacteria.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaCTX-M-1 gene carried on IncI1 plasmids in Escherichia coli as a significant factor in plasmid persistence and resistance to cefoxitin in broiler chickens.
full_output.methodology: The study involved inoculating broiler chickens with E. coli variants with and without the blaCTX-M-1 gene, followed by quantitative analysis of bacterial populations and plasmid dynamics.

full_output.paper_title: A non-beta-lactam antibiotic inhibitor for enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli O104:H4.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies BACM, a non-beta-lactam compound, as an inhibitor of E. coli O104:H4 growth by targeting the β-lactamase pathway and penicillin-binding protein.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of several antibiotic resistance genes, including bla SHV, tetO, and aadA2, in coastal soil and sediment samples from the eastern seaboard of the USA.
full_output.methodology: The study used presence/absence quantitative and digital polymerase chain reaction assays to detect antibiotic resistance genes in soil and sediment samples.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus from Patients Hospitalized during 2015-2017 in Hospitals in Poland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of multidrug resistance in MRSA isolates, with resistance to fluoroquinolones, macrolides, and lincosamides being prevalent. The blaZ and mecA genes were detected in all isolates, contributing to resistance against penicillin and methicillin, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing via disc diffusion and PCR for gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Metal impacts on the persistence and proliferation of β-lactam resistance genes in Xiangjiang River, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the persistence and proliferation of various β-lactam resistance genes (blaTEM, blaVIM, blaSHV, blaGES, blaDHA, blaOXA-1, blaOXA-2, blaOXA-10, blaCMY-2, and blaampC) in the Xiangjiang River, highlighting the impact of heavy metals on their distribution and the role of bacterial communities in their persistence.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized qPCR, microcosm experiments, and 16S rDNA sequencing to analyze the occurrence, distribution, and persistence of β-lactam resistance genes in the Xiangjiang River.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of The Pathogenic Potential of Insecticidal Serratia marcescens Strains to Humans.
full_output.key_findings: All S. marcescens strains were resistant to sulfamethoxazole due to the presence of sul1 or sul2 genes. The study highlights the potential pathogenicity of S. marcescens to humans and the risks associated with using antibiotic-resistant strains as bioinsecticides.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR for detection of resistance genes, and cytotoxicity assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the d-alanine-d-alanine ligase (Bp Ddl) from Burkholderia pseudomallei, focusing on its structural and biochemical properties as a potential antibiotic target. The research highlights challenges in identifying effective inhibitors for this enzyme.
full_output.methodology: Structural and biochemical characterization of Bp Ddl, including crystallography, enzyme kinetics, and ligand-binding assays.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of carvacrol against resistant rapidly growing mycobacteria in the planktonic and biofilm growth mode.
full_output.key_findings: Carvacrol (CAR) shows potent antimicrobial activity against resistant rapidly growing mycobacteria (RGM) in both planktonic and biofilm forms, with MIC values ranging from 16 to 512 μg/mL and significant biofilm disruption at concentrations above the MIC.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, biofilm formation assays, and vapor contact experiments were conducted to evaluate the efficacy of carvacrol against RGM strains.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence and Transmission of Drug-/Multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium leprae in a Former Leprosy Colony in the Brazilian Amazon.

folP1.evidence_note: The paper mentions that mutations in folP1 were detected in 2 relapses and 1 new case, and that these mutations are associated with resistance to dapsone.

rpoB.evidence_note: rpoB mutations were detected in M. leprae isolates and correlated with rifampicin resistance.

gyrA.evidence_note: The paper mentions mutations in gyrA (TTA97TTT) but does not explicitly state that these mutations confer resistance to ofloxacin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium leprae strains in a Brazilian Amazon leprosy colony, highlighting the emergence and transmission of resistance to dapsone, rifampicin, and ofloxacin through mutations in folP1, rpoB, and gyrA genes.
full_output.methodology: Molecular analysis of resistance genes folP1, rpoB, and gyrA via Sanger sequencing, alongside in vivo testing in mouse footpads.

full_output.paper_title: AhlX, an N-acylhomoserine Lactonase with Unique Properties.
full_output.key_findings: AhlX, an N-acylhomoserine lactonase, was identified and characterized from the marine bacterium Salinicola salaria MCCC1A01339. It exhibits high temperature stability, salt tolerance, and the ability to quench AHL-dependent quorum sensing, thereby reducing E. carotovora infection.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, cloning, expression in E. coli, biochemical characterization, and activity assays using AHL substrates and bioassays.

full_output.paper_title: Thiostrepton Hijacks Pyoverdine Receptors To Inhibit Growth of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: Thiostrepton (TS) inhibits the growth of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii by exploiting pyoverdine receptors FpvA and FpvB. The ribosomal methyltransferase Tsr confers resistance to TS in P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Screening of bioactive molecules, biofilm assays, MIC determination, and genetic manipulation of P. aeruginosa mutants.

full_output.paper_title: Acquisition of Cross-Resistance to Bedaquiline and Clofazimine following Treatment for Tuberculosis in Pakistan.

Rv0678.notes: Mutations in Rv0678 were associated with increased MICs for bedaquiline and clofazimine.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first cases of acquired resistance to bedaquiline in Pakistan, identifying mutations in Rv0678 as a cause of cross-resistance to bedaquiline and clofazimine.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and MIC testing were used to analyze resistance mechanisms in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Food Effect of Tebipenem Pivoxil Hydrobromide after Single and Multiple Ascending Oral Doses in Healthy Adult Subjects.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the safety, pharmacokinetics, and food effect of tebipenem pivoxil hydrobromide (TBPM-PI-HBr), an orally available prodrug of tebipenem, a carbapenem with activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative pathogens. The research showed that TBPM-PI-HBr was well-tolerated and had favorable pharmacokinetic properties, with high bioavailability and no significant accumulation over 14 days. The study did not identify any AMR genes or mutations.
full_output.methodology: The study was a double-blind, placebo-controlled, ascending-dose, multicohort trial involving healthy adults. Pharmacokinetic parameters were analyzed following single and multiple doses of TBPM-PI-HBr under fasted and fed conditions.
full_output.sample_size: 108 subjects in the SAD phase and 16 subjects in the MAD phase

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Activity of Imipenem-Relebactam Alone or in Combination with Amikacin or Colistin against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the in vitro activity of imipenem-relebactam alone or in combination with amikacin or colistin against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, demonstrating synergistic effects against multidrug-resistant and carbapenem-nonsusceptible isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used time-kill assays to assess the antimicrobial activity of imipenem-relebactam in combination with amikacin or colistin against Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Pandemic fluoroquinolone resistant Escherichia coli clone ST1193 emerged via simultaneous homologous recombinations in 11 gene loci.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the pandemic Escherichia coli clone ST1193 acquired fluoroquinolone resistance through simultaneous homologous recombination events affecting 11 gene loci, particularly the gyrA and parC genes, which harbor QRDR mutations S83L, D87N, and S80I.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of E. coli isolates from the Enterobase database, sequence alignment, and phylogenetic tree construction.

full_output.paper_title: The Small RNA PinT Contributes to PhoP-Mediated Regulation of the Salmonella Pathogenicity Island 1 Type III Secretion System in Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhimurium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the small RNA PinT as a posttranscriptional regulator of the Salmonella pathogenicity island 1 (SPI1) type III secretion system (T3SS). PinT represses hilA and rtsA translation, contributing to the shutdown of the SPI1 T3SS after invasion.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic and biochemical approaches, including translational fusions, sRNA overexpression, and mutational analyses, to investigate the regulatory role of PinT in Salmonella.

full_output.paper_title: Development of Staphylococcus aureus tolerance to antimicrobial photodynamic inactivation and antimicrobial blue light upon sub-lethal treatment.
full_output.key_findings: Sub-lethal antimicrobial photodynamic inactivation (aPDI) and antimicrobial blue light (aBL) treatments induced tolerance in Staphylococcus aureus, which was linked to increased mutation rates and the activation of the SOS response via the umuC and recA genes.
full_output.methodology: qRT-PCR, transposon mutant analysis, and mutation rate assays were used to evaluate gene expression and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of multiple PTM derivatives with improved antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, particularly against MRSA. Compound A28 showed potent activity with MICs of 0.125-0.5 μg/mL against MRSA strains.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility, virulence determinants profiles and molecular characteristics of Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates in Wenzhou, eastern China.

These genes were found in both clinical and colonized isolates, highlighting their importance in antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and assess antimicrobial resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Shigella species and its drug resistance pattern in Ethiopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of drug resistance in Shigella species in Ethiopia, particularly to ampicillin, amoxicillin, and erythromycin. Multi-drug resistance was also prevalent.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 29 studies on Shigella species prevalence and drug resistance patterns in Ethiopia.

full_output.methodology: Cell growth assay, site-directed mutagenesis, and fluorescence spectroscopy were used to investigate PfMATE-mediated resistance to rhodamine 6G.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial susceptibilities of bacterial pathogens in Chinese pig farms from 2013 to 2017.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Streptococcus suis (SS), Haemophilus parasuis (HPS), Escherichia coli, Pasteurella multocida (Pm), Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae (APP), Brodetella bronchiseptica (Bb), Salmonella enteria (SE), and Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae showed high levels of antibiotic resistance to multiple classes of antibiotics, with resistance rates exceeding 60% for aminoglycosides, macrolides, lincomycin, tetracycline, polymyxin, and sulfonamide. Resistance rates for β-lactam and quinolone antibiotics also increased over time.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted antimicrobial susceptibility testing using disk diffusion methods according to CLSI guidelines, and analyzed the resistance rates of bacterial isolates from pig farms in China.

full_output.paper_title: MycoResistance: a curated resource of drug resistance molecules in Mycobacteria.

Additionally, a quinolone resistance mutation (Thr86Ile) in gyrA was found in 43% of isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in silico analysis were used to characterize antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in Campylobacter isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Phages in a thermoreversible sustained-release formulation targeting E. faecalis in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that EFDG1 and EFLK1 phages, when formulated in poloxamer P407, effectively kill Enterococcus faecalis in vitro and in vivo, showing sustained release and high efficacy against both planktonic and biofilm forms of the bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the lytic activity of EFDG1 and EFLK1 phages against E. faecalis in vitro and in a rat root canal infection model, assessing gelation time, phage release, and antibacterial effects.

full_output.paper_title: Pathogens distribution and drug resistance in patients with acute cerebral infarction complicated with diabetes and nosocomial pulmonary infection.
full_output.key_findings: Gram-negative bacteria were the main cause of pulmonary infection in hospitalized patients with acute cerebral infarction, with higher drug resistance rates in diabetic patients compared to non-diabetic patients.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of pathogen distribution and drug resistance in patients with acute cerebral infarction and nosocomial pulmonary infection.

full_output.paper_title: Frequency and patterns of second-line resistance conferring mutations among MDR-TB isolates resistant to a second-line drug from eSwatini, Somalia and Uganda (2014-2016).

full_output.methodology: Agar disk diffusion, PCR, sequencing, and MIC determination were used to identify and characterize HLMR in methicillin-resistant staphylococci.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative efficacy of linezolid and vancomycin for endotracheal tube MRSA biofilms from ICU patients.

full_output.paper_title: Surveillance of antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli isolated from wild cranes on the Izumi plain in Kagoshima prefecture, Japan.

No resistance was observed to minocycline, kanamycin, enrofloxacin, chloramphenicol, cefazolin, gentamicin, fosfomycin, or colistin.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility tests were performed using the agar dilution method according to CLSI guidelines for 11 antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Gene Targets in Ocular Pathogenic Escherichia coli for Mitigation of Biofilm Formation to Overcome Antibiotic Resistance.

Additionally, mdtO and ytfR mutants retain biofilm-forming capabilities. The research highlights the role of these genes in biofilm formation and their potential as targets for mitigating antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Generation of gene-specific knockout mutants through homologous recombination, validation via PCR and RT-PCR, assessment of biofilm formation using XTT method and confocal microscopy, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Comparison of Lactobacillus helveticus Strains Highlights Probiotic Potential.
full_output.key_findings: None of the L. helveticus strains analyzed in this study exhibited antibiotic resistance phenotypically or at the genome level.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogenetic and Molecular Profile of Staphylococcus aureus Isolated from Bloodstream Infections in Northeast Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance to oxacillin, clindamycin, erythromycin, ciprofloxacin, and gentamicin among S. aureus isolates. The mecA and blaZ genes were detected, contributing to beta-lactam resistance. New sequence types (STs) were classified, indicating clonal diversity.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR for gene detection, and MLST for clonal analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of A Novel Antibacterial Peptide from Atlantic Mackerel belonging to the GAPDH-Related Antimicrobial Family and Its In Vitro Digestibility.

AMGAP.validation_method: synthetic peptide antibacterial activity and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel antibacterial peptide, AMGAP, from Atlantic mackerel hydrolysate, which exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against various bacterial strains, including Listeria species. The peptide shows rapid in vitro digestibility in the gastrointestinal tract.
full_output.methodology: Enzymatic hydrolysis, solid-phase extraction, reverse-phase HPLC purification, LC-MS/MS analysis, and in vitro antibacterial activity and digestibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Insights into the Periplasmic Proteins of Acinetobacter baumannii AB5075 and the Impact of Imipenem Exposure: A Proteomic Approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several periplasmic proteins involved in antibiotic resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii AB5075, including the beta-lactamases AmpC, OXA-23, and GES-11, as well as the RND-type efflux pump AdeT. Additionally, a novel metal-dependent hydrolase, ABUW_0920, was identified, suggesting potential roles in beta-lactam resistance.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis using SDS-PAGE and nano-HPLC-ESI-MS/MS to identify differentially expressed periplasmic proteins in response to imipenem exposure.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology of Klebsiella variicola obtained from different sources.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the molecular epidemiology of Klebsiella variicola, identifying 166 distinct sequence types (STs) and highlighting the presence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase- and carbapenemase-producing strains, indicating potential for increased pathogenicity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized whole-genome sequencing and multilocus sequence typing (MLST) to analyze the molecular epidemiology of K. variicola isolates from various sources.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of intrapartum and postnatal antibiotics on the gut microbiome and emergence of antimicrobial resistance in infants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes, cepA and msrB, which were significantly differentially abundant between the control group and the antibiotic-exposed groups. These genes were found to be present only in the control group, suggesting a reduction in AMR gene abundance in infants exposed to perinatal antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatic analysis of fecal samples from infants and their mothers to identify AMR genes and assess their abundance.

full_output.paper_title: Diabetic foot infections: Application of a nisin-biogel to complement the activity of conventional antibiotics and antiseptics against Staphylococcus aureus biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the effectiveness of nisin-biogel in enhancing the activity of conventional antibiotics and antiseptics against Staphylococcus aureus biofilms in diabetic foot infections.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro experiments to assess the inhibitory and eradication effects of nisin-biogel combined with antibiotics and antiseptics against S. aureus biofilms.

gyrA.notes: The study focuses on the detection of gyrA mutations, particularly at codon 91, which is associated with ciprofloxacin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the effectiveness of the ResistancePlus GC (beta) assay in determining Neisseria gonorrhoeae gyrA genotypes, showing improved resolution of indeterminate results compared to a prior high-resolution melt assay.
full_output.methodology: The study retested clinical specimens using the ResistancePlus GC (beta) assay and compared results with previous high-resolution melt analysis.

full_output.paper_title: New and Potent Quinuclidine-Based Antimicrobial Agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of ten new quinuclidine-based compounds with potent antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including multidrug-resistant strains. Compounds 5 and 10 showed the highest activity, particularly against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of compounds, disc diffusion assay, broth microdilution method, and MTT assay were used to evaluate antimicrobial activity and cytotoxicity.

full_output.paper_title: The Role of Orientation of Surface Bound Dihydropyrrol-2-ones (DHP) on Biological Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antibacterial activity of dihydropyrrol-2-ones (DHPs) when covalently attached to amine-functionalized glass surfaces, focusing on their orientation and effectiveness against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of DHP analogues, surface characterization by XPS and contact angle measurements, and evaluation of antibacterial activity using fluorescence microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery, synthesis and antibacterial evaluation of phenolic compounds from Cylicodiscus gabunensis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified gallic acid (1), ethyl gallate (6), and other polyphenols from Cylicodiscus gabunensis as having antibacterial activity. It also synthesized several alkyl and alkenyl gallates, demonstrating that longer alkyl chains generally increase antibacterial potency.
full_output.methodology: Bioassay-guided fractionation, GC-MS, LC-MS, NMR, and disk diffusion assays were used to identify and evaluate the antibacterial properties of compounds from Cylicodiscus gabunensis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies fosA as a significant factor influencing fosfomycin susceptibility testing accuracy in KPC-producing Enterobacterales, with fosA-positive isolates showing higher MIC distributions and reduced categorical agreement with agar dilution.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, susceptibility testing using Etest, disk diffusion, and agar dilution.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the effectiveness of molecular β-lactamase gene testing in predicting empiric β-lactam susceptibility among Enterobacteriaceae, highlighting the importance of detecting blaCTX-M, blaKPC, and blaNDM genes for accurate resistance prediction.
full_output.methodology: Molecular testing and analysis of β-lactamase gene prevalence in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Exposure of Pseudomonas aeruginosa to bactericidal hypochlorous acid during neutrophil phagocytosis is compromised in cystic fibrosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that hypochlorous acid (HOCl) is produced within neutrophil phagosomes and is bactericidal. Defective HOCl production in cystic fibrosis (CF) neutrophils is linked to impaired CFTR function, affecting bacterial killing.
full_output.methodology: The study used phagocytosis assays, LC-MS analyses, and inhibitor treatments to investigate HOCl production and bacterial GSH oxidation.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic and Phenotypic Characterization of Antimicrobial Resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae: a Cross-Sectional Study of Isolates Recovered from Routine Urine Cultures in a High-Incidence Setting.

blaTEM-1b.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic susceptibility testing

tet (M).validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla TEM-1b as a key determinant of penicillin resistance and tet (M) as a key determinant of tetracycline and doxycycline resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates. Mutations in gyrA and parC were associated with quinolone resistance, while rpsJ V57M and mtrR promoter mutations contributed to tetracycline and azithromycin resistance, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and mutations in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Enterococcus faecalis CRISPR-Cas Is a Robust Barrier to Conjugative Antibiotic Resistance Dissemination in the Murine Intestine.
full_output.key_findings: CRISPR-Cas systems in Enterococcus faecalis act as a robust barrier to the dissemination of conjugative antibiotic resistance plasmids in the murine intestine, but not in vitro.
full_output.methodology: Conjugation experiments, mouse colonization model, PCR, and plating assays.
full_output.sample_size: 14 mice for pAM714, 10 mice for pAM771

full_output.paper_title: Prevention of urinary catheter-associated infections by coating antimicrobial peptides from crowberry endophytes.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antimicrobial peptide Chain201D, which exhibits broad-spectrum activity against various bacterial and fungal strains associated with urinary catheter infections. It remains stable under diverse environmental conditions and effectively kills adherent bacteria on surfaces.
full_output.methodology: The antimicrobial activity of Chain201D was assessed through MIC assays, radial diffusion assays, and surface immobilization experiments on EG4-SAMs.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular analysis and antimicrobial resistance pattern of distinct strains of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from cystic fibrosis patients in Iran.

mutations_found.nucleotide_change: deletions and substitution mutations leading to internal stop codon and frame-shift mutations

oprD.notes: Mutations in oprD gene lead to reduced susceptibility to imipenem and meropenem

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of antibacterial and antibiofilm activity of purified recombinant Azurin from Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial and antibiofilm activity of recombinant Azurin (rAzurin) from Pseudomonas aeruginosa against various bacterial species, showing that rAzurin effectively inhibited bacterial growth and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The azurin gene was cloned, expressed, and purified in E. coli. Antibacterial and antibiofilm activities were assessed using micro-broth dilution and crystal violet assays.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular typing, antibiotic resistance profiles and biocide susceptibility in Salmonella enterica serotypes isolated from raw chicken meat marketed in Venezuela.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla TEM-1, bla CTX-M-2, and qnrB19 genes in Salmonella enterica serotypes from raw chicken meat in Venezuela, indicating multidrug resistance. All strains were susceptible to biocides.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize resistance genes and profiles.

full_output.paper_title: High-throughput time-resolved morphology screening in bacteria reveals phenotypic responses to antibiotics.

ruvA.notes: Mutant shows delayed lysis and elongation

dedD.notes: Mutant shows delayed lysis and elongation

lpxL.notes: Mutant shows delayed lysis and elongation
