mcr-5.validation_method: PCR detection of mcr genes in Cst-resistant isolates

mcr-9.validation_method: PCR detection of mcr genes in Cst-resistant isolates

qnr.validation_method: association with non-typical quinolone resistance phenotype in isolates with no mutations in quinolone resistance-determining regions

full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Salmonella isolates from poultry in Spain between 2011 and 2017, identifying various AMR genes and mutations associated with resistance to multiple antibiotics, including beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, tetracyclines, and others.
full_output.methodology: The study used antimicrobial susceptibility testing and statistical analyses to characterize AMR patterns in Salmonella isolates from poultry.

full_output.paper_title: Geographical Distribution of β-Lactam Resistance among Klebsiella spp. from Selected Health Facilities in Ghana.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various β-lactam resistance genes, including bla TEM, bla SHV, bla CTX-M, bla OXA-48, and bla NDM, in Klebsiella isolates from Ghana, highlighting the geographical variation in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic techniques, including PCR, were used to detect β-lactam resistance mechanisms in Klebsiella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Abundance and Antimicrobial Resistance of Three Bacterial Species along a Complete Wastewater Pathway.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the abundance and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) profiles of three bacterial species (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella spp., and Aeromonas spp.) along a wastewater pathway, revealing that hospital wastewater had the highest proportion of resistant bacteria, reflecting antimicrobial consumption and environmental contamination.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting and analyzing 211 wastewater samples, culturing isolates, performing antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and measuring antimicrobial residues and chemical concentrations.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of ceftazidime-avibactam in the treatment of infections due to Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae.

blaOXA-48.validation_method: molecular detection via Xpert Carba-R Kit

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the efficacy of ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) in treating infections caused by OXA-48-producing Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE). The OXA-48 gene was the predominant carbapenemase identified in CRE isolates.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing clinical outcomes of patients with CRE infections treated with CAZ-AVI versus other agents, with molecular detection of carbapenemase genes.

full_output.paper_title: Macrolide-Resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae in the United States as Determined from a National Surveillance Program.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MRMp) in the United States, with A2063G and A2064G mutations in the 23S rRNA gene being the most common. MRMp prevalence varied significantly by region, with higher rates in the South and East compared to the West.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR and Sanger sequencing were used to detect 23S rRNA mutations associated with macrolide resistance in Mycoplasma pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Updating Molecular Diagnostics for Detecting Methicillin-Susceptible and Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Isolates in Blood Culture Bottles.

mecA.evidence_note: The paper describes insertions in the orfX-SCC mec junction and a 23-bp deletion in the spa gene of Staphylococcus aureus that affect the Xpert MRSA/SA BC test results, leading to false-negative calls for methicillin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified genetic variations in Staphylococcus aureus isolates that affect the accuracy of molecular diagnostics for detecting methicillin-susceptible and methicillin-resistant strains. Key findings include the impact of insertions in the orfX-SCC mec junction and spa gene deletions on test results.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze genetic variations and their effects on molecular diagnostic tests.

full_output.paper_title: Salmonella persisters promote the spread of antibiotic resistance plasmids in the gut.

cat.mechanism: confers resistance to chloramphenicol by acetylation

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the cat gene as a key factor in conferring chloramphenicol resistance in Salmonella, facilitating plasmid transfer and persistence in the gut.
full_output.methodology: In vitro plasmid transfer kinetics, in vivo infection models, and qPCR analysis were used to investigate the role of the cat gene in antibiotic resistance and plasmid transfer.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance Profiles of Haemophilus influenzae Isolates from Children in 2016: A Multicenter Study in China.

mutations_found.validated_by: beta-lactamase detection using cefinase disc method

bla.notes: beta-lactamase production is the main mechanism of ampicillin resistance

pbp3.notes: mutation of PBP3 decreases antibiotic susceptibility of HI towards ampicillin and other beta-lactam antibiotics

full_output.key_findings: More than half of the Haemophilus influenzae (HI) strains isolated from Chinese children were resistant to ampicillin, primarily due to the production of beta-lactamase. Additionally, mutations in the penicillin-binding protein 3 (PBP3) contribute to ampicillin resistance. Third-generation cephalosporins like cefotaxime and ceftriaxone remain effective against HI infections.
full_output.methodology: Kirby-Bauer method for antibiotic susceptibility testing and cefinase disc method for beta-lactamase detection.

full_output.paper_title: The rise in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium in Germany: data from the German Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance (ARS).
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing prevalence of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREF) in German hospitals, especially in southern regions. It identifies factors associated with increased vancomycin resistance, including hospital care type and patient age.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational study analyzing data from the German Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance (ARS) database from 2012 to 2017.

full_output.paper_title: Maize phenylalanine ammonia-lyases contribute to resistance to Sugarcane mosaic virus infection, most likely through positive regulation of salicylic acid accumulation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ZmPAL genes as essential for salicylic acid (SA) biosynthesis and resistance to Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV) in maize. Silencing ZmPAL genes leads to reduced SA accumulation and increased SCMV infection, highlighting their role in SA-dependent defense mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq, RT-qPCR, and VIGS were used to analyze gene expression and function.

full_output.paper_title: HupA, the main undecaprenyl pyrophosphate and phosphatidylglycerol phosphate phosphatase in Helicobacter pylori is essential for colonization of the stomach.

hupA.encodes: undecaprenyl pyrophosphate phosphatase and phosphatidylglycerol phosphate phosphatase

full_output.key_findings: HupA is essential for H. pylori colonization of the stomach and contributes to resistance against polymyxin B.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, mutagenesis, enzyme activity assays, and mouse colonization experiments.

full_output.paper_title: AcrAB-TolC efflux pump system plays a role in carbapenem non-susceptibility in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the AcrAB-TolC efflux pump system plays a role in carbapenem non-susceptibility in Escherichia coli, with AcrA overexpression strongly correlated with ertapenem resistance and AcrB overexpression observed under imipenem stress.
full_output.methodology: qRT-PCR, MIC testing, and PFGE were used to analyze the role of the AcrAB-TolC efflux pump in carbapenem resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Pneumococcal carriage among children under five in Accra, Ghana, five years after the introduction of pneumococcal conjugate vaccine.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the tet(M) and ermB genes in Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates, which confer resistance to tetracycline and erythromycin, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Phase variation in Mycobacterium tuberculosis glpK produces transiently heritable drug tolerance.
The prevalence and impact of lysogeny among oral isolates of Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the ɸEf11 prophage in 31% of oral E. faecalis strains, and showed that lysogeny affects bacterial traits such as biofilm formation and resistance to phage endolysin.
full_output.methodology: PCR and biofilm assays were used to analyze the presence of the ɸEf11 prophage and its impact on E. faecalis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Methyl gallate and tylosin synergistically reduce the membrane integrity and intracellular survival of Salmonella Typhimurium.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that methyl gallate (MG) and tylosin (Ty) synergistically reduce the membrane integrity and intracellular survival of Salmonella Typhimurium, demonstrating a significant reduction in bacterial viability and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of microbiological techniques including MIC/MBC assays, checkerboard assays, time-kill assays, confocal microscopy, SEM, and flow cytometry to assess the effects of MG and Ty on Salmonella Typhimurium.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic polymorphisms in PXR and NF-κB1 influence susceptibility to anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified genetic polymorphisms in PXR (rs3814055) and NF-κB1 (rs78872571 and rs4647992) that are associated with susceptibility to anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (ATDILI).
full_output.methodology: Genotyping of selected SNPs and association analysis with ATDILI risk.

full_output.paper_title: European hedgehogs (Erinaceus europaeus) as a natural reservoir of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus carrying mecC in Denmark.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mecC-MRSA as a prevalent type in European hedgehogs in Denmark, highlighting their role as a natural reservoir for this specific type of MRSA.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based detection of mecC and spa typing were used to characterize MRSA isolates from hedgehogs.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology of carbapenem-resistance plasmids using publicly available sequences.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the molecular epidemiology of carbapenem-resistance plasmids, focusing on four clinically relevant carbapenemase genes (bla KPC, bla NDM, bla IMP, and bla VIM) across multiple bacterial species.
full_output.methodology: Analysis of publicly available plasmid sequences from NCBI to determine gene content, replicon types, and global spread of carbapenemase-carrying plasmids.

full_output.paper_title: Correlation of Host Range Expansion of Therapeutic Bacteriophage Sb-1 with Allele State at a Hypervariable Repeat Locus.

Sb-1.notes: The hypervariable repeat region (region 2) in the Sb-1 phage genome was found to correlate with host range expansion.

Sb-1P.notes: The hypervariable repeat region (region 2) in the Sb-1P phage genome was found to correlate with host range expansion.

Sb-1M.notes: The hypervariable repeat region (region 2) in the Sb-1M phage genome was found to correlate with host range expansion.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a hypervariable repeat region (region 2) in the Sb-1 phage genome that correlates with host range expansion. This region shows variable allele states that are associated with the ability of the phage to infect previously resistant S. aureus strains.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, PCR, and phage host range assays were used to analyze the genetic basis of host range expansion in Sb-1 phage.
full_output.sample_size: 25 military MRSA isolates, 90 global S. aureus isolates

full_output.paper_title: Acquisition of mcr-1 and Cocarriage of Virulence Genes in Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli Isolates from Municipal Wastewater Influents in Japan.

mcr-1.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mcr-1 gene in five of seven E. coli isolates from municipal wastewater in Japan, highlighting the coexistence of colistin resistance and virulence genes in avian pathogenic E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and PCR were used to identify and characterize the mcr-1 gene and associated virulence factors.

full_output.paper_title: Validation and assessment of an antibiotic-based, aseptic decontamination manufacturing protocol for therapeutic, vacuum-dried human amniotic membrane.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the effectiveness of an antibiotic-based decontamination protocol for human amniotic membrane (AM) during vacuum-drying. It demonstrates that the protocol efficiently reduces bioburden and that antibiotic-treated AM exhibits strong antibacterial activity against various bacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a combination of microbiological assays, including CFU counting, MIC/MBC tests, and disc diffusion assays, to evaluate the antibacterial efficacy of the decontamination protocol.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing-based epidemiological analysis of anti-tuberculosis drug resistance genes in Japan in 2007: Application of the Genome Research for Asian Tuberculosis (GReAT) database.

embB.encodes: embryonic stem cell membrane protein B
embryonic stem cell membrane protein B

full_output.key_findings: The study identified novel mutations in the katG, gid, and embB genes associated with resistance to isoniazid, streptomycin, and ethambutol in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Japan.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify drug resistance genes and mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Dissemination prevention of antibiotic resistant and facultative pathogenic bacteria by ultrafiltration and ozone treatment at an urban wastewater treatment plant.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the effectiveness of ultrafiltration and ozone treatment in reducing antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and facultative pathogenic bacteria in wastewater. It identified several ARGs, including sul1, blaTEM, tetM, CTX-M, CTX-M-32, blaOXA-48, blaVIM, CMY-2, vanA, mcr-1, blaNDM, ermB, and intl1, which were found to be prevalent in the wastewater. Both ultrafiltration units showed significant reduction in these ARGs and pathogenic bacteria, whereas ozone treatment was less effective.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR analysis to quantify the abundance of ARGs and taxonomic marker genes in wastewater samples before and after treatment. Metagenomic sequencing was also employed to analyze the genetic content of the retentate from ultrafiltration units.

full_output.paper_title: A review of -multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae in a neonatal unit in Johannesburg, South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (MDRE), particularly carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE), in a neonatal unit in Johannesburg, South Africa. It identifies Klebsiella pneumoniae as the most common isolate and notes the emergence of carbapenem resistance, primarily mediated by NDM and VIM carbapenemases.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of medical records and microbiological data from neonates admitted to a tertiary neonatal unit between 2013 and 2015.

full_output.paper_title: A pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic assessment of oral antibiotics for pyelonephritis.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic properties of oral antibiotics for treating pyelonephritis, focusing on amoxicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, cephalexin, ciprofloxacin, and fosfomycin. It found that these antibiotics could be effective at specific doses for certain populations of E. coli isolates, particularly those with lower MIC values.
full_output.methodology: The study used pharmacokinetic models and MIC data from E. coli isolates to perform PK/PD simulations, evaluating the probability of target attainment (PTA) and cumulative fraction of response (CFR) for different antibiotic doses.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that previous use of extended-spectrum penicillins and sulfonamides/triprim was associated with trimethoprim resistance in E. coli, while nitrofurantoin use was linked to lower trimethoprim resistance.
full_output.methodology: Nested case-control study analyzing antimicrobial drug prescriptions and trimethoprim resistance in E. coli isolates from urinary tract infections.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and characterization of OmpT-like proteases in uropathogenic Escherichia coli clinical isolates.

ompT.validation_method: FRET activity assay, proteolytic cleavage of AMPs

arlC.validation_method: multiplex PCR, FRET activity assay, proteolytic cleavage of AMPs

full_output.key_findings: The study identified and characterized OmpT and arlC, two OmpT-like proteases in uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC) clinical isolates, which cleave and inactivate antimicrobial peptides, contributing to antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR, FRET activity assay, proteolytic cleavage of AMPs, and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the role of OmpT and arlC in UPEC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Linezolid-resistant Staphylococcus haemolyticus: Emergence of G2447U & C2534U mutations at the domain V of 23S ribosomal RNA gene in a tertiary care hospital in India.

cfr.mechanism: confers resistance to phenicols, lincosamides, oxazolidinones, pleuromutilins, and streptogramin B

23S rRNA.notes: Mutations in domain V of 23S rRNA gene

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli belonging to ST131 rarely transfers bla (ctx-m-15) to fecal Escherichia coli.

blaCTX-M-15.validation_method: plasmid transfer experiments and PCR confirmation

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that E. coli ST131 rarely transfers the blaCTX-M-15 gene to fecal E. coli, suggesting that the high prevalence of CTX-M-15-producing ST131 is more likely due to clonal dissemination than conjugative transfer.
full_output.methodology: Conjugation experiments, PCR, and whole-genome sequencing were used to analyze the transfer of blaCTX-M-15.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, risk and genetic characteristics of drug-resistant tuberculosis in a tertiary care tuberculosis hospital in China.

oxyR-ahpC.encodes: transcriptional activator and alkyl hydroperoxide reductase

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility changes of Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae intra-abdominal infection isolate-derived pathogens from Chinese intra-abdominal infections from 2011 to 2015.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing resistance of Klebsiella pneumoniae to carbapenems, particularly ertapenem and imipenem, in intra-abdominal infection isolates from China between 2011 and 2015. E. coli showed relatively higher susceptibility to these antibiotics, but resistance trends were also noted.
full_output.methodology: The study determined MIC 90 and MIC 50 values for 12 antibiotics against E. coli and K. pneumoniae isolates from intra-abdominal infections.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and molecular epidemiology characteristics of carbapenem-resistant Escherichia coli in Heilongjiang Province, China.

blaNDM-1.validation_method: PCR detection, conjugation experiments, plasmid stability testing
blaNDM-1.genetic_context: a cluster of genes ( ISAba125-bla NDM-1 - ble MBL -Δ trpF ) was detected in all of the NDM-1-positive isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified five NDM-1-producing E. coli strains from water samples, highlighting the presence of carbapenemase genes in environmental isolates. The blaNDM-1 gene was successfully transferred via conjugation and showed stability in plasmids.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection, conjugation experiments, plasmid stability testing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility profile and prevalence of mecA and lukS-PV/lukF-PV genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolated from nasal and pharyngeal sources of medical students in Ecuador.

mecA.encodes: penicillin-binding protein 2', which is involved in cell wall synthesis

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of mecA and lukS-PV/lukF-PV genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from medical students in Ecuador, highlighting the high resistance to several antibiotics and the limited presence of the mecA gene in MRSA isolates.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and disk diffusion method were used to detect the presence of mecA and lukS-PV/lukF-PV genes and determine antibiotic susceptibility profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Assessment of Antibiotic Levels, Multi-Drug Resistant Bacteria and Genetic Biomarkers in the Waters of the Rio Grande River Between the United States-Mexico Border.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of extended spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes TEM, CTX-M, and SHV in water samples and bacterial isolates from the Rio Grande River. These genes confer resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics. Additionally, class 1 and 2 integrons were detected, indicating the presence of mobile genetic elements carrying resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, DNA extraction, and sequencing were used to identify ESBL genes and integrons in water and bacterial samples.

full_output.paper_title: Lysyl-tRNA Synthetase from Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Characterization and Identification of Inhibitory Compounds.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified three compounds (BM01D09, BT06F11, and BT08F04) that inhibit the function of Pseudomonas aeruginosa lysyl-tRNA synthetase (LysRS). These compounds showed varying modes of action, with BT06F11 and BT08F04 exhibiting bactericidal activity against gram-negative bacteria, while BM01D09 showed bacteriostatic activity. Additionally, BM01D09 was identified as bilirubin, a naturally occurring compound with potential antimicrobial properties.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biochemical assays, including ATP:PPi exchange reactions and aminoacylation assays, to characterize the enzymatic activity of LysRS. High-throughput screening of chemical compound libraries was conducted using scintillation proximity assay (SPA) technology to identify inhibitors of LysRS. MIC assays and time-kill studies were performed to evaluate the antibacterial activity of the identified compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of five Enterobacteriaceae species harbouring blaNDM-1 and mcr-1 plasmids from a single paediatric patient.

blaNDM-1.role_in_paper: The gene was identified as a resistance determinant in multiple Enterobacteriaceae species.
blaNDM-1.genetic_context: blaNDM-1 is located within a truncated Tn125 structure and is part of the ARI-A resistance island.
blaNDM-1.source: The gene was identified in clinical isolates from a pediatric patient.
blaNDM-1.evidence_note: The gene was detected in multiple Enterobacteriaceae species and was shown to confer resistance to carbapenems.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaNDM-1, rmtC, mcr-1, qnrB4, qnrB52, qnrA1, and aac(6')-Ib-cr1 as resistance genes in various Enterobacteriaceae species isolated from a pediatric patient.
full_output.methodology: PCR, plasmid sequencing, whole genome sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Hybrid Resistance and Virulence Plasmids in "High-Risk" Clones of Klebsiella pneumoniae, Including Those Carrying bla(NDM-5).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hybrid resistance and virulence plasmids in high-risk clones of Klebsiella pneumoniae, including those carrying bla(NDM-5). These plasmids contain both resistance and virulence genes, highlighting the emergence of multidrug-resistant and hypervirulent strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing using minION and Illumina platforms, along with PCR and bioinformatics tools for gene identification and analysis.

full_output.paper_title: The latest advances in β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combinations for the treatment of Gram-negative bacterial infections.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the development and evaluation of β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor (BL-BLI) combinations for treating Gram-negative bacterial infections, focusing on their effectiveness against resistant strains like ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae, CRE, P. aeruginosa, and A. baumannii.
full_output.methodology: Review of primary literature, conference abstracts, and clinical trials on BL-BLI combinations.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiological and clinical characteristics of Streptococcus gallolyticus subsp. pasteurianus infection in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the AMR genes and mutations in Streptococcus gallolyticus subsp. pasteurianus isolates from China, identifying erm(B), erm(A), erm(T), mef(A/E), tet(L), tet(O), and tet(M) as major contributors to erythromycin, clindamycin, and tetracycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic susceptibility testing and PCR-based detection of AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Natural outer membrane permeabilizers boost antibiotic action against irradiated resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs) in several bacterial isolates, demonstrating their role in beta-lactam resistance. Natural permeabilizers like gallic acid and thymol enhance antibiotic susceptibility by increasing outer membrane permeability.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, detection of ESBL production, and evaluation of permeabilizers' effects on bacterial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Asymptomatic pharyngeal carriage rate of Streptococcus pyogenes, its associated factors and antibiotic susceptibility pattern among school children in Hawassa town, southern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 12.2% of school children in Hawassa, Ethiopia, were colonized with Streptococcus pyogenes. Resistance to tetracycline was high, while susceptibility to penicillin, erythromycin, chloramphenicol, and ceftriaxone was high. Vancomycin resistance was low.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a cross-sectional survey of school children, with antimicrobial susceptibility testing performed using the disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of a 72-Kilobase Cointegrant, Conjugative Multiresistance Plasmid in Community-Associated Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Isolates from the Early 1990s.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a 72-kb conjugative multiresistance plasmid, pWBG731, in community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates from the early 1990s, identifying genes conferring resistance to penicillin, tetracycline, mupirocin, and trimethoprim.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid sequencing, assembly, and analysis, along with mobilization experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Inducers of the Expression of Multidrug Efflux Pumps That Trigger Pseudomonas aeruginosa Transient Antibiotic Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies dequalinium chloride, procaine, and atropine as novel inducers of the mexCD-oprJ efflux pump in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, leading to transient antibiotic resistance, particularly to ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Use of Biolog phenotype microarrays, luminescent biosensor strains, real-time PCR, and MIC testing to identify and validate efflux pump inducers.

full_output.paper_title: Adaptation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to Biofilm Growth Is Genetically Linked to Drug Tolerance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the inlps gene cluster as being specifically induced in Mycobacterium tuberculosis biofilms, contributing to the unique growth environment and drug tolerance of biofilm-forming cells.
full_output.methodology: Transposon sequencing (Tn-seq), transcriptomic analysis, and chemical analysis were used to identify genes and mutations associated with biofilm growth and drug tolerance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Toxic Shock Syndrome Toxin 1-Producing Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus of Clonal Complex 5, the New York/Japan Epidemic Clone, Causing a High Early-Mortality Rate in Patients with Bloodstream Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the tst-1 gene as a significant risk factor for early mortality in patients with Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections, particularly in CC5 methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) isolates carrying the gene.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a prospective, multicenter, observational design, including microbiological evaluations, PCR for gene detection, and statistical analyses to assess risk factors for mortality.

full_output.paper_title: Conceptual Model of Biofilm Antibiotic Tolerance That Integrates Phenomena of Diffusion, Metabolism, Gene Expression, and Physiology.

psl.notes: Deficiency in Psl polysaccharide synthesis increases ciprofloxacin susceptibility in biofilms.

relA.notes: Deficiency in the stringent response increases ciprofloxacin susceptibility in biofilms.

spoT.notes: Deficiency in the stringent response increases ciprofloxacin susceptibility in biofilms.

rpoS.notes: Deficiency in the stationary-phase response increases ciprofloxacin susceptibility in biofilms.

amgR.notes: Deficiency in the membrane stress response increases ciprofloxacin susceptibility in biofilms.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes whose deficiency increases ciprofloxacin susceptibility in P. aeruginosa biofilms, including psl, relA, spoT, rpoS, and amgR.
full_output.methodology: The study uses mutant susceptibility testing to evaluate the role of various genes in ciprofloxacin resistance in P. aeruginosa biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Functional metagenomics-guided discovery of potent Cas9 inhibitors in the human microbiome.

acrIIA11.mechanism: binds SpyCas9 and double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) and exhibits a novel mode of SpyCas9 antagonism

full_output.key_findings: The study identified AcrIIA11, a novel anti-CRISPR protein from a Lachnospiraceae phage, which effectively inhibits Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9 (SpyCas9) in both bacterial and human cells. AcrIIA11 homologs are widely distributed across diverse bacteria and inhibit both SpyCas9 and a divergent Cas9 from Treponema denticola.
full_output.methodology: Functional metagenomic selection and plasmid protection assays were used to identify and characterize AcrIIA11.

full_output.paper_title: Development of an algorithm to discriminate between plasmid- and chromosomal-mediated AmpC β-lactamase production in Escherichia coli by elaborate phenotypic and genotypic characterization.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla CMY-2 and bla DHA-1 as the primary plasmid-mediated AmpC β-lactamase genes responsible for resistance to third-generation cephalosporins in E. coli. An algorithm based on cefotaxime MIC values was developed to distinguish between plasmid-mediated and chromosomal-mediated AmpC production.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized whole-genome sequencing, Etest MICs, and machine learning to develop an algorithm for identifying plasmid-mediated AmpC β-lactamase production in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of linezolid-resistant Enterococcus faecium from the USA and Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies optrA, poxtA, and a cfr-like gene as key contributors to linezolid resistance in Enterococcus faecium isolates from Pakistan, whereas US isolates primarily exhibit resistance via the G2576T mutation in the 23S rRNA gene.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and Illumina whole-genome sequencing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes and mutations in linezolid-resistant E. faecium isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of a novel mcr-5.4 gene variant in hospital tap water by shotgun metagenomic sequencing.

mcr-5.4.validation_method: shotgun metagenomic sequencing and long-read metagenomic sequencing

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of the mcr-5.4 gene variant in a hospital water environment, highlighting the presence of mobile colistin resistance determinants in non-clinical settings.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing (SRMseq) and long-read metagenomic sequencing (LRMseq) were used to identify and characterize the mcr-5.4 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of in vitro activity of ceftazidime/avibactam and ceftolozane/tazobactam against MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Qatar.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of ceftazidime/avibactam and ceftolozane/tazobactam against MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Qatar. It identified several beta-lactamase genes, including blaTEM-116, blaVEB-1a, blaCARB-3, blaVIM-2, blaPDC-2, blaPDC-3, blaPDC-5, blaPDC-7, blaOXA-4, blaOXA-10, and blaOXA-50, which contribute to resistance against these antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing was used to identify antibiotic resistance genes in MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study explores how stochastic gene expression influences the selection of antibiotic resistance mutations, focusing on regulatory and structural mutations in efflux and enzymatic resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Agent-based modeling and computational simulations to analyze the effects of gene expression variability on antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Hospital-based Surveillance Provides Insights Into the Etiology of Pediatric Bacterial Meningitis in Yaoundé, Cameroon, in the Post-Vaccine Era.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes in Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates, including catQ, folA, folP, tetM, mef, and penicillin-binding proteins, indicating resistance to chloramphenicol, trimethoprim, tetracycline, erythromycin, and penicillin.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and mechanisms in Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Similarity of Gonococcal Homologs to Meningococcal Outer Membrane Proteins of Serogroup B Vaccine.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies common outer membrane proteins (OMPs) between Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Neisseria meningitidis, highlighting potential cross-protection against gonorrhea via MenB-4C vaccine antigens such as NhbA, FHbp, GNA2091, and GNA1030.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and in silico analysis of 970 N. gonorrhoeae isolates and 4 NmB reference strains to identify common OMPs and their sequence similarity.

full_output.paper_title: Cathelicidin Peptides Restrict Bacterial Growth via Membrane Perturbation and Induction of Reactive Oxygen Species.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies B22 and B22a as cathelicidin peptides with potent antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae, including strains resistant to polymyxins and those carrying the NDM1 gene. These peptides induce oxidative stress and membrane perturbation, leading to bacterial cell death.
full_output.methodology: The study uses single-cell fluorescence microscopy, gene expression analysis, and growth assays to evaluate the antibacterial activity of B22 and B22a.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of cleaning and disinfection procedures on microbial ecology and Salmonella antimicrobial resistance in a pig slaughterhouse.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified resistance to ampicillin, sulfamethoxazole, and tetracycline in Salmonella isolates from a pig slaughterhouse, with no significant changes in resistance patterns after cleaning and disinfection procedures.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing and PFGE analysis were used to characterize Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Design, synthesis, in silico and in vitro evaluation of novel diphenyl ether derivatives as potential antitubercular agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the design and evaluation of novel diphenyl ether derivatives as potential antitubercular agents, targeting the enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase (InhA) enzyme. Compound PYN-8 showed significant antitubercular activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv and Mycobacterium bovis.
full_output.methodology: The research involved the synthesis of diphenyl ether derivatives, computational modeling, molecular docking, and in vitro testing for antitubercular activity.

full_output.paper_title: Two cases of multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae related to travel in south-eastern Asia, France, June 2019.

full_output.paper_title: Shifts in the Human Gut Microbiota Structure Caused by Quadruple Helicobacter pylori Eradication Therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies changes in the gut microbiota and resistome following Helicobacter pylori eradication therapy, highlighting increases in ermB, CFX, and tetQ genes, and decreases in tetO and tetW genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome shotgun sequencing and metagenomic analysis were used to assess changes in gut microbiota and antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Highly Effective and Noninvasive Near-Infrared Eradication of a Staphylococcus aureus Biofilm on Implants by a Photoresponsive Coating within 20 Min.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a photoresponsive coating composed of MoS2, IR780, and RGDC that effectively eradicates Staphylococcus aureus biofilms on titanium implants within 20 minutes using near-infrared light. The system combines photothermal and photodynamic therapies to achieve high antibacterial efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, and in vitro and in vivo antibacterial assays to evaluate the effectiveness of the photoresponsive coating.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibitory Effect of Thymoquinone on Listeria monocytogenes ATCC 19115 Biofilm Formation and Virulence Attributes Critical for Human Infection.
full_output.key_findings: Thymoquinone (TQ) effectively inhibited the growth of Listeria monocytogenes strains, reduced biofilm formation, and decreased the ability of the bacteria to adhere to and invade host cells. TQ also suppressed the transcription of genes associated with motility, biofilm formation, hemolysin secretion, and host-cell adhesion and invasion.
full_output.methodology: MIC and SIC assays, swimming motility tests, biofilm formation assays, SEM, adhesion and invasion assays, hemolysis assays, and RT-qPCR analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Surveillance of multidrug-resistant bacteria in pediatric and neonatal intensive care units in Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, particularly ESBL-producing Klebsiella sp. and E. coli, MRSA, and carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (CRGNB), in pediatric and neonatal intensive care units in Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional survey using electronic data from healthcare institutions reporting MDR bacteria cases.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-mediated mcr-1 gene in Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa: first report from Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of plasmid-mediated mcr-1 gene in colistin-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Pakistan.
full_output.methodology: PCR, Sanger sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: High rate of detection of OXA-23-producing Acinetobacter from two general hospitals in Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high rate of OXA-23-producing Acinetobacter isolates from two hospitals in Brazil, highlighting the significant role of OXA-23 and OXA-51 in carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, susceptibility testing, and PFGE analysis were used to identify and characterize OXA-producing Acinetobacter isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic-resistant bacteria in neonatal intensive care units, including Bacillus cereus, Staphylococcus epidermidis, Staphylococcus saprophyticus, Staphylococcus cohnii ssp. cohnii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Streptococcus gordoni, each exhibiting resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic resistance was assessed using the BD Phoenix™ 100 system, which determines susceptibility and resistance profiles of bacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Urinary tract infection pathogens and antimicrobial susceptibilities in Kobe, Japan and Taipei, Taiwan: an international analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found differences in antimicrobial resistance patterns between UTI-causing bacteria in Kobe, Japan and Taipei, Taiwan, particularly highlighting higher resistance rates of Klebsiella pneumoniae to cephalosporins and gentamicin in Taipei compared to Kobe.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of urine culture samples and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.
full_output.sample_size: 4519 samples from Kobe University Hospital, Kobe and 25,131 samples from Shuang-Ho Hospital, Taipei

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli O157:H7: distribution, molecular characterization, antimicrobial resistance patterns and source of contamination of sheep and goat carcasses at an export abattoir, Mojdo, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all 20 isolates of E. coli O157:H7 were susceptible to Norfloxacin (NOR).
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the agar disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Type of bacterial isolates and antimicrobial resistance profile from different clinical samples at a Referral Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia: five years data analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of antimicrobial resistance among bacterial isolates, with 100% resistance to ampicillin and high resistance rates to other antibiotics such as tetracycline, doxycycline, and gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of bacteriological and antimicrobial susceptibility testing data from clinical samples over five years.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Tuberculosis Diagnosis Using Reporter Enzyme Fluorescence.

BlaC is highly conserved among tuberculosis complex members and exhibits unique structural features that distinguish it from other β-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: The study uses fluorogenic substrates and enzyme activity assays to detect BlaC in sputum samples, validating its specificity and sensitivity for tuberculosis diagnosis.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a Multidrug-Resistant Porcine Klebsiella pneumoniae Sequence Type 11 Strain Coharboring bla(KPC-2) and fosA3 on Two Novel Hybrid Plasmids.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of blaKPC-2 and fosA3 on two novel hybrid plasmids in a multidrug-resistant porcine Klebsiella pneumoniae ST11 strain, highlighting the potential for transmission between animals and humans.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid analysis, and MIC testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of 4-Amino-Thieno[2,3-d]Pyrimidines as QcrB Inhibitors in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Inactivating pathogenic bacteria in greywater by biosynthesized Cu/Zn nanoparticles from secondary metabolite of Aspergillus iizukae; optimization, mechanism and techno economic analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that Cu/Zn nanoparticles synthesized from the secondary metabolite of Aspergillus iizukae are effective in inactivating antibiotic-resistant E. coli and S. aureus in greywater. The nanoparticles exhibit strong antimicrobial activity, leading to significant reductions in bacterial load.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized response surface methodology to optimize the inactivation of E. coli and S. aureus in greywater using Cu/Zn nanoparticles. The antimicrobial activity was assessed through agar diffusion assays and characterized using FESEM, EDX, FTIR, and Raman spectroscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic relatedness in carbapenem-resistant isolates from clinical specimens in Ghana using ERIC-PCR technique.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenemase genes blaNDM-1, blaVIM-1, and blaOXA-48, along with ESBL genes blaTEM-1 and blaSHV-1, in carbapenem-resistant isolates from Ghana. These genes were prevalent in various Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting the diversity of resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: The opportunistic pathogen Stenotrophomonas maltophilia utilizes a type IV secretion system for interbacterial killing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Smlt3024 as a novel T4SS effector from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia that reduces the growth rate of E. coli when expressed in the periplasm, and Smlt3025 as its cognate immunity protein that neutralizes the toxicity of Smlt3024.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics, genetic manipulation, and microbiological assays were used to characterize the T4SS effectors and their immunity proteins.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of multidrug resistant Enterobacteriaceae among residents of long term care facilities in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (MDRGN) among residents of long-term care facilities (LTCFs) in Amsterdam, with a focus on ESBL-E. The most commonly detected ESBL genes were CTX-M-15 and CTX-M-27, along with other beta-lactamase genes such as TEM-1, SHV-2, SHV-12, TEM-52, and TEM-20.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting fecal and nasal swabs from residents of LTCFs, followed by microbiological analysis, PCR, and sequencing to detect and characterize AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of ubiquitin-proteasome system components affecting the degradation of the transcription factor Pap1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes involved in the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) that influence the degradation of the transcription factor Pap1, thereby affecting oxidative stress tolerance in fission yeast.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized genetic screens, protein carbonylation analysis, and fluorescence microscopy to investigate the roles of UPS components in regulating Pap1 levels and oxidative stress responses.

full_output.paper_title: Overcoming Fish Defences: The Virulence Factors of Yersinia ruckeri.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the virulence factors of Yersinia ruckeri, focusing on its toxins, secretion systems, and other pathogenic mechanisms. Key virulence factors include Yrp1 protease, YrpAB peptidases, yhlBA pore-forming toxin, phospholipase, and Afp18 antifeeding prophage. The study highlights the roles of these factors in causing enteric redmouth disease in fish.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and studies on Y. ruckeri virulence factors, including molecular and biochemical analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenemase-Producing Elizabethkingia Meningoseptica from Healthy Pigs Associated with Colistin Use in Spain.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and molecular analysis were used to identify carbapenemase genes in the isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial use policy change in pre-weaned dairy calves and its impact on antimicrobial resistance in commensal Escherichia coli: a cross sectional and ecological study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that antimicrobial resistance in commensal E. coli from pre-weaned dairy calves was widespread, with 85% of isolates resistant to at least three antimicrobial classes. Resistance to tetracycline, sulfisoxazole, chloramphenicol, kanamycin, streptomycin, and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole was particularly high. The study also noted that resistance patterns changed over time, with a decline in resistance following antimicrobial use policy changes.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial resistance in E. coli isolates from pre-weaned calves, examining the impact of policy changes on resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Convergent Evolution of the Barnase/EndoU/Colicin/RelE (BECR) Fold in Antibacterial tRNase Toxins.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two CdiA-CT toxin domains, CdiA-CT Kp342 and CdiA-CT EC3006, which are specific tRNases that cleave the acceptor stem of deacylated tRNA GAU Ile. These toxins show structural homology but differ in their requirements for extrinsic activation.
full_output.methodology: Structural and biochemical analysis of CdiA-CT•CdiI complexes.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of Antibiotic Resistance on Treatment of Pneumococcal Disease in Ethiopia: An Agent-Based Modeling Simulation.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the significant impact of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) on the treatment of pneumococcal disease in Ethiopia, showing that AMR leads to increased treatment failures and child deaths. It emphasizes the importance of antibiotic stewardship to mitigate the spread of AMR.
full_output.methodology: The study used an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach to simulate the dynamics of antimicrobial resistance in pneumococcal disease, incorporating data on antibiotic usage, resistance patterns, and treatment outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of synergistic effect of tazobactam with meropenem and ciprofloxacin against multi-drug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolated from burn patients in Tehran.

full_output.paper_title: High Prevalence of Antimicrobial Resistance Among Gram-Negative Isolated Bacilli in Intensive Care Units at a Tertiary-Care Hospital in Yucatán Mexico.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates among gram-negative bacilli (GNB) isolated from ICU patients, particularly Escherichia coli, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. full_output.paper_title: Horizontal Gene Transfer and Its Association with Antibiotic Resistance in the Genus Aeromonas spp.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various AMR genes in Aeromonas spp., including beta-lactamases (ampH, blaCEPH-A3, imiH), quinolone resistance genes (qnrS1, qnrB7, qnrB19, qnrD1, oqxAB), and carbapenemase (blaNDM-1) and colistin resistance gene (mcr-3). full_output.paper_title: The Contribution of Efflux Pumps in Mycobacterium abscessus Complex Resistance to Clarithromycin.
full_output.key_findings: Efflux pumps contribute significantly to clarithromycin resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus complex, alongside the erm (41) gene. Overexpression of MAB_3142 and MAB_1409 efflux pump genes was observed in multiple strains, enhancing resistance.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing, RT-qPCR, efflux activity assays, and genotyping were used to investigate resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Loci Encoding Compounds Potentially Active against Drug-Resistant Pathogens amidst a Decreasing Pool of Novel Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) in environmental pseudomonads that produce compounds capable of inhibiting multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens, including carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, phylogenetic analysis, and bioinformatics tools were used to identify and validate BGCs involved in antagonistic activity against MDR pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli Clonobiome: Assessing the Strain Diversity in Feces and Urine by Deep Amplicon Sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on assessing the strain diversity of Escherichia coli in feces and urine using deep amplicon sequencing, highlighting the presence of the pandemic multidrug-resistant E. coli clone ST131-H30 (H30) and its potential to dominate the gut and urine in healthy carriers.
full_output.methodology: The study employed deep amplicon sequencing combined with a novel algorithm (PLAP) for analyzing allelic diversity in E. coli strains, along with traditional cloning and sequencing methods for validation.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents the first structure of the class D β-lactamase CDD-1 from the pathogenic Gram-positive bacterium Clostridioides difficile, and its complex with cefotaxime. CDD-1 exhibits a unique structural feature with an extended Ω-loop that contributes to its ability to hydrolyze expanded-spectrum cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography and structural analysis of CDD-1 and its complex with cefotaxime.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance Evolution against Phage Combinations Depends on the Timing and Order of Exposure.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the timing and order of phage exposure significantly influence the strength, cost, and mutational basis of resistance evolution in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Sequential exposure allows bacteria to acquire multiple resistance mutations effective against both phages, while simultaneous exposure results in weaker resistance. Specific mutations in genes like wzy, pilB, pilN, pilR, galU, and others were identified as contributing to phage resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing of resistant mutants and comparative analysis of resistance strengths under different phage exposure regimes.

full_output.paper_title: 5-Dodecanolide interferes with biofilm formation and reduces the virulence of Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) through up regulation of agr system.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that 5-Dodecanolide (DD) reduces biofilm formation and virulence of MRSA by up-regulating the agr system, leading to down-regulation of adhesion proteins and up-regulation of matrix-degrading enzymes.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR, biofilm assays, microscopic analysis, and enzymatic activity tests were used to evaluate the effects of DD on MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Thermo-responsive triple-function nanotransporter for efficient chemo-photothermal therapy of multidrug-resistant bacterial infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a thermo-responsive nanotransporter (TRIDENT) for the treatment of multidrug-resistant bacterial infections, combining chemo-photothermal therapy with antibiotic delivery. TRIDENT effectively delivers imipenem (IMP) and IR780, enhancing antibacterial efficacy through temperature-dependent release and photothermal effects.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized nanoprecipitation to fabricate TRIDENT, characterized its physicochemical properties, and evaluated its antibacterial efficacy in vitro and in vivo.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of IncX3 Plasmid-Harboring bla (NDM-) (5) Dominated by Escherichia coli ST48 in a Goose Farm in Jiangsu, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaNDM-5-harboring Escherichia coli strains in a goose farm in Jiangsu, China, highlighting the role of IncX3 plasmids in the dissemination of carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistant strains.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a Linezolid- and Vancomycin-Resistant Streptococcus suis Isolate That Harbors optrA and vanG Operons.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first linezolid- and vancomycin-resistant Streptococcus suis isolate harboring the optrA and vanG operons, indicating the potential risk of these resistance genes spreading to other Gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Myrtenol Attenuates MRSA Biofilm and Virulence by Suppressing sarA Expression Dynamism.
full_output.key_findings: Myrtenol reduces MRSA biofilm formation and virulence by suppressing the expression of the sarA gene.
full_output.methodology: Biofilm inhibition assays, real-time PCR, and microscopic analysis were used to evaluate the effects of myrtenol on MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Ceftazidime/avibactam Improves the Antibacterial Efficacy of Polymyxin B Against Polymyxin B Heteroresistant KPC-2-Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae and Hinders Emergence of Resistant Subpopulation in vitro.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a pmrA mutation (G53R) in polymyxin B-resistant cells of B1, which is associated with heteroresistance. The combination of ceftazidime/avibactam improves the efficacy of polymyxin B against heteroresistant KPC-2-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae and prevents the emergence of resistant subpopulations.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, qRT-PCR, time-kill assays, and population analysis profiles were used to assess antimicrobial resistance and evaluate the efficacy of ceftazidime/avibactam in combination with polymyxin B.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a NDM-1-Encoding Plasmid pHFK418-NDM From a Clinical Proteus mirabilis Isolate Harboring Two Novel Transposons, Tn6624 and Tn6625.

full_output.paper_title: Pyoverdine-Dependent Virulence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolates From Cystic Fibrosis Patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the role of pyoverdine in the virulence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from cystic fibrosis patients and demonstrates that pyoverdine inhibitors can mitigate pathogenesis.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of in vitro and in vivo models, including C. elegans and murine pneumonia models, along with biochemical assays to assess pyoverdine production and its impact on virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Quorum Quenching Lactonase Strengthens Bacteriophage and Antibiotic Arsenal Against Pseudomonas aeruginosa Clinical Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the quorum quenching lactonase Sso Pox-W263I effectively reduces virulence factors and biofilm formation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates and their phage-resistant mutants, highlighting its potential as an adjunct to antibiotic and phage therapies.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro assays to measure virulence factors and biofilm formation, along with amoeba infection models to assess in vivo virulence reduction.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic-Induced, Increased Conjugative Transfer Is Common to Diverse Naturally Occurring ESBL Plasmids in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that antibiotic exposure increases conjugative transfer of various ESBL plasmids in E. coli, highlighting the potential risk of antibiotic use in promoting the spread of antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Neonatal Exposure to Amoxicillin Alters Long-Term Immune Response Despite Transient Effects on Gut-Microbiota in Piglets.
full_output.key_findings: Early life amoxicillin exposure in pigs altered immune cell phenotype and function, leading to increased pro-inflammatory responses and changes in T cell subsets, but no AMR genes or mutations were characterized in this study.
full_output.methodology: Analysis of immune cell populations, cytokine production, and microbial composition in piglets following amoxicillin exposure.

full_output.paper_title: Peptide Occurring in Enterobacteriaceae Triggers Streptococcus pneumoniae Cell Death.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the ORF 1 peptide triggers programmed cell death in Streptococcus pneumoniae by upregulating genes lytFN1 and lytFN2, which are associated with cell wall degradation and programmed cell death.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RNA-Seq and proteomic analysis to examine gene and protein expression changes in response to the ORF 1 peptide, along with growth and viability assays.

full_output.paper_title: Cannabidiol Is a Novel Modulator of Bacterial Membrane Vesicles.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that cannabidiol (CBD) inhibits membrane vesicle (MV) release from Gram-negative bacteria, enhances antibiotic efficacy, and alters MV protein profiles, suggesting potential as an adjuvant to combat antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used MV isolation, TEM, NTA, western blotting, and proteomic analysis to evaluate the effects of CBD on bacterial MVs and antibiotic sensitivity.

full_output.paper_title: An Outbreak of Carbapenem-Resistant and Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae in an Intensive Care Unit of a Major Teaching Hospital in Wenzhou, China.

full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Tracing local and regional clusters of carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae ST512 with whole genome sequencing, Finland, 2013 to 2018.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two clusters of KPC-3-producing K. pneumoniae ST512 in Finland, highlighting the role of environmental transmission and the need for improved infection control measures.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) fermentative Gram-negative bacilli, with 94.5% being MDR, 8.8% extensively drug-resistant (XDR), and 0.8% pan drug-resistant (PDR). full_output.paper_title: Anti-biofilm Agents against Pseudomonas aeruginosa: A Structure-Activity Relationship Study of C-Glycosidic LecB Inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies dimethylthiophene 22 and phenylacetylene 29 as potent inhibitors of LecB, showing strong biofilm inhibition in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Structure-activity relationship analysis, competitive binding assays, biofilm assays, and crystallography.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotics for trachoma
full_output.key_findings: The review highlights the increased risk of antibiotic resistance in S pneumoniae, S aureus, and E coli following mass azithromycin distribution, particularly for macrolides. It also notes the lack of significant resistance development for penicillin and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of cluster-randomized trials evaluating antibiotic treatment for trachoma.
full_output.sample_size: Various studies conducted in multiple countries

full_output.paper_title: Countering Gram-Negative Antibiotic Resistance: Recent Progress in Disrupting the Outer Membrane with Novel Therapeutics.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses recent advances in targeting the outer membrane (OM) of Gram-negative bacteria as a strategy to counter antibiotic resistance. It highlights the importance of OM assembly pathways involving proteins like Bam, Lpt, and Lol, and explores potential therapeutic interventions targeting these systems.
full_output.methodology: Review of literature and discussion of recent research findings on OM assembly and disruption.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-Based Design and in Silico Screening of Virtual Combinatorial Library of Benzamides Inhibiting 2-trans Enoyl-Acyl Carrier Protein Reductase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with Favorable Predicted Pharmacokinetic Profiles.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a structure-based design and in silico screening of novel benzamide inhibitors targeting InhA of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, identifying potent analogs with predicted high inhibitory potencies and favorable pharmacokinetic profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Various Vaccine Candidate Proteins in Clinical Isolates of Streptococcus pneumoniae: Characterization of the Novel Pht Fusion Proteins PhtA/B and PhtA/D.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of various vaccine candidate proteins in clinical isolates of Streptococcus pneumoniae, including the novel Pht fusion proteins PhtA/B and PhtA/D. full_output.paper_title: Possible role of L-form switching in recurrent urinary tract infection.

The probiotic strains Lactobacillus reuteri, Enterococcus faecium, Bifidobacterium animalis, and Pediococcus acidilactici showed inhibitory effects on Salmonella proliferation in vitro.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo experiments to evaluate the effects of synbiotic supplementation on Salmonella colonization in broiler birds.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and molecular characterization of Neisseria gonorrhoeae in Ghana, 2012-2015.
full_output.key_findings: High rates of resistance to tetracycline, benzylpenicillin, and ciprofloxacin were identified in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from Ghana. A mosaic penA-34 allele was associated with high cefixime MIC, indicating resistance.
full_output.methodology: AMR testing, NG-MAST, and penA sequencing were used to characterize resistance mechanisms in N. gonorrhoeae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin-resistance gene cluster, vanC, in the gut microbiome of acute leukemia patients undergoing intensive chemotherapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of vanC1 and vanC2/3 gene clusters in the gut microbiome of acute leukemia patients undergoing intensive chemotherapy, indicating low-level vancomycin resistance in Enterococcus gallinarum and Enterococcus casseliflavus.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR (qPCR) was used to detect vanC1 and vanC2/3 gene clusters in stool samples from 20 acute leukemia patients.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Resistance to β-Lactam Antibiotics and bla Genes Among Commensal Haemophilus parainfluenzae Isolates from Respiratory Microbiota in Poland.

blaTEM-1.evidence_note: The paper states that blaTEM-1 was the most prevalent beta-lactamase gene among H. parainfluenzae isolates, and it is associated with resistance to ampicillin and amoxicillin.

blaOXA.evidence_note: The paper states that bla OXA was present in 19.3% of beta-lactam-resistant isolates.

blaROB-1.evidence_note: The paper states that blaROB-1 was identified in 2.8% of beta-lactamase-positive beta-lactam-resistant H. parainfluenzae isolates.

ftsI.notes: Lys-526 substitution in ftsI gene is associated with beta-lactam resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several beta-lactamase genes (bla TEM-1, bla OXA, bla DHA, and bla SHV) in Haemophilus parainfluenzae isolates, along with the Lys-526 substitution in the ftsI gene, which contributes to beta-lactam resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing were used to detect beta-lactamase genes and mutations in the ftsI gene.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of Lipophilic Nucleoside Analogues as Inhibitors of Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetases.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on synthesizing lipophilic nucleoside analogues to inhibit aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (aaRSs) and improve bacterial membrane permeability. While several compounds showed inhibitory activity against IleRS and LeuRS, none demonstrated significant antimicrobial activity against the tested microbes.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, radiolabel transfer assay, and antimicrobial assays were conducted to evaluate the inhibitory activity and antimicrobial effects of the synthesized compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Crystal structure of ErmE - 23S rRNA methyltransferase in macrolide resistance.

ermE.validation_method: structural analysis and comparison with related enzymes

full_output.key_findings: The crystal structure of ErmE, a 23S rRNA methyltransferase involved in macrolide resistance, was determined. ErmE methylates A2058 in 23S rRNA, protecting ribosomes from macrolide binding. Structural comparisons reveal similarities with other methyltransferases like ErmC', PikR1, and PikR2.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography and structural analysis of ErmE.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance genotypes and phenotypes of Campylobacter jejuni isolated in Italy from humans, birds from wild and urban habitats, and poultry.

gyrA.notes: Only mutations in the quinolone resistance-determining region (QRDR) of gyrA were regarded to be the determinants of resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance gene tet(O), beta-lactam resistance genes blaOXA-61 and blaOXA-184, and the CmeABC efflux pump system as major contributors to antimicrobial resistance in Campylobacter jejuni isolates from Italy.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and mutations in Campylobacter jejuni isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Denture stomatitis associated with small-colony variants of Staphylococcus aureus: a case report.

mecA.mechanism: methicillin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study reports a case of denture stomatitis associated with small-colony variants (SCVs) of Staphylococcus aureus, which were found to be methicillin-susceptible but resistant to gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification of nuc and coa genes, mecA gene detection, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: The streptothricin acetyltransferase (sat) gene as a positive selectable marker for methanogenic archaea.

sat.validation_method: expression in Methanosarcina species and resistance to nourseothricin

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the sat gene from Streptomyces rochei can serve as a positive selectable marker for methanogenic archaea, particularly Methanosarcina species, by conferring resistance to nourseothricin.
full_output.methodology: The study involved constructing plasmids expressing the sat gene, transforming methanogenic archaea, and assessing nourseothricin resistance through growth experiments and PCR verification.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that nitric oxide (NO) donors, such as JS-K and DETNO, can reverse multidrug resistance in human tumor cells by inhibiting the ATPase activity of ABCB1 (P-gp) and ABCG2 (BCRP), leading to increased drug accumulation and reversal of resistance to Adriamycin, Topotecan, and Mitoxantrone.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized cytotoxicity assays, Western blot analysis, confocal microscopy, ATPase activity inhibition assays, and molecular docking studies to investigate the effects of NO donors on drug resistance in tumor cells.

full_output.key_findings: This study analyzed TetR-family transcription factors (TFTRs) in Gram-negative bacteria, focusing on their roles in efflux regulation and antimicrobial resistance. It identified core and accessory TFTRs in Escherichia and Salmonella, highlighting their conservation and variation across strains and species.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics and literature analysis were used to identify and characterize TFTRs in Escherichia and Salmonella species.

full_output.paper_title: Cathelicidin-Derived Synthetic Peptide Improves Therapeutic Potential of Vancomycin Against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: FK16 enhances the antibacterial susceptibility of vancomycin against Pseudomonas aeruginosa by increasing membrane permeability, demonstrating synergistic bactericidal activity.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution, growth inhibition assay, SYTOX-green dye uptake assay, time-kill assay, and checkerboard assay.

full_output.key_findings: The study established a multiple cross displacement amplification (MCDA) coupled with a nanoparticle-based lateral flow biosensor (LFB) assay for rapid, simple, and reliable detection of Mycoplasma pneumoniae. The assay showed higher sensitivity compared to culture-based and real-time PCR methods.
full_output.methodology: The study developed and validated an MCDA-LFB assay for M. pneumoniae detection using specific primers targeting the P1 gene, with performance evaluated through sensitivity, specificity, and clinical sample testing.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Features of Antarctic Acinetobacter radioresistens Strain A154 Harboring Multiple Antibiotic-Resistance Genes.

blaTEM−1B.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and in silico analysis
