full_output.paper_title: Outbreak of macrolide-resistant mycoplasma pneumoniae in a primary school in Beijing, China in 2018.

23S rRNA.notes: The mutation was identified in the 23S rRNA gene of M. pneumoniae strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a point mutation (A to G at position 2063) in the 23S rRNA gene of M. pneumoniae, which is associated with macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR and sequencing to detect and characterize the macrolide resistance mutation in M. pneumoniae.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that the ethyl acetate extract of Cyathea gigantea exhibited antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant organisms, including Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The extract showed synergistic effects when combined with conventional antibiotics such as ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, ampicillin, and oxacillin.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was assessed using well diffusion and broth microdilution methods to determine the diameters of growth inhibition zones, minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC). Synergistic activity with conventional antibiotics was also determined.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular investigation and phylogeny of species of the Anaplasmataceae infecting animals and ticks in Senegal.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several Anaplasmataceae species, including Anaplasma ovis, A. marginale, A. centrale, A. cf. platys, 'Candidatus Anaplasma africae', Ehrlichia canis, and Anaplasma platys, in various animals and ticks in Senegal.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization using 23S rRNA, 16S rRNA, rpoB, and groEL genes, along with sequencing and phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: International travel as source of a hospital outbreak with an unusual meticillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus clonal complex 398, Denmark, 2016.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the PVL-positive human variant of MRSA CC398 as the cause of an outbreak in a Danish maternity unit, highlighting the role of international travelers in introducing such strains into healthcare settings.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, MALDI-TOF MS, and multiplex PCR were used to characterize the outbreak strain and its resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: The Ancestral N-Terminal Domain of Big Defensins Drives Bacterially Triggered Assembly into Antimicrobial Nanonets.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the antimicrobial activity of Cg-BigDef1, a big defensin from oysters, which exhibits broad-spectrum bactericidal activity against multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and other pathogens, even at high salt concentrations. The N-terminal domain of Cg-BigDef1 is crucial for its antimicrobial activity and enables the formation of nanonets that trap and kill bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized synthetic chemistry, NMR spectroscopy, and antimicrobial assays to characterize the structure and function of Cg-BigDef1.

full_output.paper_title: The global diversity of Haemonchus contortus is shaped by human intervention and climate.

Hco-tbb-iso-1.notes: Mutations in Hco-tbb-iso-1 are associated with benzimidazole resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the Hco-tbb-iso-1 gene associated with benzimidazole resistance in Haemonchus contortus.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and genetic analysis of isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Amphiphilic Triazine Polymer Derivatives as Antibacterial And Anti-atopic Agents in Mice Model.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed amphiphilic triazine polymers (TZP3 and TZP5) with potent antibacterial activity against drug-resistant pathogens and anti-atopic effects in a mouse model of atopic dermatitis.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of antimicrobial and anti-atopic activities of triazine-based polymers in vitro and in vivo.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates in E. coli isolates from cattle in Eastern Algeria, particularly to ampicillin (59.09%) and tetracycline (43.43%). Nine extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing E. coli strains were detected, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility was determined using the disk diffusion method on Mueller-Hinton agar, with additional tests for ESBL detection and colistin MIC determination.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiological study of sausage in Algeria: Prevalence, quality assessment, and antibiotic resistance of Staphylococcus aureus isolates and the risk factors associated with consumer habits affecting foodborne poisoning.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of Staphylococcus aureus contamination in raw sausage samples from Algeria, with 25.22% of samples contaminated. High levels of multidrug resistance were observed, particularly to tetracycline, oxacillin, and fosfomycin.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting sausage samples from 230 butcheries in ten departments of Algiers and testing the isolates for antibiotic resistance using disk diffusion and E-test methods.

full_output.paper_title: In-Vitro Biofilm Formation and Antimicrobial Resistance of Escherichia coli in Diabetic and Nondiabetic Patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Escherichia coli isolates from diabetic and nondiabetic patients exhibited varying levels of antimicrobial resistance, with higher resistance rates observed in biofilm-producing strains. Imipenem, nitrofurantoin, and amikacin were the most effective antibiotics against uropathogenic E. coli, while amoxicillin, ciprofloxacin, and cotrimoxazole were least effective. Biofilm-forming E. coli showed significantly higher resistance to quinolones, cotrimoxazole, and third-generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the modified Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method, and biofilm formation was assessed using the microtiter plate method.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria from positive blood cultures using the Accelerate Pheno™ system.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the performance of the Accelerate Pheno™ system for rapid identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of bacteria from positive blood cultures, showing promising results for Gram-negative rods, staphylococci, and enterococci.
full_output.methodology: The study used the Accelerate Pheno™ system for identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing, comparing results with standard methods like MALDI-TOF MS and disk diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Plant growth promoting and antifungal activity in endophytic Bacillus strains from pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified endophytic Bacillus strains from pearl millet that exhibit antifungal activity and plant growth promoting (PGP) traits. These strains were found to possess antimicrobial peptide genes (ituD, bmyC, and srfA) which contribute to their antagonistic properties against fungal pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation of endophytic Bacillus strains, PCR amplification and sequencing of antimicrobial peptide genes, and assessment of their antifungal and PGP activities.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Emergence of Florfenicol-Resistant Invasive Non-Typhoidal Salmonella in China: A Potential Threat to Public Health.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of florfenicol-resistant invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella (iNTS) in China, highlighting the presence of resistance genes floR, fexB, and fexA, which contribute to florfenicol resistance via efflux mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: The AVR4 effector is involved in cercosporin biosynthesis and likely affects the virulence of Cercospora cf. flagellaris on soybean.
full_output.key_findings: The AVR4 effector is involved in cercosporin biosynthesis and affects the virulence of Cercospora cf. flagellaris on soybean.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, disruption, dsRNA-mediated suppression, and analysis of cercosporin production and gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Inter-host Transmission of Carbapenemase-Producing Escherichia coli among Humans and Backyard Animals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaNDM genes as the primary cause of carbapenem resistance in Escherichia coli isolates from humans, pigs, chickens, and flies in rural China, highlighting the transmission of these resistance genes between humans and backyard animals.
full_output.methodology: PCR, whole-genome sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize carbapenem-resistant Escherichia coli isolates.

pykF.encodes: pyruvate kinase that catalyzes the last step of glycolysis

full_output.key_findings: The study found that LTEE-derived strains had decreased intrinsic resistance to antibiotics compared to their ancestor, and that the evolvability of resistance was influenced by genetic background, with some strains showing reduced capacity to develop resistance to tetracycline due to specific mutations.
full_output.methodology: The study used antibiotic susceptibility testing, evolvability assays, and fluctuation tests to analyze resistance and mutation rates in E. coli strains from the LTEE.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli and Salmonella spp. isolated from Australian meat chickens remain susceptible to critically important antimicrobial agents.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA were found in two E. coli isolates with elevated ciprofloxacin MICs.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that E. coli and Salmonella isolates from Australian meat chickens remained susceptible to critically important antimicrobial agents. However, two E. coli isolates showed reduced susceptibility to ciprofloxacin due to mutations in the quinolone resistance-determining regions of gyrA.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, whole genome sequencing, and molecular analysis were used to characterize resistance mechanisms.
full_output.sample_size: 206 E. coli isolates and 53 Salmonella isolates

full_output.paper_title: What a Difference a Gene Makes: Identification of Virulence Factors of Cowpox Virus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies g7tGP, gD7L, gCrmE, and gNMDAr as virulence factors in Cowpox virus (CPXV) that significantly increase virulence in Wistar rats.
full_output.methodology: Animal experiments, BAC mutagenesis, and transcriptomic analyses were used to characterize the virulence factors of CPXV.

full_output.paper_title: Dissecting the molecular evolution of fluoroquinolone-resistant Shigella sonnei.

gyrA.mechanism: mutations in the quinolone resistance determining region (QRDR): gyrA -S83L, parC -S80I and gyrA -D87G
gyrA.genetic_context: QRDR mutations in gyrA and parC
gyrA.evidence_note: The paper describes how mutations in gyrA and parC confer resistance to fluoroquinolones in Shigella sonnei.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of a single clonal expansion of fluoroquinolone-resistant Shigella sonnei in South Asia, driven by sequential mutations in the quinolone resistance determining region (QRDR) of gyrA and parC genes. These mutations include gyrA-S83L, parC-S80I, and gyrA-D87G, which collectively confer fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and experimental evolution experiments were used to analyze the emergence and spread of fluoroquinolone-resistant Shigella sonnei.

full_output.paper_title: Dissemination of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii strains carrying the bla (GES), bla (NDM) and bla (OXA23) in Morocco.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of blaOXA-23, blaGES, and blaNDM genes in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii strains in Morocco, highlighting the dissemination of these resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: PCR, phenotypic tests, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to detect and characterize the AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative genomic analysis of the Hafnia genus reveals an explicit evolutionary relationship between the species alvei and paralvei and provides insights into pathogenicity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several aminoglycoside resistance genes (acc-1, acc-2, acc-3, acc-5) and efflux pump genes (acrAB, farB) in Hafnia alvei and paralvei, highlighting their role in antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of 47 Hafnia strains to identify resistance genes and virulence factors.

full_output.paper_title: Inactivation of folylpolyglutamate synthetase Met7 results in genome instability driven by an increased dUTP/dTTP ratio.
full_output.key_findings: Inactivation of Met7 leads to genome instability due to increased dUTP/dTTP ratio, resulting in uracil incorporation into DNA and subsequent genome instability.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, HPLC analysis, mutational assays, and DNA damage response analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Polymeric nanobiotics as a novel treatment for mycobacterial infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces polymeric nanobiotics as a novel approach for treating mycobacterial infections, demonstrating their effectiveness in delivering isoniazid (INH) and clofazimine (CFZ) to combat Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Mycobacterium marinum.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized polymer synthesis, nanoparticle formulation, and in vitro and in vivo evaluations to assess the efficacy of nanobiotics against mycobacterial infections.

full_output.paper_title: Stringent response governs the oxidative stress resistance and virulence of Francisella tularensis.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: decreased ppGpp production and increased sensitivity to oxidative stress

relA.notes: Loss of relA function leads to decreased ppGpp production and increased sensitivity to oxidative stress

mutations_found.effect_on_function: decreased ppGpp production and increased sensitivity to oxidative stress

spoT.notes: Loss of spoT function leads to decreased ppGpp production and increased sensitivity to oxidative stress

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the stringent response governed by RelA and SpoT is crucial for the oxidative stress resistance and virulence of Francisella tularensis. Deletion of relA and spoT leads to decreased ppGpp production, impaired growth, increased sensitivity to antibiotics, and reduced virulence.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion mutants and transcomplemented strains were generated, and their growth, ppGpp production, and sensitivity to antibiotics were analyzed.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, particularly extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli, were prevalent in patients with chemotherapy-induced neutropenic septic shock. Over 30% of the isolates were MDR, with 48.5% showing resistance to cefepime.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of patients with neutropenic septic shock, including microbiological studies and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: MYC predetermines the sensitivity of gastrointestinal cancer to antifolate drugs through regulating TYMS transcription.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MYC as a key regulator of TYMS transcription, which determines the sensitivity of gastrointestinal cancer cells to antifolate drugs like raltitrexed (RTX).
full_output.methodology: Genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screening, cell-based functional assays, and analysis of patient data.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that household contacts exposed to multidrug resistant tuberculosis had a higher risk of infection compared to those exposed to drug sensitive tuberculosis, but the risk of developing tuberculosis disease was similar between the two groups.
full_output.methodology: Prospective cohort study analyzing the association between drug resistance profiles of index patients and the risk of tuberculosis infection and disease among household contacts.

full_output.paper_title: Synthetic hydrophobic peptides derived from MgtR weaken Salmonella pathogenicity and work with a different mode of action than endogenously produced peptides.

mgtR.notes: Mutation in the Ala-coil motif affects interaction with MgtC
mgtR.evidence_note: The paper describes the S17I mutation in MgtR and its effect on interaction with MgtC.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that synthetic MgtR peptides, including the MgtR-S17I variant, reduce Salmonella intramacrophage replication and lower MgtC and MgtB protein levels, suggesting a different mechanism of action compared to endogenously produced peptides.
full_output.methodology: Used β-galactosidase assays, Western blot analysis, and confocal microscopy to assess the effects of synthetic peptides on Salmonella.

full_output.paper_title: A secreted metal-binding protein protects necrotrophic phytopathogens from reactive oxygen species.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IbpS and IbpP as metal-binding proteins that protect necrotrophic phytopathogens from reactive oxygen species by binding Fe3+ and Cu2+. These proteins are secreted and play a role in the infection process of Dickeya dadantii and Botrytis cinerea.
full_output.methodology: Protein purification, metal binding assays, crystallography, and infection experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Prophages and satellite prophages are widespread in Streptococcus and may play a role in pneumococcal pathogenesis.

vapE.validation_method: in vivo studies using a murine pneumococcal infection model

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a satellite prophage associated with virulence in Streptococcus pneumoniae, highlighting the role of prophages in pneumococcal pathogenesis. The gene vapE, found in the satellite prophage, contributes to virulence as demonstrated by in vivo experiments.
full_output.methodology: Genome analysis, in vivo infection models, and transcriptome studies were used to investigate the role of prophages and satellite prophages in Streptococcus pneumoniae virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Microcins: Small Peptides with Big Impacts on Bacterial Interactions
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes several genes involved in microcin immunity and resistance, including mceF, mcmM, mcmT, mchA, mcsI, mceB, mchB, mcmI, and mchS3, highlighting their roles in conferring resistance to microcins such as MccH47, MccM, and MccE492.
full_output.methodology: Experimental validation of gene function and resistance mechanisms in bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: In silico Selection and Experimental Validation of FDA-Approved Drugs as Anti-quorum Sensing Agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pimozide as a specific PqsR inhibitor that reduces PqsR-controlled virulence traits in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Virtual screening and bioluminescence assays were used to identify and validate PqsR inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Selection and dissemination of antimicrobial resistance in Agri-food production.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the selection and dissemination of antimicrobial resistance in agri-food production, highlighting the role of antimicrobial use, heavy metals, and biocides in selecting for resistance genes. It provides a comprehensive overview of various antimicrobial resistance genes and their mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews literature and presents data from various studies on antimicrobial resistance in agri-food production.

full_output.paper_title: Non-antibiotic Small-Molecule Regulation of DHFR-Based Destabilizing Domains InÂ Vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 14a, a non-antibiotic TMP derivative, as an effective stabilizer of DHFR-based destabilizing domains (DDs) in mammalian cells and in vivo in mice, without impacting the gut microbiota.
full_output.methodology: The study used biochemical assays, 16S rRNA sequencing, qPCR, western blotting, and bioluminescence imaging to evaluate the effects of 14a on DHFR DD stabilization and gut microbiota.
full_output.sample_size: n=6 mice for 16S rRNA sequencing, n=3-4 mice for bioluminescence imaging

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the QuantaMatrix Multiplexed Assay Platform for Molecular Diagnosis of Multidrug- and Extensively Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis Using Clinical Strains Isolated in Myanmar.
full_output.key_findings: The QMAP MDR/XDR assay can detect all known DNA mutations associated with drug resistance for both MDR- and XDR-MTB strains, providing a rapid molecular diagnostic tool for identifying drug-resistant tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the QMAP MDR/XDR assay by comparing its results with those of phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (pDST) and performing DNA sequencing on discordant results.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and Risk Factors for Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase-Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae Colonization in Intensive Care Units
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaCTX-M-15 as the predominant extended-spectrum beta-lactamase gene in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from ICU patients, contributing to resistance against ceftazidime and cefotaxime.
full_output.methodology: PCR-sequencing for ESBL genotyping and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis for clonal relatedness analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-Genome Analysis of bla(CTX-M-55)-Carrying (Escherichia coli) Among Pigs, Farm Environment, and Farm Workers.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla(CTX-M-55) carrying E. coli isolates from pigs, farm environment, and farm workers, highlighting the potential for dissemination of antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes and plasmid structures.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in genes such as rpsJ, rpsE, parC, gyrA, EF_3290, and 23S rRNA that contribute to collateral sensitivity and resistance in Enterococcus faecalis, revealing complex relationships between drug resistance and sensitivity profiles.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR amplification, and Sanger sequencing were used to identify mutations associated with collateral sensitivity and resistance in Enterococcus faecalis.

full_output.paper_title: Oxamniquine resistance alleles are widespread in Old World Schistosoma mansoni and predate drug deployment.

SmSULT-OR.mechanism: recessive loss-of-function mutations leading to reduced oxamniquine (OXA) activation
SmSULT-OR.validation_method: in vitro OXA activation assay and thermodynamic modeling

SmSULT-OR.notes: Recessive loss-of-function mutations in SmSULT-OR lead to oxamniquine resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies six independent oxamniquine resistance mutations in Schistosoma mansoni, including p.E142del, p.W120R, p.N171IfsX28, p.C35R, p.L179P, and p.S12X, which are widespread in Old World populations and predate drug deployment.
full_output.methodology: Exome sequencing, in vitro OXA activation assay, and thermodynamic modeling were used to identify and validate oxamniquine resistance mutations in Schistosoma mansoni.

lrrkA.mechanism: modulates Kil2 activity and intraphagosomal killing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LrrkA as a kinase with leucine-rich repeats that modulates Kil2 activity and intraphagosomal killing in Dictyostelium discoideum.
full_output.methodology: Genetic inactivation of lrrkA and phenotypic analysis of intracellular killing and proteolysis.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of Antibiotic Resistance of Coagulase-Negative Staphylococci Isolated from Healthy Turkeys in Egypt: First Report of Linezolid Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: This study identified the first report of linezolid resistance in coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) isolated from healthy turkeys in Egypt. The study found that 79.5% of the isolates were resistant to linezolid, and the resistance was associated with the presence of the cfr, optrA, and valS genes. The study also found high levels of resistance to other antibiotics, including erythromycin, chloramphenicol, oxacillin, daptomycin, and tigecycline.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and MALDI-TOF MS were used to identify and characterize the CoNS isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis of Trichodermin Derivatives and Their Antimicrobial and Cytotoxic Activities.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the synthesis of trichodermin derivatives and their evaluation for antimicrobial and cytotoxic activities. Key findings include the identification of specific trichodermin derivatives with selective antimicrobial activity against Candida albicans and notable cytotoxic effects against the MCF-7 breast cancer cell line.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, structural characterization via NMR and HRMS, and biological evaluations including antimicrobial and cytotoxic assays.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of Carbapenem-Resistant and Colistin-Resistant Escherichia coli Co-Producing NDM-1 and MCR-1 from Pig Farms in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaNDM-1 and mcr-1 as the primary resistance genes in carbapenem-resistant and colistin-resistant E. coli isolates from pig farms in China, highlighting their coexistence on plasmids and their ability to confer resistance to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes and plasmids in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Environmental Conditions May Shape the Patterns of Genomic Variations in Leishmania panamensis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genomic variations in Leishmania panamensis, including copy number variations in genes such as LPMP_230280 (encoding an ABC transporter MRPA) and LPMP_310020 (encoding an aquaglyceroporin), which are associated with antimony resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and copy number variation analysis were used to investigate genomic variations in Leishmania panamensis strains exposed to antimony.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial MgrB peptide activates chemoreceptor Fpr3 in mouse accessory olfactory system and drives avoidance behaviour.
full_output.key_findings: MgrB peptide is recognized by Fpr3, a chemoreceptor in the mouse accessory olfactory system, leading to avoidance behavior. MgrB is a virulence regulator in Enterobacteriaceae and is associated with pathogenicity.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput Ca2+ imaging, bioinformatics analyses, and in vivo behavioral assays.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a novel transposon cluster in Clostridioides difficile
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a large transposable island (023_CTnT) in Clostridium difficile clade 3 strains, containing novel genes including sortase substrates, lantibiotic transporters, and a siderophore biosynthetic cluster. Some elements of the island can excise and transfer to other strains, suggesting potential for niche adaptation and virulence enhancement.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, PCR, and expression analysis were used to characterize the genetic elements and their functionality in C. difficile strains.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization, expression profiling, and functional analysis of a Populus trichocarpa defensin gene and its potential as an anti-Agrobacterium rooting medium additive.

PtDef.validation_method: prokaryotic expression and antimicrobial activity assays

full_output.key_findings: The PtDef gene from Populus trichocarpa was identified as a defensin with potent antibacterial and antifungal activities, showing resistance against Agrobacterium tumefaciens, Escherichia coli, and several fungi. It was functionally characterized and demonstrated effectiveness as an alternative to cefotaxime in rooting media.
full_output.methodology: Molecular cloning, prokaryotic expression, antimicrobial activity assays, and qRT-PCR for gene expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome sequencing, analyses of drug resistance-conferring mutations, and correlation with transmission of Mycobacterium tuberculosis carrying katG-S315T in Hanoi, Vietnam.

rpoB.validation_method: genomic analysis and association with resistant phenotype

rpsL.validation_method: genomic analysis and association with resistant phenotype

mutations_found.validated_by: genomic analysis and association with resistant phenotype

rpoB.notes: associated with rifampicin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several mutations in genes associated with drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including katG-S315T for isoniazid resistance, gid-E173* for streptomycin resistance, emrB-F508S for ethambutol resistance, Rv1588c-P34P for isoniazid resistance, and pncA-Q141P for pyrazinamide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and variant-based GWAS were used to analyze drug resistance-conferring mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Hanoi, Vietnam.

full_output.paper_title: Surface Modification by Media Organics Reduces the Bacterio-toxicity of Cupric Oxide Nanoparticle against Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that unmodified CuO-NPs exhibited significant antibacterial activity against E. coli K-12 and S. aureus, with lower MBC values compared to modified CuO-NPs. The antibacterial effect was attributed to the generation of ROS, leading to lipid peroxidation, protein oxidation, and DNA degradation.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of CuO-NPs using MBC determination, flow cytometry to assess membrane potential, and measurement of ROS levels in E. coli cells.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of the addition of azithromycin to antimalarials used for seasonal malaria chemoprevention on antimicrobial resistance of Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the addition of azithromycin to antimalarials used for seasonal malaria chemoprevention was associated with an increase in resistance of pneumococci to azithromycin and erythromycin, which persisted 1 year after the last administration of azithromycin.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the antimicrobial resistance of Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates from nasopharyngeal swabs collected during a trial in Burkina Faso and Mali.

full_output.paper_title: Influence of Different Cell-Penetrating Peptides on the Antimicrobial Efficiency of PNAs in Streptococcus pyogenes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that CPP-coupled anti-gyrA PNAs effectively inhibit the growth of Streptococcus pyogenes by targeting the essential gene gyrA, which encodes the subunit A of DNA topoisomerase gyrase.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized bacterial kill assays, MIC determination, and Galleria mellonella infection models to evaluate the antimicrobial effects of CPP-coupled anti-gyrA PNAs.

full_output.paper_title: Tomato glycosyltransferase Twi1 plays a role in flavonoid glycosylation and defence against virus.

Twi1.mechanism: glucosyltransferase activity towards coumarins and flavonoids
Twi1.validation_method: in vitro enzymatic activity assay and transgenic plant analysis

full_output.key_findings: Twi1 is a glycosyltransferase that mediates the glycosylation of coumarins and flavonoids, playing a role in tomato defense against viral infection.
full_output.methodology: In vitro enzymatic activity assays and transgenic plant analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Xi-class mycothiol S-transferase from Corynebacterium glutamicum and its protective effects in oxidative stress.

mstX.validation_method: MIC and growth curve inhibition assay, site-directed mutagenesis, enzymatic activity assays

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the ncgl1216 gene, now named mstX, as a mycothiol S-transferase Xi class with thiol transferase and reductase activities, playing a critical role in oxidative stress resistance in Corynebacterium glutamicum.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, MIC assays, and enzymatic activity analysis were conducted to characterize the function of mstX.

full_output.paper_title: Burden of Shigella spp and Vibrio spp, and their antibiotic sensitivity pattern in the patients with acute gastroenteritis in tertiary care hospital in Nepal.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high rates of resistance among Vibrio cholerae and Shigella spp isolates, particularly to nitrofurantoin, cotrimoxazole, nalidixic acid, ampicillin, and ceftriaxone.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the modified Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of resistance and phenotypic characterization of carbapenem resistance mechanisms in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates at Sahloul University Hospital-Sousse, Tunisia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, specifically NDM-1 and OXA-48-like carbapenemases, contributing to carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic detection of carbapenemases using ROSCO KPC/MBL and OXA-48 Confirm Kit, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and phenotypic characterization of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus from clinical and community samples in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study detected 44 MRSA isolates from clinical and community samples in Abakaliki, Nigeria, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant MRSA strains with high resistance to antibiotics such as ceftazidime, tetracycline, and penicillin.
full_output.methodology: Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method and nitrocefin stick for beta-lactamase detection were used to identify MRSA isolates and assess antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies chemical modifications to tridecaptin A analogues that enhance resistance to d-peptidases BogQ and TriF, maintaining antimicrobial activity against MDR bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of tridecaptin A analogues for resistance to d-peptidases and antimicrobial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Yeast α-arrestin Art2 is the key regulator of ubiquitylation-dependent endocytosis of plasma membrane vitamin B1 transporters.

ART2.notes: Mutations in ART2 affect Thi7 endocytosis.

ART9.notes: Mutations in ART9 affect Thi7 endocytosis.

mutations_found.position_in_molecule: cytoplasmic loop between TM6 and TM7

THI7.evidence_note: The paper describes mutations in Thi7 that impair thiamine-induced endocytosis, but does not explicitly state that these mutations confer resistance to antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: Art2 is the key regulator of ubiquitylation-dependent endocytosis of the thiamine transporter Thi7. Mutations in ART2 and ART9 impair endocytosis of Thi7 and its homologs Nrt1 and Thi72.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative proteomics, genetic screening, GFP fusion analysis, and immunoblotting.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, Docking Studies, and In Vitro Evaluation of Some Novel Thienopyridines and Fused Thienopyridine-Quinolines as Antibacterial Agents and DNA Gyrase Inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of several novel thienopyridines and fused thienopyridine-quinolines as antibacterial agents and DNA gyrase inhibitors. Compounds 3a, 3b, 4a, 9b, and 12b showed high inhibitory activity against E. coli DNA gyrase, with IC50 values lower than that of novobiocin.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, in vitro antibacterial activity testing, DNA gyrase inhibition assay, and molecular docking studies.

full_output.paper_title: Evolutionary stability of collateral sensitivity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in nalC, nalD, and pmrB that contribute to re-sensitization to gentamicin and carbenicillin in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, highlighting the complex interactions between drug resistance mechanisms and evolutionary trade-offs.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, functional genetic analysis, and dose-response experiments were used to investigate the evolutionary dynamics of collateral sensitivity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Simultaneous Infection with Enterobacteriaceae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa Harboring Multiple Carbapenemases in a Returning Traveler Colonized with Candida auris.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple carbapenemase genes, including blaNDM-1, blaNDM-5, blaCTX-M-15, and blaOXA-181, in multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from a patient colonized with Candida auris.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and PCR screening were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes in the isolates.

penA-60.001.mechanism: mutation in penicillin-binding protein 2 (PBP2), including A311V (GCC to GTC)

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a LAMP assay to detect Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains carrying the penA-60.001 allele, which is associated with ceftriaxone resistance due to a mutation in penicillin-binding protein 2 (PBP2), including A311V.
full_output.methodology: Development and evaluation of a loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay targeting the penA-60.001 allele in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
full_output.sample_size: 204 N. gonorrhoeae strains and 95 strains of other Neisseria spp.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations Reducing In Vitro Susceptibility to Novel LpxC Inhibitors in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Interplay of Efflux and Nonefflux Mechanisms.

lpxC.notes: LpxC A214V reduces susceptibility to compound 3 and compound 2

fabG.notes: FabG C494T reduces susceptibility to various LpxC inhibitors

fabF1.notes: FabF1 T306A reduces susceptibility to CHIR-090

PA4465.notes: PA4465 N193T reduces susceptibility to various LpxC inhibitors

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several mutations in lpxC, fabG, fabF1, and PA4465 that reduce susceptibility to LpxC inhibitors in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Specifically, lpxC G208S and A214V, fabG C494T, fabF1 T306A, and PA4465 N193T are shown to confer resistance to various LpxC inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: The study uses single-step mutant selections, serial passage experiments, whole-genome sequencing, and MIC testing to identify and validate resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and Metabolomic Polymorphism among Experimentally Selected Paromomycin-Resistant Leishmania donovani Strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a heterozygous SNP in the MAPKKK gene (LdBPK_190007100) associated with paromomycin resistance in Leishmania donovani, alongside aneuploidy and metabolic changes.

full_output.paper_title: The Small Protein CydX Is Required for Cytochrome bd Quinol Oxidase Stability and Function in Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhimurium: a Phenotypic Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that the small protein CydX is essential for the assembly and function of the cytochrome bd complex in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, and its absence leads to increased resistance to certain antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic analysis, UV-Vis spectroscopy, oxygen consumption measurements, and antibiotic susceptibility tests.

full_output.paper_title: Pre-detection history of extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.

full_output.paper_title: Broad and Efficient Control of Klebsiella Pathogens by Peptidoglycan-Degrading and Pore-Forming Bacteriocins Klebicins.
full_output.key_findings: Nine pore-forming and peptidoglycan-degrading bacteriocins from different Klebsiella species were identified and characterized. full_output.paper_title: Broad-spectrum resistance to bacterial blight in rice using genome editing.

full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing was used to introduce mutations in SWEET gene promoters, followed by evaluation of resistance to Xoo strains.

full_output.paper_title: Diagnostic kit for rice blight resistance.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized genome editing, RT-PCR, and mutant analysis to characterize SWEET gene variants and their role in Xoo resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Fecal Transplant in Children With Clostridioides difficile Gives Sustained Reduction in Antimicrobial Resistance and Potential Pathogen Burden.
full_output.key_findings: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in children with recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) leads to a sustained reduction in antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes and potential pathogen burden.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was used to analyze changes in AMR genes and potential pathogens in stool samples from donors and recipients before and after FMT.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that higher MICs (>2 mg/L) of ceftolozane/tazobactam (C/T) were associated with increased 30-day mortality in patients with lower respiratory tract infections caused by multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa. High-dose C/T was linked to lower mortality in patients with strains having MIC ≤2 mg/L.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational study analyzing clinical outcomes of patients with MDR/XDR P. aeruginosa infections treated with C/T, focusing on the correlation between C/T MIC and 30-day mortality.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characteristics of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter spp. from clinical infection samples and fecal survey samples in Southern China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several carbapenem resistance genes, including bla OXA-23-like, bla OXA-51-like, bla OXA-58-like, and bla NDM-1, along with the mcr-1 gene for colistin resistance. Additionally, the carO gene and efflux pump genes (adeA, adeB, adeC, adeI, adeJ, adeK) were found to contribute to carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter species.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize resistance genes in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Chromosomal and plasmid-mediated fluoroquinolone resistance in human Salmonella enterica infection in Ghana.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) nasal carriage in the West of Iran, with 55 isolates out of 181 S. aureus. The mecA gene was detected in MRSA isolates, and the pvl gene was present in 14.54% of MRSA isolates.
full_output.methodology: Swabs were collected from anterior nares of 600 volunteers, and isolates were analyzed for methicillin resistance using cefoxitin disk diffusion and PCR for mecA. SCC mec types and pvl genes were determined through PCR.

full_output.key_findings: The Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) provides a curated resource for antimicrobial resistance (AMR) data, focusing on molecular sequences, detection models, and bioinformatics tools. full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates a novel fluorogenic assay for detecting carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (CPE) from bacterial colonies and positive blood cultures, demonstrating high accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods.
full_output.methodology: The study compares a fluorogenic assay with traditional phenotypic methods (mCIM, CNP, CIT) for detecting CPE, utilizing bacterial isolates and blood culture samples.

full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on using Raman spectroscopy and deep learning for rapid bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing, achieving high accuracy in classifying bacterial isolates and distinguishing between methicillin-resistant and -susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA and MSSA).
full_output.methodology: The study employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on Raman spectra of bacterial isolates to classify bacteria and predict antibiotic resistance, with validation on clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Diaminoquinazoline MMV675968 from Pathogen Box inhibits Acinetobacter baumannii growth through targeting of dihydrofolate reductase.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MMV675968 as a potent inhibitor of Acinetobacter baumannii growth by targeting its dihydrofolate reductase (AbDHFR).
full_output.methodology: Screening of Pathogen Box compounds, growth inhibition assays, and in vitro DHFR activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Human gut bacteria contain acquired interbacterial defence systems.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes acquired interbacterial defense (AID) gene clusters in Bacteroidales, including rAID-1, which provide protection against T6SS-mediated antagonism and contribute to microbiome stability.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analysis, genomic sequencing, and heterologous expression experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Point mutations in the squalene epoxidase gene of Indian ITS genotype VIII T. mentagrophytes identified after DNA isolation from infected scales.

mutations_found.validated_by: partial sequencing of the squalene epoxidase gene

squalene_epoxidase.notes: Single point mutation leading to terbinafine resistance

full_output.paper_title: Distribution and drug resistance of pathogenic bacteria in emergency patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance among pathogenic bacteria isolated from emergency patients, including Acinetobacter baumannii, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, and Candida albicans. Resistance to various antibiotics was noted, with specific resistance profiles varying among the bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolation and drug susceptibility testing were performed using standard laboratory procedures, including automated systems and agar diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in food and the prevalence in Brazil: a review.

mecA.mechanism: The mec A gene, responsible for methicillin resistance in S. aureus, is the reason for these groups of microorganisms to be considered resistant to all beta-lactam antibiotic
mecA.validation_method: detection via PCR and phenotypic testing
mecA.genetic_context: The mec A gene, responsible for methicillin resistance in S. aureus, is the reason for these groups of microorganisms to be considered resistant to all beta-lactam antibiotic
