full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the ompA gene in Cedecea neteri is crucial for biofilm formation and gut colonization in Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, highlighting its role in host-microbe interactions.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, biofilm assays, and mosquito infection experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Serotype distribution and antimicrobial resistance of human Salmonella enterica in Bangui, Central African Republic, from 2004 to 2013.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaCTX-M-15 gene in an ESBL-producing Salmonella Typhimurium isolate, which was part of a large conjugative IncHI2 plasmid. This plasmid was highly similar to those found in other sub-Saharan African countries, highlighting its role in the spread of ESBL genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and plasmid analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes and mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Quantitative dynamics of Salmonella and E. coli in feces of feedlot cattle treated with ceftiofur and chlortetracycline.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that antibiotic use decreased the overall quantity of Salmonella in cattle feces in the short term, but the quantities of antimicrobial-resistant NTS E. coli and Salmonella tended to remain constant. CTC treatment had a stronger effect on increasing the proportion of multidrug-resistant Salmonella than ceftiofur treatment.
full_output.methodology: The study used colony counting and qPCR to quantify Salmonella and NTS E. coli in fecal samples from cattle treated with ceftiofur and chlortetracycline.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of tetracycline treatment regimens on antibiotic resistance gene selection over time in nursery pigs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that tetracycline treatment regimens influenced the abundance of several tetracycline resistance genes (tet(A), tet(B), tet(O), tet(W)), as well as macrolide resistance genes (ermB, ermF) and sulfonamide resistance genes (sulI, sulII) in nursery pigs.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR to quantify the abundance of nine AMR genes in fecal samples from nursery pigs across different treatment regimens.

full_output.paper_title: Etiology of childhood diarrhoea among under five children and molecular analysis of antibiotic resistance in isolated enteric bacterial pathogens from a tertiary care hospital, Eastern Odisha, India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified NDM-1, qnrB, and aac(6')-Ib-cr genes associated with carbapenem and fluoroquinolone resistance in enteric bacterial pathogens. Mutations in gyrA (S83L) and parC (S80I) were linked to quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based detection, sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to analyze resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Nasopharyngeal carriage, spa types and antibiotic susceptibility profiles of Staphylococcus aureus from healthy children less than 5 years in Eastern Uganda.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high nasopharyngeal carriage rates of Staphylococcus aureus in children in Eastern Uganda, with 6.1% carrying MRSA. It found that MRSA isolates were more resistant to non-beta-lactam antimicrobials compared to MSSA. The study also noted high-level mupirocin resistance in some MRSA isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used BD Phoenix 100 ID/AST for antibiotic susceptibility testing and spa typing for genotyping S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Dissecting erm(41)-Mediated Macrolide-Inducible Resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus.

erm(41).genetic_context: erm(41) is located in close proximity to a gene cluster participating in the intrinsic resistance to clofazimine and bedaquiline in M. abscessus, comprising a TetR transcriptional repressor (MAB_2299c) that regulates the transcription of an MmpS/MmpL efflux pump system encoded by MAB_2300/MAB_2301
erm(41).source: Dissecting erm(41)-Mediated Macrolide-Inducible Resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus
erm(41).evidence_note: The paper describes that erm(41) encodes a ribosomal methylase that mediates macrolide-inducible resistance in M. abscessus. The gene is shown to be functional in M. abscessus subsp. abscessus and M. abscessus subsp. bolletii, and its expression is activated by the transcriptional regulator WhiB7. The study also identifies a WhiB7-binding site upstream of erm(41) that is required for macrolide-inducible expression.

erm(41).notes: T28C polymorphism is associated with loss of methylase activity and abrogation of inducible resistance
erm(41).evidence_note: The paper states that the T28C polymorphism in erm(41) is associated with loss of methylase activity and abrogation of inducible resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Exogenous Alginate Protects Staphylococcus aureus from Killing by Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: Exogenous alginate protects Staphylococcus aureus from Pseudomonas aeruginosa by downregulating the production of antimicrobial compounds such as pyoverdine, pyochelin, and HQNO, as well as reducing rhamnolipid and quorum sensing molecule production.
full_output.methodology: Experimental analysis of bacterial cocultures, siderophore and rhamnolipid quantification, qRT-PCR, and Nanostring gene expression analysis.

gyrA.evidence_note: The paper mentions that an emm 89 isolate presented high-level levofloxacin resistance and carried mutation E85K in gyrA.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified erm(B) and erm(TR) genes associated with macrolide resistance, and tet(M), tet(L), and tet(O) genes linked to tetracycline resistance in Streptococcus pyogenes isolates from invasive infections in Portugal. Additionally, mutations in parC (S79Y) and gyrA (E85K) were found to confer levofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic testing for antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effect of pH on the efficacy of antibiotics against Coxiella burnetii in axenic media. It found that moxifloxacin, doxycycline, and rifampin were effective at preventing C. burnetii growth at pH 4.75, 5.25, and 5.75, with rifampin showing bactericidal activity. The efficacy of doxycycline and moxifloxacin improved at higher pH, while rifampin activity was pH-independent.
full_output.methodology: The study used axenic media (ACCM-2) to test antibiotic susceptibility of C. burnetii under varying pH conditions, measuring growth through qPCR and assessing viability on agar plates.

full_output.paper_title: Transmission dynamics and control of multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in neonates in a developing country.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes, including blaCTX-M-15, blaCTX-M-14, and blaCTX-M-63, which contribute to multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in neonates in a Cambodian hospital.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from rectal and environmental swabs, combined with statistical modeling of transmission dynamics.

full_output.paper_title: Does Vitamin D3 Prevent the Inhibitory Effect of Vancomycin on Osteoblasts?
full_output.key_findings: Vancomycin at high concentrations inhibits osteoblast viability, while vitamin D3 does not confer protection against this cytotoxicity. However, vitamin D3 aids in the recovery of osteoblast differentiation and calcification when administered with pulsed vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: In vitro cell culture experiments with MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts, assessing cell viability, morphology, alkaline phosphatase activity, and calcification in response to vancomycin and vitamin D3.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in the TaPIN1 peptidyl prolyl isomerase gene in Theileria annulata parasites isolated in Sudan.

TaPIN1.notes: The study identifies multiple mutations in the TaPIN1 gene that may be associated with buparvaquone resistance in T. annulata parasites.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the TaPIN1 gene in T. annulata parasites isolated in Sudan, including the A53P mutation in the catalytic loop, which is associated with buparvaquone resistance. Additional mutations in the signal peptide and other regions of the gene may affect TaPin1 processing or targeting.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of the TaPIN1 gene in 67 T. annulata isolates from Sudan and comparison with reference sequences.

full_output.paper_title: Quantification and Multidrug Resistance Profiles of Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococci Isolated from Two Wastewater Treatment Plants in the Same Municipality.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanA as a prevalent vancomycin resistance gene in vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) isolated from two wastewater treatment plants. The gene was detected in various Enterococcus species, including E. faecalis, E. faecium, E. casseliflavus, and E. gallinarum.
full_output.methodology: qPCR, MIC testing, and molecular speciation techniques were used to identify and characterize AMR genes and resistance profiles in VRE isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Expression of 9-O- and 7,9-O-Acetyl Modified Sialic Acid in Cells and Their Effects on Influenza Viruses.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the roles of CasD1 and SIAE in modifying sialic acid, highlighting their impact on influenza virus infection. CasD1 adds acetyl groups to sialic acid, while SIAE removes them. These modifications influence the susceptibility of cells to influenza C and D viruses.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, flow cytometry, immunofluorescence microscopy, and HPLC analysis were used to investigate the effects of CasD1 and SIAE on sialic acid modifications and their impact on viral infection.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the accumulation of anhNAM-P5 as the activator signal underlying AmpC β-lactamase hyperproduction in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, highlighting distinct signaling pathways for AmpC regulation based on genetic mutations and environmental stimuli.
full_output.methodology: UPLC-MS analysis of muropeptides, ampC expression quantification, and mutant strain analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Schinus terebinthifolia leaf lectin (SteLL) has anti-infective action and modulates the response of Staphylococcus aureus-infected macrophages.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that SteLL, a lectin from Schinus terebinthifolia, has anti-infective properties against Staphylococcus aureus, enhances macrophage bactericidal activity, and modulates cytokine release. It also increases the effectiveness of ciprofloxacin and inhibits staphyloxanthin production.
full_output.methodology: The study used flow cytometry, time-kill assays, checkerboard assays, and in vivo infection models with Galleria mellonella larvae to evaluate the antimicrobial effects of SteLL.

full_output.paper_title: The occurrence of the multidrug resistance (MDR) and the prevalence of virulence genes and QACs resistance genes in E. coli isolated from environmental and avian sources.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of QACs resistance genes (qacEΔ1, qacA/B, and qacC/D) in E. coli isolates from environmental and avian sources, indicating their association with multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence and QACs resistance genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Serotype distribution and antimicrobial resistance patterns of invasive pneumococcal disease isolates from children in mainland China-a systematic review.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates to cefuroxime, cefaclor, and erythromycin among invasive pneumococcal disease isolates from children in mainland China.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review of published literature from 2000 to 2018 analyzing serotype distribution and antimicrobial resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility and genetic profile of Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae isolates from Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified genetic variability among Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae isolates from Brazil, including differences in the presence of specific genes such as mhp0461, mhp0272, mhp0487, mhp0107, mhp0660, mhp372, mhp199, mhp0443, p42, p97, p46, NrdF, p95, mnuA, mhp418, and p37. blaNDM-1.genetic_context: bla NDM-1 and bla CTX-M-3 genes were probed using Southern blotting, which confirmed the location of both genes on the same plasmid with molecular weight of 336.5–398.4 kb
blaNDM-1.evidence_note: The bla NDM-1 and bla CTX-M-3 genes were detected in the ROF058 trans-conjugant, indicating that bla NDM-1 can be co-transferred with bla CTX-M-3 and across species

blaCTX-M-3.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and conjugation assays

blaCTX-M-14.genetic_context: bla CTX-M-14 gene was located on a 138.9 kb plasmid in both isolates. The bla CTX-M-14 gene in ROI014 was located on a 216.9–244.4 kb plasmid.
blaCTX-M-14.evidence_note: The bla CTX-M-14 gene was identified in all the strains, and multidrug resistance was confirmed by antimicrobial susceptibility tests.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of NDM-1 and CTX-M-3 producing Raoultella ornithinolytica in human gut microbiota, highlighting the potential for inter-species transfer of drug resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, conjugation assays, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Antibacterial Activity of Designed Trp-Containing Antibacterial Peptides in Combination With Antibiotics Against Multidrug-Resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that Trp-containing peptides synergistically enhance the antibacterial activity of antibiotics against multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis by reducing the expression of resistance genes such as bla Z, tet(m), and msr A.
full_output.methodology: The study used real-time quantitative PCR to evaluate the effect of Trp-containing peptides on gene expression and checkerboard assays to determine synergistic antibacterial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Raw meat-based diets for companion animals: a potential source of transmission of pathogenic and antimicrobial-resistant Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes, including bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-3, bla CTX-M-9, bla SHV-12, mcr-1, and rmtB, in Enterobacteriaceae isolated from raw meat-based diets for companion animals. These genes confer resistance to various antibiotics, highlighting the potential public health risk associated with the consumption of such diets.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect AMR genes in isolates from raw meat-based diets.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Salmonella Bredeney Resistant to Third-Generation Cephalosporins in Saudi Arabia.

organisms_tested_in: Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Bredeney

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Salmonella Bredeney resistant to third-generation cephalosporins in Saudi Arabia, highlighting the presence of 13 cephalosporin resistance-associated genes, including a novel gene LEN-23.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and comparative genomics analysis were used to identify resistance genes and mechanisms in Salmonella Bredeney isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Legionella pneumophila regulates the activity of UBE2N by deamidase-mediated deubiquitination.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MvcA as a deubiquitinase that reverses MavC-induced ubiquitination of UBE2N, restoring its activity and allowing NFκB activation during Legionella pneumophila infection.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis, biochemical assays, and mutagenesis experiments were conducted to characterize the deubiquitinating activity of MvcA and its interaction with UBE2N.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro killing of canine strains of Staphylococcus pseudintermedius and Escherichia coli by cefazolin, cefovecin, doxycycline and pradofloxacin over a range of bacterial densities.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro bactericidal activity of cefazolin, cefovecin, doxycycline, and pradofloxacin against canine strains of Staphylococcus pseudintermedius and Escherichia coli at various bacterial densities and drug concentrations.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro kill assays to measure the effectiveness of antibiotics against bacterial strains at different concentrations and densities.
full_output.sample_size: 3 strains of S. pseudintermedius and 3 strains of E. coli

full_output.paper_title: CPO Complete, a novel test for fast, accurate phenotypic detection and classification of carbapenemases.
full_output.key_findings: The CPO Complete test was evaluated for rapid and accurate detection and classification of carbapenemases in various bacterial isolates, demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the CPO Complete test through experimental analysis of 262 CPO isolates and 67 non-CPO isolates, assessing its performance in detecting and classifying carbapenemases.

full_output.paper_title: The putative bacterial oxygen sensor Pseudomonas prolyl hydroxylase (PPHD) suppresses antibiotic resistance and pathogenicity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that PPHD suppresses antibiotic resistance and pathogenicity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Specifically, PPHD deficiency leads to increased tetracycline resistance through upregulation of the mexEF-oprN efflux pump.
full_output.methodology: The study used a PPHD knockout mutant (PAO310) and compared it to the wild-type strain (PAO1) to investigate the role of PPHD in virulence and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Giant single molecule chemistry events observed from a tetrachloroaurate(III) embedded Mycobacterium smegmatis porin A nanopore.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the MspA-M nanopore, which incorporates methionine residues to facilitate Au(III)-thioether coordination, enabling the detection of biothiols such as L-cysteine, L-homocysteine, and L-glutathione through single molecule sensing.
full_output.methodology: Electrophysiology measurements and nanopore sensing techniques were used to analyze the interaction of tetrachloroaurate(III) with the MspA-M nanopore.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified and characterized various natural variants of tridecaptin M, highlighting their antimicrobial activity against drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, including colistin-resistant strains. Some variants, particularly M11, showed potent activity with low MIC values.
full_output.methodology: The study involved purification of tridecaptin M variants via RP-HPLC, followed by antimicrobial activity testing, haemolysis assays, and in vitro drug kinetics.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity of P1 phage-like elements in multidrug resistant Escherichia coli.

blaTEM-1b.evidence_note: The paper states that pTZ20_1P contains bla TEM-1b (ampicillin resistance).

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple antibiotic resistance genes in P1-like plasmids, including blaTEM-1b, aac(3)-IV, aph(4)-Ia, dfrA12, aadA2, cmlA, aadA1, and qacI, which confer resistance to various antibiotics such as ampicillin, gentamicin, tobramycin, trimethoprim, streptomycin, spectinomycin, chloramphenicol, and quaternary ammonium compounds.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, annotation, comparative analysis, and gene characterization in plasmids.
full_output.sample_size: Three E. coli phage-like plasmids analyzed.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptional and Translational Inhibitors Block SOS Response and Shiga Toxin Expression in Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that transcriptional and translational inhibitors can block the SOS response and Shiga toxin (Stx) production in Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EHEC) by preventing the induction of the SOS response and Stx1/2 expression, even after the SOS response is fully induced.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a reporter gene-based system to monitor SOS response and Stx1 production, combined with RT-qPCR analysis to evaluate gene expression levels in response to various antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: The enemy from within: a prophage of Roseburia intestinalis systematically turns lytic in the mouse gut, driving bacterial adaptation by CRISPR spacer acquisition.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the Shimadzu phage's immunity region and VRs that contribute to its ultravirulent phenotype, along with CRISPR spacer acquisition in R. intestinalis as a resistance mechanism.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, qPCR, CRISPR analysis, and phage isolation techniques were used to characterize mutations and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: MRSA Strains in Nepalese Rhesus Macaques (Macaca mulatta) and Their Environment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in MRSA isolates from Rhesus macaques, environmental samples, and human patients in Nepal, including aacA-aadD, dfrA, erm(C), aacA-aphD, aphA3, sat, and blaZ.
full_output.methodology: DNA microarray analysis was used to characterize MRSA isolates and identify AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: A DedA Family Membrane Protein Is Required for Burkholderia thailandensis Colistin Resistance.

dbcA.genetic_context: mutation of dbcA results in >100-fold greater sensitivity to colistin
dbcA.evidence_note: Mutation of dbcA results in >100-fold greater sensitivity to colistin. Complementation of colistin sensitivity of B. thailandensis Δ dbcA was observed by expression of dbcA, E. coli yghB or E. coli yqjA.

full_output.key_findings: The DedA family protein DbcA is required for colistin resistance in Burkholderia thailandensis. Mutation of dbcA leads to increased sensitivity to colistin, and complementation with dbcA, E. coli yghB, or E. coli yqjA restores resistance.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, mass spectrometry, and site-directed mutagenesis were used to investigate the role of DbcA in colistin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Shape-Depended Biological Properties of Ag(3)PO(4) Microparticles: Evaluation of Antimicrobial Properties and Cytotoxicity in In Vitro Model-Safety Assessment of Potential Clinical Usage.
full_output.key_findings: Silver orthophosphate microparticles (SOMPs) exhibit antimicrobial activity against staphylococci and fungi, with c-SOMPs showing the highest efficacy. They demonstrate shape-dependent cytotoxicity towards mammalian cells, with c-SOMPs being the most cytotoxic.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of various shaped SOMPs, determination of antimicrobial activity via MIC and MBEC assays, and assessment of cytotoxicity using MTT and BrdU assays.

full_output.paper_title: Kalanchoe brasiliensis Cambess., a Promising Natural Source of Antioxidant and Antibiotic Agents against Multidrug-Resistant Pathogens for the Treatment of Salmonella Gastroenteritis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Kalanchoe brasiliensis as a natural source of antioxidant and antibacterial agents, particularly effective against Salmonella strains. The antibacterial action is linked to alterations in cell membrane integrity and permeability.
full_output.methodology: Chemical characterization via HPLC-DAD, antioxidant activity evaluation using DPPH, phosphomolybdenum reducing power, and β-carotene bleaching assays, and in vitro antibacterial activity assessment via MIC and time-kill assays.

full_output.paper_title: Predictors for vancomycin resistant Enterococcus faecium transforming from colonization to infection: a case control study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ICU admission, central venous catheter (CVC) use, and utilization of third- and fourth-generation cephalosporins as risk factors for vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) infection in colonized patients. It also highlights the association between concordant pulsotypes (CP) and shorter time to infection.
full_output.methodology: Case-control study analyzing risk factors for VREfm infection in colonized patients, utilizing molecular typing methods such as PFGE and MLST.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence of colistin resistance genes (mcr-1 and mcr-2) in wild birds and its public health implication in Egypt.

mcr-1.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the mcr-1 gene was first discovered in E. coli, K. pneumoniae and P. aeruginosa strains from China.

mcr-2.source: E. coli carrying mcr-1 (ID: 2012-60-1176-27) and E. coli containing mcr-2 (ID: KP37)
mcr-2.evidence_note: The paper mentions that E. coli carrying mcr-1 and E. coli containing mcr-2 were used as positive controls in PCR reactions.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1 and mcr-2 genes in wild birds, water, and human samples in Egypt, highlighting the potential environmental spread of colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to identify and characterize mcr-1 and mcr-2 genes.
full_output.sample_size: 140 wild bird fecal samples, 20 water samples, and 50 human stool samples

full_output.paper_title: Drug Resistance Characteristics of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Isolates From Patients With Tuberculosis to 12 Antituberculous Drugs in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified drug resistance profiles of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates to 12 antituberculous drugs, highlighting higher resistance rates in re-treated cases compared to initial treated cases, with specific resistance rates for various drugs including isoniazid, rifampin, and others.
full_output.methodology: The study performed drug susceptibility testing (DST) using the Myco TB system on 1,950 MTB isolates from patients in Shanghai, China.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a Novel Conjugative Plasmid in Edwardsiella piscicida Strain MS-18-199.

floR.encodes: major facilitator superfamily (MFS) antibiotic efflux pump
floR.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and functional analysis

tetA.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and functional analysis

tetR.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and functional analysis

sul2.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and functional analysis

strA.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and functional analysis

strB.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and functional analysis

arsA.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and functional analysis

arsD.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and functional analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a novel conjugative plasmid, pEPMS-18199, in Edwardsiella piscicida strain MS-18-199, which carries multiple antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes including floR, tetA, tetR, sul2, strA, strB, arsA, and arsD, conferring resistance to phenicol, tetracycline, sulfonamide, and aminoglycoside antibiotics, as well as arsenic.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, conjugation experiments, and functional analysis were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes on the plasmid.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Susceptibility and Florfenicol Resistance in Citrobacter Isolates and Whole-Genome Analysis of Multidrug-Resistant Citrobacter freundii.

floR.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the florfenicol resistance gene floR in Citrobacter isolates, which conferred resistance to florfenicol and chloramphenicol. The gene was found in a multidrug-resistant C. freundii strain and was part of a truncated transposon-like structure on a plasmid.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and MIC testing were used to identify and validate AMR genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the pharmacokinetics and safety of aztreonam/avibactam in patients with complicated intra-abdominal infections, but did not identify any specific AMR genes or mutations.
full_output.methodology: Phase 2a open-label, multicenter study assessing the PK, safety, and efficacy of aztreonam/avibactam in patients with cIAI.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the mecA gene in Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates, which confers resistance to oxacillin. The gene was experimentally validated through PCR amplification and sequencing.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing of the mecA gene in S. epidermidis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: First-line antibiotic susceptibility pattern of toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae in Indonesia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae isolates from Indonesia showed higher susceptibility to erythromycin compared to penicillin, with no resistant isolates to penicillin and 2.8% resistant to erythromycin. The susceptibility to erythromycin was better than that to penicillin.
full_output.methodology: The study used E-test to determine the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of antibiotics against C. diphtheriae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance in porcine pathogenic bacteria and relation to antibiotic usage.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed antibiotic resistance patterns in five major porcine pathogens, highlighting varying resistance levels to various antibiotics, with notable increases in resistance to florfenicol and neomycin in E. coli. Resistance to critically important compounds was generally low.
full_output.methodology: The study determined minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) for various antimicrobial agents in bacterial isolates from Danish pigs using broth microdilution methods.
full_output.sample_size: 1966 A. pleuropneumoniae, 266 B. bronchiseptica, 2923 E. coli, 168 S. hyicus, and 1482 S. suis isolates

full_output.paper_title: Mutation in MPT64 gene influencing diagnostic accuracy of SD Bioline assay (capilia).

mutations_found.protein_change: frameshift leading to stop codon after 41st amino acid
frameshift leading to stop codon after 41st amino acid
frameshift leading to stop codon after 88th amino acid

MPT64.notes: Mutations in MPT64 gene lead to false-negative results in capilia test.
MPT64.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that mutations in the MPT64 gene lead to false-negative results in the capilia test.

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in the MPT64 gene can cause false-negative results in the capilia test for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) detection.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of the MPT64 gene and comparison with the reference strain H37Rv.

full_output.paper_title: Photosensing and quorum sensing are integrated to control Pseudomonas aeruginosa collective behaviors.

algB.mechanism: phosphorylation-dependent repression of biofilm formation and virulence gene expression

bphP.mechanism: photoreceptor-mediated activation of AlgB through phosphorylation
bphP.validation_method: genetic suppression and in vitro phosphorylation assays

kinB.mechanism: regulation of biofilm formation and virulence gene expression through phosphorylation of AlgB

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the KinB-AlgB two-component system and the photosensor BphP as critical regulators of biofilm formation and virulence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, integrating quorum sensing and light signals to control collective behaviors.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screens, transposon mutagenesis, qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and in vitro phosphorylation assays were used to characterize the roles of KinB, AlgB, and BphP in regulating biofilm formation and virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Overexpressing GH3.1 and GH3.1L reduces susceptibility to Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri by repressing auxin signaling in citrus (Citrus sinensis Osbeck).
full_output.key_findings: Overexpression of CsGH3.1 and CsGH3.1L in citrus reduced susceptibility to Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri by repressing auxin signaling and enhancing defense responses.
full_output.methodology: Transgenic citrus plants were generated by overexpressing CsGH3.1 and CsGH3.1L, and their resistance to citrus canker was evaluated through phenotypic analysis, hormone content measurement, and transcriptomic profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive analysis of chromosomal mobile genetic elements in the gut microbiome reveals phylum-level niche-adaptive gene pools.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 5,219 putative chromosomal mobile genetic elements (MGEs) in the gut microbiome, highlighting their role in transferring niche-adaptive genes, including antibiotic resistance genes, bile salt detoxification genes, and genes involved in mucus degradation and sporulation.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a combination of metagenomic sequencing, computational analysis, and functional annotation to identify and classify MGEs in the gut microbiome.

full_output.paper_title: Significant reduction of vancomycin resistant E. faecium in the Norwegian broiler population coincided with measures taken by the broiler industry to reduce antimicrobial resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows a significant reduction in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VRE) in Norwegian broilers, which coincided with the removal of narasin as a feed additive. The vanA gene was identified as the primary mechanism of vancomycin resistance, and a putative narasin resistance mechanism was associated with VRE.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC testing, and in vivo experiments were used to analyze vancomycin and narasin resistance in E. faecium isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy of lyticase and β-glucosidase enzymes in degrading biofilms of Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains with different gene profiles, showing that β-glucosidase significantly reduced ceftazidime minimum biofilm eliminating concentrations (MBECs).
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR to detect biofilm-related genes, biofilm analysis via crystal violet assay, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to evaluate enzyme efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Chemotherapeutic drugs stimulate the release and recycling of extracellular vesicles to assist cancer cells in developing an urgent chemoresistance.
full_output.key_findings: Chemotherapeutic drugs enhance the release and recycling of extracellular vesicles (EVs) containing ABCB1, facilitating intercellular transfer of ABCB1 and conferring transient chemoresistance in cancer cells.
full_output.methodology: Flow cytometry, Western blotting, ELISA, and in vivo xenograft tumor models were used to assess the role of ABCB1 in chemoresistance.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular detection and antibiotic resistance pattern of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase producing Escherichia coli in a Tertiary Hospital in Enugu, Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M, bla TEM, and bla SHV genes as the primary contributors to extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) production in E. coli isolates from a Nigerian hospital. These genes were detected in 35% of the E. coli isolates, with bla CTX-M being the most prevalent.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR was used to detect ESBL genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of colistin resistance in multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli strains isolated from cancer patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1 as a plasmid-encoded colistin resistance gene in two isolates and a missense mutation in mgrB as a chromosomal cause of colistin resistance in one isolate.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to identify colistin resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of MDR1 and MRPA genes expression in different types of dry cutaneous leishmaniasis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that MDR1 and MRPA genes were over-expressed in different forms of dry cutaneous leishmaniasis, suggesting their potential role in glucantime resistance.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR was used to evaluate the expression levels of MDR1 and MRPA genes in paraffinized biopsy samples from patients with dry cutaneous leishmaniasis.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of new generation macrolides for the treatment and metaphylaxis of contagious bovine pleuropneumonia (CBPP) in cattle experimentally infected with Mycoplasma mycoides subspecies mycoides.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of new generation macrolides (tulathromycin, gamithromycin) and oxytetracycline in treating and preventing contagious bovine pleuropneumonia (CBPP) in cattle infected with Mycoplasma mycoides subspecies mycoides. Both macrolides showed significant protective effects against lung lesions and disease progression.
full_output.methodology: Experimental challenge with Mycoplasma mycoides subspecies mycoides followed by treatment with antibiotics and monitoring of clinical signs, lesion scores, and microbial recovery.
full_output.sample_size: 146 cattle in Kenya and 130 cattle in Zambia

full_output.key_findings: The study identified ST59 as the most common sequence type among community-acquired Staphylococcus aureus isolates causing skin and soft tissue infections in Shanghai, China. It also noted a high prevalence of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) and highlighted the molecular characteristics of the prevalent clone ST59.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, multilocus sequence typing (MLST), spa typing, SCC mec typing, and detection of virulence genes were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Screening of biomarkers of drug resistance or virulence in ESCAPE pathogens by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several biomarkers for drug resistance in ESCAPE pathogens using MALDI-TOF MS, including vanA for vancomycin resistance in E. faecium, mecA for methicillin resistance in S. aureus, blaOXA-24 and blaOXA-58 for carbapenem resistance in A. baumannii, and blaNDM for carbapenem resistance in K. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: MALDI-TOF MS was used to analyze protein profiles and identify potential biomarkers for drug resistance in various bacterial pathogens.
full_output.sample_size: 64 E. faecium, 67 S. aureus, 93 C. difficile, 68 A. baumannii, 55 P. aeruginosa, and 69 K. pneumoniae isolates

full_output.paper_title: Study of inhibitory potential and percent inhibition of oil of Syzygium aromaticum and leaves of Ocimum sanctum on ESBL enzyme from Escherichia coli in broilers of Jabalpur.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the inhibitory potential of Syzygium aromaticum oil and Ocimum sanctum leaves on beta-lactamase enzymes produced by ESBL-positive E. coli in broiler chickens, finding that Syzygium aromaticum oil had higher inhibitory effects compared to Ocimum sanctum leaf juice.
full_output.methodology: Colorimetric assay using CENTA and Nitrocefin as chromogenic substrates to assess the inhibitory potential of herbal extracts on beta-lactamase enzyme activity.

full_output.paper_title: Device-Associated Meningitis by Linezolid-Resistant Staphylococcus haemolyticus in a Vancomycin- Hypersensitive Patient.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the G2576T mutation in the 23S rRNA gene and the cfr gene as the molecular mechanisms of linezolid resistance in Staphylococcus haemolyticus.
full_output.methodology: Molecular analysis including PCR and sequencing of the 23S rRNA gene and detection of the cfr gene.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-51, blaOXA-23, blaVIM, and blaNDM as the primary carbapenem resistance genes in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from Egypt, with blaOXA-51 and blaOXA-23 being present in all isolates.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and molecular methods, including PCR, were used to detect carbapenemase genes and insertion sequences in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Unidirectional animal-to-human transmission of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus ST398 in pig farming; evidence from a surveillance study in southern Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) ST398 LA-MRSA in swine farm workers in southern Italy, highlighting the risk of animal-to-human transmission. All MRSA isolates were ST398, belonged to the livestock clade, and were resistant to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: MRSA isolates were characterized using spa, SCC mec, MLST, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Whole-genome sequencing was used for detailed genetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Structure Determination, Functional Characterization, and Biosynthetic Implications of Nybomycin Metabolites from a Mining Reclamation Site-Associated Streptomyces.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the isolation and characterization of three new nybomycins (nybomycins B-D) and six known compounds from Streptomyces sp. AD-3-6. Nybomycin D (3) and deoxynyboquinone (5) showed moderate to potent cancer cell line cytotoxicity, while rubromycins 6-8 exhibited moderate to potent anti-Gram+(+) bacterial and antifungal activity. Additionally, gamma-rubromycin (8) was identified as an inhibitor of axolotl embryo tail regeneration.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation, structural elucidation, and bioactivity assessment of metabolites from Streptomyces sp. AD-3-6 using NMR, HPLC, and various bioassays.

full_output.paper_title: Synthetic and Biological Studies on New Urea and Triazole Containing Cystobactamid Derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports on the synthesis and biological evaluation of thirteen new cystobactamid derivatives with improved chemical stability and antibacterial activity. The research focuses on modifying the amide bonds with urea and triazole groups, showing that certain substitutions preserve or enhance antibacterial potency against Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, including multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis and biological evaluation of new cystobactamid derivatives, including MIC testing against various bacterial strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that during natural transformation, transforming DNA (tDNA) integrates as single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) and forms a heteroduplex that is resolved by chromosome replication. This process leads to the rapid expression of integrated tDNA prior to cell division, enabling nongenetic inheritance of antibiotic resistance traits.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized fluorescent fusions, live-cell imaging, and genetic manipulation to investigate the dynamics of DNA integration during natural transformation in Vibrio cholerae and Streptococcus pneumoniae.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that increased number of antimicrobial treatments and retreatment with different mechanistic classes (bacteriostatic vs. bactericidal) were associated with a higher probability of isolating antimicrobial-resistant BRD pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of bacterial isolates from veterinary diagnostic laboratory samples with MIC testing and Bayesian statistical modeling.

full_output.paper_title: Epinecidin-1 Protects against Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Infection and Sepsis in Pyemia Pigs.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the antimicrobial peptide epinecidin-1 (Epi-1) effectively protects against Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infection in a pyemia pig model. Epi-1 reduces MRSA counts in various organs and mitigates sepsis-associated biomarkers. The study also identifies MRSA genes mecA, femA, etA, and etB as targets for Epi-1 action.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a pyemia pig model to evaluate the protective effects of Epi-1 against MRSA infection. It includes in vitro assays, pharmacokinetic studies, and molecular techniques such as multiplex PCR to assess gene expression and bacterial load.
full_output.sample_size: Various numbers of pigs were used in different experimental groups.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogenetic Diversity, Antimicrobial Susceptibility and Virulence Characteristics of Escherichia coli Isolates from Pigeon Meat.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in E. coli isolates from pigeon meat, including ampC, aadA, cmlA, sul1, sul2, and sul3, which confer resistance to beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, chloramphenicol, and sulfonamides.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and sequencing were used to identify AMR genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Thiostrepton: A Novel Therapeutic Drug Candidate for Mycobacterium abscessus Infection.
full_output.key_findings: Thiostrepton (TST) was found to be effective against Mycobacterium abscessus (Mab) strains, including drug-resistant mutants, showing significant growth inhibition in vitro and in vivo. TST also regulated proinflammatory cytokine production in infected macrophages.
full_output.methodology: Drug susceptibility tests, MIC determination, intracellular antimicrobial activity assays, and in vivo zebrafish infection models were used to evaluate TST's effectiveness against Mab.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Basis and Physiological Effects of Lipid A Hydroxylation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies lpxO1 and lpxO2 as genes responsible for lipid A hydroxylation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1, demonstrating that both enzymes hydroxylate different secondary acyl chains, with lpxO2 being primarily responsible for lipid A hydroxylation.
full_output.methodology: Generation of deletion mutants, lipid A analysis by mass spectrometry, and assessment of physiological effects.

full_output.paper_title: Biochemical and Structural Characterization of OXA-405, an OXA-48 Variant with Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase Activity.
full_output.key_findings: OXA-405 is an OXA-48 variant with extended-spectrum β-lactamase activity, capable of hydrolyzing ceftazidime, cefotaxime, and cephalothin, but with reduced carbapenemase activity due to a four-amino-acid deletion in the β5–β6 loop.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical and structural analysis, including kinetic parameters, X-ray crystallography, and molecular modeling.

full_output.methodology: The antimicrobial molecule was isolated from E. coli O103F and tested for its inhibitory effects on STEC strains under different treatments including pH, heat, and protease digestion.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of trans-Cinnamaldehyde on Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Biofilm Formation: Metabolic Activity Assessment and Analysis of the Biofilm-Associated Genes Expression.
full_output.key_findings: Trans-cinnamaldehyde (TC) reduces the metabolic activity and expression of biofilm-associated genes (eno, ebps, fib, icaA, icaD) in MRSA strains, suggesting its potential as an anti-biofilm agent.
full_output.methodology: Evaluation of TC's effect on MRSA biofilm formation through metabolic activity assessment and gene expression analysis via qRT-PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Cell Membrane-Interrupting Antimicrobial Peptides from Isatis indigotica Fortune Isolated by a Bacillus subtilis Expression System.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two novel antimicrobial peptides, IiR515 and IiR915, from Isatis indigotica, which exhibit significant antimicrobial activity against various bacterial and fungal pathogens through cell membrane disruption.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies eight ftsH genes in the Flavescence dorée phytoplasma (FDP) genome, highlighting their differential expression in various hosts, including plants and insects.

full_output.paper_title: First report of Klebsiella quasipneumoniae harboring bla(KPC-2) in Saudi Arabia.

full_output.paper_title: Experimental evolution of gallium resistance in Escherichia coli.

full_output.key_findings: E. coli K-12 MG1655 rapidly evolved resistance to gallium through mutations in the fecA gene, which encodes a ferric citrate outer membrane transporter. full_output.methodology: Experimental evolution, whole-genome sequencing, and phenotypic assays were used to identify genomic changes and validate resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Decreasing prevalence of contamination with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (ESBL-E) in retail chicken meat in the Netherlands.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and microbiological methods were used to identify ESBL genes and analyze the prevalence of ESBL-E in retail chicken meat.

full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis and well diffusion technique for antimicrobial activity testing.

full_output.paper_title: N-(2-Arylmethylthio-4-Chloro-5-Methylbenzenesulfonyl)amide Derivatives as Potential Antimicrobial Agents-Synthesis and Biological Studies.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimicrobial activity of N-(2-arylmethylthio-4-chloro-5-methylbenzenesulfonyl)amide derivatives against various bacterial and fungal strains, highlighting compounds 10 and 16 as showing high bacteriostatic activity against Staphylococcus aureus strains, including methicillin-resistant and methicillin-sensitive variants.

full_output.paper_title: An intubated 7-month-old infant with a retropharyngeal abscess and multidrug-resistant Streptococcus mitis.

full_output.paper_title: Marine macroalgae-associated heterotrophic Firmicutes and Gamma-proteobacteria: prospective anti-infective agents against multidrug resistant pathogens.

Resistance to ceftriaxone and azithromycin is also on the rise, highlighting the urgent need for improved surveillance and targeted public health interventions.

full_output.paper_title: Enhanced quantitative urine culture technique, a slight modification, in detecting under-diagnosed pediatric urinary tract infection.

full_output.paper_title: Class-A penicillin binding proteins do not contribute to cell shape but repair cell-wall defects.

full_output.paper_title: Structural Bases for the Fitness Cost of the Antibiotic-Resistance and Lethal Mutations at Position 1408 of 16S rRNA.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized NAT2 genotypes and their impact on isoniazid and N-acetyl-isoniazid pharmacokinetics in Zulu-speaking South Africans with HIV/TB co-infection.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping of NAT2 SNPs and analysis of isoniazid and N-acetyl-isoniazid concentrations in plasma.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies erm(41) as a gene conferring inducible clarithromycin resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus, highlighting its role in treatment challenges.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing and in vitro/in vivo efficacy studies were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Ceftazidime-Avibactam Resistance Associated with Increased blaKPC-3 Gene Copy Number Mediated by pKpQIL Plasmid Derivatives in Sequence Type 258 Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that increased blaKPC-3 gene copy number mediated by pKpQIL plasmid derivatives contributes to ceftazidime-avibactam resistance in sequence type 258 Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid transfer experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Lavender essential oil induces oxidative stress which modifies the bacterial membrane permeability of carbapenemase producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: Lavender essential oil (LVO) enhances the effectiveness of meropenem against carbapenemase-producing K. pneumoniae (KPC-KP) by inducing oxidative stress and disrupting the bacterial membrane. Proteomic analysis identified increased levels of beta-lactamase SHV-11 and carbapenem-hydrolyzing beta-lactamase KPC, indicating potential resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis, MIC assays, checkerboard assays, membrane permeability assays, and ROS measurement.

full_output.paper_title: Anthranilamide-based Short Peptides Self-Assembled Hydrogels as Antibacterial Agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the synthesis and evaluation of anthranilamide-based short peptides as antibacterial hydrogels, highlighting their ability to inhibit Staphylococcus aureus growth.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of anthranilamide-based short peptides and assessment of their antibacterial activity and cytotoxicity.

full_output.paper_title: Abundance and antibiotic resistance of Aeromonas isolated from the water of three carp ponds.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Aeromonas isolates from carp ponds exhibited high resistance to β-lactam and lincosamide antibiotics, while being susceptible to aminoglycosides, chloramphenicols, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic resistance profiling using the disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Dangerous passengers: multidrug-resistant bacteria on hands and mobile phones.
full_output.key_findings: The study found multidrug-resistant bacteria on hands and mobile phones, highlighting the need for improved hand hygiene and device disinfection to limit the spread of resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing were performed using biochemical tests, 16S rRNA sequencing, and automated instruments.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the Phenolic Profile of Castanea sativa Mill. By-Products and Their Antioxidant and Antimicrobial Activity against Multiresistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified phenolic compounds in chestnut by-products, including gallic acid, quercetin, and myricetin glycosides, which exhibited antioxidant and antimicrobial activities against multidrug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study used HPLC-DAD-ESI/MS for phenolic compound analysis, ABTS and DPPH assays for antioxidant activity, and the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method for antimicrobial testing.

full_output.paper_title: The combination of salvianolic acid A with latamoxef completely protects mice against lethal pneumonia caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

mutations_found.validated_by: site-directed mutagenesis and fluorescence quenching assay

full_output.key_findings: Salvianolic acid A (Sal A) was identified as an effective inhibitor of SrtA in Staphylococcus aureus, reducing bacterial adhesion, biofilm formation, and invasion. Mutants of srtA (A92L, A104L, I182A, R197A) were created and showed reduced binding affinity to Sal A.
full_output.methodology: Screening using FRET, site-directed mutagenesis, fluorescence quenching assay, and animal models.

full_output.paper_title: Burden and antimicrobial resistance of S. aureus in dairy farms in Mekelle, Northern Ethiopia.

mecA.mechanism: confers resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics by reducing their affinity
mecA.validation_method: phenotypic testing (cefoxitin disk diffusion) and molecular confirmation (PCR)

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a single MRSA isolate from a dairy farmer that was positive for the mecA gene, indicating methicillin resistance. No MRSA was found in dairy cows.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and molecular characterization of S. aureus isolates, including antimicrobial susceptibility testing and PCR for mecA detection.
full_output.sample_size: 385 lactating dairy cows and 71 dairy farmworkers

full_output.paper_title: Validation of Bedaquiline Phenotypic Drug Susceptibility Testing Methods and Breakpoints: a Multilaboratory, Multicountry Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study validated the effectiveness of different methods for determining bedaquiline susceptibility in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, focusing on mutations in Rv0678 and atpE genes that contribute to resistance.
full_output.methodology: Multilaboratory external quality assessment study evaluating the sensitivity, specificity, and reproducibility of bedaquiline minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) breakpoints and World Health Organization (WHO) critical concentrations (CCs) using agar proportion, broth microdilution, and MGIT960 methods.
full_output.sample_size: 40 M. tuberculosis isolates (20 unique strains in duplicate)

mutations_found.protein_change: Aspartic acid to Glycine at position 87

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of a multidrug-resistant strain of Shigella sonnei associated with persistent transmission in England, highlighting resistance to azithromycin and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were used to investigate the transmission dynamics and antimicrobial resistance profiles of Shigella species.

full_output.paper_title: A Common Practice of Widespread Antimicrobial Use in Horse Production Promotes Multi-Drug Resistance.

erm(46).mechanism: confers resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, and streptogramin B
erm(46).validation_method: in silico and in vitro analysis of fecal microbiome and resistome

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the use of macrolides and rifampin (MaR) in foals promotes multi-drug resistance by increasing the abundance and diversity of antimicrobial resistance genes in the fecal microbiome, particularly for macrolides, aminoglycosides, glycopeptides, phenicols, tetracycline, and bacitracin.
full_output.methodology: In silico and in vitro analysis of the fecal microbiome and resistome of foals treated with MaR or GaM, along with soil experiments to assess environmental selection for resistant bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Screening of natural compounds that targets glutamate racemase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis reveals the anti-tubercular potential of flavonoids.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies naringenin and quercetin as potential inhibitors of Mycobacterium tuberculosis glutamate racemase (MTB-MurI), demonstrating their ability to inhibit the racemization activity of the enzyme and cause cell wall damage in Mycobacterium smegmatis.
full_output.methodology: Computational docking, molecular dynamics simulations, MTT assay, fluorescence microscopy, flow cytometry, and enzyme activity assays were used to evaluate the effects of flavonoids on MTB-MurI and mycobacterial cells.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that temperate phages can drive the loss of CRISPR-Cas systems in bacteria due to immunopathological effects caused by mismatched spacers. It also highlights the role of anti-CRISPR (acr) genes in mitigating these effects and facilitating phage survival.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial strains, phage infections, PCR, whole-genome sequencing, and growth curve analyses to investigate CRISPR-Cas system dynamics during phage infections.

full_output.paper_title: Livestock-Associated Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus in Patients Admitted to Kuwait Hospitals in 2016-2017.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified LA-MRSA isolates belonging to CC96, CC97, and CC398, with CC97 being the dominant clone. Resistance genes such as erm(A), erm(C), msr(A), aacA-aphD, fusC, tet(K), cat, and dfrS1 were detected, indicating multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: DNA microarray and spa typing were used for genotyping, along with antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.methodology: Genome-wide screening of E. coli gene knockout mutants combined with conjugation assays to identify factors affecting plasmid transfer and resistance establishment.

full_output.paper_title: Colistin Combined With Tigecycline: A Promising Alternative Strategy to Combat Escherichia coli Harboring bla (NDM-) (5) and mcr-1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1 and bla NDM-5 as genes conferring resistance to colistin and carbapenems, respectively, in Escherichia coli. The combination of colistin and tigecycline showed synergistic activity against these resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used MIC testing, checkerboard assays, NPN uptake assays, and in vivo mouse models to evaluate the efficacy of colistin and tigecycline against E. coli strains harboring mcr-1 and bla NDM-5.

full_output.paper_title: Overexpression of AmpC Promotes Bacteriophage Lysis of Ampicillin-Resistant Escherichia coli.

ampC.mechanism: Overexpression of AmpC promotes lysis of E. coli by phage utilizing OmpA as a receptor
ampC.evidence_note: The paper demonstrates that overexpression of AmpC, an important β-lactamase for ampicillin resistance, promotes lysis of E. coli by phage utilizing OmpA as a receptor.

full_output.key_findings: Overexpression of AmpC, a β-lactamase, increases the susceptibility of ampicillin-resistant E. coli to phage lysis by promoting the expression of the phage receptor protein OmpA.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, Western blot analysis, phage lysis assays, and iTRAQ proteomics.

full_output.paper_title: Safety profiles of beneficial lactic acid bacteria isolated from dairy systems.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in lactic acid bacteria isolated from dairy systems, including vanC2, vanA, ermB, aac(6′)-Ie-aph(2″)-Ia, tet(S), ant(4′)-Ia, tdc, cpd, int, mur-2ed, asa1, ccf, and hyl. These genes conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as vancomycin, gentamicin, tetracycline, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and phenotypic testing to identify AMR genes and resistance patterns in lactic acid bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: An Unusual Presentation From a Sporadic Partially Acid-Fast Aerobic Actinomycete Resistant to Common Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: Nocardia farcinica exhibited resistance to several antibiotics, including cefepime, cefotaxime, ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin, clarithromycin, doxycycline, tobramycin, and was intermediate to imipenem, minocycline, and moxifloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using standard methods.

full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the genetic basis of antimicrobial resistance in anaerobic bacteria, including gene sequencing, mutational analysis, and susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Expanding Tiny Earth to genomics: a bioinformatics approach for an undergraduate class to characterize antagonistic strains.

Putative resistance genes were identified in these strains, indicating the presence of resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics analysis and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and determine the MDR phenotypes of Pseudomonas strains.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, functional assays, and bioinformatics analyses were used to identify and validate drug-resistant mutations in M. tuberculosis isolates.

CRP.mechanism: represses expression of multidrug efflux pump

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies potentially mobile antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in dust microbial communities, highlighting the presence of genes such as lnuA, which confers resistance to lincosamides, and other ARGs like AAC(3)-VIIa, ErmO, and CRP, which are associated with aminoglycoside, macrolide, and multidrug resistance, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The study combined metagenomic sequencing, cultivation, and plasmid sequencing to analyze ARGs in dust samples and validate their mobility and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Characterisation of Campylobacter spp. Isolated from Poultry in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the gyrA mutation (Thr-86-Ile), tet(O) gene, and cmeB gene as contributors to antibiotic resistance in Campylobacter spp. isolates from poultry in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and mutations in Campylobacter isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the use of whole genome sequencing (WGS) to manage an outbreak of OXA-181 carbapenemase-producing Escherichia coli, highlighting the effectiveness of WGS in containing the outbreak and reducing hospital costs.
full_output.methodology: A hybrid simulation model combining agent-based and discrete-event paradigms was used to evaluate the impact of WGS on hospital outbreak management.

full_output.paper_title: Motile aeromonads from farmed and wild freshwater fish in northern Italy: an evaluation of antimicrobial activity and multidrug resistance during 2013 and 2016.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all 95 motile Aeromonas isolates were multidrug resistant (MDR), showing high resistance to penicillins, macrolides, pleuromutilins, and sulfonamides. Resistance to certain antimicrobials like cloxacillin, spiramycin, and tilmicosin was universal, while resistance to others like colistin and ceftiofur was rare.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial resistance was determined using the disk diffusion method on Mueller Hinton Agar.

full_output.paper_title: Development of chimeric peptides to facilitate the neutralisation of lipopolysaccharides during bactericidal targeting of multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of chimeric peptides (SCPs) A6 and G6, which combine a LPS-targeting domain (LBP14) and a killing domain (N6) to effectively neutralize LPS and kill multidrug-resistant E. coli. These peptides exhibit low toxicity and no bacterial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Peptide design, physicochemical property analysis, NMR, MIC testing, and interaction studies with LPS and macrophages.

Clinical isolates of Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CIMRSA)

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antibacterial activity of hexadecynoic acid isomers, particularly 2-HDA, against multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. It finds that 2-HDA exhibits strong antibacterial effects, especially against Ciprofloxacin-resistant strains, and that the position of the triple bond in the fatty acid chain influences its efficacy. Additionally, the study explores the mechanism of action, showing that 2-HDA inhibits DNA gyrase activity in S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study synthesized various hexadecynoic acid derivatives and evaluated their antibacterial activity using MIC testing, DNA gyrase inhibition assays, and GC-MS analysis of fatty acid profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Novel MscL agonists that allow multiple antibiotics cytoplasmic access activate the channel through a common binding site.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies K05, a novel MscL agonist that activates the MscL channel, leading to increased bacterial membrane permeability and enhanced antibiotic efficacy. K05 binds to a common site on MscL, affecting channel activity and increasing the potency of various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized high-throughput screening, electrophysiology, and molecular dynamics simulations to analyze the effects of K05 on MscL channel activity and bacterial viability.

full_output.paper_title: SYN-007, an Orally Administered Beta-Lactamase Enzyme, Protects the Gut Microbiome from Oral Amoxicillin/Clavulanate without Adversely Affecting Antibiotic Systemic Absorption in Dogs.
full_output.key_findings: SYN-007, a beta-lactamase enzyme, protected the gut microbiome from damage caused by oral amoxicillin and amoxicillin/clavulanate without affecting systemic absorption of the antibiotic. It also reduced the emergence of antibiotic resistance genes, including blaTEM, blaTEM-83, and blaTEM-79.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of fecal DNA to assess changes in the gut microbiome and resistome.

full_output.paper_title: Cymbopogon Citratus Functionalized Green Synthesis of CuO-Nanoparticles: Novel Prospects as Antibacterial and Antibiofilm Agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the green synthesis of CuO-nanoparticles (CLE-CuONPs) using Cymbopogon citratus leaf extract, which exhibited potent antibacterial and antibiofilm activities against clinical isolates of E. coli, MSSA, and MRSA.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a green synthesis method involving Cymbopogon citratus leaf extract, followed by characterization techniques such as UV-Vis, XRD, TEM, and SEM, along with antibacterial and antibiofilm assays.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized BIGSI for screening genomic data, followed by genome assembly, annotation, and comparative analysis to identify and characterize SGI1-REs.

vanZ.evidence_note: The paper mentions that 'the most common determinant for teicoplanin resistance is van Z, which can be integrated into the van operon, although it is absent in the van B operon, and confers resistance to both vancomycin and teicoplanin'. This supports the 'encodes' field. The 'confers_resistance_to' field is supported by the statement that 'teicoplanin resistance is commonly associated with vancomycin resistance'. The 'organisms_tested_in' field is supported by the mention of 'Enterococcus faecalis', 'Enterococcus faecium', 'Enterococcus casseliflavus', and 'Enterococcus gallinarum' in the context of vancomycin and teicoplanin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in multidrug-resistant Enterococcus spp. isolated from wastewater treatment plants, including vancomycin resistance genes (vanA, vanM, vanG, vanC), macrolide resistance genes (ermB, msrC), tetracycline resistance genes (tetL), aminoglycoside resistance genes (aad(6'), aac(6')-Ie-aph(2")-Ia, ant(9')-Ia, aph(3')-IIIa, SAT-4, ant(6')-Ia), chloramphenicol resistance gene (cat), dihydrofolate reductase genes (dfrE, dfrF, dfrG), and lincosamide resistance genes (InuB, InuG).
full_output.methodology: Genomic screening of 39 multidrug-resistant Enterococcus spp. isolates using the CARD database.

full_output.paper_title: Integrating multiple genomic technologies to investigate an outbreak of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacter hormaechei.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaIMP-4 as a carbapenemase gene responsible for carbapenem resistance in Enterobacter hormaechei and Enterobacter cloacae complex isolates during an outbreak. The gene was located on an IncHI2 plasmid and showed high similarity to plasmids from other Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes and plasmids involved in the outbreak.

full_output.paper_title: Multiple drug binding modes in Mycobacterium tuberculosis CYP51B1.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the binding modes of three nitrogen-containing heterocycles to CYP51B1, identifying both directly-coordinated and water-bridged complexes, highlighting the complexity of drug binding in Mtb CYPs.
full_output.methodology: The study uses EPR, HYSCORE, and ENDOR spectroscopy to analyze the binding of 1,2,3-TRZ, 17-click, and PPT to CYP51B1.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility of Escherichia coli isolates obtained from wild mammals between 2013 and 2017 in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study found low prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in E. coli isolates from wild mammals in Japan, with resistance to cefotaxime (CTX) and ciprofloxacin (CIP) observed in less than 1% of isolates. A single isolate from a rat captured in a poultry house exhibited resistance to CTX and carried the blaCTX-M-1 gene, an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase gene.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using broth microdilution methods, and beta-lactamase genes were analyzed by multiplex PCR and sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Nanosilver Mitigates Biofilm Formation via FapC Amyloidosis Inhibition.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that nanosilver (AgNPs and AgNCs) can inhibit biofilm formation by targeting FapC amyloidosis in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, highlighting a novel antimicrobial strategy through amyloid inhibition.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized synthesis of bPEI-capped AgNPs and AgNCs, along with various biochemical and biophysical techniques including ThT kinetic assay, TEM, CD spectroscopy, and DMD simulations to investigate the interaction between nanoparticles and FapC.

full_output.paper_title: ATP-binding cassette (ABC) import systems of Mycobacterium tuberculosis: target for drug and vaccine development.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the role of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) import systems in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, highlighting their importance in nutrient uptake, virulence, and potential as targets for drug and vaccine development.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the molecular mechanisms behind collateral sensitivity to nitrofurantoin (NIT) in E. coli and S. enterica. Overexpression of nitroreductases nfsA and nfsB, along with increased antibiotic uptake in the hemL mutant, and interference with the SOS response in the lon mutant, contribute to NIT hypersensitivity.
full_output.methodology: Functional genetics approach involving mutant construction, overexpression studies, MIC measurements, and radiolabeled NIT uptake assays.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo efficacy of the boron-pleuromutilin AN11251 against Wolbachia of the rodent filarial nematode Litomosoides sigmodontis.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that AN11251, a boron-pleuromutilin, effectively depletes Wolbachia endosymbionts in Litomosoides sigmodontis, achieving >99% reduction in adult worms with a 10-day treatment regimen. AN11251 outperformed doxycycline and matched high-dose rifampicin in efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the in vivo efficacy of AN11251, doxycycline, and rifampicin against Wolbachia in Litomosoides sigmodontis-infected mice through oral administration and assessment of Wolbachia depletion using PCR-based methods.

full_output.paper_title: Extension of Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Time-Kill Studies To Include Lipopolysaccharide/Endotoxin Release from Escherichia coli Exposed to Cefuroxime.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the mathematical modeling of endotoxin release from Escherichia coli exposed to cefuroxime, highlighting the relationship between antibiotic concentration, bacterial growth, and endotoxin release.
full_output.methodology: The research involved time-kill experiments with static and dynamic cefuroxime concentrations, along with mathematical modeling to analyze bacterial dynamics and endotoxin release.

full_output.paper_title: Pharmacodynamics of Meropenem against Acinetobacter baumannii in a Neutropenic Mouse Thigh Infection Model.
full_output.key_findings: The study determined the pharmacodynamic parameters of meropenem against Acinetobacter baumannii, focusing on the percentage of a 24-hour period that the concentration of free drug in plasma is above the MIC (%24-h f T>MIC) required for stasis, 1 log CFU, and 2 log CFU of bacterial killing.
full_output.methodology: The study used a neutropenic mouse thigh infection model to evaluate the pharmacodynamics of meropenem against six A. baumannii clinical isolates with varying MICs.

full_output.paper_title: Transposon Mutagenesis Screen of Klebsiella pneumoniae Identifies Multiple Genes Important for Resisting Antimicrobial Activities of Neutrophils in Mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple genes, including dedA, dsbC, gntR, wzm, yaaA, and ycgE, that are crucial for K. pneumoniae's resistance to neutrophil-mediated antimicrobial activities and its virulence in lung infections.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis screen coupled with transposon sequencing (Tn-seq) and in vitro functional assays were employed to identify and validate the roles of these genes in K. pneumoniae virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of Amoxicillin in combination with Imipenem-Relebactam against Mycobacterium abscessus.

full_output.paper_title: Pathogenomics and Evolutionary Epidemiology of Multi-Drug Resistant Clinical Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolated from Pretoria, South Africa.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes and mutations in multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae isolates from South Africa, highlighting the prevalence of beta-lactamases, quinolone resistance genes, and chromosomal mutations contributing to resistance against multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the resistome, virulome, and mobilome of the isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study found no correlation between phenotypic zinc resistance and antimicrobial multi-resistance in fecal E. coli isolates from piglets, indicating no co-selection mechanism between zinc tolerance and antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Assessment of contribution of BCRP to intestinal absorption of various drugs using portal-systemic blood concentration difference model in mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the role of BCRP and P-gp in the intestinal absorption of ciprofloxacin, nitrofurantoin, topotecan, and sulfasalazine using a portal-systemic blood concentration difference model in mice. BCRP was found to have minimal impact on the absorption of ciprofloxacin and nitrofurantoin, while it significantly influenced the absorption of topotecan and sulfasalazine. P-gp was involved in the absorption and elimination of ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study used a portal-systemic blood concentration difference model in wild-type, Bcrp(-/-), and Mdr1a/1b(-/-) mice to assess the contribution of BCRP and P-gp to drug absorption.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analysis of antibiotic resistance for Acinetobacter baumannii in a critical care center.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of Antibiotic Pretreatment of an Ulcerative Colitis-Derived Fecal Microbial Community on the Integration of Therapeutic Bacteria In Vitro.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the impact of rifaximin pretreatment on the engraftment of therapeutic bacteria into an ulcerative colitis-derived microbial community, highlighting the role of antimicrobial resistance in microbial integration.

full_output.paper_title: Hydrogen sulfide stimulates Mycobacterium tuberculosis respiration, growth and pathogenesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that hydrogen sulfide (H2S) enhances Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) respiration, growth, and pathogenesis by modulating energy metabolism and the Dos regulon. full_output.paper_title: Iron competition triggers antibiotic biosynthesis in Streptomyces coelicolor during coculture with Myxococcus xanthus.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic anti-methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) activity and absolute stereochemistry of 7,8-dideoxygriseorhodin C.

full_output.paper_title: Linezolid and Rifampicin Combination to Combat cfr-Positive Multidrug-Resistant MRSA in Murine Models of Bacteremia and Skin and Skin Structure Infection.
