full_output.paper_title: Genetic Variability of the AcrAB-TolC Multidrug Efflux Pump Underlies SkQ1 Resistance in Gram-Negative Bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Potential Drug Targets for Multidrug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several potential drug targets for multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, focusing on genes involved in bacterial membrane synthesis and virulence factors. full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antibiotic resistance of rectal Mollicutes in HIV-infected men who have sex with men at the University Hospital of Dresden, Germany.

full_output.paper_title: An Alphaherpesvirus Exploits Antimicrobial β-Defensins To Initiate Respiratory Tract Infection.

full_output.paper_title: Diagnostic Accuracy of a Noninvasive Test for Detection of Helicobacter pylori and Resistance to Clarithromycin in Stool by the Amplidiag H. pylori+ClariR Real-Time PCR Assay.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the Amplidiag H. pylori +ClariR real-time PCR assay for the noninvasive detection of Helicobacter pylori and its resistance to clarithromycin in stool samples. The assay showed high sensitivity and specificity for both H. pylori detection and clarithromycin resistance testing.
full_output.methodology: The study used real-time PCR on stool samples and compared results with culture and PCR on gastric biopsy samples.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Performance of the Novel GenMark Dx ePlex Blood Culture ID Gram-Positive Panel.
full_output.key_findings: The GenMark Dx ePlex Blood Culture Identification Gram-Positive Panel effectively identifies 20 Gram-positive bacteria and detects four antimicrobial resistance genes: mecA, mecC, vanA, and vanB.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the clinical performance of the ePlex BCID-GP Panel compared to standard methods for identifying Gram-positive organisms and detecting antimicrobial resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the Revogene Carba C Assay for Detection and Differentiation of Carbapenemase-Producing Gram-Negative Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The Revogene Carba C assay effectively detects the five major carbapenemases (NDM, VIM, IMP, KPC, and OXA-48) in Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii, demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity.

full_output.paper_title: Facile One Pot Greener Synthesis of Sophorolipid Capped Gold Nanoparticles and its Antimicrobial Activity having Special Efficacy Against Gram Negative Vibrio cholerae.

full_output.paper_title: High quality 3C de novo assembly and annotation of a multidrug resistant ST-111 Pseudomonas aeruginosa genome: Benchmark of hybrid and non-hybrid assemblers.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of Beta-Lactamases in Urinary Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolates from Croatia; from Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamases to Carbapenemases and Colistin Resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Acinetobacter baumannii Biofilm Formation: Association with Antimicrobial Resistance and Prolonged Survival under Desiccation.

full_output.methodology: The study used molecular characterization, antibiotic susceptibility testing, biofilm formation assays, and desiccation tolerance experiments to investigate the relationship between biofilm formation and antimicrobial resistance in A. baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: The Combination of Salmonella Phage ST-3 and Antibiotics to Prevent Salmonella Typhimurium In Vitro.

full_output.methodology: Isolation of mutants, genetic analysis, and biochemical procedures including restriction endonuclease digestion and electrophoresis.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of transposable elements inserted in the genomes of bacteriophages Mu and P1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IS1 as a transposable element and Tn9 as a chloramphenicol resistance transposon in bacteriophages Mu and P1. IS1 was found to be present in the P1 genome, and Tn9 was shown to contain one copy of IS1 at each end.
full_output.methodology: DNA blotting-hybridization, restriction endonuclease analysis, and DNA-DNA hybridization techniques were used to analyze the genomes of bacteriophages Mu and P1.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Tn9, a chloramphenicol resistance transposon, consisting of a cam determinant flanked by two IS1 sequences. Tn9 insertion varies in location and orientation in Mu X cam mutants, affecting DNA packaging.
full_output.methodology: Electron microscopy of DNA heteroduplexes to analyze Tn9 insertion sites and orientations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline and ampicillin resistance in vibrios isolated from shrimp farms, highlighting the prevalence of antibiotic-resistant vibrios and the role of plasmid-mediated resistance in aquaculture systems.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and characterization of vibrios from shrimp samples, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and plasmid curing experiments to determine the nature of antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Metal-containing landfills as a source of antibiotic tolerance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that metal-containing landfills, particularly those from metal processing sites in Slovakia and Poland, exhibit significant antibiotic tolerance among bacterial isolates. It highlights the co-occurrence of metal and antibiotic tolerance, suggesting a potential for co-selection of resistance mechanisms in these environments.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed bacterial isolates from metal-contaminated landfills, assessing their tolerance to antibiotics and metals through minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) tests and correlation analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Novel N-α-amino acid spacer-conjugated phthalimide-triazine derivatives: synthesis, antimicrobial and molecular docking studies.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of novel phthalimide-triazine derivatives with antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Compound 6d showed the highest antimicrobial activity with a MIC value of 1.25 µg/mL.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized, characterized using spectroscopic methods, and evaluated for antimicrobial activity using the MABA test. Molecular docking studies were performed to analyze the binding modes of the compounds to DNA gyrase.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Peptide MPX with Broad-Spectrum Bactericidal Activity Promotes Proper Abscess Formation and Relieves Skin Inflammation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the antimicrobial peptide MPX as having broad-spectrum bactericidal activity against Gram-positive bacteria, Gram-negative bacteria, and fungi, particularly against E. coli with a low MIC value. MPX was shown to destroy the integrity of microbial cell membranes, increase membrane permeability, and alter membrane potential, leading to bacterial death.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of MPX using MIC determination, time-kill kinetics, membrane permeability assays, and electron microscopy to assess its mechanism of action.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the emergence of antibiotic resistance mechanisms, focusing on beta-lactamases like TEM, which confer resistance to penicillins and cephalosporins. It highlights the role of plasmids and transposons in spreading resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Review of historical data, experimental validation of resistance mechanisms, and analysis of plasmid-mediated resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a machine-learning pipeline for identifying potent antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) capable of combating multidrug-resistant pathogens. The identified peptides, CRRI3, CRRI4, and CRRI7, demonstrated strong antimicrobial activity against a variety of clinical isolates, including Acinetobacter baumannii, with low off-target toxicity and no resistance development after 100 generations of bacterial culture.
full_output.methodology: The study employs a machine-learning pipeline called SMEP, which uses a combination of empirical selection, classification, ranking, and regression models to identify potent AMPs from a vast peptide library. Wet-lab validation was conducted to confirm the antimicrobial activity and toxicity of the predicted peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Hydrothermal pre-treatment followed by anaerobic digestion for the removal of tylosin and antibiotic resistance agents from poultry litter.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the removal of tylosin and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) from poultry litter using hydrothermal pre-treatment followed by anaerobic digestion. It identifies the reduction of ermB, intI1, sul1, and tetA genes, indicating effective mitigation of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study uses qPCR to quantify ARGs and evaluates the effectiveness of hydrothermal pre-treatment and anaerobic digestion in reducing antibiotic resistance in poultry litter.

full_output.paper_title: Gold drugs as colistin adjuvants in the fight against MCR-1 producing bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that gold-based drugs and nanoparticles can act as colistin adjuvants by substituting the zinc cofactor in the MCR-1 enzyme, thereby restoring colistin efficacy against MCR-1 producing bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, equilibrium dialysis, ICP-MS, and MIC assays were used to investigate the interaction between gold-based drugs and the MCR-1 enzyme.

full_output.paper_title: Activity of ceftolozane/tazobactam and imipenem/relebactam against clinical gram-negative isolates from Czech Republic, Hungary, and Poland-SMART 2017-2020.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the activity of ceftolozane/tazobactam (C/T) and imipenem/relebactam (IMI/REL) against clinical gram-negative isolates from Czech Republic, Hungary, and Poland. C/T showed high activity against Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, while IMI/REL was highly effective against non-Morganellaceae Enterobacterales.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using CLSI reference broth microdilution methods, and β-lactamase genes were screened using published multiplex PCR assays.

full_output.paper_title: Re-identification and Characterization of Multidrug-Resistant Corynebacterium haemomassiliense-Like Organisms from Humans.
full_output.key_findings: Two multidrug-resistant Corynebacterium haemomassiliense-like isolates were identified, showing resistance to most antibiotics except vancomycin, meropenem, and linezolid.
full_output.methodology: 16S rRNA, rpoB, and gyrA gene sequencing, MALDI-TOF MS, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: A hospital outbreak of antibiotic-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: Six patients were colonized with a multiply resistant strain of Streptococcus pneumoniae, showing resistance to penicillin, chloramphenicol, tetracycline, methicillin, and co-trimoxazole, but susceptibility to erythromycin, clindamycin, vancomycin, and rifampicin.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using 'sensititre' microtitre plates.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of surfactants and other body fluids on in vitro activity of a novel β-lactamase inhibitor enmetazobactam in combination with cefepime against clinical isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that surfactants, urine, and serum did not significantly affect the in vitro activity of the β-lactamase inhibitor enmetazobactam in combination with cefepime (FPE) against clinical isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The study used minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing and time kill curves to assess the impact of surfactants, urine, and serum on the antibacterial activity of FPE and piperacillin-tazobactam (TZP).

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple bacterial species isolated from cutaneous leishmaniasis wounds in the Nkwanta South District of Ghana, with a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant strains, particularly against beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolates were identified using MALDI-TOF MS and antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby Bauer agar disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Antibiotic-Resistant Stenotrophomonas Isolates from Painted Turtles Living in the Wild.

smeABC.evidence_note: The paper states that 'S. maltophilia 15A also contains the aminoglycoside resistance genes aph(3′)-IIc and acc(6′)-lz' and 'the genes for the efflux systems smeABC and smeDEF'. It also mentions that 'SmeABC and SmeDEF encode RND efflux pumps to allow the bacteria to become intrinsically multidrug resistance.'

full_output.key_findings: Two Stenotrophomonas isolates, Stenotrophomonas sp. 9A and S. maltophilia 15A, were found to exhibit multidrug resistance. Key resistance mechanisms included chromosomal beta-lactamases (blaL1 and blaL2), aminoglycoside resistance genes (aac(6')-lz and aph(3')-llc), and efflux pumps (smeABC and smeDEF).
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Proteus mirabilis isolated from untreated hospital wastewater, Ibadan, Southwestern Nigeria showed low-level resistance to fluoroquinolone and carried qnrD3 on Col3M plasmids.

qnrD3.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and plasmid analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies qnrD3 on Col3M plasmids in Proteus mirabilis isolates from hospital wastewater in Nigeria, indicating low-level fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and plasmid analysis were used to identify resistance genes and plasmids in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and abundance of antibiotic-resistant genes in culturable bacteria inhabiting a non-polar passu glacier, karakorum mountains range, Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic-resistant genes (ARGs) in culturable bacteria from a non-polar glacier in Pakistan, highlighting the presence of resistance mechanisms against various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing of 16S rRNA gene, ARGs, and class 1 integron integrase genes.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of carbapenem resistant E. coli of fish origin reveals the dissemination of NDM-5 in freshwater aquaculture environment by the high risk clone ST167 and ST361.

bla_NDM-5.validation_method: molecular detection via PCR and sequencing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla NDM-5 as a critical gene in carbapenem-resistant E. coli (CREC) isolated from freshwater fish, highlighting its dissemination through high-risk clones ST167 and ST361 in aquaculture environments.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection of AMR genes via PCR, sequencing, and conjugal transfer experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Global profiling of antibiotic resistomes in maize rhizospheres.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes in maize rhizosphere, including blaTEM-116, blaACT-4, blaACT-6, FosA2, RbpA, vanRO, mtrA, and dfrB, which were found to be associated with resistance to various antibiotics such as beta-lactams, fosfomycin, rifamycin, glycopeptides, penam, macrolide, and trimethoprim.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis to profile the antibiotic resistomes in maize rhizosphere samples from different regions.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid diagnostics and ceftazidime/avibactam for KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infections: impact on mortality and role of combination therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the impact of rapid diagnostics and ceftazidime/avibactam on mortality in patients with KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infections, highlighting the effectiveness of ceftazidime/avibactam in reducing mortality rates.
full_output.methodology: The study was a retrospective observational analysis of patients with KPC-Kp bloodstream infections, assessing the impact of ceftazidime/avibactam and rapid diagnostics on mortality.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic analysis reveals patterns and hosts of antibiotic resistance in different pig farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in pig manure samples from different regions of Shanxi, China, highlighting the prevalence of tetracycline, aminoglycoside, macrolide, and phenicol resistance genes. Key ARGs included tet(W), tet(40), tet(Q), erm(B), erm(F), mef(A), aph(3')-III, ant(6)-Ia, cfr(C), floR, blaACI-1, optrA, cat, cfxA4, cfxA5, blaCTX-M-105, blaCTX-M-65, fexB, erm(T), mdf(A), and ole(B).
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify and characterize ARGs and their potential hosts in pig manure samples.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that fosfomycin is effective against multidrug-resistant strains of Klebsiella pneumoniae and Klebsiella oxytoca, with 92.2% and 100% sensitivity rates, respectively. The fosA gene was detected in all fosfomycin-resistant isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and MLST analysis were used to evaluate fosfomycin resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance and resistance mechanism of Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii isolated from patients with mastadenitis.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in the QRDR of the gyrA gene were associated with ciprofloxacin resistance.
gyrA.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that 62 ciprofloxacin-resistant C. kroppenstedtii strains showed 1 or 2 amino acid mutations in the QRDR of the gyrA gene.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified erm(X), sul(1), and tet(W) genes in Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii isolates, which confer resistance to erythromycin, clindamycin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and tetracycline. Additionally, mutations in the gyrA gene were linked to ciprofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Carbapenemase-Producing Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae in Switzerland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies carbapenemase-producing hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates in Switzerland, including those with bla OXA-48, bla KPC-3, bla KPC-41, and bla NDM-1 genes, as well as virulence factors such as aerobactin, yersiniabactin, colibactin, and ferric iron uptake systems.
full_output.methodology: PCR, plasmid analysis, sequencing, and bioinformatics tools for genome assembly and annotation.

full_output.paper_title: Local Regulator AcrR Regulates Persister Formation by Repression of AcrAB Efflux Pump during Exponential Growth in Aeromonas veronii.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the local regulator AcrR represses the AcrAB efflux pump during exponential growth in Aeromonas veronii, influencing persister formation against chloramphenicol, tetracycline, and β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized gene deletion, complementation, and overexpression experiments, along with qRT-PCR and efflux pump activity assays to investigate the role of AcrR in regulating the AcrAB efflux pump and persister formation.

full_output.paper_title: Ferritin from Mycobacterium abscessus is involved in resistance to antibiotics and oxidative stress.
full_output.key_findings: Deletion of the mycma_0076 gene in Mycobacterium abscessus subsp. massiliense leads to increased susceptibility to antibiotics and oxidative stress, altered cell envelope structure, and reduced biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockout, complementation, SEM, GPL extraction, biofilm assay, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Riverine antibacterial resistance gradient determined by environmental factors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified increased antibacterial resistance in river water samples downstream, particularly at sites influenced by agricultural runoff and wastewater treatment plant effluents. Resistance to chloramphenicol, erythromycin, tetracycline, ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, and vancomycin was observed in various bacterial isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted physicochemical and bacteriological analyses, along with disk diffusion and micro-dilution tests to determine antibacterial resistance levels in river water samples.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two recombinant phage lysins, Lysin 1 and Lysin 2, which show broad antimicrobial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). These lysins were cloned, expressed, and tested for their lytic activity against MRSA isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, cloning, expression, and lytic activity assays were performed to characterize the recombinant phage lysins.

full_output.paper_title: Fluoroquinolone-resistance mechanisms and molecular epidemiology of ciprofloxacin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates in Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance genes (qnrS, qnrD, qnrB, qnrA, qepA, aac(6')-Ib-cr, and qnrC) and target site mutations in gyrA (S83I) and parC (S129A, A141V) as key mechanisms of ciprofloxacin resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates in Iran.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and biofilm-inhibitory effects of vancomycin-loaded mesoporous silica nanoparticles on methicillin-resistant staphylococcus aureus and gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Vancomycin-loaded mesoporous silica nanoparticles (Van-MSNs) showed inhibitory effects on methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Gram-negative bacteria, with improved antibacterial activity compared to free vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of Van-MSNs, MIC and MBIC determination, bacterial membrane permeabilization assays, and cytotoxicity evaluation using MTT assay.
full_output.sample_size: 10 MRSA isolates and 8 Gram-negative bacteria isolates

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin Loaded Amino-Functionalized MCM-48 Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles as a Promising Drug Carrier in Bone Substitutes for Bacterial Infection Management.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that vancomycin-loaded amino-functionalized MCM-48 mesoporous silica nanoparticles (AF-MSNs) exhibit enhanced antibacterial efficacy against Staphylococcus aureus, including biofilm inhibition, due to their positive surface charge and sustained drug release properties.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized physicochemical characterization techniques, in vitro antibacterial assays, and microscopic analyses to evaluate the antibacterial properties of vancomycin-loaded AF-MSNs.

full_output.paper_title: Enhanced bacterial killing with a combination of sulbactam/minocycline against dual carbapenemase-producing Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes OXA-23 and NDM carbapenemases in dual carbapenemase-producing Acinetobacter baumannii isolates and evaluates the synergistic activity of sulbactam-based combinations against these isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of carbapenemase-encoding genes and time-kill experiments to evaluate synergistic activity of antibiotic combinations.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the susceptibility of relatively penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae to newer cephalosporin antibiotics, finding that cefuroxime, cefotaxime, and ceftriaxone were effective against these strains.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using serial dilution in Mueller-Hinton II agar with 5% horse blood.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel Anti-CRISPR AcrIE9.2 Is Associated with Dissemination of blaKPC Plasmids in Klebsiella pneumoniae Sequence Type 15.
full_output.key_findings: A novel anti-CRISPR protein, AcrIE9.2, was identified as being prevalent in Klebsiella pneumoniae ST15 and associated with the dissemination of blaKPC plasmids by inhibiting the type I-E* CRISPR-Cas system.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, transformation assays, conjugation experiments, and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize AcrIE9.2 and its impact on blaKPC plasmid dissemination.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance of Pseudomonas species.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the mechanisms of antibiotic resistance in Pseudomonas species, focusing on plasmid-mediated beta-lactamases and aminoglycoside modifying enzymes. It highlights the role of transposable elements in the dissemination of resistance genes and mentions chromosomal mutations leading to constitutive expression of enzymes like cephalosporinase.
full_output.methodology: The study examines the resistance mechanisms in Pseudomonas species through experimental analysis of plasmid-mediated genes and chromosomal mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the in vivo transfer of antibiotic resistance from a kanamycin, tetracycline, and ampicillin-resistant Escherichia coli strain to a nalidixic acid and streptomycin-resistant Salmonella arizonae strain.
full_output.methodology: Two trials were conducted to assess the in vivo transfer of antibiotic resistance in turkey poults inoculated with E. coli and S. arizonae strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates a broth disk elution (BDE) method for determining the in vitro susceptibility of the combination of aztreonam (ATM) and ceftazidime-avibactam (CZA) against multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative organisms, showing high categorical agreement with reference broth microdilution (BMD) methods.
full_output.methodology: The study compares the BDE method with reference BMD for assessing the susceptibility of MDR Gram-negative organisms to ATM-CZA.

full_output.paper_title: Dolutegravir-associated resistance mutations after first-line treatment failure in Brazil.

full_output.paper_title: Flowering phenophases influence the antibacterial and anti-biofilm effects of Thymus vulgaris L. essential oil.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the antibacterial and anti-biofilm activities of Thymus vulgaris L. essential oil vary depending on the flowering phenophase, with the highest activity observed in oils distilled from fresh plant material collected at the beginning of the flowering period.
full_output.methodology: The study used gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and gas chromatography-flame ionization detection (GC-FID) to analyze the chemical composition of essential oils, along with antibacterial and anti-biofilm assays including broth microdilution, TLC-DB, and crystal violet assays.

full_output.paper_title: Removal of AMR plasmids using a mobile, broad host-range CRISPR-Cas9 delivery tool.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of immigration on antibiotic resistance genes in activated sludge: A study using digital droplet PCR and amplicon sequencing

full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that immigration of influent wastewater into activated sludge leads to an increase in the abundance of over 70% of the quantified antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). full_output.methodology: The study utilized controlled manipulative experiments, droplet digital PCR, and multiplexed amplicon sequencing to track ARGs and their sequence variants across the immigration interface between influent wastewater and activated sludge.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial susceptibility of Acinetobacter spp. in a tertiary care hospital in Peshawar: a cross-sectional study.

High levels of methicillin resistance were observed in clinical staff and young infants.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of Sub-Minimum Inhibitory Concentrations of Bacteriocin BM173 on Listeria Monocytogenes Biofilm Formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that sub-inhibitory concentrations (SICs) of bacteriocin BM173 significantly inhibit biofilm formation in Listeria monocytogenes by reducing adhesion, swimming motility, and exopolysaccharide production, as well as down-regulating the expression of biofilm-associated genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized crystal violet staining, swimming motility assays, plate counting, ruthenium red staining, scanning electron microscopy, and RT-qPCR to evaluate the effects of BM173 on biofilm formation and gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Situation Report on mcr-Carrying Colistin-Resistant Clones of Enterobacterales: A Global Update Through Human-Animal-Environment Interfaces.
full_output.key_findings: This review highlights the global spread of mcr-carrying colistin-resistant clones of Enterobacterales, emphasizing the role of plasmids in the dissemination of mcr genes and the importance of monitoring these resistant strains across human, animal, and environmental interfaces.
full_output.methodology: This study is a comprehensive review analyzing the global distribution and characteristics of mcr-carrying colistin-resistant Enterobacterales clones.

full_output.paper_title: Cloning, Purification, and Biophysical Characterization of FemB Protein from Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Inhibitors Screening
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the FemB protein from Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) as a key player in methicillin resistance through its role in peptidoglycan cross-linking. The protein was cloned, purified, and characterized, and a novel inhibitor was identified that shows potent activity against MRSA.
full_output.methodology: The study involved cloning, overexpression, purification, and biophysical characterization of the FemB protein, along with in vitro antibacterial assays and molecular docking studies to identify potential inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Phages overcome bacterial immunity via diverse anti-defence proteins.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies four distinct families of phage anti-defence proteins that inhibit the Gabija, Thoeris, and Hachiman defence systems. These proteins include Gad1, Gad2, Tad2, and Had1, which neutralize the respective bacterial defence mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Genome comparisons, gene clustering, and experimental validation through phage infection assays and genetic manipulation.

full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the design, screening, and efficacy of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) targeting Streptococcus mutans, highlighting their potential as alternatives to antibiotics for preventing and treating dental caries.
full_output.methodology: This is a review article summarizing current research on AMPs targeting S. mutans, focusing on their mechanisms of action, design strategies, and efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia Belonging to Novel Sequence Types ST473 and ST474 in Wild Birds Inhabiting the Brazilian Amazonia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two novel sequence types, ST473 and ST474, of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia in wild birds from the Brazilian Amazonia, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant strains with resistance genes including efflux pumps, beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, and quinolone resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed on S. maltophilia strains isolated from wild birds.

full_output.paper_title: Semi-mechanistic modeling of resistance development to β-lactam and β-lactamase-inhibitor combinations.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified porin down-regulation and efflux pump up-regulation as key mechanisms contributing to PIP-TAZ resistance in a CTX-M-15-producing K. pneumoniae isolate.
full_output.methodology: Semi-mechanistic mathematical modeling combined with antibiotic sensitivity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterial FtsZ and inhibitors: a promising target for the anti-tubercular drug development.
full_output.key_findings: The review highlights the potential of Mycobacterium tuberculosis FtsZ as a target for anti-tubercular drug development, focusing on its role in cell division and the identification of various inhibitors that target FtsZ polymerization, assembly, and GTPase activity.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and experimental studies on Mtb FtsZ, analyzing its structure, function, and the effects of various inhibitors on its activity.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance rates of urogenital Mycoplasma hominis and Ureaplasma species before and during the COVID-19 pandemic: results from a Greek survey, 2014 to 2022.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports increasing resistance rates to clindamycin and erythromycin in Ureaplasma spp. and Mycoplasma hominis, while resistance to ofloxacin, tetracycline, and doxycycline remained relatively low. Azithromycin resistance significantly increased in M. hominis.

full_output.paper_title: Draft genome of neotropical Bacillus thuringiensis UFT038 and its potential against lepidopteran soybean pests.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro evaluation of biofilm phenotypic and genotypic characteristics among clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Hamadan, West of Iran.

full_output.paper_title: The use of combination therapy for the improvement of colistin activity against bacterial biofilm.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the use of combination therapies to enhance colistin's effectiveness against bacterial biofilms, particularly in multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria. full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing studies on combination therapies for improving colistin activity against bacterial biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Thirteen new peptaibols with antimicrobial activities from Trichoderma sp.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports thirteen new peptaibols with antimicrobial activities from Trichoderma sp., including seven 18-residue peptaibols (neoatroviridins E-K) and six 14-residue peptaibols (harzianins NPDG J-O). Some of these peptaibols show moderate inhibitory activity against Staphylococcus aureus and one, compound 9, shows antifungal activity against Candida albicans.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-resistant staphylococci in clinical bovine mastitis: occurrence, molecular analysis, and biofilm production.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci (MR-CoNS) in clinical bovine mastitis, highlighting the presence of the mecA gene responsible for methicillin resistance. full_output.methodology: The study used molecular techniques including PCR for identification of S. aureus and detection of mecA and icaA genes, as well as spa typing and SCCmec characterization for MRSA strains.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Peptides (Bacteriocins) Produced by Lactococcus lactis and Pediococcus pentosaceus Strains with Activity Against Clinical and Food-Borne Pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and Characterization of Antimicrobial Peptides Isolated from Brevibacillus halotolerans 7WMA2 for the Activity Against Multidrug-Resistant Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) produced by Brevibacillus halotolerans 7WMA2 that exhibit broad-spectrum activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens, including MRSA and Clostridium difficile. full_output.paper_title: The fate of antibiotic resistance genes during anaerobic digestion of sewage sludge with ultrasonic pretreatment.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the CBASS phage defense system in Vibrio cholerae enhances sensitivity to antifolate antibiotics such as sulfamethoxazole (SMX) and trimethoprim (TMP), leading to increased bacterial lysis. It also reveals that antifolate resistance genes can negate this effect.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of genetic knockout experiments, MIC testing, fluorescence microscopy, and biochemical assays to investigate the interaction between the CBASS system and antifolate antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Horizontal gene transfer facilitates the molecular reverse-evolution of antibiotic sensitivity in experimental populations of H. pylori.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that horizontal gene transfer (HGT) can facilitate the molecular reverse-evolution of antibiotic resistance in Helicobacter pylori. Specifically, the 23S rRNA gene, which confers resistance to clarithromycin, was shown to revert to an antibiotic-sensitive genotype through HGT.
full_output.methodology: The study used experimental evolution with HGT, amplicon Sanger sequencing, and whole-population metagenome sequencing to analyze the genetic changes in H. pylori populations.

full_output.paper_title: The potentiation activity of β-lactam by phomoidrides and oxasetin against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies phomoidrides A-D and a new analog, phomoidride H, along with oxasetin, as potentiation agents that enhance the efficacy of β-lactam antibiotics against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and structural elucidation of phomoidrides and oxasetin from the fungal strain Neovaginatispora clematidis FKI-8547, followed by evaluation of their potentiation activity against MRSA using disk diffusion and broth microdilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analysis of diverse environmental Acinetobacter isolates identifies plasmids, antibiotic resistance genes, and capsular polysaccharides shared with clinical strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified plasmids, antibiotic resistance genes, and capsular polysaccharides in environmental Acinetobacter isolates that are shared with clinical strains, highlighting the potential for environmental strains to acquire and disseminate clinically important antibiotic resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, whole-genome sequencing, and plasmid transfer assays were used to identify antibiotic resistance genes and their genetic contexts in environmental Acinetobacter isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Novel resistance ICEs carrying the blaFIM-1 metallo-β-lactamase gene from an ST235 Pseudomonas aeruginosa sublineage.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms in the Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains.

These plasmids are transferable between different streptococcal groups and exhibit similar molecular weights and restriction patterns.
full_output.methodology: The study characterizes plasmids from group B streptococcus through DNA isolation, restriction enzyme digestion, agarose gel electrophoresis, and transformation experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The study detected Mycoplasma gallisepticum (MG) in commercial chicken farms and determined the tylosin susceptibility of isolates, revealing varying levels of resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used immunoassay testing, culture, PCR, and broth microdilution to assess tylosin susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of Neolamarckia cadamba leaves extract on microbial community and antibiotic resistance genes in cecal contents and feces of broilers challenged with lipopolysaccharides.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Neolamarckia cadamba leaves extract (NCLE) reduced the abundance of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in cecal contents of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced broilers by maintaining microbial balance.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis was used to investigate the effects of NCLE on microbial communities and ARGs in cecal contents and feces of broilers challenged with LPS.

full_output.paper_title: New Polyene Macrolide Compounds from Mangrove-Derived Strain Streptomyces hiroshimensis GXIMD 06359: Isolation, Antifungal Activity, and Mechanism against Talaromyces marneffei.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the isolation of four new polyene macrolide compounds (antifungalmycin B-E) and seven known analogs from Streptomyces hiroshimensis GXIMD 06359, demonstrating their antifungal activity against Talaromyces marneffei, particularly compound 1, which exhibits potent antifungal effects by disrupting the cell membrane and mitochondrial function.
full_output.methodology: Structural elucidation using spectroscopic techniques, antifungal activity assessment via MIC and MFC, and investigation of the mechanism of action through cell membrane integrity, ATPase activity, and mitochondrial function analyses.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that 34.04% of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates were carbapenem-resistant (CR) and 26.32% were multidrug-resistant (MDR). Resistance rates varied among antibiotics, with the highest resistance to aztreonam (39.44%) and low resistance to aminoglycosides, broad-spectrum cephalosporins, fluoroquinolones, and polymyxin B.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing antimicrobial resistance profiles of P. aeruginosa isolates from bloodstream infections in two Chinese hospitals.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogenetic Aspects of Antibiotic Resistance and Biofilm Formation of P. aeruginosa Isolated from Clinical Samples.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of virulence genes pslA, pelA, pelB, brlR, mexA, and mexB in P. aeruginosa isolates, highlighting their association with biofilm formation and multidrug resistance. The pslA gene was predominantly found in biofilm-producing isolates, and mexA was linked to multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, biofilm formation assessment, and PFGE genotyping were used to analyze the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Streptococcus suis Research Update: Serotype Prevalence and Antimicrobial Resistance Distribution in Swine Isolates Recovered in Spain from 2020 to 2022.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance genes in Streptococcus suis isolates from Spain, including tet(O), erm(B), lnu(B), lsa(E), tet(M), and mef(A/E). High resistance levels were observed for clindamycin, chlortetracycline, and sulfadimethoxine.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect resistance genes and assess resistance patterns in S. suis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of Temperature, pH, and a(w) on Cereulide Synthesis and Regulator Genes Transcription with Respect to Bacillus cereus Growth and Cereulide Production.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the effects of temperature, pH, and water activity on the expression of cereulide synthesis-related genes (cesA, cesB, cesP, codY, and abrB) in Bacillus cereus. It revealed that lower pH and reduced water activity enhance the expression of these genes, promoting cereulide production.
full_output.methodology: RT-qPCR analysis of gene expression under varying environmental conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal Diversity, Antibiotic Resistance, and Virulence Factor Prevalence of Community Associated Staphylococcus aureus in Southeastern Virginia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified five virulence factor genes (clfA, spA, sbi, scpA, and vwb) that were present in all 122 S. aureus isolates. These genes are involved in immune evasion and are crucial for the pathogenicity of S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the genetic variability and antibiotic resistance of S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Diagnosis of Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis-Opportunities and Challenges.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the challenges and opportunities in the rapid diagnosis of drug-resistant tuberculosis, focusing on the limitations of traditional methods and the development of molecular assays for detecting resistance to first- and second-line drugs.
full_output.methodology: Review of literature on diagnostic methods for drug-resistant tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Pathogenic Potential and Antibiotic Susceptibility: A Comprehensive Study of Enterococci from Different Ecological Settings.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes in Enterococcus isolates, including ermB (macrolide resistance), vanA (glycopeptide resistance), aphA3 (aminoglycoside resistance), aac6′-aph2″ (aminoglycoside resistance), and cat pIP501 (chloramphenicol resistance).
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify and validate the presence of antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Enteropathogenic Yersinia with Public Health Relevance Found in Dogs and Cats in Finland.

sul1.evidence_note: The paper mentions that three Y. enterocolitica strains expressed high MIC values to sulfamethoxazole, two of which carried the sul1 gene and one carried the sul2 gene.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant Yersinia enterocolitica strains carrying resistance genes such as blaA, catA1, aadA12, sul1, aph, sul2, and tet(A). These genes conferred resistance to ampicillin, chloramphenicol, streptomycin, sulfamethoxazole, and tetracycline.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm Producing Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) Infections in Humans: Clinical Implications and Management.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the role of various genes in biofilm formation by MRSA, highlighting their importance in the persistence and resistance of MRSA infections.
full_output.methodology: Review of literature and discussion of experimental findings related to MRSA biofilm formation and management.

full_output.paper_title: First Report of Benzimidazole Resistance in Field Population of Haemonchus contortus from Sheep, Goats and Cattle in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

full_output.methodology: The study used rt-qPCR to detect the F200Y mutation in the beta-tubulin gene of H. contortus.

full_output.paper_title: Streptococcal arginine deiminase system defences macrophage bactericidal effect mediated by XRE family protein XtrSs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies XtrSs as a negative regulator of the arginine deiminase system (ADS) in Streptococcus suis, showing that XtrSs represses ADS transcription by directly binding to the argR promoter, thereby reducing bacterial virulence and acid resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis, qRT-PCR, EMSA, and bacterial survival assays in mouse models.

full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the clinical trial data and real-world evidence of ceftolozane/tazobactam for treating serious healthcare-associated Gram-negative infections, highlighting its effectiveness against multidrug-resistant pathogens like Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Production of a Bacteriocin Like Protein PEG 446 from Clostridium tyrobutyricum NRRL B-67062.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PEG 446, a bacteriocin-like protein from Clostridium tyrobutyricum NRRL B-67062, which exhibits antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria such as Lactococcus lactis, Limosilactobacillus fermentum, and Listeria innocua.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, genome mining, cloning, expression in E. coli and B. subtilis, and antibacterial activity assays including gel overlay, well diffusion, and microplate reader-based growth inhibition.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that piscidin peptides p1 and p3 act as antibiotic adjuvants, enhancing the efficacy of metronidazole, vancomycin, and fidaxomicin against Clostridioides difficile by increasing antibiotic penetration through the cell membrane.
full_output.methodology: The study used growth inhibition assays, membrane leakage assays, and electron microscopy to evaluate the adjuvant effects of piscidin peptides with various antibiotics against C. difficile.

full_output.methodology: The study used MIC testing, Ribo-seq, and Western blotting to analyze the effects of ermB on antibiotic resistance and translation.

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin-Polyguanidino Dendrimer Conjugates Inhibit Growth of Antibiotic-Resistant Gram-Positive and Gram-Negative Bacteria and Eradicate Biofilm-Associated S. aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development of vancomycin-polyguanidino dendrimer conjugates, V-triguan-6C and V-triguan-2C, which show potent antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including multidrug-resistant strains. These conjugates effectively inhibit bacterial growth and eradicate biofilms, demonstrating improved efficacy compared to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized antimicrobial susceptibility assays, biofilm eradication tests, time-kill kinetics, membrane permeability assessments, and HPLC-MS analysis to evaluate the efficacy and mechanisms of action of the vancomycin conjugates.

full_output.paper_title: Short-duration selective decontamination of the digestive tract infection control does not contribute to increased antimicrobial resistance burden in a pilot cluster randomised trial (the ARCTIC Study).
full_output.key_findings: The study found no significant increase in clinically relevant antimicrobial resistance gene burden in critically ill children treated with SDD-enhanced infection control compared to standard care.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomic microbiome and resistome analysis on serial oropharyngeal and faecal samples from critically ill children.

full_output.paper_title: Role of membrane vesicles in the transmission of vancomycin resistance in Enterococcus faecium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanA and vanB genes as the primary determinants of vancomycin resistance in Enterococcus faecium isolates. Despite the presence of these resistance genes in membrane vesicles, no phenotypic transfer of vancomycin resistance was observed.
full_output.methodology: Genotypic and phenotypic analysis of vancomycin resistance, nanoparticle tracking analysis, PCR, and whole-genome sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Interaction of designed cationic antimicrobial peptides with the outer membrane of gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effects of Lys clustering in cationic antimicrobial peptides (CAPs) on their interaction with the outer membrane (OM) of gram-negative bacteria, demonstrating that Lys-clustered peptides exhibit enhanced binding affinity to lipopolysaccharides (LPS) and increased antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The study used a designed peptide library derived from Ponericin W1, evaluated antimicrobial efficacy through MIC assays, and analyzed peptide-LPS interactions using DPX displacement assays, CD spectroscopy, and tryptophan fluorescence.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of Staphylococcus aureus in cattle and humans in farming communities of Isingiro and Kamuli districts, Uganda.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from cattle and humans in Uganda, with resistance primarily observed against Nitroimidazoles and Penicillins. Multidrug resistance (MDR) was prevalent, particularly in cattle isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby Bauer disc diffusion method on S. aureus isolates from nasal swabs of cattle and humans in farming communities.

full_output.key_findings: The review highlights the presence of various antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the soil-microbe-plant resistome, including sulfonamide resistance genes (sul1, sul2), tetracycline resistance genes (tetW, tetL, tetA, tetM), macrolide resistance gene (ermB), aminoglycoside resistance gene (aac(6')-Ib), glycopeptide resistance gene (vanA), and mobile genetic elements (intI1). These genes are associated with anthropogenic activities such as manure application and wastewater irrigation.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of existing studies on the soil-microbe-plant resistome.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomics reveals the temporal dynamics of the rumen resistome and microbiome in goat kids.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified numerous antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the rumen of goat kids, highlighting the dynamic nature of the resistome influenced by age and diet. Key ARGs included RPOB, GYRA, GYRBA, ROB, MDTF, ACRF, ACRB, MGTA, MLS23S, TUFAB, TET44, TET32, APH2-DPRIME, SAT, BRO, TETQ, ERMF, NIMJ, ACI, MEFA, RRSC, RRSH, CAP16S, TETX, LNUC, TETW, TETO, and TET40, which were associated with resistance to various antibiotics such as drugs, MLS, tetracyclines, and others.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the rumen resistome and microbiome in goat kids, along with RT-qPCR and metatranscriptomics for validation.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Modeling Studies to Probe the Binding Hypothesis of Novel Lead Compounds against Multidrug Resistance Protein ABCB1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies four novel lead compounds ('A', 'D', 'E', and 'F') that effectively inhibit the multidrug resistance protein ABCB1, demonstrating stable interactions within the binding pocket and showing promise as potential inhibitors for overcoming multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Molecular docking simulations, molecular dynamics simulations, and pharmacokinetic analyses were conducted to evaluate the binding and inhibitory potential of the lead compounds against ABCB1.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and Functional Evaluation of Two Lacticaseibacillus paracasei and Two Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Strains, Isolated from a Rearing Tank of Rotifers (Brachionus plicatilis), as Probiotics for Aquaculture.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified and functionally characterized a multi-bacteriocinogenic gene cluster in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum BF12 and WT12, leading to the production of plantaricins, including PlnE/F, which exhibited antimicrobial activity against several bacterial pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, bioinformatic analysis, in vitro cell-free protein synthesis, and antimicrobial activity assays were employed to evaluate the probiotic potential and antimicrobial mechanisms of the strains.
full_output.sample_size: Four strains (two Lacticaseibacillus paracasei and two Lactiplantibacillus plantarum)

full_output.paper_title: Innovative Biomedical and Technological Strategies for the Control of Bacterial Growth and Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the challenges posed by bacterial resistance to antibiotics and highlights the use of genomics, nanotechnology, and computational methods in the development of new antimicrobial strategies. It mentions the discovery of novel antibiotics like lugdunin and malacidins, as well as the role of resistance genes in bacterial pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews current literature on bacterial resistance mechanisms, genomic approaches, and technological innovations in antimicrobial development.

full_output.paper_title: Therapeutic Potential of a Novel Lytic Phage, vB_EclM_ECLFM1, against Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacter cloacae.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the novel lytic phage ECLFM1 and identifies the blaIMP-8 gene in the clinical strain ECL73134, which confers resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, morphological characterization, host range determination, one-step growth experiments, and genomic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Probiotic-Induced Modulation of Microbiota Composition and Antibiotic Resistance Genes Load, an In Vitro Assessment.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that probiotics significantly reduced the levels of tetM and tetO genes, as well as the blaTEM gene, in fecal cultures from both normal-weight and extremely obese individuals.
full_output.methodology: In vitro fecal culture model combined with qPCR for quantification of antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the Interplay of the CRISPR-CAS System with Antibiotic Resistance in Staphylococcus aureus: A Poultry Meat Study from Lahore, Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of antibiotic resistance genes mecA, tetM, ermA, and gyrA in multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates from poultry meat, suggesting a link between the CRISPR-Cas system and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and qRT-PCR were used to detect antibiotic resistance genes and analyze CRISPR-Cas system expression in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed and validated a UPLC-MS/MS method for quantifying first-line anti-TB agents in urine, focusing on their stability under various conditions.
full_output.methodology: The study developed and validated a UPLC-MS/MS method for quantifying anti-TB drugs in urine, assessing their stability under different storage conditions and pH levels.

full_output.paper_title: Mode of Antibacterial Action of Tomatidine C3-Diastereoisomers.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antibacterial action of tomotidine C3-diastereoisomers, TM-02 and TM-03, focusing on their interaction with the bacterial ATP synthase subunit c (atpE).
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, ATP synthase inhibition assays, in silico docking, and bactericidal activity measurements were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Bimetallic bis-Aroyldihydrazone-Isatin Complexes of High O=V(IV) and Low Cu(II) Valent Ions as Effective Biological Reagents for Antimicrobial and Anticancer Assays.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of bimetallic complexes VOLph and CuLph, which show potent antimicrobial and anticancer activities. These complexes exhibit significant inhibition of microbial growth and cancer cell proliferation, suggesting their potential as effective biological reagents.
full_output.methodology: The paper describes the preparation and structural elucidation of the complexes using spectroscopic techniques, followed by biological evaluations including antimicrobial assays, antiproliferative studies, and DNA interaction experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Chemical Composition, and Antioxidant and Antimicrobial Activity of Oregano Essential Oil.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the chemical composition, antioxidant, and antimicrobial activities of four oregano essential oils (OEOs). Carvacrol was identified as the main component, contributing to the antimicrobial activity against various bacteria and fungi.
full_output.methodology: The chemical composition of OEOs was determined by GC/MS, and antimicrobial activity was assessed using the double-dilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and Structure Elucidation of New Metabolites from the Mariana-Trench-Associated Fungus Aspergillus sp. SY2601.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolated and identified 28 metabolites from the Mariana-Trench-associated fungus Aspergillus sp. SY2601, including five new compounds. One of the new compounds, 12 S -aspertetranone D (26), exhibited antibacterial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli with MIC values of 3.75 and 5 μg/mL, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The metabolites were isolated from cultures of Aspergillus sp. SY2601 grown in EY liquid and rice solid media. Structural elucidation was performed using NMR, HRESIMS, optical rotation, ECD, and 13C NMR calculations. Antimicrobial activity was assessed using the micro-broth dilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Effective Isolation and Characterization of Mycobacteriophages with the Ability to Lyse Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the isolation and characterization of 12 novel mycobacteriophages capable of lysing Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (MAP). These phages showed varied host ranges and were effective in reducing mycobacterial counts in milk replacer.
full_output.methodology: Phages were isolated using an optimized protocol involving fecal spiking, enrichment with MAP and M. smegmatis, and restriction enzyme analysis. Host range was assessed using qPCR.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a Thermostable Endolysin of the Aeribacillus Phage AeriP45 as a Potential Staphylococcus Biofilm-Removing Agent.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the thermostable endolysin LysAP45 from the Aeribacillus phage AP45, demonstrating its ability to hydrolyze peptidoglycans from various Staphylococcus species and disrupt biofilms formed by multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The endolysin LysAP45 was produced in E. coli, purified, and tested for enzymatic activity against peptidoglycans and biofilms of Staphylococcus species.

full_output.paper_title: Drug Resistance and Molecular Characteristics of Carbapenem-Resistant OXA-48-Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae Strains in Hainan, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified three OXA-48-producing carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (CR-hvKP) strains in Hainan, China, and demonstrated the high stability of blaOXA-48-harboring plasmids in these strains. Ceftazidime/avibactam was found to be effective against these strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid conjugation, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the molecular characteristics and resistance mechanisms of the strains.

full_output.paper_title: Gulls in Porto Coastline as Reservoirs for Salmonella spp.: Findings from 2008 and 2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Salmonella spp. isolates from gull feces and water samples in Porto, Portugal, including genes conferring resistance to aminoglycosides, tetracyclines, sulfonamides, beta-lactams, trimethoprim, erythromycin, antiseptics, florfenicol, and fosfomycin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and resistance profiles in Salmonella isolates.

full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR with dual fluorescent probes targeting 23S rRNA gene mutations at positions 2063 and 2064.

full_output.paper_title: Beyond the Wild MRSA: Genetic Features and Phylogenomic Review of mecC-Mediated Methicillin Resistance in Non-aureus Staphylococci and Mammaliicocci.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mecC gene as a key mediator of methicillin resistance in non-aureus staphylococci and mammaliicocci, highlighting its prevalence in various species and its association with multidrug resistance. The genetic environment of mecC is found to vary significantly, with some strains carrying hybrid SCC mec-mecC elements.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenomic analysis were used to investigate the genetic features and resistance mechanisms of mecC-carrying isolates.

full_output.methodology: Genome annotation and comparative analysis using bioinformatics tools such as antiSMASH, CARD, and PGAP.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Susceptibility Patterns and Genetic Diversity of Campylobacter spp. Isolates from Patients with Diarrhea in South Korea.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of resistance to fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin: 83.3%) and tetracyclines (32.3%) in Campylobacter spp. isolates from patients with diarrhea in South Korea, with a decreasing trend in tetracycline resistance. Low resistance rates were observed for macrolides, lincosamides, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using MICs for eight antimicrobial agents, and MLST was used to assess genetic diversity.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Chimeric Staphylococcus aureus Strains from Waterfowl.
full_output.key_findings: Chimeric Staphylococcus aureus strains from waterfowl were characterized, revealing the presence of the collagen adhesin gene cna, which is typically absent from CC133 strains. These strains exhibited genomic insertions from other S. aureus lineages, contributing to their unique genetic makeup.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and microarray hybridization were used to characterize the genetic features of the S. aureus strains.

full_output.paper_title: Enterococci, Van Gene-Carrying Enterococci, and Vancomycin Concentrations in the Influent of a Wastewater Treatment Plant in Southeast Germany.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Vibrio parahaemolyticus isolated from farmed Pacific white shrimp, including blaCARB, sulI, sulII, sulIII, strA, strB, qnrVC136, qnrVC457, qnrA, cat, optrA, floR, cfr, and erm. full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Activity and Mechanism of Sanguinarine with Polymyxin B against Gram-Negative Bacterial Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies sanguinarine (SA) as a compound that enhances the antibacterial activity of polymyxin B (PMB) against Gram-negative bacteria, demonstrating synergistic effects in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized checkerboard assays, time-kill curves, and an in vivo peritonitis model to evaluate the synergistic activity of SA and PMB against various Gram-negative bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical assays rapidly predict bacterial susceptibility to monoclonal antibody therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces MAb10, a novel monoclonal antibody with broad binding to Acinetobacter baumannii strains, demonstrating protective efficacy in vivo. It establishes two rapid clinical susceptibility assays using flow cytometry and latex bead agglutination to predict the effectiveness of monoclonal antibodies against bacterial infections.
full_output.methodology: The study employed flow cytometry and latex bead agglutination assays to assess the binding and efficacy of monoclonal antibodies against Acinetobacter baumannii strains, alongside in vivo infection models in mice and rats.

full_output.paper_title: A novel conjugative transposon carrying an autonomously amplified plasmid.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel conjugative transposon, CTn214, which carries the tetracycline resistance gene tetQ. The transposon exhibits an autonomously amplified plasmid-like form that remains active regardless of tetracycline exposure, offering insights into the persistence of antibiotic resistance mechanisms in Bacteroides fragilis.
full_output.methodology: Genome and transcriptome sequencing of Bacteroides fragilis isolates under various antibiotic treatments, along with PCR and metagenomic read mapping.

full_output.paper_title: The mechanism of ceftazidime and cefiderocol hydrolysis by D179Y variants of KPC carbapenemases is similar and involves the formation of a long-lived covalent intermediate.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the D179Y variants of KPC carbapenemases (KPC-31 and KPC-33) and shows that they confer resistance to ceftazidime and cefiderocol by altering the rate-limiting step of the hydrolysis mechanism, leading to the formation of a long-lived covalent intermediate.
full_output.methodology: Steady-state and pre-steady-state enzyme kinetics were used to analyze the catalytic properties of KPC-2, KPC-3, KPC-31, and KPC-33 β-lactamases with ceftazidime and cefiderocol as substrates.

full_output.paper_title: Global genetic diversity and Asian clades evolution: a phylogeographic study of Staphylococcus aureus sequence type 5.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various antimicrobial resistance genes in Staphylococcus aureus sequence type 5, highlighting the genetic diversity and resistance mechanisms across different clades.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and resistance gene detection using ResFinder database.

full_output.paper_title: AgrA directly binds to the promoter of vraSR and downregulates its expression in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that AgrA directly binds to the promoter of vraSR and downregulates its expression in Staphylococcus aureus, contributing to reduced vancomycin susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study used qRT-PCR, western blotting, and EMSA to analyze the expression and binding of vraSR.

full_output.paper_title: Deciphering the molecular mechanism and regulation of formaldehyde detoxification in Mycobacterium smegmatis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Fmh, a metallo-beta-lactamase, as essential for formaldehyde detoxification in Mycobacterium smegmatis when co-expressed with mscR. MscR, a formaldehyde dehydrogenase, is shown to be indispensable for formaldehyde detoxification.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic knockout and complementation experiments, NMR spectroscopy, and biochemical assays to characterize the roles of mscR and fmh in formaldehyde detoxification.

full_output.paper_title: Association between multidrug-resistant bacteria and outcomes in intensive care unit patients: a non-interventional study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria were associated with higher in-hospital mortality rates in ICU patients. Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) and extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) producers were the most frequently encountered resistance profiles. The use of certain antimicrobials, including meropenem and vancomycin, was linked to increased mortality.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the in vitro antibacterial activity of several antiretroviral drugs against key commensal bacteria from the human microbiota, including zidovudine, abacavir, efavirenz, bictegravir, and elvitegravir. Notably, elvitegravir showed activity against vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus spp. and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study determined the in vitro antibacterial activity of 16 antiretroviral drugs against a set of clinically relevant and human commensal bacterial strains using the broth microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Unravelling staphylococcal small-colony variants in cardiac implantable electronic device infections: clinical characteristics, management, and genomic insights.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes associated with staphylococcal small-colony variants (SCVs) in cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) infections, including aap, EQW00_01465, EQW00_02070, EQW00_00920, EQW00_10990, EQW00_00200, EQW00_00250, EQW00_07660, EQW00_00780, EQW00_09465, EQW00_00140, EQW00_01285, EQW00_00380, EQW00_00285, ebh, and EQW00_07700. full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and comparative genomics analysis were used to identify genes and mutations associated with staphylococcal SCVs in CIED infections.

full_output.paper_title: Mixed Alkyl/Aryl Phosphonates Identify Metabolic Serine Hydrolases as Antimalarial Targets.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies abH112 as a critical target of the antimalarial compound 22, highlighting its role in parasite killing when inhibited alongside other serine hydrolases.
full_output.methodology: Chemoproteomic identification, biochemical screens, and functional assays were used to characterize the targets and mechanisms of action of the synthesized phosphonates.

full_output.paper_title: An Arm-to-Disarm Strategy to Overcome Phenotypic AMR in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a prodrug strategy to overcome phenotypic antimicrobial resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis by enhancing drug permeability and accumulation, particularly in non-replicating persisters. The lead compound, 1e, shows improved efficacy compared to moxifloxacin (MXF) in both replicating and non-replicating Mtb.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and evaluation of MXF prodrugs, assessment of their bioreductive activation, and determination of their antibacterial activity against Mtb using various in vitro and in vivo models.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that gallein, a polyphosphate kinase inhibitor, enhances the antibacterial effect of isoniazid (INH) against Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) by preventing INH-induced accumulation of polyP and disrupting cell envelope formation.
full_output.methodology: The study used Mtb growth assays, polyP quantification, transmission electron microscopy, and metabolomics to analyze the effects of gallein and INH on Mtb.

full_output.paper_title: Beyond antibiotic resistance: The whiB7 transcription factor coordinates an adaptive response to alanine starvation in mycobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies whiB7 as a key transcriptional activator involved in an adaptive response to alanine starvation in mycobacteria, revealing its role in regulating alanine metabolism through a feedback loop with aspC.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide CRISPRi epistasis screen, reporter systems, qPCR, and mutagenesis experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Specifically targeted antimicrobial peptides synergize with bacterial-entrapping peptide against systemic MRSA infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies P18, P18E6, and SP5 as effective antimicrobial peptides against MRSA, demonstrating their ability to disrupt cell membranes and entrap bacteria, enhancing antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a combination of computational design, machine learning, and experimental validation to identify and characterize antimicrobial peptides.

full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that viral communities contribute more to the lysis of antibiotic-resistant bacteria than to the transduction of antibiotic resistance genes in anaerobic digestion. It identifies the prevalence of specific antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) such as aadE, ermF, tetM, sul1, and sul2 in different substrates and highlights the role of conjugation in the horizontal transfer of ARGs.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing, qPCR, and bioinformatic analyses were used to profile the antibiotic resistome and assess the role of viral communities in anaerobic digestion.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid and visual identification of β-lactamase subtypes for precision antibiotic therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a paper-based sensor (BSV sensor) capable of rapidly and visually identifying β-lactamase subtypes, including BSBL, ESBL, AmpC, and carbapenemases, enabling precise antibiotic therapy.
full_output.methodology: The BSV sensor uses chromogenic β-lactamase substrates to detect and differentiate β-lactamase subtypes through color changes, validated with clinical samples and biochemical assays.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of dietary tall oil fatty acids and hydrolysed yeast in SNP2-positive and SNP2-negative piglets challenged with F4 enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that dietary supplementation with tall oil fatty acids (TOFA) and yeast hydrolysate (YH) reduced F4-ETEC shedding and improved resilience in piglets. SNP2+ piglets showed higher F4-ETEC shedding and diarrhea prevalence compared to SNP2- piglets.
full_output.methodology: The study involved experimental challenges with F4-ETEC in SNP2+ and SNP2- piglets, assessing the effects of dietary supplements on fecal shedding, diarrhea, and growth performance.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high rates of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in E. coli isolates causing invasive disease in hospitalized older adults, particularly to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, ciprofloxacin, and levofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Prospective, multinational observational study assessing clinical presentation and AMR patterns of E. coli isolates from patients with invasive E. coli disease.

full_output.paper_title: Cross-border differences in the prevalence and risk factors for carriage of antimicrobial resistance in children attending daycare centers: a point prevalence study in the Netherlands and Belgium.
full_output.key_findings: The study found significant differences in the prevalence of ESBL-E and CipR-E carriage between children in the Netherlands and Belgium, with higher rates in Belgium. Antimicrobial use and hospital admissions were also higher in Belgium. Travel to Asia was identified as a risk factor for ESBL-E carriage, while antimicrobial use was a risk factor for CipR-E carriage.
full_output.methodology: A point-prevalence study was conducted in daycare centers in the Netherlands and Belgium, involving stool sample collection and microbiological analyses to determine antimicrobial resistance carriage rates.

Disruption of oxyR led to increased catalase activity, decreased urease activity, enhanced ApxI toxin secretion, and reduced virulence in a mouse model.

It found that BALF mNGS had high sensitivity but lower specificity for pneumonia diagnosis, and identified resistance genes such as bla KPC and bla NDM in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
