full_output.paper_title: In vitro susceptibility of Neisseria gonorrhoeae to netilmicin and etimicin in comparison to gentamicin and other aminoglycosides.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that etimicin and netilmicin exhibited higher susceptibility against Neisseria gonorrhoeae compared to gentamicin and other aminoglycosides. Additionally, propylamycin showed improved activity against N. gonorrhoeae due to its 4'-propyl modification.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion, agar dilution, and E tests.

full_output.key_findings: The study found a prevalence of rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (RR-TB) of 7.42% among MTB-positive patients, with higher rates in elderly patients and those with a history of anti-TB drug exposure.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of Xpert® MTB/RIF assay results from 2015 to 2021.

full_output.paper_title: The prevalence and clinical context of antimicrobial resistance amongst medical inpatients at a referral hospital in Rwanda: a cohort study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high rates of antimicrobial resistance among Gram-negative organisms, particularly Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, with significant resistance to ceftriaxone, gentamicin, and piperacillin-tazobactam. Carbapenem resistance was noted in Acinetobacter species.
full_output.methodology: Prospective observational cohort study analyzing microbiological cultures and susceptibility testing data from 122 adult medical inpatients.

full_output.paper_title: Where do the antibiotic resistance genes come from? A modulated analysis of sources and loads of resistances in Lake Maggiore.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and quantifies various antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in Lake Maggiore and its surrounding areas, highlighting the influence of anthropogenic activities on the distribution and abundance of these genes. Key findings include the persistent presence of sul2 and tetA genes, the seasonal dynamics of blaCTX-M, and the association of ermB and qnrS with anthropogenic pressures.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) was used to quantify the abundance of selected ARGs in water samples from Lake Maggiore, its tributaries, and a wastewater treatment plant effluent.
full_output.sample_size: Samples covering ~80% of the annual water inflow of Lake Maggiore

full_output.methodology: The study used transmission electron microscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and microbiological assays to characterize the nanomedicine and evaluate its antibacterial and antibiofilm properties.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and encapsulation of bacteriophage with chitosan nanoparticles for biocontrol of multidrug-resistant methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolated from broiler poultry farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains with high resistance to streptomycin and other antibiotics. It also explored the use of chitosan nanoparticles (CS-NPs) to encapsulate bacteriophages, enhancing their stability and lytic activity against MRSA.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and characterization of MRSA strains, detection of antimicrobial resistance, and evaluation of bacteriophage encapsulation with CS-NPs.

full_output.paper_title: Ciprofloxacin loaded PEG coated ZnO nanoparticles with enhanced antibacterial and wound healing effects.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed ciprofloxacin-loaded PEG-coated ZnO nanoparticles (CIP-PEG-ZnO-NPs) with enhanced antibacterial activity against clinical isolates of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, showing significant inhibition zones and effective wound healing properties in vivo.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of ZnO nanoparticles via chemical and green methods, functionalization with PEG and ciprofloxacin, characterization using FTIR, XRD, and SEM, and evaluation of antibacterial activity through disc diffusion, MIC, and MBC assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study explores global epistasis in plasmid-mediated antimicrobial resistance, focusing on the pOXA-48 plasmid and its interactions with bacterial hosts, revealing patterns of epistatic interactions that influence fitness and antibiotic resistance levels.
full_output.methodology: The study re-analyzed data from previous studies on clinical enterobacteria carrying the pOXA-48 plasmid, examining fitness effects and antibiotic resistance levels through competition assays and MIC measurements.

full_output.paper_title: Boronic acid inhibitors of penicillin-binding protein 1b: serine and lysine labelling agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates boronic acid derivatives as inhibitors of penicillin-binding protein 1b (PBP1b), focusing on their ability to covalently label the catalytic serine and lysine residues. Compounds 29 and 30 were identified as inhibitors of PBP1b, while compound 33 exhibited slight activity. The research highlights the potential of boronic acids to target PBP1b through covalent modifications, particularly involving lysine residues.
full_output.methodology: Virtual screening, synthesis, and biochemical assays were used to evaluate the inhibitory activity of boronic acid derivatives against PBP1b.

full_output.paper_title: Opposing genetic polymorphisms of two ABC transporters contribute to the variation of nukacin resistance in Streptococcus mutans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two ABC transporters, LctFEG and MukFEG, as critical factors in nukacin resistance in Streptococcus mutans. Genetic polymorphisms in these transporters contribute to varying levels of resistance, with LctFEG being more effective in conferring resistance compared to MukFEG.
full_output.methodology: Genome analysis, gene knockout and complementation experiments, susceptibility tests, and quantitative PCR were used to investigate the role of LctFEG and MukFEG in nukacin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic bactericidal effects of phage-enhanced antibiotic therapy against MRSA biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that combining daptomycin (DAP) and ceftaroline (CPT) with phage cocktails (Intesti13 + Sb-1 and Intesti13 + Sb-1 + Romulus) exhibits synergistic bactericidal activity against MRSA biofilms, particularly against DAP-non-susceptible vancomycin-intermediate S. aureus (DNS VISA) and DAP-susceptible MRSA strains. The phage-antibiotic combinations effectively reduced bacterial viability without inducing resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used modified checkerboard and 24-h time-kill assays to evaluate phage-antibiotic synergy against MRSA biofilms, along with in vitro biofilm PK/PD models to assess bactericidal activity and resistance development.

full_output.paper_title: Ethambutol and meropenem/clavulanate synergy promotes enhanced extracellular and intracellular killing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

This synergy is attributed to the disruption of the cell wall, allowing better access of beta-lactams to their targets.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized checkerboard assays, growth curve analysis, and flow cytometry to evaluate the synergistic effects of EMB with beta-lactams against Mtb strains.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanistic Insights into the Mutagenic Incorporation of 5-Fluorodeoxyuridine Triphosphate by DNA Polymerase η

full_output.key_findings: Polη efficiently incorporates 5FdUTP into DNA, leading to mutagenesis, and is upregulated in response to 5-FU treatment. ITPA and POLB are also upregulated, suggesting their roles in 5-FU metabolism and DNA repair.
full_output.methodology: Kinetic studies, crystallography, and qRT-PCR were used to analyze the incorporation of 5FdUTP by polη and the gene expression responses to 5-FU.

full_output.paper_title: Global diversity of enterococci and description of 18 previously unknown species.
full_output.key_findings: This study identifies 18 previously unknown species of Enterococcus, expands the understanding of their genetic diversity, and reveals unique genomic features associated with different clades.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and phylogenetic studies of 886 enterococcal isolates from diverse hosts and environments.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of MDR E. coli strains isolated from Pet Dogs with clinic diarrhea: A pool of antibiotic resistance genes and virulence-associated genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and virulence-associated genes (VAGs) in multidrug-resistant (MDR) E. coli strains isolated from pet dogs with clinical diarrhea. Key findings include the high prevalence of tetA, blaTEM, and blaCTX-M genes, along with various VAGs such as fimC, iucD, and sitA.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR detection to identify ARGs and VAGs in 74 MDR E. coli strains, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing and phylogenetic grouping.

full_output.paper_title: Protein-Based Rechargeable and Replaceable Antimicrobial and Antifouling Coatings on Hydrophobic Food-Contact Surfaces.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces protein-based coatings using tannic acid, gelatin, and soy protein hydrolysate that form N-halamine structures, exhibiting strong antimicrobial activity against E. coli and L. innocua. These coatings are rechargeable and removable, showing potential for use on hydrophobic food-contact surfaces.
full_output.methodology: The coatings were developed through crosslinking reactions and tested for antimicrobial efficacy, stability, and rechargeability under various conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Cryo-EM analysis of S. aureus TarL, a polymerase in wall teichoic acid biogenesis central to virulence and antibiotic resistance.

TarL.encodes: polymerase in wall teichoic acid biogenesis

mutations_found.effect_on_function: inactivates the putative function of H300 as the catalytic base

full_output.paper_title: Proteomics-based vaccine targets annotation and design of multi-epitope vaccine against antibiotic-resistant Streptococcus gallolyticus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies penicillin-binding protein and ATP synthase subunit as potential vaccine targets for Streptococcus gallolyticus, focusing on their epitopic regions for vaccine design.
full_output.methodology: In silico methods including proteomics, epitope prediction, and vaccine design were used.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of florfenicol dosing regimen on the phenotypic and genotypic resistance of enteric bacteria in steers.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of florfenicol resistance genes floR and fexA in enteric bacteria, which conferred resistance to phenicols. These genes were detected through metagenomic sequencing.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze resistance profiles in enteric bacteria from steers administered florfenicol.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of Helicobacter pylori resistance in patients with different gastric diseases.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the resistance rates of Helicobacter pylori to amoxicillin (AMX), clarithromycin (CLR), levofloxacin (LVX), and furazolidone (FR) in patients with various gastric diseases. It found that resistance rates varied significantly among different gastric mucosal lesions, with atrophic gastritis being associated with higher resistance rates. The study also identified factors such as age, sex, and PPI treatment history influencing H. pylori resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted an 8-year clinical retrospective cohort study involving 2847 patients, analyzing antibiotic resistance through antimicrobial susceptibility testing and statistical analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the antimicrobial and antiproliferative potential of Origanum punonense essential oil (EO), showing potent activity against various bacterial and fungal strains, including MRSA and Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales.
full_output.methodology: Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and broth microdilution assays were used to analyze the phytochemical composition and evaluate the antimicrobial and antiproliferative effects of the EO.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Salmonella spp. from Food-Producing Animals and Human Cases in the EU

erm(B).mechanism: modifies 23S rRNA to prevent binding of macrolides

cfr(C).encodes: phenicol, lincosamide, pleuromutilin, and oxazolidinone resistance

erm(B).notes: Detected in C. coli isolates from broilers and fattening turkeys.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes, including bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-14b, bla SHV-12, tet(X3), and tet(X4), in Salmonella isolates from food-producing animals and human cases in the EU. These genes confer resistance to various antibiotics, highlighting the spread of multidrug-resistant Salmonella strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Data from multiple countries across Europe

full_output.paper_title: Comparative investigation of derivatives of (E)-N-((E)-3-phenylallylidene)aniline: Synthesis, structural characterization, biological evaluation, density functional theory analysis, and in silico molecular docking.
full_output.key_findings: The study synthesized and evaluated a series of Schiff base derivatives (CA1-CA10) for their antimicrobial and antifungal activities, with CA3, CA4, CA9, and CA10 showing the most potent activity against various bacterial and fungal strains.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of Schiff bases, structural characterization via spectroscopy, and biological evaluation using broth microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Mutation of wbtJ, a N-formyltransferase involved in O-antigen synthesis, results in biofilm formation, phase variation and attenuation in Francisella tularensis.

wbtJ.notes: Mutation in wbtJ leads to biofilm formation and O-Ag modification

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the wbtJ gene, a formyltransferase involved in O-antigen synthesis, as responsible for biofilm formation, phase variation, and attenuation in Francisella tularensis.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, SNP analysis, and construction of a ΔwbtJ mutant to validate the role of wbtJ in biofilm formation and virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibilities of Campylobacter fetus: report from a reference laboratory.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of Campylobacter fetus isolates, highlighting favorable MICs for gentamicin and meropenem, while ciprofloxacin shows variable results.
full_output.methodology: Agar dilution antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed on C. fetus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of N-acetyl cysteine, rifampicin, and ozone on biofilm formation in pan-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae: an experimental study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of carbapenem resistance genes OXA-48 and NDM-1 in pan-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates. Ozonated water at 4.78 mg/L was found to effectively reduce bacterial counts in biofilms by ≥ 2 log10.
full_output.methodology: PCR for detection of carbapenem resistance genes, colony counting, and laser scanning confocal microscopy for evaluating biofilm formation and efficacy of antibiofilm agents.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic toxicity with copper contributes to NAT2-associated isoniazid toxicity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NAT2 and ATP7B genotypes as potential contributors to the risk of AT-DILI, with NAT2 ultraslow acetylators (UAs) and ATP7B 832R/R homozygosity being significantly associated with increased risk of isoniazid-induced hepatotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: Targeted sequencing of 380 pharmacogenes, genotyping for NAT2 and ATP7B, and functional assays in cell lines.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae capsular types, antibiotic resistance and virulence factors in China: a longitudinal, multi-centre study.

blaKPC-2.validation_method: PCR detection in 98.2% of CRKP isolates

blaNDM.validation_method: PCR detection in 4.8% of CRKP isolates

blaOXA-48-like.validation_method: PCR detection in 1.8% of CRKP isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla KPC-2, bla NDM, and bla OXA-48-like as the primary carbapenem resistance genes in CRKP isolates in China, with bla KPC-2 being the most prevalent.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of carbapenemase genes and capsular genotyping of CRKP isolates.

full_output.paper_title: New insights into bioaugmented removal of sulfamethoxazole in sediment microcosms: degradation efficiency, ecological risk and microbial mechanisms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies sul1 and sul2 genes as sulfonamide resistance genes in Paenarthrobacter sp. R1 and Pseudomonas sp. M2, and characterizes the sadA gene involved in sulfamethoxazole degradation.
full_output.methodology: qPCR, metagenomic sequencing, DNA-SIP, and 16S rRNA gene sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic characterization of ESBL-producing urinary isolates of E. coli and Klebsiella spp. in a tertiary care children's hospital in Nepal.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of ESBL-producing E. coli and Klebsiella spp. in pediatric urinary isolates, highlighting the need for antimicrobial stewardship and targeted empirical treatment options such as nitrofurantoin and gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study with antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method and phenotypic identification of ESBL producers.

full_output.paper_title: Mathematical modelling of antibiotic interaction on evolution of antibiotic resistance: an analytical approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a mathematical model exploring the population dynamics of wildtype and mutant bacteria under interacting antibiotics, highlighting the impact of antibiotic interactions on the evolution of resistance.
full_output.methodology: Developed and analyzed a mathematical model investigating the relationship between synergistic and antagonistic antibiotic interactions and the growth rate of mutant bacteria acquiring resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Adipocyte‑rich microenvironment promotes chemoresistance via upregulation of peroxisome proliferator‑activated receptor gamma/ABCG2 in epithelial ovarian cancer.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PPARγ and ABCG2 as critical players in adipocyte-rich microenvironment-mediated chemoresistance in epithelial ovarian cancer, demonstrating that PPARγ upregulates ABCG2 expression, thereby enhancing drug efflux and reducing chemotherapy effectiveness.
full_output.methodology: In vitro experiments, Western blotting, luciferase reporter assays, RNA sequencing, and animal models were used to investigate the role of PPARγ and ABCG2 in chemoresistance.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of meropenem-vaborbactam plus aztreonam against metallo-β-lactamase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the in vitro activity of meropenem-vaborbactam plus aztreonam (MEV-ATM) against metallo-β-lactamase (MBL)-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, identifying OmpK36 134-135GD-insertion and increased copy numbers of bla NDM-1 and bla OXA-48-like as key factors in MEV-ATM non-susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, gene cloning, and broth microdilution MIC testing were used to evaluate AMR mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Reduced peptidoglycan synthesis capacity impairs growth of E. coli at high salt concentration.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the deletion of mrcB (encoding PBP1B) leads to significant fitness reduction under high salt stress, highlighting the critical role of PBP1B in maintaining cell viability under such conditions. Additionally, the study reveals that the activity of class A PBPs, particularly PBP1A and PBP1B, is significantly reduced at high salt concentrations, affecting peptidoglycan synthesis and cell wall integrity.
full_output.methodology: Genetic interaction screens, morphological analyses, and enzymatic activity assays were conducted to evaluate the effects of gene deletions and salt stress on E. coli growth and peptidoglycan synthesis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaOXA-23, blaOXA-24, and blaOXA-51 as key genes associated with carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii, and highlights the importance of PCR-based detection for accurate identification of CRAB carriers.
full_output.methodology: The study uses PCR-based detection of carbapenemase genes and selective agar plates for the identification and confirmation of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Sulbactam-durlobactam: a β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combination targeting Acinetobacter baumannii.

adeJ.encodes: component of the AdeIJK efflux system of Acinetobacter
adeJ.notes: The G288S mutation in AdeJ was associated with increased efflux capacity and higher sulbactam-durlobactam MIC.

mutations_found.validated_by: purified mutant enzymes and isogenic strains
purified mutant enzymes and isogenic strains
purified mutant enzymes and isogenic strains

pbp3.notes: Mutations in pbp3 were associated with increased sulbactam-durlobactam MIC values.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the pbp3 gene and the adeJ gene that contribute to resistance to sulbactam-durlobactam in Acinetobacter baumannii. Specifically, T526S, A515V, and G523V mutations in pbp3 and a G288S mutation in adeJ were associated with increased MIC values for sulbactam-durlobactam.
full_output.methodology: Genetic engineering, susceptibility testing, and in vitro studies were used to validate the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and functional characterization of AfsR, an SARP family transcriptional activator of antibiotic biosynthesis in Streptomyces.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structural and functional aspects of AfsR, an SARP family transcriptional activator involved in antibiotic biosynthesis in Streptomyces. It reveals how AfsR interacts with DNA and RNA polymerase to activate transcription, and identifies the role of its NOD and TPR domains in regulating this activity.
full_output.methodology: The research employed cryo-electron microscopy, fluorescence polarization assays, and in vitro transcription assays to analyze the structure and function of AfsR.

full_output.paper_title: Optimization of an in vitro Pseudomonas aeruginosa Biofilm Model to Examine Antibiotic Pharmacodynamics at the Air-Liquid Interface.
full_output.key_findings: The study optimized an in vitro air-liquid interface pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic biofilm model to evaluate the activity of inhaled and intravenous polymyxin B and tobramycin against P. aeruginosa strains. It found that inhaled antibiotic exposures were more active than their intravenous counterparts against both biofilm and planktonic populations, with tobramycin showing greater activity by the end of the experiment.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized an in vitro air-liquid interface PK/PD biofilm model, broth microdilution for MIC determination, and CLSM for biofilm visualization.

full_output.paper_title: Enhancing colistin efficacy against Salmonella infections with a quinazoline-based dual therapeutic strategy.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: derepress the system and thus increase resistance to polymyxins

mgrB.evidence_note: The paper states that mutations or disruptions of mgrB, which encodes for MgrB, a transmembrane peptide that inhibits the PhoQ/PhoQ system, derepress the system and thus increase resistance to polymyxins.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that CA439 enhances colistin efficacy against Salmonella by targeting the PhoP/PhoQ system and related resistance mechanisms, reducing the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of colistin and demonstrating effectiveness against resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized checkerboard assays, mutant strain analyses, and reporter constructs to investigate the mechanism of action of CA439 in enhancing colistin activity.

full_output.paper_title: Semi-purified Antimicrobial Proteins from Oyster Hemolymph Inhibit Pneumococcal Infection.
full_output.key_findings: Fraction 7 of oyster hemolymph exhibited strong antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against multi-drug-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae, containing carbonic anhydrase, cofilin, cystatin B–like, and gelsolin-like proteins.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial-biofilm inhibition coupled assays, proteomic analysis, and HPLC fractionation were used to evaluate the activity of oyster hemolymph fractions against S. pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance and virulence genes profile of Non typhodial Salmonella species isolated from poultry enteritis in India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes including blaTEM, blaSHV, blaCTX-M, tet(A), tet(B), tet(C), sul1, sul2, and sul3 in multidrug-resistant Salmonella isolates from poultry enteritis in India.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to detect antibiotic resistance genes and assess resistance patterns in Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Development of Antimicrobial Peptides Derived from Lipopolysaccharide-Binding Domains for Enhanced Antibacterial Activity
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on optimizing antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) using machine learning and genetic algorithms, resulting in the development of LBD A-D with enhanced antimicrobial activity against pathogens like Vibrio alginolyticus and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study employed machine learning and genetic algorithms to optimize the structure of LBD Mj, a lipopolysaccharide-binding domain from an antimicrobial peptide, leading to the creation of modified peptides with improved antimicrobial properties.

full_output.paper_title: Multi-platform whole genome sequencing for tuberculosis clinical and surveillance applications.

eis.evidence_note: The eis gene was found to be deleted in isolate S27, and overexpression of eis is a leading cause of resistance to kanamycin. Its complete deletion could enhance the susceptibility of M. tuberculosis to antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed 59 M. tuberculosis isolates from Thailand using Illumina and ONT platforms, identifying various drug resistance mutations in genes such as katG, fabG1, rpoB, ethA, pncA, gyrA, gyrB, thyX, rpsL, rrs, embA, embB, whiB6, Rv3083, Rv1258c, eis, thyA, gid, embR, and fbiC, contributing to resistance against isoniazid, rifampicin, ethionamide, pyrazinamide, ciprofloxacin, fluoroquinolones, para-aminosalicylic acid, streptomycin, ethambutol, kanamycin, amikacin, capreomycin, and delamanid.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing using Illumina and ONT platforms, followed by bioinformatics analysis for variant calling and drug resistance profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Vibrio fluvialis Bacteremia in an Immunocompetent Patient with Acute Cholangitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several bile acid resistance-associated genes in Vibrio fluvialis, including toxR, leuO, ompU, tolC, yrbK, rpoS, and damX, which may contribute to the development of acute cholangitis and subsequent bacteremia in immunocompetent patients.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of Vibrio fluvialis was conducted to identify bile acid resistance-associated genes.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence and clonal expansion of Aeromonas hydrophila ST1172 that simultaneously produces MOX-13 and OXA-724.

blaOXA-724.validation_method: genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

imiH.validation_method: genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

blaMOX-13.validation_method: genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of a novel carbapenem-resistant Aeromonas hydrophila sequence type (ST1172) that simultaneously produces MOX-13 and OXA-724 beta-lactamases, leading to resistance against multiple beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and comparative genomic analysis were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms and clonal relatedness of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: CRISPR/Cas9-edited ROS1 + non-small cell lung cancer cell lines highlight differential drug sensitivity in 2D vs 3D cultures while reflecting established resistance profiles.

ROS1.evidence_note: The paper describes the introduction of the mutations G2032R, L2026M, and S1986Y in the ROS1 kinase domain of HCC78 cells, which are associated with resistance to various TKIs. The study validates the resistance conferred by these mutations through drug screening in 2D and 3D cultures.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes three ROS1 kinase domain mutations (G2032R, L2026M, and S1986Y) that confer resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) in ROS1+ non-small cell lung cancer cell lines. These mutations were introduced using CRISPR/Cas9 and validated through drug sensitivity assays in 2D and 3D cultures.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, drug screening in 2D and 3D cultures, immunoblotting, and statistical analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence and mechanisms of tigecycline resistance in carbapenem- and colistin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in Thailand.

acrB.mechanism: overexpression of efflux pump acrB gene and its regulator RamA
acrB.validation_method: qRT-PCR and efflux pump inhibition assay
acrB.genetic_context: mutations in RamR (M184V, Y59C, I141T, A28T, C99/C100 insertion), in RamR binding site (PI) of ramA gene (C139T), in MarR (S82G), and/or in AcrR (L154R, R13Q)
acrB.evidence_note: The major mechanism of tigecycline resistance was the overexpression of efflux pump acrB gene and its regulator RamA, which was caused by mutations in RamR, RamR binding site (PI) of ramA gene, MarR, and AcrR.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mechanisms of tigecycline resistance in carbapenem- and colistin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting the roles of acrB and ramA overexpression, as well as the presence of mutated tet(A) efflux pump genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, qRT-PCR, and efflux pump inhibition assays were used to analyze tigecycline resistance mechanisms in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal Distribution and Its Association With the Carbapenem Resistance Mechanisms of Carbapenem-Non-Susceptible Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolates From Korean Hospitals.

mutations_found.protein_change: frameshift mutation leading to premature stop codon

oprD.notes: Frameshift mutations in oprD result in truncated or non-functional OprD protein, reducing carbapenem permeability.

full_output.key_findings: Carbapenem resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Korean hospitals is mainly due to frameshift mutations in the oprD gene, along with the production of metallo-beta-lactamases (blaIMP-6, blaVIM-2, blaNDM-1) or hyperproduction of AmpC beta-lactamase.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and MLST analysis were used to characterize resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Unveiling distinct genetic features in multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli isolated from mammary tissue and gut of mastitis induced mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in multidrug-resistant E. coli strains isolated from mastitis-induced mice, highlighting the complex resistome and potential for horizontal gene transfer.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli strains.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiogram and molecular characterization of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing pathogens implicated in chronic suppurative otitis media.

blaSHV.evidence_note: The paper states that blaSHV was the most predominant ESBL genotype, and that ESBL-producing GNB pathogens were resistant to cephalosporins, penicillins, and monobactams.

blaCTX-M.evidence_note: The paper mentions blaCTX-M as an ESBL gene but does not explicitly state that it confers resistance to cephalosporins, penicillins, and monobactams.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaSHV, blaTEM, and blaCTX-M as the most prevalent ESBL genes in ESBL-producing GNB pathogens isolated from CSOM patients, highlighting the emergence of multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Microbiological analysis, antibiogram determination, and PCR-based detection of ESBL genes.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of Siderophore-Platinum(IV) Conjugates Reveals Differing Antibacterial Activity and DNA Damage Depending on the Platinum Cargo.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports two new siderophore-platinum(IV) conjugates, L/D-EOP, which show enhanced antibacterial activity against E. coli compared to oxaliplatin alone. The conjugates utilize the Ent transport machinery for cytoplasmic delivery, leading to DNA damage and bacterial lysis.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of L/D-EOP conjugates, assessment of antibacterial activity, DNA damage, and Pt uptake in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance and the Prevalence of the Panton-Valentine Leukocidin Gene among Clinical Isolates of Staphylococcus aureus in Lithuania.

mecA.mechanism: horizontal acquisition of the mecA gene, which encodes PBP2a, an alternative transpeptidase with poor affinity for the majority of β-lactam antibiotics, confers resistance to methicillin as well as almost all other members of the broad class of β-lactam antibiotics
mecA.genetic_context: horizontal acquisition of the mecA gene
mecA.evidence_note: The mecA gene was found in 6.4% of all 745 tested S. aureus strains. In 95.6% of MRSA strains, the presence of mecA was detected.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from Lithuania, highlighting the dominance of ermC in erythromycin resistance, tetK in tetracycline resistance, and mecA in methicillin resistance. Additionally, the pvl gene encoding Panton-Valentine leukocidin was found in 7.3% of isolates, predominantly in MRSA strains.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex real-time PCR was used to detect antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, Identification, Antimicrobial Resistance, Genotyping, and Whole-Genome Sequencing Analysis of Salmonella Enteritidis Isolated from a Food-Poisoning Incident.

blaTEM-1.validation_method: genome sequencing and CARD database annotation

tetA.validation_method: genome sequencing and CARD database annotation

sul1.validation_method: genome sequencing and CARD database annotation

sul2.validation_method: genome sequencing and CARD database annotation

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella Enteritidis strain 21A, including aac(6')-Iaa, blaTEM-1, qnrB, floR, tetA, sul1, and sul2, which conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as aminoglycosides, beta-lactams, quinolones, tetracyclines, and sulfonamides.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and CARD database annotation were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella Enteritidis strain 21A.

full_output.paper_title: Machine Learning-Based Virtual Screening of Antibacterial Agents against Methicillin-Susceptible and Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study utilized machine learning models to identify potential antibacterial compounds against methicillin-susceptible (MSSA) and resistant (MRSA) Staphylococcus aureus strains, leading to the discovery of six compounds with significant antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: The research involved machine learning-based virtual screening, in vitro assays, and determination of minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) against various S. aureus strains.

full_output.paper_title: Adaptive evolution of plasmid and chromosome contributes to the fitness of a blaNDM-bearing cointegrate plasmid in Escherichia coli.

mutations_found.validated_by: transcriptome analysis, in vitro transcription assay

sspA.notes: The mutation in sspA reduces its transcriptional inhibitory capacity, thereby improving bacterial fitness, biofilm formation ability, and gut colonization ability.

psiB.notes: The deficiency of anti-SOS gene psiB is found responsible for the impaired horizontal transferability.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the role of sspA mutation in improving bacterial fitness, biofilm formation, and gut colonization ability, and highlights the importance of psiB in plasmid horizontal transferability.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MIC testing, conjugation frequency measurement, transcriptome analysis, and in vitro transcription assays were used to validate the findings.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular basis of TMPRSS2 recognition by Paeniclostridium sordellii hemorrhagic toxin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TcsH as a hemorrhagic toxin that binds to TMPRSS2 through the CROP unit-VI, and mutations in TcsH impair this binding, reducing toxicity.
full_output.methodology: Cryo-EM, pull-down assays, site-directed mutagenesis, and biochemical assays were used to characterize TcsH-TMPRSS2 interactions.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the antibacterial activity of silver nanoparticles coated with a carbon shell (AgNPs@C) against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, showing superior efficacy compared to Ceftazidime. The nanoparticles inhibited the expression of virulence-related genes fimH, rmpA, and mrkA, suggesting a mechanism involving disruption of bacterial adhesion and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of AgNPs@C via electrical arc discharge, followed by evaluation of antibacterial activity using disc diffusion, MIC, MBC, real-time PCR, and microscopic techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm formation and antimicrobial resistance pattern of uropathogenic E. coli ST131 isolated from children with malignant tumors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenem resistance genes blaVIM, blaNDM, blaKPC, and blaIMP in E. coli ST131 isolates, along with biofilm-related genes lasR, pelA, and lecA. ST131 isolates showed higher antimicrobial resistance and biofilm-forming capabilities compared to non-ST131 isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, PCR for gene detection, and biofilm formation assessment using the microtiter plate method.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance patterns, virulence genes, and biofilm formation in enterococci strains collected from different sources.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of virulence genes esp, efaA, and ace in Enterococcus faecalis and E. faecium strains, with esp being the most dominant in E. faecalis. High resistance to kanamycin and quinupristin-dalfopristin was observed in E. faecalis isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR to detect virulence genes and disk agar diffusion for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Staphopain mediated virulence and antibiotic resistance alteration in co-infection of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa: an animal model.
full_output.key_findings: Staphopain A was found to disrupt biofilms and reduce the viability of S. aureus and P. aeruginosa. It also decreased resistance to vancomycin and doripenem in these bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study used an animal model and cell culture experiments to evaluate the effects of staphopain A on biofilm disruption and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Culturable Streptomyces spp. from high-altitude, oligotrophic North Western Himalaya: a comprehensive study on the diversity, bioactivity and insights into the proteome of potential species.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes various Streptomyces isolates from the North Western Himalaya, highlighting their bioactive potential and antimicrobial properties. However, no specific AMR genes or mutations were experimentally validated in this paper.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro anti-Helicobacter pylori activity and the underlining mechanism of an empirical herbal formula - Hezi Qingyou.

full_output.paper_title: Conjugation to Native and Nonnative Triscatecholate Siderophores Enhances Delivery and Antibacterial Activity of a β-Lactam to Gram-Negative Bacterial Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that conjugation of ampicillin (Amp) to a synthetic triscatecholate siderophore (TC) enhances its antibacterial activity against Gram-negative pathogens, including those with intrinsic β-lactam resistance. TC-Amp exhibits improved delivery and efficacy compared to free Amp, leveraging the Ent OM receptors FepA and IroN for uptake.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of biochemical assays, microbial growth inhibition tests, and structural characterization to evaluate the antibacterial activity of TC-Amp and its comparison to conventional antibiotics and other conjugates.

full_output.paper_title: Common and varied molecular responses of Escherichia coli to five different inhibitors of the lipopolysaccharide biosynthetic enzyme LpxC.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing and analysis of Chryseobacterium arthrosphaerae from Rana nigromaculata.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 10 antibiotic resistance genes in Chryseobacterium arthrosphaerae strain FS91703, including genes conferring resistance to folate pathway inhibitors, penicillins, cephalosporins, carbapenems, phenicols, tetracyclines, and erythromycin. Additionally, two multidrug-resistant efflux pump genes, adeG and farA, were detected.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and analysis, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and bioinformatics tools were used to identify and characterize the antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities of biosynthesized starch/silver-selenium nanocomposite (St/Ag-Se NC). The nanocomposite also exhibited significant biofilm suppression against S. epidermidis and S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of biochemical assays, microscopy, and microbiological techniques to characterize the nanocomposite and assess its antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic, molecular detection, and Antibiotic Resistance Profile (MDR and XDR) of Aeromonas hydrophila isolated from Farmed Tilapia zillii and Mugil cephalus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Aeromonas hydrophila isolates from farmed fish, including bla_pse1, bla_SHV, tetA, and sul1, which confer resistance to beta-lactams, tetracyclines, and sulfonamides.
full_output.methodology: PCR and molecular identification techniques were used to detect AMR genes in A. hydrophila isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Uncovering the spread of drug-resistant bacteria through next-generation sequencing based surveillance: transmission of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales by a contaminated duodenoscope.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla CTX-M-15 in Citrobacter freundii and bla SHV-12 in Klebsiella pneumoniae as the resistance mechanisms responsible for the transmission of multidrug-resistant organisms through a contaminated duodenoscope.
full_output.methodology: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) was used to analyze the genomes of ESBL-producing isolates, and molecular typing was performed to track the outbreak.

full_output.paper_title: What are the optimal pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic targets for β-lactamase inhibitors? A systematic review.
full_output.key_findings: This systematic review analyzed the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) targets for β-lactamase inhibitors (BLIs) in combination with β-lactam antibiotics. It identified the optimal PK/PD indices for various BLIs, highlighting the importance of maintaining adequate drug concentrations to ensure efficacy against resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review of studies reporting PK/PD indices and exposure requirements for BLIs in combination with β-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Emerging resistome diversity in clinical Vibrio cholerae strains revealing their role as potential reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in clinical Vibrio cholerae strains, including strA, strB, sul2, catB9, floR, CRP, dfrA1, almG, and varG, highlighting their potential as reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping, PCR, genome annotation, and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in Vibrio cholerae strains.

full_output.paper_title: Early transcriptional changes of heavy metal resistance and multiple efflux genes in Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris under copper and heavy metal ion stress.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes involved in heavy metal resistance and efflux in Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris under copper stress, including czcB, copL, copA, copB, cohA, cohB, cohL, and cusA, which show differential expression under various heavy metal stresses.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq and qPCR were used to analyze gene expression in Xcc strain BrA1 under copper stress and other heavy metals.

full_output.key_findings: D-histidine inhibited biofilm formation and increased susceptibility of Pseudomonas aeruginosa to amikacin.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR, biofilm formation assays, and minimum inhibitory concentration testing.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting Iron - Respiratory Reciprocity Promotes Bacterial Death.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies FeoB and PotH as critical targets for N-104, demonstrating that their absence leads to resistance. Additionally, YaiW is shown to facilitate N-104's outer membrane translocation.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized a combination of genetic screens, biochemical assays, and molecular techniques to investigate the mechanism of action of N-104.

full_output.paper_title: Relationship between biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance of Klebsiella pneumoniae and updates on antibiofilm therapeutic strategies.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the relationship between biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting genes involved in biofilm formation such as wza, wzm, wbbM, mrkABCDF, treC, sugE, wcaG, luxS, acrA, emrB, oqxA, and qacEΔ1. It discusses the role of biofilms in enhancing antibiotic resistance and explores various therapeutic strategies against biofilms.
full_output.methodology: The paper analyzes genes involved in biofilm formation through mutant analysis and transcription studies, examining their impact on biofilm development and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Establishment and application of a rapid molecular diagnostic platform for the isothermal visual amplification of group B Streptococcus based on recombinase polymerase.

cfb.mechanism: specific detection of Group B Streptococcus (GBS)

full_output.key_findings: The study established a rapid molecular diagnostic platform for the isothermal visual amplification of Group B Streptococcus (GBS) using recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) coupled with lateral flow chromatography (LFS). The method targets the cfb gene, which encodes the Christie–Atkins–Munch–Petersen (CAMP) factor, a virulence gene specific to GBS. The platform demonstrated high specificity, detecting GBS without cross-reactivity with other pathogens and achieving a detection limit of 100 copies. The method showed a 95.92% agreement rate with TaqMan real-time PCR in clinical samples.
full_output.methodology: The study employed RPA technology combined with nfo enzyme and LFS for visual detection of GBS. The cfb gene was targeted for amplification, and the method was validated using various bacterial and parasite strains, as well as clinical vaginal swab samples.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of institutional antimicrobial stewardship guidelines on prescription of critically important antimicrobials for dogs and cats.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the impact of institutional antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) guidelines on the prescription of critically important antimicrobials (CIA) for dogs and cats. Fluoroquinolones were the most frequently prescribed CIA class in both species, with adherence to guidelines being suboptimal. The implementation of AMS guidelines increased culture and susceptibility testing but did not significantly alter the rates of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of electronic medical records from a university veterinary hospital, assessing antimicrobial prescriptions and adherence to guidelines.
full_output.sample_size: 1040 case visits from 1027 unique animals (779 dogs and 248 cats)

These genes were validated through MIC tests and complementation experiments, demonstrating their role in BA resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide screening of Keio collection mutants, MIC tests, and complementation experiments were performed to identify and validate genes responsible for intrinsic BA resistance in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the broad-spectrum antibacterial activity of bacteriocin-like inhibitory substance-producing probiotics isolated from fermented foods.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bacteriocin gene clusters in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum CYLB47, including plnT, plnU, plnV, and plnW, which are involved in the production of bacteriocin-like inhibitory substances (BLIS) with broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Perturbation and resilience of the gut microbiome up to 3 months after β-lactams exposure in healthy volunteers suggest an important role of microbial β-lactamases.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the role of β-lactamases in the gut microbiome, showing that they contribute to the resilience of the microbiota by degrading β-lactam antibiotics, thus reducing their impact on the gut ecosystem.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis, targeted and untargeted metabolomics, and phenotypic analysis of fecal samples from healthy volunteers.

full_output.paper_title: Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Due to Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae-Induced Pneumonia: Clinical Features and Prognostic Factors.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high mortality rate (57.69%) of acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) caused by carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP)-induced pneumonia. CRKP isolates were all multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains, showing resistance to various antibiotics, including amikacin, ciprofloxacin, aztreonam, cefepime, ceftazidime, imipenem, meropenem, piperacillin/tazobactam, tobramycin, and levofloxacin. All CRKP isolates were MDR, whereas 12.82% of non-CRKP isolates were also MDR.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective case-control study analyzing clinical features and prognostic factors of CRKP-induced pneumonia in AECOPD patients.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Detection of Multidrug Resistance and Characterizations of Mutations in Mycobacterium Tuberculosis Using Polycarbonate Track-Etched Membrane Based DNA Bio-Chip.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a DNA bio-chip for rapid detection of mutations in rpoB, katG, and inhA genes associated with rifampicin and isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: The study used a DNA bio-chip with specific probes targeting mutations in rpoB, katG, and inhA genes, validated by sequencing and culture-based drug susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Immune priming modulates Galleria mellonella and Pseudomonas entomophila interaction. Antimicrobial properties of Kazal peptide Pr13a.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the Kazal peptide Pr13a as having antibacterial activity against Pseudomonas entomophila and Bacillus thuringiensis.
full_output.methodology: In vitro antimicrobial assay and purification of the peptide.

full_output.paper_title: PqsA mutation-mediated enhancement of phage-mediated combat against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the knockout of the pqsA gene enhances the bactericidal effect of phages vB_Pae_QDWS and vB_Pae_S1 against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, suggesting that pqsA is a potential target for improving phage therapy.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockout, phage infection assays, and growth curve analysis were used to evaluate the effect of pqsA deletion on phage efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-encoded gene duplications of extended-spectrum β-lactamases in clinical bacterial isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies plasmid-encoded gene duplications of extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs) in clinical bacterial isolates, demonstrating that these duplications lead to increased resistance to ceftazidime.
full_output.methodology: Long-read whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the plasmid-encoded ESBL gene duplications and their impact on antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.methodology: Genomes of 146 H. pylori isolates were analyzed using bioinformatics tools such as Abricate, CARD RGI, MLST, Prokka, Roary, and others to identify AMR and virulence genes.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa ventricular assist device infections: findings from ineffective phage therapies in five cases.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed five cases of Pseudomonas aeruginosa ventricular assist device (LVAD) infections treated with phage therapy, but all treatments were unsuccessful. Key findings included variable phage susceptibility, serum neutralization of phages, and emergence of bacterial isolates with reduced phage susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical cases, phage susceptibility testing, bacterial isolate sequencing, and evaluation of phage-antibiotic synergy.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial insights into alternariol and its derivative alternariol monomethyl ether produced by a marine fungus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies alternariol (AOH) and alternariol monomethyl ether (AME) as potent antibacterial compounds produced by the marine fungus Alternaria alternata FB1, demonstrating their ability to inhibit methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Vibrio anguillarum through disruption of cell division and membrane integrity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized purification, structural analysis, and in vitro and in vivo assays to evaluate the antibacterial properties of AOH and AME, along with transcriptomic and morphological analyses to elucidate their mechanisms of action.

full_output.paper_title: Murepavadin promotes the killing efficacies of aminoglycoside antibiotics against Pseudomonas aeruginosa by enhancing membrane potential.
full_output.key_findings: Murepavadin enhances the bactericidal effects of tobramycin and amikacin against Pseudomonas aeruginosa by increasing membrane potential and promoting intracellular uptake of aminoglycoside antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Experimental evaluation of murepavadin's effect on Pseudomonas aeruginosa, including membrane potential measurements, antibiotic uptake assays, and in vivo mouse pneumonia model.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the role of two-component systems (TCSs) in virulence regulation of Staphylococcus aureus, revealing their complex interactions and regulatory networks. It identifies specific TCSs and their impact on various virulence factors such as biofilm formation, hemolysis, and protein A production.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized transposon mutants of TCS components and analyzed their effects on virulence determinants through various assays, including biofilm formation, hemolysis, and protein A production.

full_output.paper_title: SP-CHAP, an endolysin with enhanced activity against biofilm pneumococci and nasopharyngeal colonization.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes SP-CHAP, a novel endolysin with enhanced activity against Streptococcus pneumoniae, including biofilm pneumococci and nasopharyngeal colonization. SP-CHAP shows higher lytic activity than Cpl-1 and effectively reduces biofilm biomass and nasopharyngeal colonization without toxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study involves cloning, expression, purification, and biochemical characterization of SP-CHAP, along with evaluating its antimicrobial activity through various assays including turbidity reduction, colony-forming unit, minimum inhibitory concentration, and biofilm disruption assays.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Epilancin A37 Production and Its Mode of Action Against Corynebacteria
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the lantibiotic epilancin A37 produced by Staphylococcus epidermidis A37, highlighting its potent antibacterial activity against corynebacteria and its unique mode of action involving cytoplasmic localization and intracellular vesicle formation without membrane disruption.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics, microbiological assays, biophysical analyses, and microscopic techniques including cryo-electron tomography were employed to investigate the mode of action of A37.

full_output.paper_title: Development and Evaluation of Novel Polymyxin Analogues with Enhanced Properties
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the development of polymyxin antibiotics and their toxicity, focusing on recent advancements in creating analogues with reduced nephrotoxicity while maintaining antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews recent research on polymyxin antibiotics, including structural modifications and evaluations of their antibacterial activity and toxicity.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence genes, antimicrobial resistance profile, phylotyping and pathotyping of diarrheagenic Escherichia coli isolated from children in Southwest Mexico.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various virulence genes associated with diarrheagenic Escherichia coli (DEC) strains isolated from children in Southwest Mexico, highlighting the prevalence of aEPEC and the association of specific genes with different pathotypes and clinical outcomes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to identify DEC pathotypes and assess antibiotic resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Serotype distribution and antimicrobial resistance of pediatric Streptococcus pneumoniae isolated from inpatients and outpatients at Beijing Children's Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates from both inpatients and outpatients, particularly against penicillin, cefuroxime, imipenem, erythromycin, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Serotypes 19F, 19A, 23F, and 6A were prevalent, and multidrug-resistant isolates were common.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using E-test and disk diffusion methods, and serotyping was done with diagnostic pneumococcal antisera.

full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the application of CRISPRi and CRISPRa technologies in studying multidrug resistance (MDR) and biofilm formation in various bacterial and fungal pathogens. It highlights the use of these tools to identify and validate essential genes involved in MDR mechanisms, such as efflux pumps, resistance genes, and regulatory pathways. The study emphasizes the importance of CRISPRi in overcoming challenges posed by essential genes and in developing targeted therapies against MDR pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The paper discusses the use of CRISPRi and CRISPRa technologies for gene silencing and activation, along with experimental validations through CRISPRi-mediated silencing and functional assays.

full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews alternative therapies for treating drug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae, focusing on antimicrobial peptides, fatty acids, and nano-formulations. It highlights the potential of monocaprin, Bald's eyesalve, alpha-linolenic acid, chitosan nanoparticles, silver nanoparticles, and nano-mupirocin as effective agents against N. gonorrhoeae.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Features and Treatment Outcomes of Carbapenem-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Keratitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the carbapenemase-resistance genes blaVIM80 and blaGES9 in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa keratitis, highlighting their role in carbapenem resistance and the challenges in treating these infections.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing and PCR were used to identify carbapenemase-resistance genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and molecular characterization of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from neonatal intensive care units in General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University, China, 2017-2021.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaNDM-5 as the most prevalent carbapenem resistance gene in CRKP isolates, along with other beta-lactamase genes such as blaSHV, blaOXA-48, blaTEM, blaIMP, and blaVIM. A hypervirulent ST23 CRKP strain (KP-63) was characterized, showing high similarity to known virulence plasmids and possessing multiple virulence genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and whole-genome sequencing were used to characterize CRKP isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting host deoxycytidine kinase mitigates Staphylococcus aureus abscess formation.
full_output.key_findings: (R)-DI-87, a deoxycytidine kinase (dCK) inhibitor, mitigates Staphylococcus aureus abscess formation by protecting phagocytes from death-effector deoxyribonucleosides.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo experiments using tissue culture models, flow cytometry, and mouse infection models.

full_output.paper_title: The ABC toxin complex from Yersinia entomophaga can package three different cytotoxic components expressed from distinct genetic loci in an unfolded state: the structures of both shell and cargo.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the YenC3 protein from Yersinia entomophaga, which forms a complex with YenB and is capable of encapsulating its C-terminal cargo. Structural analysis reveals that YenC3 CTD is encapsulated in an unfolded state within the shell formed by YenB and YenC3 NTD.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis using X-ray crystallography and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), along with biochemical assays and mass spectrometry.

full_output.paper_title: Investigating the cause of increased tetracycline-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae in England, 2016-20.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a significant increase in tetracycline resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, especially among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM), correlating with increased bacterial STI tests and antimicrobial treatment. The resistance was primarily low-level chromosomally mediated.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed national surveillance data from three large sexual health services in London, examining correlations between bacterial STI tests, antimicrobial treatment, and tetracycline resistance in N. gonorrhoeae.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome sequencing and molecular epidemiology of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolated from patients with bacteraemia in Slovenia.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the molecular epidemiology of 82 MRSA strains from Slovenia, identifying various resistance genes such as blaZ, ermA, aadD, ant(9)-Ia, ant(6)-Ia, and aph(3')-III, which confer resistance to penicillin, erythromycin, clindamycin, and gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and molecular epidemiology of MRSA strains.

ETP-mono-resistant CRE strains showed lower carbapenemase positivity and higher susceptibility to certain antibiotics compared to MEM/IPM-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and phenotypic detection of carbapenemase production were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms in CRE strains.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the potential of bis(thiazol-5-yl)phenylmethane derivatives as novel candidates against genetically defined multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates bis(thiazol-5-yl)phenylmethane derivatives against multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, identifying compounds 23a and 28b as having strong antibacterial activity. These compounds show selective activity against S. aureus, with 23a and 28b demonstrating near MIC bactericidal activity against genetically defined resistant strains. Computational modeling suggests that these compounds may target the MurC ligase of S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution to determine MIC and MBC, molecular docking to predict interactions with S. aureus proteins, and biofilm integrity assays to assess effectiveness against biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Supercharged precision killers: Genetically engineered biomimetic drugs of screened metalloantibiotics against Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Zn(Bq)2 as a highly effective metal complex against multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, demonstrating strong antibacterial activity with low minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and no resistance development after 30 passages. The Zn(Bq)2 complex was combined with Ce6 and ZIF-8 to create a nanodrug (ZnBq/Ce6@ZIF-8@OMV) that shows exceptional antibacterial efficacy, including the eradication of biofilms and meningitis infections.
full_output.methodology: The study involved screening FDA-approved antimicrobial compounds, evaluating the antibacterial efficacy of Zn(Bq)2, characterizing the synthesized nanodrug ZnBq/Ce6@ZIF-8@OMV, and conducting in vitro and in vivo tests to assess its antibacterial properties and effectiveness against A. baumannii infections.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis transmission in Shandong, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several drug-resistant mutations in MDR-TB isolates in Shandong, including katG S315T (INH), rpoB S450L (RIF), embB M306V (EMB), pncA-11T > C (PZA), rpsL K43R (SM), gyrA A90V and D94G (FQs), rrs A1401G (SLID), fabG1-15C > T (ETO), and thyA H75N (PAS). These mutations were associated with clustering and transmission of MDR-TB in the region.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing was used to identify drug-resistant mutations and analyze the transmission patterns of MDR-TB isolates in Shandong, China.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in the efflux pump regulator MexZ shift tissue colonization by Pseudomonas aeruginosa to a state of antibiotic tolerance.

mexZ.encodes: negative regulator of the expression of the mexXY efflux pump genes

mutations_found.validated_by: construction of a loss-of-function mutant in mexZ and analysis of its infection behavior

mexZ.notes: The mutation in mexZ leads to overexpression of the MexXY-OprM efflux pump, which contributes to antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in mexZ, which encode a negative regulator of the mexXY efflux pump genes, lead to a shift in tissue colonization by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, resulting in increased protection from antibiotics. This is due to the overexpression of the MexXY-OprM efflux pump and alterations in quorum sensing signaling.
full_output.methodology: Construction of a loss-of-function mutant in mexZ, transcriptomic analysis, and evaluation of infection behavior in an airway epithelium model.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of non-aureus staphylococci and Mammaliicoccus from Hipposideros bats in Southwest Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mecA, SalA, and qacE as antibiotic resistance genes in Mammaliicoccus sciuri and Staphylococcus gallinarum isolates from Hipposideros bats in Nigeria, highlighting the potential for these bacteria to act as reservoirs of resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize antibiotic resistance genes in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Fluorescent reporters give new insights into antibiotics-induced nonsense and frameshift mistranslation.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed dual-fluorescent mistranslation reporters to analyze antibiotic-induced mistranslation in E. coli, revealing that amikacin increases stop-codon readthrough and azithromycin induces both frameshifting and stop-codon readthrough, highlighting the complex effects of antibiotics on translational fidelity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized dual-fluorescent reporters (GFP and mScarlet-I) to monitor mistranslation in E. coli under various antibiotic treatments, employing flow cytometry and microscopy for analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid detection of major enterotoxin genes and antibiotic resistance of Staphylococcus aureus isolated from raw milk in the Yazd province, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of multiple enterotoxin genes (sea, sed, seg, sei, sej) and antibiotic resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from raw milk in Yazd province, Iran. All isolates showed 100% resistance to penicillin G, with variable resistance to other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR and Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method were used for detection of enterotoxin genes and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of Pasteurella multocida in cats, characterized its capsular and LPS types, and detected various virulence-associated genes. It also found that most isolates were resistant to ampicillin, clindamycin, lincomycin, streptomycin, and penicillin.
full_output.methodology: The study used biochemical tests, PCR, and disk diffusion to characterize P. multocida isolates from cats, identify capsular and LPS types, detect virulence genes, and assess antibiotic sensitivity.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro and in silico studies of enterobactin-inspired Ciprofloxacin and Fosfomycin first generation conjugates on the antibiotic resistant E. coli OQ866153.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effectiveness of enterobactin-conjugated Ciprofloxacin and Fosfomycin against antibiotic-resistant E. coli OQ866153. The conjugates showed strong antibacterial activity, with Fe+3-enterobactin-Ciprofloxacin having a MIC of 31.25 µg/ml and Fe+3-enterobactin-Fosfomycin having a MIC of 500 µg/ml. The conjugates inhibited DNA gyrase and biofilm formation, demonstrating enhanced efficacy compared to the individual antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA-gyrase inhibition assay, antibiofilm quantitative assay, and molecular docking studies.
