full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity of the antimicrobial peptide PMAP-36 in combination with tetracycline against porcine extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli in vitro and in vivo.

tetB.validation_method: quantitative RT-PCR showing PMAP-36 inhibited tetB transcription

full_output.key_findings: PMAP-36 inhibited the transcription of the tetracycline resistance gene tetB, reducing tetracycline resistance in porcine ExPEC PCN033.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative RT-PCR to assess tetB gene expression and in vitro synergy assays with PMAP-36 and tetracycline.

full_output.paper_title: APLF facilitates interstrand DNA crosslink repair and replication fork protection to confer cisplatin resistance.
full_output.key_findings: APLF is involved in interstrand DNA crosslink repair and fork protection, contributing to cisplatin resistance in cancer cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular biology techniques including immunofluorescence microscopy, Western blotting, and siRNA knockdown to investigate the role of APLF in cisplatin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: High-throughput screening of small-molecules libraries identified antibacterials against clinically relevant multidrug-resistant A. baumannii and K. pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 72 compounds with activity against multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae and A. baumannii, including three compounds (GARDP0021789, GARDP0015589, and GARDP0016418) showing potent activity against XDR A. baumannii. The paper characterizes the resistance mechanisms of the strains used, including the presence of blaOXA-23, armA, and blaKPC-3 genes.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput phenotypic screening of compound libraries against multidrug-resistant bacterial strains, followed by dose-response experiments and genomic analysis to validate resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: A genetic screen identifies a role for oprF in Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm stimulation by subinhibitory antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies oprF, dsbA, PA2200, and sigX as crucial genes involved in sub-MIC antibiotic-induced biofilm stimulation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis screen, mutant analysis, and complementation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-mediated phenotypic noise leads to transient antibiotic resistance in bacteria.

blaTEM-1.validation_method: expression in E. coli and fluorescence measurements

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaTEM-1 as a gene that contributes to transient antibiotic resistance via plasmid copy number variability, demonstrating that plasmid-mediated phenotypic noise enhances bacterial survival under antibiotic stress.
full_output.methodology: Computational modeling combined with single-cell and population-level experiments using E. coli MG1655 with plasmid pBGT carrying blaTEM-1.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant conjugative plasmid carrying mphA confers increased antimicrobial resistance in Shigella.

mphA.evidence_note: The mphA gene was found to be the key macrolide resistance factor in Shigella, and it was confirmed in transconjugants and their plasmid DNAs by PCR.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mphA gene as a key factor in macrolide resistance in Shigella, carried on a conjugative plasmid, leading to increased resistance to azithromycin.
full_output.methodology: PCR, plasmid transfer, and whole genome sequencing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic, functional, and metabolic enhancements in multidrug-resistant Enterobacter bugandensis facilitating its persistence and succession in the International Space Station.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple antibiotic resistance genes in multidrug-resistant Enterobacter bugandensis strains isolated from the International Space Station, highlighting their potential to persist and succeed in extreme environments.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, metagenomic sequencing, and functional annotation were used to characterize resistance mechanisms in E. bugandensis.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and hemocompatibility potentials of nano-gold-cored alginate preparation against anaerobic bacteria from acne vulgaris.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial activity of gold/alginate nanoparticles (GANPs) against anaerobic bacteria isolated from acne patients, including Clostridium innocuum, Lactobacillus plantarum, Peptoniphilus asaccharolyticus, and Anaerococcus prevotii. GANPs showed significant inhibitory effects against these bacteria, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) ranging from 200 to 400 µg/ml. Additionally, GANPs exhibited hemocompatibility, suggesting potential as an antibacterial agent for acne.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar well diffusion and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) assays to evaluate the antibacterial activity of GANPs against anaerobic bacteria isolated from acne patients. Hemocompatibility was assessed by examining the effects of GANPs on human blood parameters.

full_output.paper_title: A comparative study of genotyping and antimicrobial resistance between carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii isolates at a tertiary pediatric hospital in China.

blaVIM.evidence_note: blaVIM was detected in all 48 CRAB isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenemase genes bla KPC, bla IMP, bla NDM in CRKP isolates and bla VIM, bla OXA-23, bla OXA-51 in CRAB isolates, highlighting differences in resistance mechanisms between the two pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping using REP-PCR and detection of carbapenemase genes via singleplex PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a Straboviridae phage vB_AbaM-SHI and its inhibition effect on biofilms of Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the phage vB_AbaM-SHI, which exhibits bacteriolytic activity against Acinetobacter baumannii, including strains with antibiotic resistance. The phage's endolysin has unique structural features, including two additional β-strands due to an amino acid substitution at position 21 (lysine replaced by arginine).
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, genomic sequencing, endolysin structure analysis, and bacteriolytic activity assessment via spot tests and biofilm inhibition experiments.

full_output.paper_title: The Prevalence, Risk Factors, and Antimicrobial Resistance Determinants of Helicobacter pylori Detected in Dyspeptic Patients in North-Central Bangladesh.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several mutations associated with antimicrobial resistance in Helicobacter pylori, including A2147G in 23S rRNA (clarithromycin resistance), T556S in PBP-1A (amoxicillin resistance), N87K and D91N in GyrA (levofloxacin resistance), and a 200 bp deletion in rdxA (metronidazole resistance).
full_output.methodology: PCR, Sanger sequencing, and PCR-RFLP were used to detect and characterize antimicrobial resistance mutations in H. pylori.

full_output.paper_title: Role of amino acid 159 in carbapenem and temocillin hydrolysis of OXA-933, a novel OXA-48 variant.

blaOXA-933.validation_method: expression in E. coli and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes OXA-933, a novel OXA-48 variant with a D159N mutation, which exhibits reduced carbapenem and temocillin hydrolysis compared to OXA-48.
full_output.methodology: Expression of OXA-933 in E. coli, MIC testing, and kinetic parameter analysis.

full_output.paper_title: A One Health Perspective on Salmonella enterica Serovar Infantis, an Emerging Human Multidrug-Resistant Pathogen.

aadA1.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and AMR determinant screening

sul1.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and AMR determinant screening

tetA.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and AMR determinant screening

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica serovar Infantis, particularly in poultry and poultry products, with significant associations between the presence of the pESI plasmid and resistance to multiple antimicrobial classes including aminoglycosides, sulfonamides, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and AMR determinant screening using ARIBA tool with resfinder and plasmidfinder databases.

full_output.paper_title: Infection and antibiotic-associated changes in the fecal microbiota of C. rodentium ϕstx2(dact)-infected C57BL/6 mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the impact of C. rodentium ϕstx2dact infection and antibiotic treatment on the fecal microbiota of C57BL/6 mice, highlighting significant changes in microbial community structure and diversity, particularly with antibiotic treatments.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA gene sequencing to analyze the fecal microbiota composition in mice infected with C. rodentium ϕstx2dact and treated with various antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: When the Trojan horse is unable to reach inside the city: investigation of the mechanism of resistance behind the first reported cefiderocol-resistant E. coli in Canada.

blaNDM-5.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

cirA.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

mutations_found.validated_by: whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the first cefiderocol-resistant E. coli isolate in Canada, highlighting the role of blaNDM-5, PBP3, and cirA mutations in resistance. The NDM-5 region, along with PBP3 and cirA mutations, is associated with cefiderocol resistance, although the exact mechanism remains unclear.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and analysis of plasmid content.

full_output.paper_title: A simple solid media assay for detection of synergy between bacteriophages and antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study develops a solid media assay to detect synergistic interactions between bacteriophages and antibiotics, demonstrating that such interactions can enhance the effectiveness of antibiotics against vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE) and other antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a solid media assay to evaluate the synergistic effects of bacteriophages and antibiotics against various bacterial isolates, including VRE and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Lasso Peptide Cloacaenodin Utilizes a Unique TonB-Dependent Transporter to Access Susceptible Bacteria.

cloU.mechanism: mediates outer membrane uptake of cloacaenodin
cloU.validation_method: genetic knockout and complementation, heterologous expression, spot-on-lawn assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cloU as a novel TonB-dependent transporter responsible for cloacaenodin uptake in susceptible Enterobacter strains. CloU enables cloacaenodin to cross the outer membrane, and its absence or mutation leads to resistance. The transporter is specific to certain Enterobacter species and is critical for the antimicrobial activity of cloacaenodin.
full_output.methodology: Genetic knockout and complementation, heterologous expression, spot-on-lawn assays, molecular dynamics simulations, and bioinformatics analyses.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro investigation of relationship between quorum-sensing system genes, biofilm forming ability, and drug resistance in clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates. It found a significant correlation between quorum-sensing (QS) genes (rhlI, rhlR, lasI, lasR) and biofilm formation as well as drug resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR to detect QS genes and evaluated biofilm formation via microtiter plate assay. Antimicrobial susceptibility was tested using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: LysSYL: a broad-spectrum phage endolysin targeting Staphylococcus species and eradicating S. aureus biofilms.

LysSYL.validation_method: expression in E. coli and lytic activity assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LysSYL, a broad-spectrum phage endolysin that effectively targets Staphylococcus species, including MRSA, and demonstrates potent antibacterial activity against biofilms and persisters.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, endolysin cloning, expression, purification, and assessment of lytic activity against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Phenotypic Antibiotics Susceptibility Analysis by a 3D Printed Prototype.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a rapid phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing method using a 3D-printed microfluidic device with electrochemical detection, achieving high sensitivity and specificity for detecting resistance to kanamycin and oxytetracycline in clinically relevant bacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a 3D-printed microfluidic device with screen-printed electrodes (SPEs) for electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and differential pulsed voltammetry (DPV) to detect bacterial growth and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteria-Targeting Nanoparticles with ROS-Responsive Antibiotic Release to Eradicate Biofilms and Drug-Resistant Bacteria in Endophthalmitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel ROS-responsive nanoparticle system (MXF@UiO-UBI-PEGTK) designed for targeted antibiotic release to combat bacterial biofilms and drug-resistant bacteria in endophthalmitis. The system shows improved antibacterial efficacy, especially in the presence of reactive oxygen species (ROS), and effectively targets and eradicates biofilms formed by Staphylococcus aureus, methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized transmission electron microscopy (TEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and in vitro and in vivo antibacterial assays to characterize the nanoparticle system and evaluate its effectiveness against bacterial biofilms and drug-resistant strains.

full_output.paper_title: Spectrum and antibiotic sensitivity of bacterial keratitis: a retrospective analysis of eight years in a Tertiary Referral Hospital in Southwest China.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the antibiotic susceptibility of bacterial keratitis isolates, highlighting high sensitivity of Gram-positive bacteria to linezolid, vancomycin, tigecycline, quinupristin/dalfopristin, and rifampin, while Gram-negative bacteria showed high sensitivity to cefoperazone sodium/sulbactam, piperacillin/tazobactam, meropenem, amikacin, ceftazidime, and cefepime.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 660 bacterial keratitis cases with microbiological culture and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Target enrichment improves culture-independent detection of Neisseria gonorrhoeae and antimicrobial resistance determinants direct from clinical samples with Nanopore sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that target enrichment improves the detection of Neisseria gonorrhoeae and antimicrobial resistance determinants in clinical samples using Nanopore sequencing. It identifies blaTEM-1 as a beta-lactamase gene and detects gyrA mutations (S91F, D95G) associated with quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Nanopore sequencing with target enrichment using custom probes, followed by bioinformatics analysis to detect AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Altered PBP4 and GdpP functions synergistically mediate MRSA-like high-level, broad-spectrum β-lactam resistance in Staphylococcus aureus.

pbp4.mechanism: mutated pbp4 leads to increased cell wall cross-linking, reducing susceptibility to β-lactams
pbp4.validation_method: MIC assay, Bocillin assay, population assay

gdpP.mechanism: loss-of-function mutations in gdpP lead to increased cyclic-di-AMP (CDA) levels, promoting β-lactam tolerance
gdpP.validation_method: MIC assay, CDA measurement, population assay

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in pbp4 and gdpP synergistically mediate high-level, broad-spectrum β-lactam resistance in Staphylococcus aureus, similar to MRSA.
full_output.methodology: MIC assay, Bocillin assay, population assay, CDA measurement, and in vivo C. elegans infection assays.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of clumpy adhesion of Escherichia coli to human cells and associated factors influencing antibiotic sensitivity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes involved in clumpy adhesion of E. coli and their effects on antibiotic resistance. Deletion of flgH reduces adhesion and motility, while deletion of ffp and spnT increases resistance to ampicillin. Deletion of yggT increases susceptibility to gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic and proteomic analysis, gene deletion mutants, complementation, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Aminoglycoside resistance genes in early members of the Acinetobacter baumannii ST78A (SMAL, Italian clone) reside in an IS26-bounded island in the chromosome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three aminoglycoside resistance genes (aadB, aphA1, and aac(6')-Ian) in the early ST78A isolate SMAL2002, along with sul2 and floR, located in an IS26-bounded chromosomal resistance island.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR, and disc diffusion assays were used to analyze the resistance genes and mechanisms in SMAL2002.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the diversity of type IV secretion system-encoding plasmids in Acinetobacter.

blaOXA-23.validation_method: resistance gene identification via CARD and ResFinder

blaOXA-82.validation_method: resistance gene identification via CARD and ResFinder

blaGES-11.validation_method: resistance gene identification via CARD and ResFinder

aadA2.validation_method: resistance gene identification via CARD and ResFinder

sul1.validation_method: resistance gene identification via CARD and ResFinder

cmlA1.validation_method: resistance gene identification via CARD and ResFinder

qacEΔ1.validation_method: resistance gene identification via CARD and ResFinder

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the diversity of T4SS-encoding plasmids in Acinetobacter, identifying various antibiotic resistance genes such as blaOXA-23, blaOXA-82, blaGES-11, aph(3')-VIa, aadA2, sul1, dfrA7, cmlA1, and qacEΔ1, highlighting their role in multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized bioinformatic analyses, including blastn, CARD, and ResFinder, along with conjugation assays and PCR to identify and characterize resistance genes in T4SS-encoding plasmids.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance burden pre and post-COVID-19 pandemic with mapping the multidrug resistance in Egypt: a comparative cross-sectional study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a significant increase in antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in K. pneumoniae, A. baumannii, E. coli, and MRSA post-COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt, with notable increases in multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains.
full_output.methodology: A multicenter cross-sectional study analyzing culture results from 2430 isolates across 16 governorates in Egypt, comparing pre- and post-COVID-19 AMR patterns.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies natural products that inhibit the glycosyltransferase MurG in Escherichia coli, focusing on their binding affinities and interactions with the enzyme's active site.
full_output.methodology: In silico methods including virtual screening, molecular docking, ADMET prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze potential inhibitors of MurG.

full_output.paper_title: Repurposing fusidic acid as an antimicrobial against enterococci with a low probability of resistance development.

fusA.notes: Only one mutation (M651I) was detected in the fus A gene of the resistant strain derived from serial passage of E. faecium ATCC 27270.

full_output.key_findings: Fusidic acid (FA) showed effective antimicrobial activity against enterococci, including vancomycin-resistant strains, with a low probability of resistance development. A single mutation (M651I) in the fusA gene was identified in a resistant strain after serial passage.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, in vivo infection model, and genetic sequencing were used to evaluate FA's efficacy and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Redirecting pantoprazole as a metallo-beta-lactamase inhibitor in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: Pantoprazole was identified as a novel inhibitor of metallo-beta-lactamases (MBLs) in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, demonstrating significant inhibition of bla NDM and bla VIM gene expression and carbapenemase activity.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR, disk diffusion, and in silico docking studies were used to evaluate the effect of pantoprazole on MBLs and carbapenem resistance.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of omadacycline against clinical isolates of Nocardia.
full_output.key_findings: Omadacycline showed varying in vitro activity against different Nocardia species, with the highest activity against N. paucivorans, N. asiatica, N. abscessus complex, N. beijingensis, and N. otitidiscaviarum, and the lowest activity against N. farcinica.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using broth microdilution against 300 Nocardia clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the links between SOS response, mutagenesis, and resistance during the recovery period.

recA.notes: The study focuses on the role of RecA in SOS response and mutagenesis, but no specific mutations in recA are mentioned.

full_output.methodology: The study uses E. coli strains with reporter plasmids, UV exposure experiments, and various inhibitors to analyze the SOS response and mutagenesis.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance begets more resistance: chromosomal resistance mutations mitigate fitness costs conferred by multi-resistant clinical plasmids.
full_output.key_findings: Chromosomal resistance mutations in E. coli (nfsAB deletion, gyrA S83L, rpsL K42N) mitigate the fitness costs of multi-resistant clinical plasmids, allowing resistant strains to outcompete susceptible strains in the absence of antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Conjugation of clinical plasmids into E. coli strains with chromosomal resistance mutations followed by growth rate and competition experiments.

full_output.paper_title: The functional small RNA interactome reveals targets for the vancomycin-responsive sRNA RsaOI in vancomycin-tolerant Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies RsaOI as a vancomycin-responsive sRNA that post-transcriptionally represses the translation of mRNAs involved in carbon metabolism and cell wall turnover, contributing to vancomycin tolerance in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Used RNase III-CLASH to capture sRNA-mRNA interactions, combined with RNA-seq, Ribo-seq, and proteomics data to analyze post-transcriptional regulation.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting intracellular nontuberculous mycobacteria and M. tuberculosis with a bactericidal enzymatic cocktail.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces EC1, a bactericidal enzymatic cocktail composed of LysA, LysB, alpha-amylase, and isoamylase, which effectively kills various mycobacterial species including NTM and M. tuberculosis by degrading the mycobacterial envelope. EC1 demonstrates synergistic effects with standard-of-care antibiotics and protects macrophages from necrotic death.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in silico analysis, protein expression screening, and in vitro experiments to evaluate the bactericidal effects of EC1 against mycobacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Community Emergence of Cefixime-Resistant Escherichia coli Belonging to ST12 with Chromosomal AmpC Hyperproduction.

full_output.paper_title: Assessing the Microbial Quality of Shrimp (Xiphonaeus kroyeri) and Mussels (Perna perna) Illegally Sold in the Vitória Region, Brazil, and Investigating the Antimicrobial Resistance of Escherichia coli Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: None of the 10 E. coli isolates carried genes associated with antibiotic resistance such as blaCTX-M-1, blaCTX-M-2, blaCTX-M-3, blaCTX-M-15, mcr-1, mcr-2, mcr-3, mcr-4, and tet. full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Microevolution and Co-Selection Assessment of Amoxicillin and Cefotaxime Impact on Escherichia coli Resistance Development.

full_output.paper_title: Generation and Characterization of Stable Small Colony Variants of USA300 Staphylococcus aureus in RAW 264.7 Murine Macrophages.

full_output.paper_title: Importance of the Aspergillus fumigatus Mismatch Repair Protein Msh6 in Antifungal Resistance Development.

full_output.paper_title: New Frontier on Antimicrobial Therapy: Long-Acting Lipoglycopeptides.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the use of long-acting lipoglycopeptides (LGPs) such as dalbavancin and oritavancin for treating various bacterial infections, highlighting their effectiveness against Gram-positive pathogens and their potential as alternatives to conventional antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Insights into Staphylococcus aureus Isolates Exhibiting Diminished Daptomycin Susceptibility.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in mprF, rpoB, cls1, cls2, and fakA genes associated with diminished daptomycin susceptibility in Staphylococcus aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular detection of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli from bat caves on Lombok Island.

full_output.paper_title: Hygienic status of beef butcher shop facilities and antibiotic resistance profile of Salmonella enterica in Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 16.7% of beef carcasses from butcher shops in Ethiopia were contaminated with Salmonella enterica, and only 20% of the isolates were resistant to ampicillin and tetracycline. The majority of the isolates were susceptible to 11 antimicrobials tested.
full_output.methodology: The study used microbiological analysis, including qPCR for Salmonella identification and disk diffusion assays for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Engineering a nanoantibiotic system displaying dual mechanism of action.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a nanoantibiotic system combining a disruptor of cylindrical proteases (LJC) and a nanocarrier that damages bacterial membranes, demonstrating improved antimicrobial efficacy through dual mechanisms of action.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of computational modeling, morphological analysis, and antimicrobial activity evaluations to characterize the nanoantibiotic system.

full_output.paper_title: Episymbiotic Saccharibacteria TM7x modulates the susceptibility of its host bacteria to phage infection and promotes their coexistence.
full_output.key_findings: TM7x induces downregulation of a CWP gene cluster in XH001, reducing phage binding and resistance. Overexpression of the CWP cluster restores phage sensitivity, demonstrating its role in phage interaction.
full_output.methodology: RNA-Seq, qRT-PCR, phage adsorption assays, and fluorescent microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Pyrrole-based inhibitors of RND-type efflux pumps reverse antibiotic resistance and display anti-virulence potential.

MexAB-OprM.mechanism: efflux pump overexpression leads to reduced susceptibility to antibiotics
MexAB-OprM.validation_method: MIC determination and efflux pump inhibition assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pyrrole-based compounds that inhibit RND-type efflux pumps, reversing antibiotic resistance and demonstrating anti-virulence properties in E. coli and P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and screening of pyrrole derivatives, checkerboard broth microdilution assay, molecular docking, biophysical studies, and in vivo models.

full_output.paper_title: Engineering strategies and challenges of endolysin as an antibacterial agent against Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews engineering strategies for endolysins to target Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting several endolysins with extracellular activity against various Gram-negative pathogens.
full_output.methodology: In vitro testing of endolysins against different bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Salmonella Typhimurium employs spermidine to exert protection against ROS-mediated cytotoxicity and rewires host polyamine metabolism to ameliorate its survival in macrophages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies GspSA, a novel antioxidative enzyme in Salmonella Typhimurium, regulated by spermidine, which protects against oxidative damage. Mutants lacking spermidine transport (STM ΔpotCD) or biosynthesis (STM ΔspeED) show reduced survival in macrophages and increased ROS levels.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockout, intracellular survival assays, and redox status determination.

full_output.paper_title: A folate inhibitor exploits metabolic differences in Pseudomonas aeruginosa for narrow-spectrum targeting.
full_output.key_findings: Fluorofolin is a dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) inhibitor that effectively targets Pseudomonas aeruginosa, showing potent activity against various clinical isolates. Resistance to fluorofolin can emerge through mutations in nfxB and mexS, which lead to overexpression of efflux pumps and reduced virulence.
full_output.methodology: The study involved in vitro assays, metabolomics, molecular docking, and in vivo mouse infection models to evaluate the mechanism and efficacy of fluorofolin against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.sample_size: Clinical isolates from CDC and FDA Antibiotic Resistant P. aeruginosa Isolate Bank and 22 clinical isolates from blood stream infections.

full_output.paper_title: Serotype diversity and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae isolated in Italian pig farms from 2015 to 2022.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed 572 Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae (APP) isolates from Italian pig farms, revealing serotype diversity and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) patterns. Key findings include high resistance rates to tetracycline (53%) and ampicillin (33%), with notable associations between serotypes and resistance profiles, such as serotype 9/11 showing strong resistance to florfenicol and enrofloxacin and the highest multidrug resistance (MDR) proportions.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the microdilution method, and serotyping was done via molecular methods including multiplex PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence and genomic chion of Proteus mirabilis harboring bla(NDM-1) in Korean companion dogs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the first carbapenemase-producing Proteus mirabilis isolate from a companion dog in South Korea, highlighting the presence of 20 different antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes, including 2 tandem copies of bla(NDM-1), contributing to multidrug resistance (MDR).
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and MIC testing were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes in the isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-Wide Investigation Reveals Potential Therapeutic Targets in Shigella spp.

tolC.validation_method: protein-protein interaction analysis and network clustering

mdtA.validation_method: protein-protein interaction analysis and network clustering

gyrA.validation_method: protein-protein interaction analysis and network clustering

full_output.key_findings: The study identified four hub proteins (tolC, acrR, mdtA, and gyrA) in Shigella spp. that are associated with antibiotic resistance mechanisms, primarily efflux pumps and target alterations. These proteins are potential therapeutic targets for combating multidrug-resistant Shigella strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify antibiotic resistance genes and their mechanisms in Shigella spp.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance of avian pathogenic Escherichia coli isolated from broiler, layer, and breeder chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) isolates from commercial chickens in Nepal, including blaTEM, sul1, qnrA, tetB, cat1, ereA, mcr1, and aac(3)-IV, which confer resistance to various antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, multiplex PCR, and statistical analysis were used to detect and characterize antibiotic resistance genes in APEC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Sub-MIC Ciprofloxacin Treatment Led to Substantial Changes at Multiple Omics Levels Without Affecting the Growth Rate
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various genes involved in the SOS response in E. coli K-12 MG1655 following sub-MIC ciprofloxacin treatment, highlighting their roles in DNA repair and stress response mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Longitudinal multi-omics analysis combining transcriptomics, signalomics, and metabolomics to investigate the SOS response in E. coli K-12 MG1655 after ciprofloxacin treatment.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bacterial isolates from primary endodontic infections and assessed their antimicrobial susceptibility. Some Enterococcus isolates showed resistance to erythromycin, ciprofloxacin, and tetracycline, while a Staphylococcus epidermidis isolate was multidrug-resistant. Five Streptococcus isolates were non-susceptible to all antibiotics tested.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolates were identified using the Vitek 2 system, and antimicrobial susceptibility was tested using the disk diffusion method on Mueller-Hinton agar.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing of clinical isolates from tuberculosis patients in India: real-world data indicates a high proportion of pre-XDR cases.

rpoB.notes: Mutations in the rifampicin resistance-determining region (RRDR) of rpoB are responsible for rifampicin resistance.

katG.notes: The Ser315Thr mutation in katG is associated with isoniazid resistance.

embB.notes: Mutations in embB are associated with ethambutol resistance.

rpsL.notes: The Lys43Arg mutation in rpsL is associated with streptomycin resistance.

pncA.notes: Mutations in pncA are associated with pyrazinamide resistance.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA are associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.

ndh.notes: The Arg268His mutation in ndh is associated with isoniazid and ethambutol resistance.

rrs.notes: Mutations in rrs are associated with resistance to aminoglycosides.

eis.notes: Mutations in eis are associated with kanamycin resistance.

rplC.notes: The Cys154Arg mutation in rplC is associated with linezolid resistance.

atpE.notes: The Ala63Pro mutation in atpE is associated with bedaquiline resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high proportion of pre-XDR-TB cases and characterized mutations in genes such as rpoB, katG, embB, rpsL, pncA, gyrA, ndh, rrs, eis, rplC, atpE, and Rv0678 that confer resistance to various anti-TB drugs.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing was used to analyze drug resistance mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from 600 patients in India.

full_output.paper_title: Carbon starvation raises capacities in bacterial antibiotic resistance and viral auxiliary carbon metabolism in soils.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that carbon-poor soils had higher abundance of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), especially in low-abundance drug classes, suggesting increased microbial competition and potential spread of antibiotic resistance in chemical-fertilizer-based agriculture.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of soil samples from long-term fertilization experiments, including annotation of CAZyme and ARGs using databases like CAZy and CARD.
full_output.sample_size: Four long-term fixed fertilization experiments in China

full_output.paper_title: The proliferation of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and microbial communities in industrial wastewater treatment plant treating N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) by AAO process.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that the AAO process in industrial WWTPs acts as a microbial source increasing the total abundance of ARGs rather than reducing it. Certain ARGs such as aac(6')-II, aadA-1-01, aadA-1-02, blaIMP-01, blaPER, cmr, cmx(A), dfrA1, mexE, tnpA-03, MexF, tna-04, and qacEdelta1-02 were identified as prevalent in the influent and their abundance increased during the treatment process.
full_output.methodology: High throughput quantitative PCR (HT-qPCR) and 16S rRNA sequencing were used to analyze the abundance and distribution of ARGs and bacterial communities in wastewater samples collected from different stages of the AAO process.

full_output.paper_title: Contribution of the patient microbiome to surgical site infection and antibiotic prophylaxis failure in spine surgery.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 86% of surgical site infections (SSIs) originated from the patient's preoperative microbiome, and the preoperative resistome was associated with prophylaxis-resistant infections. Resistance phenotypes of SSI isolates correlated with the patient's preoperative resistome.
full_output.methodology: The study used genomic analysis, including 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing and metagenomic sequencing, to compare the preoperative microbiome and resistome with postoperative SSI isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic determinants of resistance to antimicrobial therapeutics are rare in publicly available Clostridioides difficile genome sequences.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several genetic determinants associated with reduced susceptibility to antimicrobial agents in Clostridioides difficile, including point mutations in rpoB, rpoC, marR, vanS, and vanR, as well as the plasmid pCD-METRO and the P nimB G promoter mutation. These findings highlight the rarity of antimicrobial resistance in C. difficile and emphasize the importance of updating resistance marker databases for accurate detection.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 26,557 C. difficile genome sequences using bioinformatics tools and experimental susceptibility testing to identify genetic determinants of resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Clarithromycin Resistance in Helicobacter pylori Using MmaxSure™ H. pylori & ClaR Assay.

full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, gene sequencing, and culture methods to evaluate the diagnostic performance of MmaxSure™ and DPO-PCR for detecting H. pylori and the A2143G mutation.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of genes related to the efflux pump and porin in multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli strains isolated from patients with COVID-19 after secondary infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the efflux pump genes acrA, acrB, and porin genes ompF and ompC as being significantly associated with resistance to various antibiotics in multidrug-resistant E. coli isolates from patients with secondary infections after COVID-19.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to characterize the efflux pump and porin genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Quenching of quorum sensing in multi-drug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa: insights on halo-bacterial metabolites and gamma irradiation as channels inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the effect of halo-bacterial metabolites and gamma irradiation on the virulence of multi-drug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa, focusing on the downregulation of quorum sensing systems (las/rhl) and the identification of quorum quenching compounds.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized real-time PCR to analyze gene expression, LC-ESI-MS/MS for metabolite characterization, and various biochemical assays to assess virulence factors.
full_output.sample_size: Four clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and five halophilic bacterial strains.

full_output.methodology: Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) and Xpert MTB/RIF assay were used for detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and antimicrobial resistance mutations in clinical isolates and sputum specimens.

full_output.paper_title: Difficult-to-treat (DTR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa harboring Verona-Integron metallo-β-lactamase (blaVIM): infection management and molecular analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaVIM-2 as a gene responsible for carbapenem resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, highlighting its role in difficult-to-treat infections and the need for targeted infection control measures.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery and Derivatization of Tridecaptin Antibiotics with Altered Host Specificity and Enhanced Bioactivity.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the discovery of new tridecaptin antibiotics, tridecaptin A 5 and tridecaptin D, with altered host specificity and enhanced bioactivity. A single amino acid substitution at position 9 from Phe to Trp in tridecaptin A 1 changes its bioactivity profile from Gram-negative to broad-spectrum activity. Tridecaptin D shows predominant activity against Gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Genome mining, bioinformatics analysis, chemical synthesis, and antimicrobial testing were used to identify and characterize the tridecaptin antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro anti-Helicobacter pylori activity and antivirulence activity of cetylpyridinium chloride.
full_output.key_findings: Cetylpyridinium chloride (CPC) exhibits significant in vitro activity against Helicobacter pylori, with MICs ranging from 0.16 to 0.62 μg/mL and MBCs ranging from 0.31 to 1.24 μg/mL. CPC reduces the expression of virulence genes (flaA, flaB, babA, alpA, alpB, ureE, ureF) and inhibits urease activity.
full_output.methodology: MIC and MBC assays, SEM, RT-qPCR, and urease activity measurements were used to assess CPC's effects on H. pylori.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid detection and molecular epidemiology of β-lactamase producing Enterobacteriaceae isolated from food animals and in-contact humans in Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed and validated a multiplex qPCR assay for detecting β-lactamase genes (bla CTX-M, bla TEM, and bla SHV) in Enterobacteriaceae isolated from food animals and in-contact humans in Nigeria. The assay showed 100% sensitivity and specificity. The prevalence of bla TEM and bla SHV varied among different species and sampling locations, with Klebsiella pneumoniae showing the highest prevalence of these genes.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex qPCR and whole genome sequencing were used to detect and characterize β-lactamase genes in Enterobacteriaceae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A protective role for type I interferon signaling following infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis carrying the rifampicin drug resistance-conferring RpoB mutation H445Y.

rpoB.notes: The rpoB H445Y mutation confers rifampicin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the rpoB H445Y mutation as a rifampicin resistance-conferring mutation in Mycobacterium tuberculosis and demonstrates that type I interferon signaling plays a protective role in the absence of IL-1 signaling during infection with this mutant strain.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, infection experiments, and flow cytometry analyses were used to investigate the role of type I interferon signaling in Mtb infection.

full_output.paper_title: A sophisticated virulence repertoire and colistin resistance of Citrobacter freundii ST150 from a patient with sepsis admitted to ICU in a tertiary care hospital in Uganda, East Africa: Insight from genomic and molecular docking analyses.
full_output.key_findings: Citrobacter freundii strain RSM030 was found to possess chromosomal beta-lactam resistance genes (blaCMY-79, blaCMY-116, blaTEM-1B) and polymyxin resistance genes (arnD, arnT, eptA, eptB) that confer resistance to multiple antibiotics, including colistin. Additionally, mutations in PmrA/PmrB, mgrB, and PhoP/PhoQ were associated with colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, ResFinder analysis, and manual search for resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Hypothiocyanous acid reductase is critical for host colonization and infection by Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Har, a hypothiocyanous acid reductase, as critical for the colonization and invasion of Streptococcus pneumoniae in mouse models. Deletion of har significantly reduced bacterial load in the nasopharynx and lungs, indicating its role in resisting hypothiocyanous acid (HOSCN) stress.
full_output.methodology: Mouse colonization and invasion models, enzymatic kinetic assays, and crystallography were used to analyze the role of Har in S. pneumoniae.
full_output.sample_size: Seven mice per strain for colonization model, eight mice per strain for invasion model

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and antibiofilm activity of halogenated phenylboronic acids against Vibrio parahaemolyticus and Vibrio harveyi.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that 3,5-diiodo-2-methoxyphenylboronic acid (DIMPBA) and 2-fluoro-5-iodophenylboronic acid (FIPBA) exhibited antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against Vibrio parahaemolyticus and Vibrio harveyi, reducing biofilm formation and virulence factors.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial and antibiofilm activity of 34 halogenated acids using MIC tests, biofilm inhibition assays, and live cell imaging.

full_output.paper_title: Silver Organometallics that are Highly Potent Thioredoxin and Glutathione Reductase Inhibitors: Exploring the Correlations of Solution Chemistry with the Strong Antibacterial Effects.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes silver NHC halido complexes (NHC)AgX (X=Cl, Br, I) as potent inhibitors of thioredoxin reductase (TrxR) and glutathione reductase (GR), demonstrating their strong antibacterial activity against Gram-negative bacteria. The iodide complexes (3c, 4c) exhibited superior antibacterial activity compared to their chloride and bromide counterparts, with low cytotoxicity towards Caco-2 cells.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of silver NHC complexes, evaluation of antibacterial activity through broth microdilution assays, assessment of enzyme inhibition using purified TrxR and GR, and cytotoxicity testing on Caco-2 cells.

full_output.paper_title: Target-Mediated Fluoroquinolone Resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae: Actions of Ciprofloxacin against Gyrase and Topoisomerase IV.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of S. aureus in milk and milk products in the Arsi highlands of Ethiopia, with high resistance to ampicillin and penicillin. The mecA and blaZ genes were detected in 50% of the isolates each, indicating methicillin-resistant and β-lactamase-producing strains.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing and PCR were used to detect resistance genes in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Etiology of bacterial pneumonia and multi-drug resistance pattern among pneumonia suspected patients in Ethiopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of bacterial pneumonia and multidrug resistance (MDR) in Ethiopia, with Klebsiella pneumoniae and Streptococcus pneumoniae being the most common bacterial isolates. The pooled prevalence of MDR among bacteria isolated from pneumonia patients was 67.73%.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on bacterial pneumonia and MDR in Ethiopia.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of attaining aggressive vs. conservative PK/PD target on the clinical efficacy of beta-lactams for the treatment of Gram-negative infections in the critically ill patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that achieving aggressive beta-lactam PK/PD targets significantly improved clinical cure rates and reduced the risk of beta-lactam resistance development in critically ill patients with Gram-negative infections. Factors such as male gender, BMI > 30 kg/m², augmented renal clearance, and MIC values above the clinical breakpoint were identified as predictors of failure in attaining aggressive PK/PD targets.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies assessing the impact of beta-lactam PK/PD targets on clinical outcomes in critically ill patients with Gram-negative infections.

full_output.key_findings: The study reveals the high prevalence of blaNDM genes in the food chain, highlighting the role of IncX3 plasmids in their transmission between animals, food, and humans.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and epidemiological analysis were used to characterize blaNDM genes and their transmission routes.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization and descriptive analysis of carbapenemase-producing Gram-negative rod infections in Bogota, Colombia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC-2 and blaKPC-3 as the most prevalent carbapenemase-encoding genes in carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative rods in Bogota, Colombia. These genes were frequently found in co-occurrence with blaVIM-2 and blaNDM-1 in healthcare-acquired infections.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing was used to identify carbapenemase-encoding genes and analyze their associations with clinical outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Inactivation of the ribosome assembly factor RimP causes streptomycin resistance and impairs motility in Salmonella.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies rimP as a novel gene involved in streptomycin resistance in Salmonella. Inactivation of rimP increases streptomycin resistance and impairs motility.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial evolution experiments, whole-genome sequencing, and various biochemical and microbiological assays to analyze the role of rimP in streptomycin resistance and motility.

full_output.paper_title: Repurposing approved drugs as potential efflux pump inhibitors in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified promethazine (PMZ), fluoxetine (FLU), and carbonyl cyanide 3-chlorophenylhydrazone (CCCP) as potential efflux pump inhibitors (EPIs) against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. These compounds effectively reduced the metabolic activity and biomass of P. aeruginosa biofilms and enhanced the susceptibility of the bacteria to antimicrobials by inhibiting efflux pumps.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the effect of PMZ, FLU, and CCCP on P. aeruginosa using ethidium bromide accumulation assays, minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum biofilm eradication concentration (MBEC) determinations, and confocal laser scanning microscopy to assess biofilm structure.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance of genital mycoplasmas recovered from nonpregnant women in Greece: trends over the last 15 years.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the declining susceptibility of genital mycoplasmas to azithromycin and fluoroquinolones, while doxycycline, pristinamycin, and josamycin remain effective treatments.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing using the Mycoplasma IST2 kit and analysis of clinical samples from nonpregnant women.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiological Characteristics and Antibiotic Sensitivity in Patients with Nosocomial Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis Caused by Escherichia coli: A Multicenter Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 47% of E. coli isolates from nosocomial SBP cases produced extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs), and 62% were multidrug-resistant (MDR). ESBL-producing and MDR E. coli showed high resistance to third-generation cephalosporins but were mostly susceptible to carbapenems, beta-lactamase inhibitors, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective study analyzing microbiological characteristics and antibiotic susceptibility of E. coli isolates from nosocomial SBP cases in liver cirrhosis patients.

full_output.paper_title: Burden of Antimicrobial Resistance Among Women with Post-Partum Infections in Low-Middle Income Countries: A Systematic Review.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high burden of post-partum infections caused by multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens, particularly methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacterales in low-middle income countries (LMICs).
full_output.methodology: Systematic review of literature from 2005 to 2023, analyzing data from 22 studies involving 14,804 bacterial isolates.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the resistance profiles of Salmonella Typhi isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Successful Treatment of Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Meningitis With Sulbactam-Durlobactam.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of bla OXA-23 and bla OXA-66 genes contributing to carbapenem resistance in a carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolate. Additionally, mutations in piuC, pirA, and PBP3 were associated with reduced cefiderocol susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance mechanisms in the isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence, virulence, and resistance genes in Salmonella enterica isolated from an integrated poultry company in Jordan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM as the most prevalent antimicrobial resistance gene in Salmonella isolates from an integrated poultry company in Jordan, conferring resistance to multiple antibiotics including ampicillin, tetracycline, ciprofloxacin, nalidixic acid, doxycycline, and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim.
full_output.methodology: PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and molecular detection of resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Respiratory carriage of hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae by indigenous populations of Malaysia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates with limited antimicrobial resistance, primarily ESBL producers without carbapenemases. No significant carbapenem resistance was observed.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of respiratory isolates from indigenous communities in Malaysia, including MLST, virulence gene detection, and antibiotic resistance profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative efficacy of difloxacin and nano-emulsion difloxacin as antibacterial agents against Salmonella enterica Serovar enteritidis in chickenss.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial efficacy of nano-emulsion difloxacin (NED) and commercial difloxacin (CD) against Salmonella enterica Serovar enteritidis in chickens. NED showed greater in vitro effectiveness compared to CD, with lower minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs).
full_output.methodology: The study used agar well diffusion tests and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) assays to evaluate the antibacterial activity of NED and CD against S. enteritidis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of extended spectrum beta-lactamase producing E. coli harboring carbapenem and colistin-resistant genes from poultry farms in Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in ESBL-producing E. coli from poultry farms in Egypt, including bla TEM-3, bla SHV-4, bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-14, bla NDM-1, and mcr-1, highlighting the public health risks associated with multidrug-resistant E. coli.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect AMR genes in E. coli isolates from poultry farms.

full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to identify AMR genes and resistance patterns in C. perfringens isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Summer mortality syndrome bacterial pathogens in farmed Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Aeromonas hydrophila, Vibrio spp., and Streptococcus iniae as the most prevalent bacterial pathogens associated with summer mortality in farmed Nile tilapia. full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolates were identified through phenotypic and molecular methods, including PCR, and antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the disc diffusion method.

full_output.key_findings: The review discusses the mechanisms of antibiotic resistance in pathotypes of E. coli, focusing on the role of beta-lactamases, carbapenemases, and other resistance genes. It highlights the importance of understanding these mechanisms to combat the growing problem of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of existing studies on antibiotic resistance mechanisms in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Thymoquinone is a natural antibiofilm and pathogenicity attenuating agent in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: Thymoquinone significantly inhibited biofilm formation, pyocyanin, protease activity, and swarming motility in P. aeruginosa PAO1. It downregulated the expression of quorum sensing (QS) genes lasI, lasR, rhlI, and rhlR, demonstrating antivirulence activity.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibiofilm and antivirulence effects of thymoquinone using subinhibitory concentrations, analyzed gene expression via RT-PCR, and conducted in vivo mouse survival tests.

full_output.key_findings: TRQ inhibits biofilm formation in K. pneumoniae by down-regulating the expression of biofilm-related genes (luxS, wbbm, wzm, lsrK) and reducing AI-2 activity.
full_output.methodology: q-RT PCR, crystal violet staining, SEM, and guinea pig lung infection model.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of OXA-48-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae in Lithuania, 2023: a multi-cluster, multi-hospital outbreak.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three distinct clusters of OXA-48-producing K. pneumoniae, highlighting the importance of whole-genome sequencing in tracking antimicrobial resistance outbreaks.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, PCR, and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes and determine the genetic relationships among the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial efficiency of bromhexine hydrochloride against endometritis-causing Escherichia coli and Trueperella pyogenes in bovines.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified virulence genes plo, fimA, nanH, fimH, and csgD in E. coli and T. pyogenes isolates. Bromhexine hydrochloride showed antimicrobial activity against E. coli and T. pyogenes, with synergistic effects when combined with antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolation, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR for virulence genes, and biofilm formation assessment.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiological and clinical infection characteristics analysis of Ralstonia.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the molecular epidemiology and clinical characteristics of Ralstonia pickettii, identifying its susceptibility to certain antibiotics and highlighting the need for accurate identification methods.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, 16S rDNA sequencing, and MLST for strain identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Type II and IV toxin-antitoxin systems coordinately stabilize the integrative and conjugative element of the ICESa2603 family conferring multiple drug resistance in Streptococcus suis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SezAT and AbiE as type II and IV toxin-antitoxin systems that stabilize the integrative and conjugative element ICESa2603, contributing to multidrug resistance in Streptococcus suis.
full_output.methodology: Deletion experiments, MIC testing, PCR analysis, and qPCR were used to assess the role of SezAT and AbiE in genetic stability and drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains isolated at tertiary care hospital in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all MRSA isolates were resistant to several antibiotics, including amoxicillin + clavulanic acid, ampicillin, imipenem, oxacillin, cloxacillin, and penicillin. Resistance to vancomycin was observed in 0.3% of isolates, and 2.9% were resistant to linezolid.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the Vitek 2 system.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence on the inhibitory effect of Brassica plants against Acinetobacter baumannii lipases: phytochemical analysis, in vitro, and molecular docking studies.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several Brassica plant metabolites with inhibitory effects on Acinetobacter baumannii lipases, suggesting potential therapeutic applications against A. baumannii infections.
full_output.methodology: Phytochemical analysis, in vitro assays, and molecular docking studies were employed to evaluate the antibacterial and lipase inhibitory effects of Brassica extracts.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence, antibiotic resistance phenotypes and molecular characterisation of Vibrio furnissii isolates from patients with diarrhoea.

strB.genetic_context: transposon islands containing antibiotic resistance genes
strB.evidence_note: The paper mentions that strB is part of transposon islands in VFBJ05 and VFBJ07, which contain antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in Vibrio furnissii isolates, including strA, strB, aph(3''-Ib), aph(6)-Id, sul1, sul2, tetA, tetB, tetR, floR, and aac(6')-IIa, which conferred resistance to streptomycin, sulfonamides, tetracycline, chloramphenicol, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and bioinformatic analysis were used to characterize the antibiotic resistance genes and virulence factors in Vibrio furnissii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of Escherichia coli isolates recovered from broilers with cellulitis.

qnrS.mechanism: Protection of DNA gyrase from quinolones

qnrB.mechanism: Protection of DNA gyrase from quinolones

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in E. coli isolates from broilers with cellulitis, including blaTEM, aadA1, aadA2, strA, strB, sul1, sul2, sul3, dfrA1, dfrA5, tet(A), tet(B), qnrS, qnrB, catA1, cmlA, floR, and mcr-1. These genes conferred resistance to multiple antibiotics, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug resistance in these isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, MIC testing, and sequencing to identify and characterize AMR genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic evaluation of gamithromycin against rabbit pasteurellosis.
full_output.key_findings: Gamithromycin demonstrated favorable pharmacokinetic properties in rabbits, including high subcutaneous bioavailability and a prolonged terminal half-life. It showed concentration-dependent bactericidal activity against Pasteurella multocida, with PK/PD indices correlating well with efficacy.
full_output.methodology: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic analyses were conducted using in vitro susceptibility testing, time-killing curves, and ex vivo antimicrobial activity assessments in rabbit plasma.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and genomic characterization of Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli harboring tet(X4) in black kites (Milvus migrans) in Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the first occurrence of the tet(X4) gene in Klebsiella pneumoniae from wild birds in Pakistan, highlighting the potential spread of tigecycline resistance beyond E. coli.
full_output.methodology: PCR, whole-genome sequencing, and conjugation experiments were used to detect and characterize the tet(X4) gene in isolates from black kites.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, biofilm formation inhibitory, and inflammation inhibitory activities of new coumarin derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the synthesis and evaluation of new coumarin derivatives for their antimicrobial, biofilm formation inhibitory, and anti-inflammatory activities. Compounds 4d, 4e, 4f, 6a, and 9 showed significant antimicrobial activity against various pathogens, with compound 9 demonstrating the highest potency. Additionally, compound 4d exhibited notable anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting nitric oxide production in LPS-stimulated macrophages.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of coumarin derivatives, followed by antimicrobial activity testing using agar well diffusion and MIC/MBC assays, biofilm formation inhibition using the crystal violet method, and anti-inflammatory activity assessment through nitric oxide production inhibition in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages.

full_output.paper_title: An effective antibiofilm strategy based on bacteriophages armed with silver nanoparticles.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel silver nanoparticle-binding peptide (Ag-XII) that enhances the antibiofilm efficacy of T7 phages when combined with silver nanoparticles.
full_output.methodology: Phage display library screening, binding efficiency assay, UV-Vis spectroscopy, biofilm eradication assays, and cytotoxicity analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Improving the production of carbamoyltobramycin by an industrial Streptoalloteichus tenebrarius through metabolic engineering.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TobR as a transcriptional regulator affecting carbamoyltobramycin production and TobO as a putative alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent non-heme iron enzyme involved in the biosynthesis pathway.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockout, overexpression, EMSA, and HPLC analysis were used to investigate the roles of TobR and TobO in carbamoyltobramycin production.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and carbapenemase dissemination in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Libyan hospitals: a call for surveillance and intervention.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaNDM and blaGES-1 as the most prevalent carbapenemase genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Libyan hospitals, highlighting the urgent need for surveillance and intervention.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR screening for resistance genes, and biofilm and alginate production assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of iodinated hydrocarbons against Vibrio parahaemolyticus and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified iodopropynyl butylcarbamate (IPBC) as effective against biofilm formation and virulence factors of Vibrio parahaemolyticus and Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating antibiofilm, antibacterial, and anti-virulence activities.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibiofilm and antibacterial activities of 22 iodinated hydrocarbons using crystal violet assays, time-to-kill assays, and qRT-PCR to assess gene expression changes.

full_output.paper_title: Laser-assisted surface alloying of titanium with silver to enhance antibacterial and bone-cell mineralization properties of orthopedic implants.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that laser-assisted surface alloying of titanium with silver (LSA-TiAg) enhances antibacterial properties and bone-cell mineralization without altering the bulk mechanical properties of titanium implants. The optimal surface was achieved with 32 W laser power, showing prolonged superhydrophilicity and antibacterial efficacy against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, along with a significant increase in bone mineralization.
full_output.methodology: The study used laser-assisted surface alloying of titanium with silver nanoparticles, followed by material characterization, antimicrobial assays, and cell mineralization studies to evaluate the antibacterial and osteoinductive properties of the modified surfaces.

full_output.paper_title: Drug resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains have altered cell envelope hydrophobicity that influences infection outcomes in human macrophages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that drug-resistant (DR) Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.tb) strains exhibit increased levels of hydrophobic phthiocerol dimycocerosates (PDIMs) and decreased levels of hydrophilic higher-order phosphatidyl-myoinositol mannosides (PIMs), resulting in an elevated PDIMs:PIMs ratio. This alteration correlates with decreased association with human macrophages and increased intracellular growth in certain DR strains.
full_output.methodology: The study employed lipid extraction, thin-layer chromatography (TLC), and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) to analyze cell envelope lipid compositions in 11 M.tb strains ranging from drug-susceptible (DS) to pre-extensively drug-resistant (pre-XDR).

full_output.paper_title: Neisseria meningitidis with decreased susceptibility to penicillin G and molecular characterization of the penA gene in strains isolated at University Hospital Centers of Casablanca and Marrakech (Morocco).

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific mutations in the rpoB and rpoC genes of Neisseria gonorrhoeae that contribute to high-level resistance to corallopyronin A (CorA). These mutations include L1328S in rpoB and K347R and E1329K in rpoC, which alter the structure of RNA polymerase to reduce CorA binding and efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular techniques including PCR, sequencing, and transformation to identify and validate mutations in rpoB and rpoC that confer resistance to CorA.

full_output.paper_title: Triterpenoid saponin from Panax ginseng increases the sensitivity of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus to β-lactam and aminoglycoside antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ginsenoside Rg3 and compound K as effective antibiotic adjuvants that increase the sensitivity of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) to β-lactam and aminoglycoside antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used MIC testing, FIC index calculations, and TLC analysis to evaluate the synergistic effects of RGE, ginsenosides, and compound K on MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis of New D-π-A Phenothiazine-Based Fluorescent Dyes: Aggregation Induced Emission and Antibacterial Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The paper describes the synthesis of new phenothiazine-based fluorescent dyes, PTZ-1 and PTZ-2, which exhibit antibacterial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. PTZ-2 showed better antibacterial affinity compared to PTZ-1.
full_output.methodology: The dyes were synthesized through a series of chemical reactions involving phenothiazine, sulfadiazine, and sulfathiazole. Their antibacterial activity was evaluated using the cup agar diffusion method and colony-forming unit (CFU) assay.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterisation of a novel Silviavirus bacteriophage promising antimicrobial agent against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolated and characterized a novel Staphylococcus phage, vB_SauM_VL10 (VL10), which shows potent lytic activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and effectively reduces MRSA biofilms. VL10 demonstrates potential as a therapeutic agent for MRSA infections.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, transmission electron microscopy, host range analysis, and in vitro and in vivo assays were used to characterize VL10's properties and efficacy against MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: High cure rates of Mycoplasma genitalium following empiric treatment with azithromycin alongside frequent detection of macrolide resistance in Austria.

mutations_found.position_in_molecule: region V of the 23S rRNA gene

23S_rRNA.notes: Mutations in the 23S rRNA gene were detected in azithromycin-resistant Mycoplasma genitalium isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of azithromycin resistance mutations in Mycoplasma genitalium isolates in Austria, with 68% of tested isolates harboring the A2058G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene. Despite this, empiric azithromycin treatment resulted in a 68% cure rate.
full_output.methodology: Genotypic resistance analysis was performed on Mycoplasma genitalium isolates using molecular techniques.

full_output.paper_title: The evaluation of Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis in hospital air, their antibiotic resistance and sensitivity of S. aureus to cefoxitin.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 33.3% of S. aureus isolates were resistant to cefoxitin, while 40.6% were sensitive. The emergency ward had the highest percentage of resistant S. aureus strains, and the skin outpatient operating room had the highest percentage of sensitive strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used the disc diffusion method to determine the resistance and sensitivity of S. aureus to cefoxitin.
full_output.sample_size: 96 colonies of S. aureus and 25 colonies of S. epidermidis

full_output.paper_title: Unveilling genetic profiles and correlations of biofilm-associated genes, quorum sensing, and antibiotic resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolated from a Malaysian Teaching Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several biofilm-associated genes and the agrI quorum sensing system as being significantly associated with antibiotic resistance in S. aureus isolates from a Malaysian hospital.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of biofilm-associated genes and agr/sar quorum sensing genes in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Ceftriaxone-Resistant Haemophilus influenzae Among Korean Children.

full_output.paper_title: Computer-Aided Design of Antimicrobial Agents Targeting Bacterial Biofilms
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several compounds with potent antibiofilm and antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting their potential as novel antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized QSAR models and in vitro biofilm assays to evaluate the antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity of selected compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium abscessus WhiB7 regulates a species-specific repertoire of genes to confer extreme antibiotic resistance
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies whiB7 as a critical gene involved in conferring extreme antibiotic resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus.
