full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the misidentification of Kluyvera bacteremia by molecular panels and the detection of CTX-M resistance markers despite susceptibility to third and fourth generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Molecular panels, MALDI-TOF MS, and standardized AST were used for identification and susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Novel antimony-based antimicrobial drug targets membranes of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SbPh4ACO as a novel antimony-based antimicrobial compound with broad-spectrum bactericidal activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, and Staphylococcus aureus. It disrupts bacterial membranes, increases membrane permeability, and shows synergistic effects with antibiotics like polymyxin B and cefoxitin. Additionally, it exhibits low cytotoxicity at synergistic concentrations.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of SbPh4ACO through MIC and MBC assays, time-kill assays, TEM imaging, and membrane permeability tests using NPN and PI staining. Synergy with antibiotics was assessed via checkerboard assays.

full_output.paper_title: First report of the chromosomal integration of carbapenemase gene bla(IMP-19) in Acinetobacter baumannii AB322: the legacy of integron in phage-plasmid?
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first chromosomal integration of the carbapenemase gene blaIMP-19 in Acinetobacter baumannii AB322, suggesting potential mechanisms involving integrons and phage elements.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, susceptibility testing, and conjugation experiments were performed to characterize the AMR profile of AB322.

full_output.paper_title: A novel member of drug/metabolite transporter (DMT) family efflux pump, SA00565, contributes to tetracycline antibiotics resistance in Staphylococcus aureus USA300.

sa00565.validation_method: generation of sa00565 gene deletion mutant and assessment of susceptibility to antibiotics, MIC assays, EtBr accumulation and efflux assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SA00565, a novel efflux pump in the DMT superfamily, as a contributor to tetracycline and doxycycline resistance in Staphylococcus aureus USA300.
full_output.methodology: Generation of sa00565 gene deletion mutant, MIC assays, EtBr accumulation and efflux assays, and phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Mucus polymer concentration and in vivo adaptation converge to define the antibiotic response of Pseudomonas aeruginosa during chronic lung infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that increasing concentrations of mucin and host-derived extracellular DNA (eDNA) in respiratory mucus enhance antibiotic tolerance of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, particularly to tobramycin, without involving genetic resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: In vitro experiments using synthetic CF sputum medium (SCFM2) with varying concentrations of mucin and eDNA to assess P. aeruginosa survival after antibiotic treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Reduction of product composition variability using pooled microbiome ecosystem therapy and consequence in two infectious murine models.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that pooled microbiotherapy products are more homogeneous, diverse, and effective in reducing pathogenicity in murine models of Salmonella and Clostridioides difficile infections compared to single donor-derived products. Pooled products also showed inhibitory effects against drug-resistant bacteria like Enterococcus faecium vanA and Klebsiella pneumoniae oxa48.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized 16S rDNA sequencing, in vitro growth inhibition assays, and murine infection models to analyze the effectiveness of pooled versus single donor-derived microbiotherapy products.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of cefiderocol against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii carrying various β-lactamase encoding genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla PER−1, bla OXA−23, and bla OXA−24 as significant contributors to cefiderocol resistance in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR screening for resistance genes and cefiderocol susceptibility testing via broth microdilution and disk diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and genomic-based antimicrobial resistance analysis of Avibacterium paragallinarum isolates in Guangdong Province, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in Avibacterium paragallinarum isolates from Guangdong, China, including tet(B), aph(3')-Ia, aph(3'')-Ib, aph(6)-Id, aad-A, sul2, sul3, catP, floR, blaOXA-1, blaCTX-M-14, erm(X), mef(B), and fosA3. These genes were associated with resistance to tetracycline, streptomycin, kanamycin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, chloramphenicol, ampicillin, erythromycin, and fosfomycin.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and disk diffusion testing were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and phenotypic resistance in Avibacterium paragallinarum isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Gram-positive bacteria as the predominant causative agents of microbial keratitis in Malawi, with Staphylococcus aureus being one of the most frequently isolated bacteria. Whole-genome sequencing revealed the presence of virulence factors associated with S. aureus keratitis, but no specific AMR genes were characterized in this study.
full_output.methodology: The study used a corneal impression membrane (CIM) for sample collection, followed by culture, PCR, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to identify causative microorganisms and analyze their virulence factors.

full_output.paper_title: In situ captured antibacterial action of membrane-incising peptide lamellae.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the design and characterization of lamellin-2K and lamellin-3K, lysine-rich heterochiral β3-peptides that form supramolecular structures upon interaction with bacterial lipopolysaccharides (LPS), leading to membrane disruption and antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized molecular dynamics simulations, electron microscopy, circular dichroism spectroscopy, and antibacterial assays to investigate the structural and functional properties of the peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Biodiversity of carbapenem-resistant bacteria in clinical samples from the Southwest Amazon region (Rondônia/Brazil).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various carbapenemase-encoding genes, including bla KPC -like, bla NDM -like, bla OXA-23 -like, bla OXA-58 -like, bla OXA-143 -like, bla OXA-48 -like, bla SPM -like, bla VIM -like, and bla IMP -like, in carbapenem-resistant bacteria from Rondônia, Brazil.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization of carbapenemase-encoding genes using PCR and analysis of laboratory data.

full_output.paper_title: What Contributes to the Minimum Inhibitory Concentration? Beyond β-Lactamase Gene Detection in Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the complex interplay between β-lactamases and outer membrane porins in determining β-lactam resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae. Plasmid-encoded β-lactamases such as CTX-M-14, CTX-M-15, CMY-2, and DHA-1, as well as chromosomal SHV-5, were found to confer resistance to various β-lactam antibiotics. Additionally, loss of outer membrane porins OmpK35, OmpK36, and PhoE was associated with meropenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized cloning of β-lactamase genes into Kp 23 and KPM 20, followed by determination of minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) using agar dilution and Etest methods.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial activity of cefepime-tazobactam combination against extended spectrum beta-lactamase and/or AmpC beta-lactamase-producing gram-negative bacilli.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that cefepime-tazobactam showed high sensitivity against ESBL and/or AmpC-producing Gram-negative bacilli, with 91.48% sensitivity, suggesting it could be a viable alternative to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: The study used disc diffusion and confirmatory tests to detect ESBL and AmpC production, and evaluated the susceptibility of isolates to various antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: A challenging case of carbapenem resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae-related pyogenic liver abscess with capsular polysaccharide hyperproduction: a case report.

The study suggests that imipenem may promote resistance to carbapenems and colistin in K. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and molecular techniques were used to identify resistance genes and characterize the isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and molecular characterization of β-lactamase-producing Klebsiella species among children discharged from hospital in Western Kenya.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M, bla SHV, bla TEM, and bla OXA genes as the most prevalent β-lactamase genes in Klebsiella isolates from children in western Kenya, contributing to resistance against third-generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect β-lactamase genes and assess resistance patterns in Klebsiella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Fungus-mediated synthesis of Se-BiO-CuO multimetallic nanoparticles as a potential alternative antimicrobial against ESBL-producing Escherichia coli of veterinary origin.

full_output.methodology: Systematic review of literature on Oligella spp. with emphasis on antimicrobial resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Overexpression of the flagellar motor protein MotB sensitizes Bacillus subtilis to aminoglycosides in a motility-independent manner.
full_output.key_findings: Overexpression of MotB sensitizes Bacillus subtilis to aminoglycosides independently of motility. The proton-binding site of MotB is crucial for this effect, as evidenced by the D24A mutation reducing aminoglycoside sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: Gene overexpression, survival assays, western blotting, and mutagenesis.

full_output.paper_title: EGLN1 Promotes Antiviral Innate Immunity by Enhancing IRF3 Activation Through Proline 10 Hydroxylation

mutations_found.validated_by: mutant mouse model and functional assays

Irf3.notes: The P10A mutation in Irf3 impairs antiviral responses.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Irf3 proline 10 hydroxylation as a critical mechanism for antiviral innate immunity, with the P10A mutation impairing IRF3 activation and antiviral responses.
full_output.methodology: The study uses mutant mouse models, functional assays, and biochemical analyses to characterize the role of Irf3 hydroxylation in antiviral immunity.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors for bacteremic pneumonia and mortality (28-day mortality) in patients with Acinetobacter baumannii bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Acinetobacter baumannii in the pneumonia-related bacteremia group exhibited high antibiotic resistance, with only polymyxin showing a susceptibility rate above 80%. Recent surgery was identified as a significant independent predictor for pneumonia-related Acinetobacter baumannii bacteremia.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective monocenter observational study analyzing clinical characteristics and risk factors for pneumonia-related Acinetobacter baumannii bacteremia.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic use and resistance patterns at Rumphi District Hospital in Malawi: a cross-sectional study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance among patients at Rumphi District Hospital, including resistance to penicillins, cephalosporins, and aminoglycosides. It highlighted the need for improved antimicrobial stewardship and the importance of antimicrobial susceptibility testing.
full_output.methodology: The study used a cross-sectional design, analyzing antibiotic use and resistance patterns through microbiological testing and data review.

full_output.paper_title: Short reads-based characterization of pathotype diversity and drug resistance among Escherichia coli isolated from patients attending regional referral hospitals in Tanzania.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes and mutations in E. coli isolates from Tanzania, including beta-lactamases (blaOXA-1, blaTEM-1B, blaCTX-M-15), dihydrofolate reductase variants (dfrA1, dfrA5, dfrA7, dfrA8, dfrA12, dfrA14, dfrA17), tetracycline resistance genes (tet(A), tet(B), tet(D)), aac(6')-Ib-cr, qnrS1, and quinolone resistance mutations in gyrA, parC, and parE.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing using Illumina Nextseq550 followed by bioinformatics analysis with CGE tools.

full_output.paper_title: Chitosan-Loaded Lagenaria siceraria and Thymus vulgaris Potentiate Antibacterial, Antioxidant, and Immunomodulatory Activities against Extensive Drug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Vancomycin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus: In Vitro and In Vivo Approaches.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory activities of Lagenaria siceraria, Thymus vulgaris, and their chitosan nanocomposites against XDR P. aeruginosa and VRSA, demonstrating potent inhibitory effects.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo assays, including antimicrobial susceptibility testing, GC-MS analysis, and RT-qPCR, were used to evaluate the effects of the nanocomposites.

full_output.paper_title: Chitosan-Aspirin Combination Inhibits Quorum-Sensing Synthases (lasI and rhlI) in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The chitosan-aspirin combination inhibits quorum-sensing synthases lasI and rhlI in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, reducing AHL production, biofilm formation, and virulence factors.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution, real-time PCR, and molecular docking to assess the inhibitory effects of aspirin and chitosan on P. aeruginosa virulence factors and gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activities of α-Helix and β-Sheet Peptides against the Major Bovine Respiratory Disease Agent, Mannheimia haemolytica.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activities of α-helix and β-sheet peptides (PRW4, WRL3, and WK2) against multidrug-resistant (MDR) Mannheimia haemolytica. WK2 showed the most efficacy, demonstrating bactericidal activity against M. haemolytica without cytotoxic effects on bovine turbinate cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro MIC assays, biofilm screening, and membrane permeability assessments to evaluate the antimicrobial activities of the peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and Characterization of Streptomyces Species for Antimicrobial Activity
full_output.key_findings: The study identified four novel metabolites in Streptomyces species, including cyclo-(Ile-Ser), 3-[(6-methylpyrazin-2-yl) methyl]-1H-indole, 2-n-hexyl-5-n-propylresorcinol, and cyclo-(d-Leu-l-Trp), which showed antimicrobial activity against various pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized LC-MS/MS analysis and GNPS-based molecular networking to identify and characterize metabolites from Streptomyces species isolated from Nepalese soils.

full_output.paper_title: Regulation of Cysteine Homeostasis and Its Effect on Escherichia coli Sensitivity to Ciprofloxacin in LB Medium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several genes involved in cysteine homeostasis, including gshA, cysB, tcyP, mstA, cysK, cyuA, eamA, and tnaA, and examined their effects on E. coli sensitivity to ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study used mutants in cysteine homeostasis mechanisms and microbiological and biochemical methods to analyze the impact of these genes on cysteine levels, glutathione synthesis, and ciprofloxacin sensitivity.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology of Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella aerogenes in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified six carbapenem-resistant K. aerogenes strains harboring carbapenemase genes, including blaIMP-1, blaIMP-6, blaNDM-1, and blaNDM-5. These genes were found to confer resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and PCR were used to identify carbapenemase genes in K. aerogenes isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of the Genetic Spread of Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in a Tertiary Greek Hospital.

blaOXA-23-like.genetic_context: bla OXA-23 gene accompanied by IS Aba1
blaOXA-23-like.evidence_note: The intrinsic bla OXA-51-like gene was found in all isolates. The bla OXA-23 gene accompanied by IS Aba1 was prevalent in nearly all A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla OXA-23-like, bla OXA-51-like, and bla OXA-58-like genes as the primary contributors to carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from a Greek hospital. The bla OXA-23-like gene was prevalent in most isolates, while bla OXA-58-like was found in one isolate. No class B metallo-beta-lactamase genes (bla VIM or bla NDM) were detected.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and molecular typing techniques were used to detect and characterize AMR genes in A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Macrolide and/or Fluoroquinolone Resistance Genes in Mycoplasma genitalium Strains Isolated from Men in the Northwest Region of Croatia in 2018-2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study detected high prevalence of macrolide resistance (60.4%) and fluoroquinolone resistance (19.2%) in Mycoplasma genitalium strains, with 18.2% co-resistance. Mutations in the 23S rRNA gene (A2058G, A2059G) and parC gene (S83R, D87N) were associated with resistance.
full_output.methodology: MT-PCR was used to detect mutations in the 23S rRNA and parC genes associated with macrolide and fluoroquinolone resistance.

full_output.paper_title: TiO(2) Nanocomposite Coatings and Inactivation of Carbapenemase-Producing Klebsiella Pneumoniae Biofilm-Opportunities and Challenges.
full_output.key_findings: The review discusses the challenges and opportunities of using TiO2 nanocomposite coatings to inactivate carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae biofilms, highlighting their antimicrobial efficacy and potential applications in hospital settings.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review of studies on TiO2 nanocomposite coatings and their effects on KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Resistome Analysis of Klebsiella pneumoniae Complex from Residential Aged Care Facilities Demonstrates Intra-facility Clonal Spread of Multidrug-Resistant Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes and mutations in K. pneumoniae isolates from RACFs, including beta-lactamases (bla DHA-1, bla SHV-1, bla SHV-27, bla CTX-M-14), fluoroquinolone resistance determinant qnrB4, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole resistance determinants dfrA17 and sul1. Mutations in ompK35, ompK37, prmA, pmrB, eptA, and parC were also found to contribute to resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and manual probing for mutations were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The Prediction of LptA and LptC Protein-Protein Interactions and Virtual Screening for Potential Inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study predicts the protein-protein interaction between LptA and LptC and identifies compound 18593 as a potential inhibitor of this interaction, which could disrupt lipopolysaccharide transport in Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Computational modeling, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to predict the interaction between LptA and LptC and to screen for potential inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Trends in and Risk Factors for Drug Resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis in HIV-Infected Patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high resistance rates to rifampicin and quinolones in Mycobacterium tuberculosis among HIV/AIDS patients, with increasing trends over time. Age and a history of previous anti-tuberculosis treatment were identified as major risk factors for drug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic drug susceptibility testing using the proportion method and logistic regression analysis to identify risk factors.

full_output.paper_title: Ferrous sulfate combined with ultrasound emulsified cinnamaldehyde nanoemulsion to cause ferroptosis in Escherichia coli O157:H7.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antimicrobial effects of ferrous sulfate (FeSO4) and cinnamaldehyde nanoemulsion (CALNO) on Escherichia coli O157:H7, revealing that FeSO4 induces ferroptosis and that the combination of FeSO4 and CALNO exhibits synergistic bactericidal effects.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized antimicrobial activity assays, measurement of lipid peroxidation and reactive oxygen species, qRT-PCR for gene expression analysis, and microscopic observations to evaluate the effects of FeSO4 and CALNO on E. coli O157:H7.

full_output.paper_title: Vesicle protrusion induced by antimicrobial peptides suggests common carpet mechanism for short antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the mechanism of action of short cationic alpha-helical antimicrobial peptides (SCHAMPs) using molecular dynamics simulations, revealing a carpet-like mechanism involving membrane perturbation and vesicle protrusion at high peptide concentrations.
full_output.methodology: Molecular dynamics simulations (both all-atom and coarse-grained) were used to analyze the interaction of SCHAMPs with anionic membranes and vesicles.

full_output.key_findings: This paper discusses the origin, fate, and impact of microplastics (MPs) and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs). It highlights the role of MPs in facilitating the spread of ARGs through horizontal gene transfer and their accumulation in sludge, contributing to environmental and health concerns.
full_output.methodology: The study reviews existing literature and analyzes the mechanisms of MPs and ARGs in WWTPs, focusing on their interactions and environmental implications.

full_output.key_findings: Regional antibiotic delivery (RAD) with vancomycin or gentamicin significantly reduces the risk of sternal wound infections (SWI) in cardiac surgery patients, with no evidence of systemic toxicity or resistant strain emergence.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating the effectiveness of RAD for SWI prophylaxis.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of urinary tract infections causing bacterial isolates and associated risk factors among HIV patients in Tigray, Northern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 12.5% of HIV patients in Tigray, Ethiopia, had urinary tract infections (UTIs) caused by bacterial isolates. E. coli was the most common isolate, followed by K. pneumoniae and S. aureus. Resistance to ampicillin, cotrimoxazole, and tetracycline was high, while susceptibility to nitrofurantoin, ciprofloxacin, and gentamicin was notable.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed bacterial isolates from urine samples of HIV patients using standard microbiological protocols and the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: High-resolution genomics identifies pneumococcal diversity and persistence of vaccine types in children with community-acquired pneumonia in the UK and Ireland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified pneumococcal serotypes and their antibiotic resistance profiles, highlighting the persistence of vaccine types and the emergence of non-vaccine serotypes like 23B1, which showed penicillin non-susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and susceptibility testing were conducted on pneumococcal isolates from children with community-acquired pneumonia.

full_output.paper_title: Seasonal meropenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii and influence of temperature-driven adaptation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies adeJ, oxa-51, and oxa-23 as genes contributing to meropenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii, with their expression upregulated at low temperatures.
full_output.methodology: Expression analysis, plasmid transfer, and MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: The detailed analysis of the microbiome and resistome of artisanal blue-veined cheeses provides evidence on sources and patterns of succession linked with quality and safety traits.

sul1.validation_method: Assembly-based analysis and ResFinder database search

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in the microbiome of artisanal blue-veined cheeses, including beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside adenyltransferases, sulfonamide resistance genes, and tetracycline efflux pumps. These genes were primarily associated with bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Salmonella enterica, Acinetobacter, and Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting the potential risks of ARG transmission in cheese production environments.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), assembly-based analysis, and the ResFinder database to identify and characterize ARGs in cheese samples and their environments.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenemase genes in clinical and environmental isolates of Acinetobacter spp. from Quito, Ecuador.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several carbapenemase genes, including bla OXA-23, bla OXA-24, bla OXA-51, bla OXA-72, and bla OXA-143, in clinical and environmental isolates of Acinetobacter spp. from Quito, Ecuador. These genes were found to confer resistance to carbapenems such as imipenem and meropenem.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize carbapenemase genes in Acinetobacter isolates.

full_output.paper_title: PDADMAC/Alginate-Coated Gold Nanorod For Eradication of Staphylococcus Aureus Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents PDADMAC/alginate-coated gold nanorods (GNR/Alg/PDADMAC) as an effective agent for eradicating Staphylococcus aureus biofilms, demonstrating superior efficacy compared to triclosan at significantly lower concentrations.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of nanoparticles, biofilm eradication assays, microscopic analysis, and biocompatibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: AMR mechanisms in L. interrogans serovars: a comprehensive study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 32 AMR genes in Leptospira interrogans serovars, with 20 key genes consistently present across most strains. Unique efflux pump systems were found in serovar Pomona, suggesting distinct resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and analysis using the PATRIC tool.

full_output.paper_title: Upregulation of pmrA, pmrB, pmrC, phoQ, phoP, and arnT genes contributing to resistance to colistin in superbug Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from human clinical samples in Tehran, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the upregulation of pmrA, pmrB, pmrC, phoQ, phoP, and arnT genes as contributing to colistin resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, PCR, and Real-Time PCR were used to analyze resistance mechanisms in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid eradication of vancomycin and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus by MDP1 antimicrobial peptide coated on photocrosslinkable chitosan hydrogel: in vitro antibacterial and in silico molecular docking studies.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that MDP1, a melittin-derived antimicrobial peptide, effectively eradicates vancomycin-resistant and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. MDP1 exhibits potent antibacterial activity and can be incorporated into a photocrosslinkable chitosan hydrogel for rapid bacterial eradication.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial efficacy of MDP1 against S. aureus strains using MIC and MBC assays, and assessed the interaction of MDP1 with chitosan hydrogels via molecular docking and surface loading experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance patterns and genes of Campylobacter jejuni isolated from chickens in Pasuruan, Indonesia.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant Stenotrophomonas maltophilia in residential aged care facilities: An emerging threat.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaL1 and blaL2 beta-lactamase genes, eptA1 and eptA2 phosphoethanolamine transferases, and other resistance mechanisms in multidrug-resistant Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolates from residential aged care facilities.

full_output.paper_title: Assessment of the ability of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus to create biofilms during wound healing in a rat model treated with carboxymethyl cellulose/carboxymethyl chitosan hydrogel containing EDTA.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial effects of a carboxymethyl cellulose/carboxymethyl chitosan hydrogel containing EDTA against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating its effectiveness in inhibiting bacterial growth and improving wound healing.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the antibacterial efficacy of EDTA-containing hydrogels using MIC and MBC tests, along with in vivo wound healing assessments in a rat model.

full_output.paper_title: Elastic and Self-Healing Copolymer Coatings with Antimicrobial Function.

full_output.paper_title: Targeted potent antimicrobial and antitumor oxygen-heterocyclic-based pyran analogues: synthesis and computational studies.

full_output.methodology: Synthesis of compounds followed by antimicrobial and antitumor activity evaluations using agar diffusion and MTT assays, along with molecular docking studies.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic analyses of IncHI2 plasmids from enteric bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various AMR genes encoded on IncHI2 plasmids from enteric bacteria, including sulfonamide, aminoglycoside, chloramphenicol, tetracycline, carbapenem, colistin, heavy metal, and disinfectant resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Tracking antimicrobial resistance transmission in urban and rural communities in Bangladesh: a One Health study of genomic diversity of ESBL-producing and carbapenem-resistant Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various beta-lactamase genes, including bla CTX-M-15, bla TEM-1b, bla OXA-1, and carbapenem resistance genes like bla NDM-5, bla NDM-7, and bla NDM-1, in ESBL-producing and carbapenem-resistant E. coli isolates from Bangladesh.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analyses were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: New-generation biofilm effective antimicrobial peptides and a real-time anti-biofilm activity assay: CoMIC.
full_output.key_findings: Four novel antimicrobial peptides (NET1, NET2, NET3, and NET4) were designed and shown to effectively inhibit biofilm formation and exhibit antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE).
full_output.methodology: Peptides were designed, synthesized, and tested for antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity using MIC assays, HPLC, protease resistance tests, and SEM.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that human-derived collagen hydrogel embedded with antibiotics effectively elutes inhibiting concentrations of gentamicin and clindamycin for up to 48 hours, disrupting bacterial biofilms of MRSA and C. perfringens without harming mammalian cells.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a modified Kirby-Bauer assay, crystal violet assay, biofilm inhibition visualization, and mammalian cell viability assays to evaluate the efficacy of collagen hydrogel embedded with antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Gentamicin loaded niosomes against intracellular uropathogenic Escherichia coli strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed gentamicin-loaded niosomes to enhance the intracellular delivery of gentamicin against uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) strains, showing improved antibacterial activity and reduced invasion rates.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized niosome preparation, physical-chemical characterization, MIC determination, and cytotoxicity assays to evaluate the effectiveness of gentamicin-loaded niosomes against UPEC.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity of Hungarian varietal honeys against respiratory pathogens as a function of storage time.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of Hungarian varietal honeys against respiratory pathogens, showing that linden and sunflower honeys had the strongest inhibitory effect, while black locust honey was the least active. Storage time significantly affected the antibacterial potency of honeys, with fresher honeys exhibiting greater efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution to determine minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentrations (MBC), along with crystal violet assays to assess biofilm inhibition. Membrane degradation was also analyzed.
full_output.sample_size: Various honey samples from different years

full_output.paper_title: Multi-locus sequence typing, antimicrobials resistance and virulence profiles of Salmonella enterica isolated from bovine carcasses in Minas Gerais state, Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified five sequence types (STs) among 17 Salmonella enterica isolates from bovine carcasses in Minas Gerais, Brazil, with ST10 being the most prevalent. The isolates exhibited diverse virulence gene profiles and resistance to multiple antibiotics, including clindamycin, sulfamethoxazole, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: The study employed multi-locus sequence typing (MLST) and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to analyze the genetic and resistance profiles of Salmonella enterica isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and molecular characterization of colistin resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates: insights from a study in Ardabil hospitals.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified colistin resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Ardabil hospitals, with mechanisms involving mutations in pmrB and phoQ genes, overproduction of efflux pumps, and down-regulation of porin oprD.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar dilution MIC, PCR, sequencing, and qRT-PCR to analyze colistin resistance mechanisms in P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of NDM-producing Enterobacterales infections in companion animals from Argentina.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first molecular characterization of NDM-producing Enterobacterales causing infections in companion animals from Argentina, identifying bla NDM-1 and bla NDM-5 variants along with ESBLs and AmpC genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, Sanger sequencing, PFGE, and conjugation assays were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in Streptococcus suis serotype 4, including genes conferring resistance to tetracyclines, macrolides, lincosamides, aminoglycosides, oxazolidinones, and chloramphenicol. Prophages were identified as the primary vehicle for the dissemination of these resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and ResFinder 4.1 analysis were used to identify antibiotic resistance genes in S. suis serotype 4 strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the epidemiological and clinical features of carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (CP-Kp) and Escherichia coli (CP-Ec) in Spain, highlighting the prevalence of healthcare-associated and community-acquired infections, with a focus on carbapenemase genes such as bla OXA-48, bla KPC-3, and bla VIM-1.
full_output.methodology: Prospective cohort study involving 59 Spanish hospitals, with molecular characterization of 403 isolates, including detection of carbapenemase genes via PCR and whole-genome sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of multidrug-resistant bacteria in the nasal cavities and evaluation of sinus disorders in patients undergoing Le Fort I osteotomy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in the nasal cavities of patients undergoing Le Fort I osteotomy, highlighting the potential risk of post-operative complications from such bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolation, MALDI-TOF identification, and antibiotic susceptibility testing via disk diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial and anti-biofilm properties of oleuropein against Escherichia coli and fluconazole-resistant isolates of Candida albicans and Candida glabrata.
full_output.key_findings: Oleuropein exhibits antimicrobial and anti-biofilm properties against Escherichia coli, Candida albicans, and Candida glabrata, significantly reducing the expression of biofilm-associated genes such as Hwp1, Als3, Epa1, Epa6, LuxS, and Pfs.
full_output.methodology: Microbroth dilution method, MTT assay, and RT-qPCR were used to evaluate the antimicrobial and anti-biofilm effects of oleuropein.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiology reveals multiple mechanisms of linezolid resistance in clinical enterococci in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified optrA as the most common linezolid resistance mechanism in clinical enterococci in China, along with cfr(D) and poxtA. Mutations in rplC and rplD were also associated with linezolid resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and PCR were used to identify linezolid resistance mechanisms in enterococci.

SPIN.notes: SPIN is a peroxidase inhibitor that interacts with MPO to inhibit its activity.

full_output.key_findings: Residue-level investigation of the helical bundle domain of SPIN revealed that specific residues (L49, E50, H51, E52, Y55, and Y75) are crucial for its inhibitory activity against MPO. Mutations in these residues significantly reduced SPIN's ability to inhibit MPO, primarily by diminishing its initial interaction with the enzyme.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, SPR, and enzyme activity assays were used to investigate the functional contributions of specific residues in SPIN.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and antibiogram profile of diarrheagenic Escherichia coli isolated from two abattoir settings in northwest Ethiopia: a one health perspective.
full_output.key_findings: The study detected diarrheagenic Escherichia coli (DEC) isolates with various virulence genes, including stx2, eae, hlyA, and st. All DEC isolates were resistant to erythromycin and vancomycin, and 82.4% exhibited multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial culture, biochemical tests, PCR for virulence genes, and Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: This study evaluates computational methods for predicting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) phenotypes from genomic data, focusing on machine learning (ML) and rule-based approaches. It identifies the performance of various AMR prediction tools across 78 species-antibiotic datasets, highlighting the superiority of ML methods in many cases, especially for closely related strains, while rule-based methods like ResFinder excel for divergent genomes.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a benchmarking workflow with three sample splitting methods (random, phylogeny-aware, homology-aware) and evaluates ML and rule-based AMR prediction software across 78 species-antibiotic datasets.

full_output.paper_title: Turbidimetric bioassays: A solution to antimicrobial activity detection in asymptomatic bacteriuria isolates against uropathogenic Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies microcin H47, colicin E9, microcin V, and colicin E7 as antimicrobial agents produced by ABU isolates that show activity against uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC) strains. These findings highlight the potential of ABU bacteriocin-producers as alternatives to conventional antibiotics in treating UTIs.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized turbidimetric growth assays and bioinformatic analyses to evaluate the antimicrobial activity of cell-free supernatants from ABU isolates against UPEC strains.
full_output.sample_size: Nine ABU isolates and eight UPEC strains

full_output.paper_title: The Distribution of Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter Species and High Prevalence of CC92 OXA-23-Producing Acinetobacter Baumannii in Community Hospitals in South Korea.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-23 as the dominant carbapenem resistance gene in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from community hospitals in South Korea, with additional detection of blaNDM-1 and blaVIM-2 in non-baumannii Acinetobacter species.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and MLST analysis were used to identify carbapenem resistance genes and assess genetic relatedness of isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacter cloacae Complex in Southwest China: Molecular Characteristics and Risk Factors Caused by NDM Producers.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaNDM-1 and blaNDM-5 as the primary carbapenem resistance genes in CREC strains, with blaNDM-1 being the most prevalent. These genes were found to be plasmid-borne and transferable, contributing to the spread of carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, conjugation experiments, and MLST were used to characterize the resistance genes and molecular profiles of CREC strains.

full_output.methodology: The research involved the preparation and characterization of solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) loaded with quorum-sensing inhibitors, coated with chitosan, and immobilized with alginate lyase, along with in vitro and in vivo evaluations of their efficacy.

full_output.key_findings: KSP-1007, a novel broad-spectrum β-lactamase inhibitor, significantly enhances the efficacy of meropenem against carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, including those producing various serine- and metallo-β-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: MIC and MBC testing, in vivo murine infection models, and β-lactamase inhibition assays.

full_output.paper_title: Drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis among Nepalese patients at a tuberculosis referral center.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the gyrA gene (MUT1 and MUT3C) and the rrs gene (MUT1) associated with fluoroquinolone and second-line injectable drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Nepalese patients.
full_output.methodology: Line probe assay (GenoType MTBDRsl) was used to detect mutations in the gyrA, gyrB, rrs, and eis genes associated with drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Prolonged mass azithromycin distributions and macrolide resistance determinants among preschool children in Niger: A sub-study of a cluster-randomized trial (MORDOR).
full_output.key_findings: The study found that prolonged mass azithromycin distributions increased macrolide resistance determinants in the gut of preschool children in Niger, but resistance may plateau after 2 to 3 years of treatment. No significant increase in non-macrolide resistance determinants was observed.
full_output.methodology: The study used a cluster-randomized trial with DNA sequencing and bioinformatics to analyze antibiotic resistance determinants in rectal swabs from 5,340 children.

full_output.methodology: Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) assays and head-to-head competition experiments were conducted to assess the fitness effects of AMR mutations in different environments.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial aetiology, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, and factors associated with urinary tract infection among under-five children at primary health facility, North-Western Tanzania.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus as the most common pathogens causing urinary tract infections (UTIs) in under-five children. High levels of multidrug resistance were observed, particularly to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, gentamycin, ampicillin, and penicillin.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted a cross-sectional analysis of urine cultures and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to determine the bacterial aetiology and resistance patterns in children with UTIs.

full_output.paper_title: A finely balanced order-disorder equilibrium sculpts the folding-binding landscape of an antibiotic sequestering protein.

TipAS.notes: TipAS is involved in the sequestration of thiopeptide-antibiotics, but no specific mutations were identified in this paper.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TipAS, an antibiotic-sequestering protein from Streptomyces lividans, as a key player in the resistance mechanism against thiopeptide antibiotics. TipAS exhibits a dynamic conformational landscape with a pre-equilibrium between binding-competent and binding-incompetent states, allowing it to sample multiple conformations for effective antibiotic binding.
full_output.methodology: Combining experiments, simulations, and statistical modeling, the study investigates the conformational dynamics and binding mechanisms of TipAS.

This mutation results in a dysfunctional CARD9 protein, leading to impaired TNF-α production upon stimulation with β-glucan.

full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from a hospital in Malawi.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic insights into the diversity, virulence, and antimicrobial resistance of group B Streptococcus clinical isolates from Saudi Arabia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes including erm(B), erm(A), lsa(C), mef(A), tet(M), tet(O), aac(6')-aph(2''), ant(6)-Ia, aph(3')-III, and aadE in GBS isolates from Saudi Arabia, highlighting the prevalence of resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, tetracycline, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in GBS isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Peptides LE-53 and LE-55: Mechanisms of Action and Efficacy Against Multidrug-Resistant Bacteria
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LE-53 as a potent antimicrobial peptide with broad-spectrum activity against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, demonstrating lower MIC values compared to LE-55 and conventional antibiotics like tobramycin. LE-53's efficacy is linked to its hydrophobicity and ability to induce vesicle fusion in bacterial membranes without toxicity to eukaryotic cells.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of LE-53 and LE-55 using MIC assays, structural analyses, and biophysical techniques to investigate their mechanisms of action.

full_output.paper_title: OXA-48-like carbapenemases in Proteus mirabilis - novel genetic environments and a challenge for detection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified novel genetic environments for blaOXA-48-like genes in Proteus mirabilis, highlighting the challenges in detecting OXA-48-like carbapenemases due to low MICs for carbapenems and piperacillin-tazobactam. It also demonstrated the transferability of these genes between P. mirabilis and other Enterobacterales.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, conjugation experiments, and MIC testing were used to characterize the genetic environments and resistance mechanisms of OXA-48-like-producing P. mirabilis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a Selective and Stable Antimicrobial Peptide.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of a novel synthetic antimicrobial peptide, DTr18-dab, which exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, is nonhemolytic, and remains effective against colistin-resistant isolates. It also demonstrates efficacy against bacterial biofilms and shows activity in human serum and a Galleria mellonella infection model.
full_output.methodology: The research involved the identification and modification of antimicrobial peptides through structural analysis, alanine scanning, and the incorporation of nonnatural amino acids to enhance stability and activity.

full_output.paper_title: Antimony susceptible Leishmania donovani: evidence from in vitro drug susceptibility of parasites isolated from patients of post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis in pre- and post-miltefosine era.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that recent Leishmania donovani isolates from PKDL patients are susceptible to antimonials (SAG) in vitro, suggesting that antimonial drugs can still be used in combination therapies for PKDL treatment.
full_output.methodology: In vitro drug susceptibility assays and sequence analysis of AQP1 and LdMT genes were performed on PKDL isolates from pre- and post-miltefosine eras.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of ceftazidime-avibactam combined with different antimicrobials against carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the combination of ceftazidime-avibactam (CZA) with meropenem (MEM) showed the highest level of synergistic effect against KPC-producing and carbapenemase-non-producing isolates, while CZA combined with aztreonam (ATM) demonstrated complete synergy against metallo-beta-lactamase (MBL)-producing strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used checkerboard assays, time-kill curve assays, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to evaluate the efficacy of CZA in combination with various antimicrobials against carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial metallothionein, PmtA, a novel stress protein found on the bacterial surface of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and involved in management of oxidative stress and phagocytosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PmtA, a bacterial metallothionein, as a novel stress protein involved in managing oxidative stress and resisting phagocytosis in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Overexpression of pmtA in PAO1, assessment of survival under oxidative stress, and phagocytosis assays using THP-1 macrophages.

full_output.paper_title: The Streptococcus pyogenes stand-alone regulator RofA exhibits characteristics of a PRD-containing virulence regulator.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies RofA as a PRD-containing virulence regulator (PCVR) in Streptococcus pyogenes, demonstrating its role in regulating virulence factors and carbohydrate metabolism. RofA is phosphorylated in vitro and in vivo, and its phosphorylation is influenced by glucose concentration.
full_output.methodology: The study used RNA-seq, Western blot, and in vitro phosphorylation assays to analyze RofA's function and regulation.

full_output.paper_title: A pyocin-like T6SS effector mediates bacterial competition in Yersinia pseudotuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: YPK_0952 is a pyocin-like T6SS effector with DNase activity that is toxic to Yersinia pseudotuberculosis and Escherichia coli. YPK_0953 acts as the cognate immunity protein that neutralizes YPK_0952 toxicity.
full_output.methodology: Toxicity assays, complementation analysis, site-directed mutagenesis, GST pull-down assay, bacterial two-hybrid assay

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, antimicrobial resistance and detection of virulence genes of Escherichia coli and Salmonella spp. isolated from white-lipped peccaries and collared peccaries.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified E. coli isolates from white-lipped and collared peccaries carrying virulence genes such as iss, tsh, papC, and eae, indicating potential pathogenicity and multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and identification of E. coli and Salmonella spp. from fecal samples, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing and PCR-based detection of virulence genes.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of multidrug resistance Salmonella species isolated from clinical specimens at University of Gondar comprehensive specialized hospital Northwest Ethiopia: A retrospective study.

High resistance rates were observed against ampicillin, tetracycline, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and chloramphenicol.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple chromosomally-mediated antimicrobial resistance genes in the high-risk international clone II Acinetobacter baumannii AB073, including beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, and sulfonamide resistance genes, contributing to multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing combined with in silico analysis and phenotypic assays were used to characterize the antimicrobial resistance and virulence profiles of A. baumannii AB073.

full_output.paper_title: Triggering Toll-Like Receptor 5 Signaling During Pneumococcal Superinfection Prevents the Selection of Antibiotic Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that adjunct flagellin therapy with amoxicillin reduces the selection of antibiotic-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae, allowing for a 200-fold reduction in antibiotic dose while maintaining therapeutic efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial coinfection models in mice, along with mathematical modeling, to investigate the impact of flagellin on antibiotic resistance selection.

full_output.paper_title: Lipid phase separation impairs membrane thickness sensing by the Bacillus subtilis sensor kinase DesK.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the role of the Bacillus subtilis des system in membrane thickness sensing and antibiotic resistance, but found no evidence that the des system acts as a reporter for antibiotic-induced changes in membrane fluidity or thickness.
full_output.methodology: The study used promoter activation assays, DesK-GFP localization, and susceptibility testing of deletion mutants to investigate the role of the des system in membrane thickness sensing and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Defining the phylogenetics and resistome of the major Clostridioides difficile ribotypes circulating in Australia.

gyrA.notes: most common resistance-conferring mutation

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AMR genes such as ermB, tetM, aac(6')-Ib, sat4A, ant6-Ia, and aph3-III in Clostridioides difficile strains, particularly in RT014/020. Mutations in gyrA and gyrB contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance. AMR is uncommon, with limited evidence of clonal transmission.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in C. difficile strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of blaCTX-M-15 genes encoding ESBL resistance on phage-plasmids from two S. Typhi isolates.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput bioinformatics pipeline for detecting P1-like phage-plasmids and analyzing their genetic content.

full_output.paper_title: sRNA expression profile of KPC-2-producing carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae: Functional role of sRNA51.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies sRNA51 as a regulator of acrA expression, which influences carbapenem resistance in KPC-2-producing CRKP. Overexpression of sRNA51 reduces acrA expression and carbapenem resistance, while overexpression of acrA restores resistance.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq, qRT-PCR, western blotting, and microbroth dilution assays were used to analyze sRNA expression and validate the role of acrA in carbapenem resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of multi-drug resistant bacteria in intensive care units at Tripoli University Hospital, Tripli, Libya.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria in intensive care units (ICUs) at Tripoli University Hospital, with Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa showing high resistance rates to multiple antibiotics. ESBL and MRS were also identified in most strains.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using MicroScan auto-SCAN 4 panel.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Escherichia coli pathogenicity and drug resistance in yolk peritonitis.

aph(3')-Ib.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the gene APH(3')-Ib was detected and verified in the E. coli strain, indicating its presence and role in aminoglycoside resistance.

aph(6)-Id.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the gene was identified through whole genome sequencing and validated by PCR and drug sensitivity tests.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple drug resistance genes in E. coli isolates from yolk peritonitis cases, including aadA5, APH(3")-Ib, APH(6)-Id, TEM-1, sul1, sul2, parC, gyrA, mfd, kdpE, mphA, and Mrx, which confer resistance to aminoglycosides, beta-lactams, sulfonamides, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR, drug sensitivity tests, and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify and characterize drug resistance genes in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Serine deamination by human serine racemase synergizes with antibiotics to curtail the replication of Chlamydia trachomatis.
full_output.key_findings: Human serine racemase (SRR) deaminates serine, generating ammonia, which restricts the replication of Chlamydia trachomatis. SRR's role in this process was validated through immunoblotting and functional assays.
full_output.methodology: Immunoblotting, functional assays, and quantitative analysis of serine and ammonia levels.

full_output.paper_title: Innovative Vancomycin-Loaded Hydrogel-Based Systems - New Opportunities for the Antibiotic Therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed vancomycin-loaded hydrogel-based composites for local antibiotic therapy, demonstrating effective encapsulation and sustained release of vancomycin, with antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: The hydrogels were characterized for size, stability, and encapsulation efficiency using dynamic light scattering, zeta potential measurements, and UV–Vis spectroscopy. Antibacterial activity was assessed against Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Interactions between Aeromonas caviae and Yersinia enterocolitica isolated from a case of diarrhea: evaluation of antimicrobial susceptibility and immune response of infected macrophages.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that mixed infections of Aeromonas caviae and Yersinia enterocolitica led to increased cell damage and altered antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, including increased resistance to ciprofloxacin, trimethoprim, chloramphenicol, gentamicin, and ertapenem.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated antimicrobial susceptibility using disk diffusion assays and analyzed immune responses through gene expression profiling in macrophages.

full_output.paper_title: Development of Antimicrobial Coatings Using CaCO3/AgNP Hybrids
full_output.key_findings: The study developed antimicrobial coatings using CaCO3/AgNP hybrids, demonstrating their effectiveness against E. coli, MRSA, and P. aeruginosa. The addition of PVP and mucin improved the stability and uniformity of the coatings, enhancing their antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized SEM, EDS, FTIR, and XRD for coating characterization, along with resazurin reduction and MTT assays for evaluating antibacterial and cytotoxic effects.

23S rRNA.notes: mutations in macrolide-resistance-hypervariable sites

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of fidaxomicin, thuricin CD, vancomycin and nisin highlights the narrow spectrum nature of thuricin CD.
full_output.key_findings: The study compares the antimicrobial activity of fidaxomicin, thuricin CD, vancomycin, and nisin against Clostridioides difficile and other bacteria, highlighting the narrow spectrum of thuricin CD. Fidaxomicin and vancomycin showed broader activity against gram-positive bacteria, while thuricin CD was specifically active against C. difficile and some Bacillus spp.
full_output.methodology: The study used well-diffusion assays and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) tests to evaluate the antimicrobial activity of the compounds against a panel of bacterial strains, including C. difficile and commensal gut bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: GDP-mannose pyrophosphorylase is an efficient target in Xanthomonas citri for citrus canker control.

xanB.encodes: phosphomannose isomerase (PMI) and guanosine diphosphate-mannose pyrophosphorylase (GMP) activities
xanB.validation_method: deletion and complementation studies, biofilm formation, motility, UV resistance, and enzyme activity assays

full_output.key_findings: The xanB gene is essential for Xanthomonas citri pathogenicity, and its inhibitors can effectively reduce citrus canker severity.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, biofilm formation, motility, UV resistance, and enzyme activity assays were performed.

full_output.paper_title: The unusual mode of action of the polyketide glycoside antibiotic cervimycin C.

gyrB.notes: Downregulation of gyrB increases susceptibility to cervimycin.
gyrB.evidence_note: The paper states that artificial downregulation of the DNA gyrase subunit B gene (gyrB) increased the activity of cervimycin in agar diffusion tests.

walK.notes: Cervimycin-resistant S. aureus mutants carried SNPs in the walK gene.

full_output.key_findings: Cervimycin C (CmC) affects DNA gyrase and the WalRK two-component system, leading to cell division and chromosome segregation defects in Gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Fluorescence microscopy, transcriptomics, proteomics, and in vitro enzyme activity assays were used to analyze the effects of CmC on bacterial cells.

full_output.paper_title: Accumulation of resistance genes in Salmonella Typhimurium transmitted between poultry and dairy farms increases the risk to public health.

blaCTX-M-55.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial sensitivity tests

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the bla CTX-M-55 gene in Salmonella Typhimurium isolates from a dairy farm, which confers resistance to extended-spectrum cephalosporins, highlighting the risk of antimicrobial resistance transmission between poultry and dairy farms.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial sensitivity tests were performed on Salmonella Typhimurium strains isolated from a dairy and poultry farms.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and genetic relatedness of Salmonella serotypes isolated from food, asymptomatic carriers, and clinical cases in Shiyan, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) Salmonella strains from food, asymptomatic carriers, and clinical cases in Shiyan, China, highlighting the severity of AMR in asymptomatic carriers comparable to clinical cases.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed serotype distribution, antimicrobial resistance, and MLST profiles of 114 Salmonella isolates using Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion and MLST.

full_output.paper_title: Substrate Analogues Entering the Lipoic Acid Salvage Pathway via Lipoate-Protein Ligase 2 Interfere with Staphylococcus aureus Virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Lpl-004, Lpl-008, and Lpl-0023 as lipoic acid analogues that interfere with the lipoic acid salvage pathway in Staphylococcus aureus, leading to impaired growth and reduced virulence. These compounds bind to E2 subunits of dehydrogenase complexes, disrupting their activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized virtual screening, molecular docking, and experimental validation to identify and characterize lipoic acid analogues that target the lipoic acid salvage pathway in S. aureus.

full_output.key_findings: Miconazole and phenothiazine exhibit anti-virulence activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa by inhibiting biofilm formation, pyocyanin production, rhamnolipid activity, protease activity, and hemolysin activity. They also reduce the expression of quorum-sensing genes such as lasI, lasR, rhlR, and pqsR.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic assays, qRT-PCR, molecular docking, and in vivo mouse survival experiments were conducted to evaluate the anti-virulence effects of miconazole and phenothiazine.

full_output.paper_title: ARGNet: using deep neural networks for robust identification and classification of antibiotic resistance genes from sequences.
full_output.key_findings: ARGNet is a deep neural network that identifies and classifies antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) without relying on sequence alignment, demonstrating superior performance over existing models.
full_output.methodology: ARGNet uses an autoencoder for sequence reconstruction and a convolutional neural network (CNN) for classification of ARGs.

full_output.paper_title: Hybrid Illumina-Nanopore assembly improves identification of multilocus sequence types and antimicrobial resistance genes of Staphylococcus aureus isolated from Vermont dairy farms: comparison to Illumina-only and R9.4.1 nanopore-only assemblies.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from Vermont dairy farms, including beta-lactam resistance genes (blaZ, blaI, blaR), tetracycline resistance genes (tet(K), tet(38)), erythromycin resistance genes (erm(T), erm(A)), lincomycin resistance gene (lnu(G)), aminoglycoside resistance genes (aaC3, ant(9)-la), multidrug resistance efflux pumps (lmrS, mepA, mepR, mepB, norA, norB, arlS, arlR, mgrA), and fosfomycin resistance gene (fosB).
full_output.methodology: Genome assembly and annotation using a hybrid Illumina-Nanopore approach, followed by identification of antimicrobial resistance genes via bioinformatics tools and phenotypic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Aberrant Expression of SLC7A11 Impairs the Antimicrobial Activities of Macrophages in Staphylococcus Aureus Osteomyelitis in Mice.

SLC7A11.mechanism: regulates intracellular ROS and lipid peroxidation

full_output.key_findings: SLC7A11 expression is up-regulated in macrophages during S. aureus osteomyelitis and its inhibition enhances macrophage bactericidal activity by increasing ROS and lipid peroxidation.
full_output.methodology: Pharmacological inhibition, genetic knockout, and in vitro/in vivo experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome analysis of Escherichia coli isolated from wild Amur tiger (Panthera tigris altaica) and North China leopard (Panthera pardus japonensis).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 68 resistance genes and point mutations in E. coli isolates from wild Amur tigers and North China leopards, with a focus on fluoroquinolone and tetracycline resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence and spread of a mupirocin-resistant variant of the European epidemic fusidic acid-resistant impetigo clone of Staphylococcus aureus, Belgium, 2013 to 2023.

mupA.validation_method: PCR detection of the mupA gene

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a mupirocin-resistant variant of the European epidemic fusidic acid-resistant impetigo clone of Staphylococcus aureus, which carries the mupA gene for mupirocin resistance and the fusB gene for fusidic acid resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and PCR detection of resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Machine Learning Models Identify Inhibitors of New Delhi Metallo-β-lactamase.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies compound 72922413 as a novel inhibitor of NDM-1, a metallo-β-lactamase, which reduces the MIC of meropenem in E. coli and K. pneumoniae clinical isolates expressing NDM-1.
full_output.methodology: Machine learning models were trained on HTS data and used to screen chemical libraries, leading to the identification and validation of a novel NDM-1 inhibitor.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa ST179 producing both IMP-16 and KPC-2: a case study of introduction from Peru to Spain.

blaIMP-16.genetic_context: within a type 1 integron structure and was flanked by additional ARGs, such as bla OXA-2 , bla OXA-4 , and aadA11
blaIMP-16.evidence_note: bla IMP-16 gene was located within a type 1 integron structure and was flanked by additional ARGs, such as bla OXA-2 , bla OXA-4 , and aadA11

blaKPC-2.genetic_context: bla KPC-2 gene was located in an IncP6 plasmid
blaKPC-2.evidence_note: bla KPC-2 and bla KPC-35 were located in an IncP6 plasmid

blaKPC-35.genetic_context: bla KPC genes were located in the same plasmid and genetic context among the five isolates, which was not the canonical Tn4401 element typically associated with bla KPC but consisted of a composite transposon of approximately 17 kbp containing an IS Kpn27-bla KPC-2 -ΔIS Kpn6 core structure as well as Tn3- associated structures, as previously described in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates recovered from the same hospital in 2018 ( 28 ) ( Fig. 3 ).
blaKPC-35.evidence_note: The paper describes the presence of blaKPC-35 in Pseudomonas aeruginosa ST179 isolates and its location in an IncP6 plasmid.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the emergence of carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa ST179 carrying blaIMP-16, blaKPC-2, and blaKPC-35 genes, highlighting the global threat of multidrug-resistant clones and the importance of monitoring resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive genomic landscape of antibiotic resistance in Staphylococcus epidermidis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies core antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in Staphylococcus epidermidis, including norA, dfrC, blaZ, mecA, mecR1, mecI, msrA, mphC, qacA, tet(K), aac(6')-Ie-aph(2'')-Ia, mupA, vgaA, and cat, highlighting their prevalence and association with sequence types and resistance phenotypes.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of 405 S. epidermidis genomes, including 35 environmental isolates from the Han River, using whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics tools to detect and characterize ARGs.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in respiratory tract pathogens during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly noting the rise in ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae, carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP), and carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii (CRAB).
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 3517 isolates from respiratory samples collected between 2019 and 2022 using automated bacterial identification and susceptibility testing systems.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and Dynamic Features of Acinetobacter baumannii OXA-66 β-Lactamase Explain Its Stability and Evolution of Novel Variants.

blaOXA-66.mechanism: mutations in the active site enhance carbapenem binding and resistance
blaOXA-66.validation_method: structural and dynamic analysis, molecular dynamics simulations, X-ray crystallography

P130A.evidence_note: The paper states that P130A mutation is part of a series of clinical variants that confer increased carbapenem resistance.

I129L.evidence_note: The paper states that the I129L mutation is found in clinical variants and that it results in greatly lowered K M values in OXA-51-like β-lactamases, indicating increased carbapenem binding affinity.

L167V.evidence_note: The paper states that L167V is a clinical variant and that it confers increased carbapenem resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes mutations in OXA-66 β-lactamase that enhance carbapenem binding and resistance, including I129L, L167V, P130Q, P130A, and W222L. These mutations alter the rotamer equilibrium and reduce steric hindrance, improving carbapenem binding affinity.
full_output.methodology: Molecular dynamics simulations, X-ray crystallography, and thermal denaturation studies were used to analyze the structural and dynamic features of OXA-66 and its variants.

full_output.paper_title: Assessment of three antibiotic combination regimens against Gram-negative bacteria causing neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes and mutations in Gram-negative bacteria causing neonatal sepsis in LMICs, including ESBLs, carbapenemases, and aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, highlighting the high prevalence of multidrug resistance and the need for effective antibiotic combinations.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize AMR genes and mutations in bacterial isolates from neonatal sepsis cases.

full_output.paper_title: Three concurrent mechanisms generate gene copy number variation and transient antibiotic heteroresistance.

aac(6')-Ib-cr.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and MIC testing

tet(A).validation_method: whole genome sequencing and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three mechanisms (tandem amplification, increased plasmid copy number, and transposition of resistance genes) that generate gene copy number variation and transient antibiotic heteroresistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, MIC testing, and mouse gut colonization model.
full_output.sample_size: 83 mutants analyzed in K. pneumoniae and 56 E. coli isolates.

cmlA1.evidence_level: Supporting evidence from co-localization analysis in plasmid contigs.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies widespread co-localization of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) with other resistance and virulence genes in the infant gut microbiome, highlighting the association with an immature gut microbial composition. Key findings include the frequent co-localization of tetracycline and fluoroquinolone resistance genes, as well as the presence of class 1 integrons on plasmids.
full_output.methodology: The study employed metagenomic sequencing of fecal samples from 662 Danish children to analyze genetic co-localization of resistance genes and their association with gut microbial maturation.

full_output.paper_title: Overcoming antibiotic resistance: non-thermal plasma and antibiotics combination inhibits important pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the combination of non-thermal plasma (NTP) and antibiotics as a strategy to combat antibiotic resistance, highlighting its effectiveness against multidrug-resistant pathogens like MRSA and P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews experimental studies on the use of NTP in combination with antibiotics to inhibit pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Volatile Fatty Acids Effective as Antibacterial Agents against Three Enteric Bacteria during Mesophilic Anaerobic Incubation.
full_output.key_findings: Volatile fatty acids (VFAs) demonstrate antibacterial effects against Enterococcus faecalis, Escherichia coli, and Klebsiella pneumoniae, with higher concentrations (4 g/L) showing significant bactericidal activity. The VFA cocktail was the most effective, while propionic acid was the least effective.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial effects of various VFAs on three enteric bacteria using mesophilic anaerobic incubation, measuring bacterial kinetics, pH changes, and minimum bactericidal concentrations (MBC).

full_output.paper_title: Green Preparation and Antibacterial Activity Evaluation of AgNPs-Blumea balsamifera Oil Nanoemulsion.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a green antibacterial nanoemulsion containing silver nanoparticles (AgNPs@BBO-TS NE) using Blumea balsamifera oil (BBO) and tea saponin (TS). The nanoemulsion exhibited strong antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The nanoemulsion was prepared using ultrasonic emulsification, and its antibacterial activity was evaluated through bacterial inhibition circles, MIC, and MBC assays.

full_output.paper_title: Enhancing Mechanical and Antimicrobial Properties of Dialdehyde Cellulose-Silver Nanoparticle Composites through Ammoniated Nanocellulose Modification.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on enhancing the mechanical and antimicrobial properties of dialdehyde cellulose-silver nanoparticle (DAC@Ag1) composites by modifying cellulose nanofibers (CNFs) with ammonia (N-CNF). The results showed that the optimal mass ratio of N-CNF to DAC@Ag1 was 5:5, leading to significant improvements in mechanical properties and antimicrobial efficacy against E. coli and S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study used FT-IR, XPS, and XRD analyses to characterize the composite films, along with mechanical testing and antimicrobial assays to evaluate the properties of the modified composites.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, Electronic, and Antibacterial Properties of 3,7-Di(hetero)aryl-substituted Phenothiazinyl N-Propyl Trimethylammonium Salts.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and antibacterial activity of 3,7-di(hetero)aryl-substituted phenothiazine salts, showing effective inhibition of several pathogenic bacterial strains including Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized through a modular approach involving dibromination, Michael addition, and Suzuki coupling. Their antibacterial activity was evaluated using MIC assays against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Design, Synthesis and Biological Activity of Novel Methoxy- and Hydroxy-Substituted N-Benzimidazole-Derived Carboxamides.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on designing and synthesizing novel N-substituted benzimidazole carboxamides with varying numbers of methoxy and hydroxy groups. Among the tested compounds, compound 8 showed the highest antibacterial activity against E. faecalis with a MIC of 8 μM. The study also highlighted the importance of hydroxy groups in enhancing the biological activities of the compounds.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized using organic chemistry techniques and evaluated for their antiproliferative, antioxidant, and antibacterial activities using in vitro assays.
