full_output.paper_title: Genomic and Clinical Analysis of Staphylococcus haemolyticus in Neonatal Intensive Care Units

aph(3')-III.source: In silico prediction of antibiotic resistance-encoding genes Building upon the genomic analysis, we utilized in silico methods to predict the presence of antibiotic resistance-encoding genes in all 53 S. haemolyticus strains. These strains were predicted to be MDR due to the presence of blaZ, mecA, mph(C), msr(A) , aac(6’)-aph(2’’), and norA genes, combined with (S84L) and (S80L) mutations in gyrA and parC genes, respectively. These findings were in complete agreement with in vitro phenotypes ( Table 3 ). Resistance to streptogramin A and related antibiotics was due to vga(A)LC and erm(C) genes detected in 46 (86.7%) and 2 (3.8%) isolates. The aminoglycosides resistance encoding gene aadD and the mupirocin resistance encoding gene mup A were only detected in ST29 strains ( p < 0.001), while aph(3’)-III gene encoding for an aminoglycoside phosphotransferase, and the dfrG gene responsible for cotrimoxazole resistance, were present in ST29 and ST25 strains.
aph(3')-III.evidence_note: The presence of the aph(3')-III gene was predicted in silico and confirmed by in vitro phenotypes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes and mutations in S. haemolyticus, including blaZ, mecA, mph(C), msr(A), vga(A)LC, erm(C), aph(3')-III, aadD, aac(6')-aph(2''), norA, dfrG, mupA, qacE, qacH, mdeA, mepA/mepR, bltR, copZ, copA, copB, czrB, czrA_2, arsB_1, arsB_2, arsB_3, arsC_1, arsC_2, arsR_1, arsR_2, cadD_2, and czcD, as well as mutations in gyrA (S84L) and parC (S80L) and rpoB (I180V, S796A).

full_output.paper_title: Dual-function antimicrobial-antibiofilm peptide hybrid to tackle biofilm-forming Staphylococcus epidermidis.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel antibiofilm peptide, BiF2_5K7K, which shows effective biofilm inhibition and antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus epidermidis, with minimal hemolytic effect and cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and evaluation of peptide derivatives for their antibiofilm and antimicrobial activities using various in vitro assays.

full_output.paper_title: Unraveling the adaptive strategies of Mycoplasma hominis through proteogenomic profiling of clinical isolates.

DeoD.notes: The F188Y substitution in DeoD is associated with altered enzyme activity and may contribute to the activation of the ribonucleoside utilization pathway in clinical isolates.

ParC.notes: Mutations in ParC are associated with reduced susceptibility to ofloxacin in clinical isolates.

ParE.notes: Mutations in ParE are associated with reduced susceptibility to ofloxacin in clinical isolates.

GyrA.notes: Mutations in GyrA are associated with reduced susceptibility to ofloxacin in clinical isolates.

GyrB.notes: Mutations in GyrB are associated with reduced susceptibility to ofloxacin in clinical isolates.

full_output.key_findings: Clinical isolates of Mycoplasma hominis show resistance to ofloxacin, with certain isolates exhibiting significant resistance linked to amino acid substitutions in topoisomerases and gyrases. Additionally, unique genes related to restriction-modification systems and mobile genetic elements were identified.
full_output.methodology: Proteogenomic profiling, whole-genome sequencing, and comparative analysis of clinical isolates and a laboratory strain.

full_output.paper_title: An Eco-Friendly Synthesis Approach for Enhanced Photocatalytic and Antibacterial Properties of Copper Oxide Nanoparticles Using Coelastrella terrestris Algal Extract.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the synthesis of copper oxide nanoparticles (CuO NPs) using Coelastrella terrestris algal extract, highlighting their enhanced photocatalytic and antibacterial properties. The CuO NPs exhibited significant antibacterial activity against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa, with zone of inhibition (ZOI) values of 22 mm and 17 mm, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The CuO NPs were synthesized using algal extract and characterized using XRD, FTIR, SEM, and EDS. Their photocatalytic and antibacterial activities were evaluated through dye degradation and MIC assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance spectrums of Escherichia coli and Enterococcus spp. strains against commonly used antimicrobials from commercial meat-rabbit farms in Chengdu City, Southwest China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in E. coli and Enterococcus spp. strains from meat-rabbit farms, including blaTEM, tetA, qnrS, floR, and aac[6']-Ie-aph[2']-Ia, which confer resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing to identify AMR genes and their resistance profiles in E. coli and Enterococcus spp. strains.
full_output.sample_size: 75 E. coli and 210 Enterococcus spp. strains

full_output.paper_title: Serovar and sequence type distribution and phenotypic and genotypic antimicrobial resistance of Salmonella originating from pet animals in Chongqing, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella isolates from pet animals in Chongqing, China, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug-resistant strains and the presence of genes such as blaTEM, blaCTX-M, qnrS, tet(A), and sul1.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the detection and characterization of AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella isolates through molecular techniques and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Dual β-lactam for treatment of pulmonary Mycobacterium abscessus in a child.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the successful treatment of a child with pulmonary Mycobacterium abscessus using a dual β-lactam regimen, highlighting the potential benefit of combining ceftaroline and meropenem for drug-resistant infections.
full_output.methodology: Clinical case report with antimicrobial susceptibility testing and treatment outcome analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Temperate phage-antibiotic synergy across antibiotic classes reveals new mechanism for preventing lysogeny.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that protein synthesis inhibitors like gentamicin, kanamycin, tetracycline, and azithromycin synergize with temperate phage HK97 to reduce lysogeny and enhance antibacterial efficacy, revealing a novel SOS-independent mechanism for modulating phage behavior.
full_output.methodology: Checkerboard assays, qPCR, and fluorescence-based reporter constructs were used to assess phage-antibiotic synergy and evaluate the impact on lysogeny and phage behavior.

full_output.paper_title: Increased resistance against tellurite is conferred by a mutation in the promoter region of uncommon tellurite resistance gene tehB in the ter-negative Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli O157:H7.

tehB.validation_method: complementation of tehA and tehB in isogenic strains and quantitative RT-PCR

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic amikacin resistance may not indicate poor response to amikacin in Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that phenotypic amikacin resistance in Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease did not correlate with clinical outcomes or rrs gene mutations, suggesting that high MICs may not accurately predict treatment response.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing amikacin resistance and clinical outcomes in patients with Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of a simple method for testing aztreonam and ceftazidime-avibactam synergy in New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase producing Enterobacterales.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated a simple method for testing aztreonam (AZT) and ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) synergy in New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase (NDM)-producing Enterobacterales. The proposed method showed high sensitivity and specificity in detecting synergy, with 97.14% sensitivity and 100% specificity. The method involves supplementing Mueller Hinton Agar (MHA) with CAZ-AVI and placing an AZT disc to assess synergy.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of broth microdilution, E-strip disc diffusion, double disc diffusion, disc replacement, and a proposed supplemented agar disc diffusion method to evaluate AZT and CAZ-AVI synergy in NDM-producing Enterobacterales.

full_output.paper_title: PAI-1 mediates acquired resistance to MET-targeted therapy in non-small cell lung cancer.
full_output.key_findings: Overexpression of SERPINE1 (PAI-1) was found to mediate resistance to crizotinib in MET-amplified lung cancer cell lines, and its knockdown restored sensitivity to the drug.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis, Western blot, and colony formation assays were used to investigate the role of PAI-1 in crizotinib resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriological analysis and antibiotic resistance in patients with diabetic foot ulcers in Dhaka.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various bacterial isolates from diabetic foot ulcers, with Escherichia coli showing the highest multidrug resistance. Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus spp., Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Staphylococcus aureus also exhibited significant resistance patterns.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial cultures, biochemical tests, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were performed using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Differences of protein expression in enterococcus faecalis biofilm during resistance to environmental pressures.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several ABC transporters and ATP synthase subunits that were highly expressed in Enterococcus faecalis biofilms under high alkaline and NaOCl stress conditions, indicating their potential role in the bacterium's resistance to environmental pressures.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative proteomics using TMT labeling and LC-MS/MS analysis combined with qPCR and PRM verification.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Presentation, Antimicrobial Resistance, and Treatment Outcomes of Aeromonas Human Infections: A 14-Year Retrospective Study and Comparative Genomics of 2 Isolates From Fatal Cases.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes, including bla OXA, ampC, cphA, and mcr-3, in Aeromonas dhakensis isolates from fatal cases. These genes conferred resistance to carbapenems, piperacillin-tazobactam, and colistin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze AMR genes and resistance patterns in Aeromonas isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic insights unveil the plasmid transfer mechanism and epidemiology of hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae in Vietnam.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes in hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Vietnam, highlighting the role of plasmids in the spread of resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and plasmid analysis were used to characterize AMR genes and their distribution among isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis suppresses host antimicrobial peptides by dehydrogenating L-alanine.

Rv2780.mechanism: Rv2780 dehydrogenates L-alanine and reduces the level of L-alanine in macrophages, thereby suppressing the expression of AMPs to facilitate survival of mycobacteria
Rv2780.resistance_mechanism_class: metabolic manipulation of host immune responses
Rv2780.validation_method: Gene deletion and complementation experiments, enzymatic activity assays, and transcriptomic analysis
Rv2780.evidence_note: The paper describes Rv2780 as a secreted alanine dehydrogenase that suppresses AMPs by dehydrogenating L-alanine, but does not indicate that it confers resistance to antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Rv2780, an L-alanine dehydrogenase from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, as a critical virulence factor that suppresses the expression of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) by degrading L-alanine, thereby impairing host immune defenses.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, enzymatic activity assays, transcriptomic analysis, and in vivo infection experiments.

full_output.paper_title: LIGAND-BASED PHARMACOPHORE HYPOTHESIS DEVELOPMENT AND 3D QSAR MODELING STUDIES
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on developing a 3D-QSAR model and pharmacophore hypothesis for DprE1 inhibitors, identifying key structural features and interactions critical for biological activity.
full_output.methodology: The research involved 3D-QSAR modeling, pharmacophore hypothesis generation, and molecular docking studies to evaluate DprE1 inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of Streptococcus pyogenes upper respiratory tract infections in Poland (2003-2017).
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the prevalence of erythromycin and tetracycline resistance genes (mefA, ermA, ermB, tetM, tetO) in Streptococcus pyogenes isolates from Poland between 2003 and 2017.
full_output.methodology: PCR and MIC assays were used to detect and validate antibiotic resistance genes in S. pyogenes isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study compared the performance of the BD Phoenix CPO Detect panel and the Cepheid Xpert Carba-R assay for detecting carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates. The Xpert Carba-R assay identified KPC, NDM, VIM, OXA-48, and IMP genes, while the CPO panel classified carbapenemases into Ambler Classes A, B, and D.
full_output.methodology: The study used the BD Phoenix CPO Detect panel for phenotypic carbapenemase detection and the Xpert Carba-R assay for molecular detection of carbapenemase genes.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility patterns and trends of the gram-negative bacteria isolated from the patients in the emergency departments in China: results of SMART 2016-2019.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed antibiotic resistance patterns of Gram-negative bacteria in Chinese emergency departments, highlighting high resistance rates to commonly used antibiotics among E. coli, K. pneumoniae, and P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted antimicrobial susceptibility testing using CLSI broth microdilution and evaluated resistance profiles of 656 isolates collected from 18 hospitals across China between 2016 and 2019.

full_output.paper_title: Coaggregated E. faecalis with F. nucleatum regulated environmental stress responses and inflammatory effects.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that coaggregation of Enterococcus faecalis (Ef) with Fusobacterium nucleatum subsp. polymorphum (Fnp) enhanced Ef's resistance to environmental stressors such as alkalinity, hyperosmosis, nutrient starvation, and antibiotic challenges. Additionally, coaggregation facilitated Ef's invasion of dTHP-1 cells and improved its intracellular survival, while reducing the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines by macrophages.
full_output.methodology: The study used coaggregation assays, confocal laser scanning microscopy, environmental stress survival assays, bacterial infection of dTHP-1 cells, and transcriptomic analysis to investigate the effects of coaggregation on microbial behavior and host immune responses.

full_output.paper_title: Vitamin D and vitamin K1 as novel inhibitors of biofilm in Gram-negative bacteria.

cusD.encodes: a copper transporter involved in biofilm formation
cusD.notes: The wild-type cusD gene was not experimentally validated as an AMR gene, but its expression was affected by vitamins.

bssS.notes: The wild-type bssS gene was not experimentally validated as an AMR gene, but its expression was affected by vitamins.

pelA.notes: The wild-type pelA gene was not experimentally validated as an AMR gene, but its expression was affected by vitamins.
pelA.evidence_note: The paper shows that pelA is a biofilm-associated gene and that its expression is downregulated by vitamins D and K1. However, there is no evidence that mutations in pelA confer resistance to antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: Vitamin D and K1 significantly reduced biofilm formation in A. baumannii, K. pneumoniae, and P. aeruginosa by downregulating the expression of biofilm-related genes cusD, bssS, and pelA.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR was used to analyze the expression of biofilm-related genes in bacterial isolates treated with vitamin D and K1.

full_output.paper_title: Generation and maintenance of the circularized multimeric IS26-associated translocatable unit encoding multidrug resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the amplification of the P2 region containing multiple AMR genes, including bla CTX-M-14, tet(A), drfA, and sul1, in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates under antimicrobial selection pressure.
full_output.methodology: Digital PCR, long-read sequencing, and PFGE analysis were used to analyze the amplification and maintenance of the P2 region in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Nanocomposite alginate hydrogel loaded with propranolol hydrochloride kolliphor(®) based cerosomes as a repurposed platform for Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus-(MRSA)-induced skin infection; in-vitro, ex-vivo, in-silico, and in-vivo evaluation.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated a nanocomposite alginate hydrogel loaded with propranolol hydrochloride (PNL) cerosomes for treating MRSA-induced skin infections. The PNL-loaded CERs nanocomposite showed superior performance in inhibiting biofilm formation and eradicating MRSA compared to PNL solutions and composites.
full_output.methodology: The study used in-vitro, ex-vivo, in-silico, and in-vivo evaluations to assess the effectiveness of PNL-loaded CERs against MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of baicalin on eradicating biofilms of bovine milk derived Acinetobacter lwoffii.
full_output.key_findings: Baicalin significantly reduced the biomass and viable bacteria of biofilms in A.lwoffii. It also decreased the content of trehalose, which may be related to biofilm eradication. Several genes, including ahpC, otsA, otsB, mprA, rcsC-3, and betB, were differentially expressed in response to baicalin treatment.
full_output.methodology: The study used RNA-seq, qRT-PCR, molecular docking, and biochemical assays to investigate the effects of baicalin on A.lwoffii biofilms.

These genes were found to be prevalent and their abundance was influenced by various physicochemical factors.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR was used to detect and quantify the abundance of ARGs and intI 1 in wastewater samples.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Klebsiella pneumoniae Clinical Isolates Through Whole-Genome Sequencing: A Comprehensive Analysis of Serotypes, Sequence Types, and Antimicrobial and Virulence Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes, including bla SHV, bla CTX-M-15, bla TEM, bla OXA, bla NDM-1, and bla NDM-5, in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates. These genes conferred resistance to beta-lactams and carbapenems. The study also highlighted the presence of hypervirulent K. pneumoniae strains carrying these AMR genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was used to identify AMR and virulence genes in 18 multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Characterization of Silver Nanoparticles Using Bacterial Cultures for Antimicrobial and Dye Removal Applications
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using bacterial cultures, focusing on their antimicrobial activity and ability to remove methyl orange (MO) dye. The AgNPs synthesized by Micrococcus luteus (AgNPs-M) showed the highest MO dye removal efficiency and antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized bacterial cultures to synthesize AgNPs, analyzed their physicochemical properties using techniques such as UV-Vis spectroscopy, XRD, FTIR, and FESEM, and evaluated their antimicrobial activity through zone of inhibition (ZOI) assays and dye removal efficiency.

full_output.paper_title: High intestinal carriage of Clostridium perfringens in healthy individuals and ICU patients in Hangzhou, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high prevalence of Clostridium perfringens in healthy individuals and ICU patients, with significant resistance to erythromycin, clindamycin, and tetracycline mediated by erm(Q), lnu(P), tetB(P), and tetA(P).
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of C. perfringens isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Cryptic environmental conjugative plasmid recruits a novel hybrid transposon resulting in a new plasmid with higher dispersion potential.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel hybrid transposon Tn7714 carrying multiple antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) that was transferred from an IncF plasmid to a cryptic IncX plasmid, resulting in a new multidrug-resistant conjugative plasmid with significantly higher conjugation efficiency.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, conjugation experiments, MIC tests, and gel electrophoresis were used to analyze the transfer and functionality of the ARGs.
full_output.sample_size: One environmental isolate (E. coli SW4848) and derived strains.

full_output.paper_title: Lipid A modification of colistin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae does not alter innate immune response in a mouse model of pneumonia.
full_output.key_findings: The mcr-1 plasmid confers colistin resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae without altering bacterial fitness or immune response in a mouse model.
full_output.methodology: MIC testing, bacterial growth kinetics, cytokine production analysis, and mouse infection model.

full_output.paper_title: Multimodal inhibitory effect of matcha on Porphyromonas gingivalis.
full_output.key_findings: Matcha extract (ME) effectively inhibits the growth of Porphyromonas gingivalis, causing morphological and physiological changes in the bacterial envelope, including nano-particle formation and decreased membrane fluidity/permeability. full_output.paper_title: Genomic characterization of carbapenem and colistin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from humans and dogs.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized carbapenem and colistin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from humans and dogs in Thailand, identifying multiple beta-lactamase genes, fosfomycin resistance genes, quinolone resistance genes, and the mcr-3.5 gene for colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize resistance genes in the isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Six isolates from humans and dogs.

full_output.paper_title: Unraveling the efficacy of verbascoside in thwarting MRSA pathogenicity by targeting sortase A.
full_output.key_findings: Verbascoside was identified as a potent inhibitor of SrtA, reducing S. aureus adhesion, invasion, and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Fluorescence quenching, molecular docking, and biochemical assays were used to evaluate the interaction between verbascoside and SrtA.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the potential of isorhapontigenin: attenuating Staphylococcus aureus virulence through MgrA-mediated regulation.

mgrA.notes: MgrA is a transcriptional regulator, not an AMR gene.

full_output.key_findings: Isorhapontigenin attenuates Staphylococcus aureus virulence by modulating MgrA-mediated regulation, reducing hemolytic activity, cytotoxicity, and intra-macrophage survival without conferring antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Experimental validation of isorhapontigenin's effects on S. aureus virulence factors, including hemolysis, cytotoxicity, and macrophage survival, along with molecular assays to assess gene expression and protein interactions.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-wide CRISPRi screens for high-throughput fitness quantification and identification of determinants for dalbavancin susceptibility in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes that influence susceptibility to dalbavancin in Staphylococcus aureus using CRISPRi-seq, including kapB, dltABCD, vraFG, ezrA, rpsF-ssb-rpsR, nrdF, facZ, pbp4, sagB, aroB, ebpS, and SAOUHSC_00659. Knockdown of these genes increases sensitivity to dalbavancin, highlighting their roles in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: CRISPRi-seq and direct selection methods were used to identify genes affecting dalbavancin susceptibility in Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic investigation and clinical correlates of the in vitro β-lactam: NaHCO(3) responsiveness phenotype among methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates from a randomized clinical trial.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified specific genotypic markers associated with the NaHCO3-responsive phenotype in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates, particularly mutations in the mecA gene regulatory region, which were linked to reduced resistance to β-lactams.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, broth microdilution, and genotypic analysis were used to investigate the NaHCO3-responsive phenotype in MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Clostridioides difficile-mucus interactions encompass shifts in gene expression, metabolism, and biofilm formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes such as CDR0455, CDR0693, and CDR2495 that are upregulated in response to mucus and play roles in transport and metabolism, enhancing C. difficile growth.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq, mutant analysis, and growth assays were used to investigate C. difficile-mucus interactions.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, identification, antibiotic resistance profile and molecular analysis of Ornithobacterium rhinotracheal isolates from turkeys.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of adk, copA, and vapD genes in Ornithobacterium rhinotracheale isolates from turkeys, along with high levels of resistance to several antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies oxygen as a critical resource limiting the growth of Candida albicans in the gut. It shows that restoring epithelial hypoxia, either through probiotic Escherichia coli or the drug 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA), can enhance colonization resistance against C. albicans after antibiotic treatment.
full_output.methodology: The study used mouse models, metabolomic analyses, and in vitro growth assays to investigate the role of oxygen and microbiota in C. albicans colonization resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Ribosomal RNA methylation in Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli: effect of the "MLS" (erythromycin resistance) methylase.

ermB.validation_method: analysis of methylation of 23S rRNA and resistance to erythromycin

ermC.validation_method: analysis of methylation of 23S rRNA and resistance to erythromycin

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the MLS methylase genes ermB and ermC, which confer resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, and streptogramin B by methylating specific adenosine residues in the 23S rRNA of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: Analysis of methylation of 23S rRNA and resistance to erythromycin in various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Contribution of beta-lactamases to bacterial resistance and mechanisms to inhibit beta-lactamases.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the role of beta-lactamases in bacterial resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics and highlights the TEM enzyme as a common plasmid-mediated beta-lactamase found in various bacterial species. It also describes the mechanism of action of clavulanic acid as a beta-lactamase inhibitor.
full_output.methodology: Review and discussion of experimental studies on beta-lactamases and their inhibition.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a colistin resistant, hypervirulent hospital isolate of Acinetobacter courvalinii from Canada.

udp-glucose dehydrogenase.mechanism: involved in capsule formation and colistin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies an intrinsic phosphoethanolamine transferase (mcr-like gene) and a UDP-glucose dehydrogenase gene as potential contributors to colistin resistance in the Acinetobacter courvalinii isolate AB222-IK40.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, phylogenomic analysis, and lipidomics were used to investigate colistin resistance mechanisms in AB222-IK40.

full_output.paper_title: Failure of ceftazidime/avibactam experimental therapy in the treatment of Klebsiella pneumoniae ST11 co-producing NDM-1 and OXA-48 carbapenemases infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the failure of ceftazidime/avibactam (CAZ-AVI) in treating a Klebsiella pneumoniae ST11 infection co-producing NDM-1 and OXA-48 carbapenemases, highlighting the importance of susceptibility testing before using CAZ-AVI for carbapenem-resistant organisms.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection of carbapenemase genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antagonistic Effects and the Underlying Mechanisms of Bacillus velezensis and its Antibacterial Peptide LCI Against Aeromonas hydrophila Infection in Largemouth Bass.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LCI, an antimicrobial peptide from Bacillus velezensis FLU-1, which shows potent antagonistic activity against Aeromonas hydrophila by disrupting membrane integrity, reducing biofilm formation, and affecting DNA structure.
full_output.methodology: The study used transcriptomic analysis, phenotypic tests, and gel-retardation analysis to investigate the antibacterial mechanisms of LCI.

full_output.paper_title: Correlation between Antibiotics-Resistance, Virulence Genes and Genotypes among Klebsiella pneumoniae Clinical Strains Isolated in Guangzhou, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenemase genes KPC, VIM, and NDM, along with virulence genes entB, mrkD, ybtS, kfu, iutA, rmpA, and allS in Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolates. High resistance rates to penicillin and cephalosporins were observed, with KPC being the most prevalent carbapenemase gene.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and ERIC-PCR were used for detection of carbapenemase and virulence genes, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the BD Phoenix-100 system.

full_output.paper_title: Single-/Co-Driving of Tetracycline, Triclocarban and Zinc on Microbial Community, Resistome and Function in the Cyanobacteria-Blooming Freshwater Ecosystem.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effects of tetracycline, triclocarban, and zinc on the microbial community, resistome, and function in a cyanobacteria-blooming freshwater ecosystem. It found that these chemicals altered the microbial community structure, increased the antibiotic resistome, and identified several genera potentially carrying antibiotic resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used amplicon and metagenomic sequencing to analyze microbial community composition, resistome, and functional pathways in a mesocosm experiment.

full_output.paper_title: Purification of Potential Antimicrobial Metabolites from Endophytic Fusarium oxysporum Isolated from Myrtus communis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two bioactive compounds, ethyl iso-allocholate and 1-monolinoleoylglycerol trimethylsilyl ether, from the endophytic fungus Fusarium oxysporum, which showed significant antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.methodology: The study used column chromatography, TLC, GC-MS, and in vitro antibacterial assays to isolate and evaluate the antimicrobial potential of compounds from Fusarium oxysporum.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance among extended-spectrum β-lactamase isolates of E. coli and K. pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance genes, including qnrS, qnrC, qnrD, qnrB, and qnrVC, in extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing E. coli and K. pneumoniae isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR, plasmid profiling, and conjugation experiments were used to detect and characterize plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Suppressing Mycobacterium tuberculosis virulence and drug resistance by targeting Eis protein through computational drug discovery.

eis.mechanism: The Eis protein functions by adding acetyl groups to aminoglycoside antibiotics, which interferes with their ability to bind to the bacterial ribosome, thereby preventing them from inhibiting protein synthesis and killing the bacterium.
eis.role_in_paper: The Eis protein is targeted to suppress Mycobacterium tuberculosis virulence and drug resistance by inhibiting its acetyltransferase activity.
eis.validation_method: Computational drug discovery and molecular dynamics simulations were used to identify natural compounds that inhibit the Eis protein.
eis.genetic_context: The eis gene encodes the Eis protein, which is an acetyltransferase enzyme of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
eis.source: The study focuses on the Eis protein as a target for developing inhibitors against drug-resistant tuberculosis.
eis.evidence_note: The paper describes the mechanism of the Eis protein in conferring resistance to aminoglycoside antibiotics by acetylation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several natural compounds that inhibit the Eis protein of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which is involved in drug resistance and virulence. These compounds show potential as inhibitors of the Eis protein, which could help restore the effectiveness of aminoglycoside drugs against drug-resistant TB.
full_output.methodology: The study uses computational drug discovery methods, including virtual screening, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations, to identify and evaluate natural compounds that inhibit the Eis protein of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Novel quinolone substituted 1,3,4-oxadiazole derivatives: design, synthesis, antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory potential.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design, synthesis, and evaluation of novel quinolone-substituted 1,3,4-oxadiazole derivatives with antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory potential. Compounds 4f, 4h, and 4k showed significant antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli with MICs of 8 µg/mL. Compound 4k exhibited high anti-inflammatory activity with 41.4% inhibition. However, none of the compounds were found to possess AMR genes or mutations.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and characterized using IR, NMR, and mass spectrometry. Their antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activities were evaluated using MIC assays and carrageenan-induced paw oedema tests in rats.

full_output.key_findings: The paper describes the use of synthetic oligonucleotides for gene isolation, site-directed mutagenesis, and total gene synthesis, focusing on the engineering of human alpha-1-antitrypsin variants with altered functional properties.
full_output.methodology: Synthetic oligonucleotides were used for gene isolation, site-directed mutagenesis, and total gene synthesis, with functional validation through expression in E. coli and biochemical assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 874 antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the Three Gorges Reservoir sediments, with macB being the dominant ARG. The major resistance mechanism was antibiotic efflux, and the primary contributors to ARGs were Betaproteobacteria and Gammaproteobacteria.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing was used to analyze the abundance, diversity, and distribution of ARGs in the sediments of the Three Gorges Reservoir.

full_output.paper_title: The Occurrence of Colistin Resistance in Potential Lactic Acid Bacteria of Food-Producing Animals in India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1 and mcr-3 genes in colistin-resistant lactic acid bacteria from food-producing animals in India, highlighting the need for enhanced surveillance of colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic analyses, including PCR, MIC testing, and biofilm formation assays.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a KPC-84 harboring Klebsiella pneumoniae ST11 clinical isolate with ceftazidime-avibactam resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel KPC variant, KPC-84, in a Klebsiella pneumoniae ST11 clinical isolate from China, which exhibits resistance to ceftazidime-avibactam. KPC-84 shows slightly higher hydrolysis of ceftazidime and reduced affinity to avibactam compared to KPC-2, but restores susceptibility to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, cloning, MIC assessment, qRT-PCR, and enzyme kinetics analysis.

full_output.paper_title: The relationship between resistance evolution and carbon metabolism in Staphylococcus xylosus under ceftiofur sodium stress.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the relationship between resistance evolution and carbon metabolism in Staphylococcus xylosus under ceftiofur sodium stress, revealing changes in protein expression related to glycolysis, peptidoglycan hydrolase, and the TCA cycle, suggesting a potential role of carbon metabolism in resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The study used iTRAQ-based comparative proteomics to analyze protein expression changes in S. xylosus under ceftiofur sodium stress, along with qRT-PCR and metabolite analysis to validate findings.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity of endophytic bacteria with antimicrobial potential isolated from marine macroalgae from Yacila and Cangrejos beaches, Piura-Peru.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of iturin C and fengycin D genes in Kluyvera ascorbata YAFE21 and Bacillus sp. YCFE4, respectively, indicating their potential for antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing of iturin, fengycin, and surfactin genes from selected endophytic bacteria strains.

full_output.paper_title: Excellent adsorption of toxic Cd (II) ions from water with effective antibacterial activity by novel GO-ZnO-curcumin composite.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a novel GO-ZnO-curcumin composite with high adsorption capacity for Cd(II) ions and effective antibacterial activity against Bacillus subtilis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of the composite, adsorption studies, and MIC testing for antibacterial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a novel phage against multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.

wbaP.notes: Mutation in wbaP gene leads to loss of capsule polysaccharide, resulting in increased antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel phage, RCIP0100, with broad lytic activity against multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (MDR-KP) strains, including carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CR-KP). A phage-resistant mutant strain, KP1738r, was found to have a mutation in the wbaP gene, leading to increased antibiotic susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, genome sequencing, host range determination, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and characterization of a novel type II toxin-antitoxin system in Aeromonas veronii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes a novel type II toxin-antitoxin system, AvtA-AvtT, in Aeromonas veronii. AvtA functions as a toxin, while AvtT functions as an antitoxin, forming a genuine TA system. The system was validated through host killing and rescue assays in E. coli, demonstrating their interaction and functionality.
full_output.methodology: The study used host killing and rescue assays, dot blotting, co-immunoprecipitation, and fluorescence microscopy to validate the AvtA-AvtT toxin-antitoxin system in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Modern beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the development and characteristics of modern beta-lactam antibiotics, focusing on their structure, activity, and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews the chemistry, microbiology, and pharmacology of beta-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Deeper Exploration of Gut Microbiome: Profile of Resistome, Virome and Viral Auxiliary Metabolic Genes of Three Ethnic Indian Groups.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance genes tet(W), erm(F), and tet(Q) in the gut microbiomes of three Indian ethnic groups, with higher burdens observed in the Khargone and Ladakh groups compared to the Jaisalmer group.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis using Groot and Resfinder tools to profile antibiotic resistance genes and viromes.

full_output.paper_title: Infection by a multidrug-resistant Corynebacterium diphtheriae strain: prediction of virulence factors, CRISPR-Cas system analysis, and structural implications of mutations conferring rifampin resistance.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: The mutation causes a serine to tyrosine substitution at position 442, leading to a more hydrophobic environment in the rifampin binding pocket, which reduces the effectiveness of rifampin.

rpoB.notes: Mutation in rpoB gene causes rifampin resistance
rpoB.evidence_note: The paper states that the strain IHP6573 was identified as MDR and that the mutation in rpoB gene was associated with rifampin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: The effect of novel β-lactam derivatives synthesized from substituted phenethylamines on resistance genes of MRSA isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of mecA and blaZ resistance genes in MRSA isolates and demonstrated that novel β-lactam derivatives (10) and (12) inhibited β-lactamase, reduced the expression of resistance genes, and exhibited low cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, disc diffusion, microdilution, qRT-PCR, and nitrocefin assays to evaluate the antibacterial activity and resistance gene expression of novel β-lactam derivatives against MRSA isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Clinical MRSA isolates from Atatrk University Research Hospital and Yeditepe University Hospital

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance pattern of bacterial strains emerged using frequent hand sanitizers during corona pandemic.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains, including Bacillus sp., Staphylococcus sp., Paenibacillus sp., Lysinibacillus sp., Exiguobacterium sp., and Leclercia sp., which exhibited resistance to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting bacterial strains from volunteers' hands before and after using different hand sanitizers, followed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and antibiotic resistance profiling using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: A first study of meat-borne enterococci from butcher shops: prevalence, virulence characteristics, antibiotic resistance and clonal relationship.

tet(L).validation_method: PCR detection of antibiotic resistance genes

aac(6')-Ie-aph(2\")-la.validation_method: PCR detection of antibiotic resistance genes

ermB.validation_method: PCR detection of antibiotic resistance genes

full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance gene tet(L), aminoglycoside resistance gene aac(6')-Ie-aph(2")-la, and macrolide/lincosamide/streptogramin B resistance gene ermB in Enterococcus isolates from meat samples.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of antibiotic resistance genes and virulence factors, along with pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) for genetic fingerprinting.

full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed plastic debris in the Periyar River and found that bacterial isolates exhibited high levels of antimicrobial resistance, particularly to colistin. Six isolates with high multiple antibiotic resistance (MAR) indices were identified as Bacillus species, including Bacillus pumilus, Bacillus cereus, and others.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolates were obtained from plastic debris, screened for antimicrobial resistance, and identified using 16S rRNA sequencing. Biofilm formation was assessed on plastic samples in different media.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and molecular characterization of multidrug-resistant coagulase negative staphylococci from urban wastewater in Delhi-NCR, India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in multidrug-resistant coagulase negative staphylococci (MR-CoNS) isolated from urban wastewater in Delhi-NCR, India, including mecA, blaZ, msrA, aac(6')-Ib, aph(3')-IIIa, ant(4')-Ia, dfrG, dfrA, tetK, and tetM.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based detection of antibiotic resistance genes in MR-CoNS isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study isolated and characterized three Acinetobacter baumannii phages (vB_AbaS_Ftm, vB_AbaS_Eva, and vB_AbaS_Gln) from hospital sewage and evaluated their antibacterial effects against extensively drug-resistant (XDR) A. baumannii strains. The phages exhibited siphovirus morphology and showed synergistic effects when combined with antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, morphology analysis, host range determination, genome sequencing, and time-kill assays were performed to evaluate the antibacterial effects of the phages and their combinations with antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Tapping into haloalkaliphilic bacteria for sustainable agriculture in treated wastewater: insights into genomic fitness and environmental adaptation
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several heavy metal resistance genes in Oceanobacillus picturae M4W.A2, including chrA, copA, cobZ, and cdmA, which confer resistance to chromium, copper, cadmium, and zinc. Additionally, the strain possesses genes for oxidative stress response and ectoine biosynthesis, aiding in its adaptation to extreme environments. The presence of an ABC-type antimicrobial peptide transport system suggests potential resistance to antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.methodology: Genomic annotation, RAST annotation, antiSMASH server prediction, and IslandViewer4 analysis were used to identify and characterize the genes and genomic features of Oceanobacillus picturae M4W.A2.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three classes of trifluorothymidine-resistant (TFTr) mutants in L5178Y/TK+/− mouse lymphoma cells, namely large colony (λ), small colony (σ), and tiny colony (τ) mutants. The σ and τ mutants are associated with chromosomal abnormalities, while λ mutants exhibit normal karyotypes. All mutants analyzed were TK-deficient, indicating a disruption in the thymidine kinase gene.
full_output.methodology: The study employed mutagen treatment, cloning techniques, cytogenetic analysis, and thymidine kinase enzyme assays to characterize TFTr mutants.

full_output.paper_title: Pneumolysin-responsive liposomal platform for selective treatment of Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a cholesterol-rich liposomal platform that selectively releases nisin in response to pneumolysin, demonstrating effective antibacterial activity against Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The study used liposomal formulation, hemolytic activity assays, and antibacterial testing to evaluate the performance of the cholesterol-rich liposomal platform.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of Pathogenic Cronobacter Species as Bacteriological Risks Indicator in Powdered Infant Formula Available to Deprived Infants in Lagos Metropolis, Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Cronobacter spp. in 13% of powdered infant formula (PIF) samples, highlighting their potential as bacteriological risks. These isolates exhibited resistance to several antibiotics, including cefotaxime, ceftriaxone, gentamicin, and amoxicillin-clavulanic acid.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolates were characterized using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, antibiotic sensitivity testing, and phenotypic assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies penicillinase-producing Neisseria gonorrhoeae (PPNG) strains and their antimicrobial susceptibility profiles, highlighting resistance to co-trimoxazole, tetracycline, and streptomycin, while remaining susceptible to spectinomycin, cefuroxime, kanamycin, amoxycillin combined with clavulanic acid, and rosoxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed PPNG strains isolated from patients at the Whitechapel Clinic, performing antimicrobial susceptibility testing and plasmid typing.

full_output.paper_title: Bismuth-based drugs sensitize Pseudomonas aeruginosa to multiple antibiotics by disrupting iron homeostasis.
full_output.key_findings: Bismuth-based drugs enhance the efficacy of multiple antibiotics against Pseudomonas aeruginosa by disrupting iron homeostasis, leading to impaired electron transport chain activity and efflux pump dysfunction.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analyses, MIC determination, synergy tests, and biochemical assays were used to evaluate the effects of bismuth on P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Understanding the rationale and clinical impact of the revised CLSI 2024 minocycline susceptibility breakpoints against Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the reduced susceptibility of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia to minocycline following the revised CLSI 2024 breakpoints, emphasizing the need for updated treatment strategies.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 201 S. maltophilia isolates using broth microdilution to determine MICs and assess susceptibility to various antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence, distribution, and ecological risks of antibiotics and antibiotic resistance genes in the surface waters of Gaoyou Lake, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified sulfonamide resistance genes sul1 and sul2, as well as the integron gene intl1, in the surface waters of Gaoyou Lake, China. These genes were found to be highly abundant, indicating a significant presence of antibiotic resistance in the lake's ecosystem.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR to analyze the occurrence and distribution of antibiotic resistance genes in surface water samples from Gaoyou Lake.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of bacteriocin produced by a new strain of Enterococcus faecalis BDR22.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a bacteriocin produced by Enterococcus faecalis BDR22 that exhibits significant antibacterial and antibiofilm activities against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The bacteriocin effectively reduces biofilm formation and disrupts the extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) of the biofilm.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and characterization of the bacteriocin-producing strain BDR22, purification of the bacteriocin, and assessment of its antibacterial and antibiofilm activities through various experimental techniques including agar well diffusion assay, MIC/MBC determination, biofilm eradication assays, and molecular docking studies.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of antibiotic resistance genes, heavy metal, and bacterial community composition in sea sediments influenced by Eriocheir sinensis breeding aquaculture.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in sea sediments influenced by Eriocheir sinensis breeding aquaculture, including sul1, sul2, aadA, strA, strB, tetM, and tetQ. These genes were predominantly found in wastewater discharge areas, indicating a significant impact of aquaculture practices on the spread of ARGs.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR to quantify ARGs and 16S rRNA sequencing to analyze bacterial community composition in sediment samples from wastewater discharge and control areas.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, spectroscopic characterization, DFT calculations, in silico-ADMET and molecular docking analysis of novel quinoline-substituted 5H-chromeno [2,3-b] pyridine derivatives as antibacterial agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and in vitro antibacterial evaluation of novel quinoline-substituted 5H-chromeno[2,3-b] pyridine derivatives. Compounds 4A, 4F, 4G, 4J, and 4K showed strong antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Molecular docking analysis revealed that these compounds interact with DNA gyrase, suggesting a potential mechanism of action.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and characterized using spectroscopic techniques. Their antibacterial activity was assessed using the agar-well diffusion method. Molecular docking studies were conducted to investigate their interaction with DNA gyrase.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of antibiotic resistance genes in different drinking water treatment processes in a northwest Chinese city.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring Antimicrobial Potency, ADMET, and Optimal Drug Target of a Non-ribosomal Peptide Sevadicin from Bacillus pumilus, through In Vitro Assay and Molecular Dynamics Simulation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified sevadicin, a non-ribosomal peptide from Bacillus pumilus, which inhibits bacterial growth by targeting the MurE enzyme involved in cell wall synthesis.
full_output.methodology: In vitro assays, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to evaluate the antimicrobial potency and mechanism of sevadicin.
